semin-durr:4-4.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةً}: a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It is the plural of «صَدُقة», with fatḥa on the ṣād and ḍamma on the dāl, on the pattern of «سَمُرة», and what is meant by it is the bridal gift (mahr). This is the well-known reading, and it is the dialect of the Ḥijāz. Qatāda read: «صُدْقاتهن», with ḍamma on the ṣād and sukūn on the dāl, plural of صُدْقة on the pattern of غُرْفة. Mujāhid and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with ḍamma on both, and it is the plural of صُدُقة with ḍamma on the ṣād and the dāl, which is the "heavy" form of the one with a quiescent dāl, made for vowel harmony (itbāʿ). Ibn Waththāb and al-Nakhaʿī read: «صُدُقَتَهُنَّ», with ḍamma on both, in the singular. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the heavy form of «صُدْقة», like their saying «ظُلُمة» for «ظُلْمة»." We have already mentioned a disagreement: is it permissible to make "heavy" (vowel) a quiescent letter whose first radical has ḍamma? It was also read: «صَدْقاتِهن», with fatḥa on the ṣād and sukūn on the dāl, which is the lightened form of the well-known reading, like their saying عَضْد for عَضُد.

In the accusative of «نِحْلة» there are four views. First: it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), its governor being the verb before it, because «آتُوهُنَّ» has the meaning of «انحِلوهُنَّ» (give them freely); so it is a maṣdar not from the verb's own root (ʿalā ghayr al-ṣadr), as in «قَعَدْت جلوساً» (I sat down a sitting).

Second: it is a maṣdar standing in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial). As to the one whom the ḥāl describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl), there are three possibilities. First: it is the fāʿil (agent) in «فآتُوهُنَّ», i.e., "then give them, freely giving." Second: it is the first object, namely «النساء». Third: it is the second object, namely «صدقاتهن», i.e., "freely given."

The third view: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), if it is interpreted in the sense of «شِرْعة» (a prescribed law).

The fourth view: it is accusative by an implied verb with the meaning of "prescribed," i.e., "Allah has given this as a nihla," meaning He prescribed it as a law and a religion.

Al-niḥla: a gift given willingly; al-niḥla: a law (shirʿa) — and from this is «نِحْلة الإِسلام خير النِحَل» (the creed of Islam is the best of creeds), and "so-and-so yantaḥilu such-and-such," i.e., he professes it as a religion; and al-niḥla: an obligatory duty.

Al-Rāghib said: "Al-niḥla and al-naḥla: a gift given by way of voluntary generosity; it is more specific than a hiba (gift), since every niḥla is a hiba, but not the reverse. Its derivation, as I see it, is from al-naḥl (bees), with regard to their activity, as if «نَحَلْتُه» meant 'I gave him the gift of the bee.'" Then he said: "And it is possible that al-niḥla is the origin, and the bees were named that with regard to their activity." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "From 'he naḥala him such-and-such': he gave it to him and granted it to him willingly, niḥla and naḥl; and from this is the ḥadīth of Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him: 'I had given you (naḥaltuki) the harvest of twenty wasqs.'"

His words: «منه» are in the position of the genitive (majrūr), because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «شيء», so it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted word, i.e., "about something that is from it." As for «مِنْ» there, there are two views. First: it is partitive, and for that reason she may not give him the whole bridal gift; this was the view of al-Layth. Second: it is explicative (for clarifying the genus), and for that reason she may give him the whole bridal gift. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«مِنْ» here is for clarifying the genus, and for that reason she may give away the whole mahr; had it been partitive, that would not have been permissible." End of quote. It was mentioned above that al-Layth forbids that, so its being partitive presents no difficulty.

As for this pronoun, there are several views. First: it refers back to the bridal gift (al-ṣadāq) indicated by «صَدُقاتِهِنَّ». Second: it refers back to «الصَّدُقات» because the singular can fill its place: had it been said «صَداقَهُنَّ», the meaning would not have been disturbed. This resembles their saying: «هو أحسنُ الفتيان وأجملُه» (he is the finest of the young men and the handsomest of them [lit. "of it"]), because had it been said «هو أحسن فتىً» (he is the finest young man), the meaning would be correct. Similar to it is:

1539 - وطابَ ألبانُ اللِّقاح وبَرَدْ
(And the milk [pl.] of the milch-camels was good and became cool [sing.].)

In «برد» there is a pronoun referring back to «ألبان», because «لَبَن» (milk, sing.) can fill its place. Third: it also refers back to «الصَّدُقات», but by treating the pronoun the way a demonstrative is treated, for a demonstrative may, in the masculine singular, point to several things that preceded it, as in His words: {قُلْ أَؤُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِخَيْرٍ مِّن ذلكم} [Āl ʿImrān: 15], after He had mentioned several things before it. And you have already met, in al-Baqara, what is related about Ruʾba when he was asked about his words:

1540 - فيها خطوطٌ من سوادٍ وبَلَقْ ... كأنَّه في الجلدِ تَوْليعُ البَهَقْ
(In it are streaks of black and piebald white, as if it [masc. sing.] on the skin were the blotching of leucoderma.)

[He answered:] "I meant 'that'," so he treated the pronoun the way a demonstrative is treated. Fourth: it refers back to wealth (al-māl), even though it has not been mentioned, because the bridal gifts indicate it. Fifth: it refers back to the giving (al-ītāʾ) indicated by «آتُوا»; al-Rāghib and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. Sixth: al-Zamakhsharī said: "The pronoun may be masculine so that it refers to the single bridal gift, and so it covers part of it; had it been feminine, its apparent sense would cover giving away the whole bridal gift, because 'part of the bridal gifts' is one of them or more." And the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "I say: what makes the masculine pronoun good is that the meaning of «فإنْ طِبْنَ» is 'if each one of them is pleased'; for that reason He said «منه», i.e., from her bridal gift. It is parallel to {وَأَعْتَدَتْ لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَئاً} [Yūsuf: 31], i.e., for each one of them, and for that reason He made «مُتَّكأً» singular."

His words: «نَفْساً» is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), and here it is transferred from the fāʿil, since the underlying form is "if their souls are pleased." Similar to it is: {واشتعل الرأس شَيْباً} [Maryam: 4]. This is accusative after the completion of the sentence. The tamyīz was brought here in the singular, even though a plural precedes it, because there is no ambiguity, since it is known that they do not all share in a single soul. Similar to it is: «قَرَّ الزيدون عيناً» (the Zayds were cool of eye), and «أنفساً» and «أعيناً» are also permissible. And we must touch on a rule of general benefit: when a tamyīz occurs after a plural, accusative after the completion of the sentence, then it is either in agreement in meaning with what precedes it or different from it. If it is the first, the tamyīz must agree with what precedes it, as in: «كَرُمَ الزيدون رجالاً» (the Zayds were noble as men), just as it agrees with it as a khabar (predicate), an adjective or a ḥāl.

If it is the second, then it either has a single referent or differing referents. If it has a single referent, the tamyīz must be singular, as you say of the sons of one man: «كَرُم بنو زيد أباً أو أصلاً» (the sons of Zayd were noble in father, or in origin), i.e., they all have one father who is characterised by nobility. Similar to it is: «كَرُم الأتقياءُ سَعْياً» (the pious were noble in endeavour), if you do not intend by the maṣdar a difference of kinds owing to the difference of those in whom it resides.

If it has differing referents, then either making the tamyīz singular would cause ambiguity or it would not. If it would cause ambiguity, agreement is required, as in: «كَرُم الزيدون آباء» (the Zayds were noble in fathers), i.e., each one has a father different from the other's father, characterised by nobility; had it been made singular here, it would be imagined that they are all the sons of one father, while the intent is the opposite. If it would not cause ambiguity, both are permissible, agreement and the singular, and the singular is preferable; for that reason the noble verse came in accordance with it. The ruling for the dual in this is like the plural.

What also made the singular good here is what was mentioned earlier as making the masculine and singular pronoun in «منه» good, namely that the meaning is: "if each one of them is pleased in soul." One of the Basrans said: "It was made singular only because what is meant by 'soul' here is desire (al-hawā), and desire is a maṣdar, and maṣdars are not made dual or plural." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«نفساً» is a tamyīz, and it is singular because the purpose is to state the genus, and the singular indicates it." Abū al-Baqāʾ took a similar line, and likened it to «درهماً» in your saying «عشرون درهماً» (twenty dirhams).

The grammarians disagreed about whether the tamyīz may be placed before its governor when the governor is a fully inflected (mutaṣarrif) verb. Sībawayh forbade it, while al-Mubarrad and a group allowed it, citing as evidence their saying:

1541 - أَتَهْجُرُ ليلى بالفراقِ حبيبها ... وما كان نفساً بالفراقِ تَطِيب
(Does Laylā forsake her beloved by parting, when she was never, in soul, content with parting?)

And his words:

1542 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . إذا عِطْفاه ماءً تَحَلَّبا
(... when his two flanks dripped with water [i.e., sweat].)

The underlying forms are «تطيبُ نفساً» and «تحلَّبا ماء». There is long discussion of the two verses which this is not the place for. Sībawayh's argument for forbidding it is that the tamyīz is in origin a fāʿil, and the fāʿil does not come first, and so likewise what is equivalent to it. This was objected to with «زيداً» in your saying «أخرجْتُ زيداً» (I brought Zayd out), for «زيداً» was in origin a fāʿil before the transfer, since the underlying form is «خرج زيد» (Zayd went out). But the difference is clear. The tamyīz has many types, mentioned in the books of the grammarians.

The two prepositional phrases in His words: «فإن طِبْنَ لكم عن شيءٍ» are attached to the verb before them, which is made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of turning away (from a claim); for that reason it is made transitive with «عَنْ», as if it were said: "if they turn away for you from something, willing in soul." The fāʾ in «فَكُلوه» is the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis) and it is obligatory, and the hāʾ in «فَكُلوه» refers back to «شيء».

His words: {هَنِيئاً مَّرِيئاً}: in the accusative of «هنيئاً» there are four views. First: it is accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, the implied form being "an eating that is wholesome." Second: it is accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «فكلوه», i.e., "made wholesome," that is, easy. Third: it is accusative as a ḥāl governed by a verb that may never be made overt at all, because this ḥāl is intended to substitute for its verb, as in «أقائماً وقد قعد الناس» (standing, when the people have sat down?), just as a maṣdar substitutes for its verb, as in «سُقْياً له ورَعْياً» (may he be watered and cared for). Fourth: they are two adjectives that have taken the place of a maṣdar intended for supplication which substitutes for its verb. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "One may pause at «فكلوه» and begin «هنيئاً مريئاً» as a supplication, on the view that they are two adjectives set in the place of two maṣdars, as if it were said: هَنْئاً مَرْءاً."

The Shaykh said: "This is a distortion of the grammarians' words, and his distortion is that he made them stand in the place of the maṣdar, so that their accusative is the accusative of the maṣdar; for that reason he said 'as if it were said: هَنْئاً مَرْءاً,' so that it became like your saying «سُقْياً لك» and «رَعْياً لك». What shows his distortion and the correctness of the grammarians' view is that maṣdars intended for supplication do not put an overt noun in the nominative: you do not say «سقياً الله لك» nor «رعياً الله لك», even though that is permissible with their verbs; whereas «هنيئاً مريئاً» do put an overt noun in the nominative, as evidenced by his words:

1543 - هنيئاً مريئاً غيرَ داءٍ مُخامِرٍ ... لعَزَّةَ مِنْ أَعْراضِنا ما استحَلَّتِ
(Wholesome and pleasant, no lingering malady, be to ʿAzza whatever of our honour she has deemed lawful.)

So «ما» is nominative through «هنيئاً» or through «مريئاً», by way of iʿmāl (two governors competing for one noun). That was permissible even though there is no link between the two governors by a conjunction or anything else, because «مريئاً» is only used as a follower of «هنيئاً», so the two are as one governor; had you said «قام قعد زيد», it would not be a case of iʿmāl except by intending a conjunction." End of quote.

However, there is in Sībawayh's wording what points to what al-Zamakhsharī said, for he said: "«هنيئاً مريئاً» are two adjectives whose accusative is the accusative of maṣdars used in supplication, by the verb whose overt use is not employed, elided because the speech indicates it, as if they said: 'that has become established, wholesome and pleasant'." So the beginning of the wording supports al-Zamakhsharī, while its end, namely his implied form "as if they said: 'that has become established, wholesome'," muddies it for him. So on the first two views «هنيئاً مريئاً» are connected to the sentence before them in wording and meaning, while on the last two they are cut off in wording, because their governor is implied from another sentence, as was established above.

The grammarians disagreed about your saying, to someone who said "So-and-so obtained good": «هنيئاً له ذلك» (wholesome to him be that): is «ذلك» nominative through the implied verb, the implied form being "that became established for him, wholesome," with «ثبت» elided and «هنيئاً», which is a ḥāl, taking its place; or is it nominative through «هنيئاً» itself, because when it took the place of the verb it put in the nominative what the verb would put in the nominative — just as in your saying «زيدٌ في الدار» (Zayd is in the house), «في الدار» [carries] a pronoun that was latent in "being settled" (al-istiqrār), and when "being settled" was elided and the prepositional phrase took its place, it put in the nominative the pronoun that had been in it? Al-Sīrāfī held the first view and placed in «هنيئاً» a pronoun referring back to «ذلك»; Abū ʿAlī held the second and made «هنيئاً» empty of a pronoun because it puts the overt noun in the nominative. If you say «هنيئاً» without saying «ذلك», then on al-Sīrāfī's view there is in «هنيئاً» a pronoun referring back to the one described by the ḥāl, which is the agent pronoun that was latent in the elided «ثَبَتَ»; and on al-Fārisī's view there is in «هنيئاً» a pronoun that is its fāʿil, which is the pronoun that was the fāʿil of «ثَبَتَ», and «هنيئاً» has taken the place of the elided verb, empty of a pronoun.

As for the accusative of «مريئاً», there are five views [Translator's note: only two are enumerated in the text as given]. First: it is an adjective of «هنيئاً»; al-Ḥūfī held this. Second: it is accusative in the same way as «هنيئاً», and the views about that have been mentioned above. Al-Fārisī rejected its being an adjective of «هنيئاً», saying: "Because «هنيئاً» has taken the place of the verb, and the verb is not qualified by an adjective, and likewise what takes its place." What supports al-Fārisī's statement is that the active participle, the passive participle, the intensive forms and maṣdars, when qualified by an adjective, do not govern as the verb does.

«مريئاً» was only used as a follower of «هنيئاً». Some reported that it may come not as a follower, but this is rejected, because the Arabs used it only as a follower. Are «هنيئاً مريئاً» in origin active participles on an intensive pattern, or are they two maṣdars that came on the pattern faʿīl, like al-ṣahīl (neighing) and al-hadīr (braying)? There is disagreement. The Shaykh transmitted the second view from Abū al-Baqāʾ, saying: "Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed them to be two maṣdars that came on the pattern faʿīl, like al-ṣahīl and al-hadīr, though they are not of the type in which faʿīl is regular for the maṣdar." End of quote. In Abū al-Baqāʾ's wording there is a difficulty, so we must touch on it so that what is in it may be known. He said: "«هنيئاً» came on the pattern faʿīl, and it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e., an eating that is wholesome. It was also said: it is a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl from the hāʾ, the implied form being 'made wholesome'; and «مريئاً» is like it. Al-marīʾ is faʿīl in the sense of mufʿil, because you say: 'the thing was pleasant to me (amraʾanī)'." The point of difficulty is: after ruling that they are maṣdars, how can he make them adjectives of an omitted maṣdar, and how can he explain «مريئاً», the maṣdar, in the sense of an active participle?

Al-Zamakhsharī held that they are adjectives; he said: "al-hanīʾ and al-marīʾ are two adjectives from 'the food was wholesome (hanuʾa)' and 'was pleasant (maruʾa)', when it goes down easily with nothing to spoil it." End of quote.

Hanā yahnā, without hamza, is also a second dialect form. One says: «هَنَأني الطعامُ ومَرَأني» (the food was wholesome and pleasant to me); if you use «مَرَأني» alone, it is only used as a four-letter verb, so you say «أَمْرأَني»; it is used as a three-letter verb only for symmetry with «هَنأَني». This is as they said: «أَخَذَه ما قَدُم وما حَدُث» (what was old and what was new seized him), with ḍamma on the dāl of «حدث» for symmetry with «قَدُم»; were it used alone, it would only be used with fatḥa on the dāl. It has other parallels. One says: «هَنَأْتُ الرجل أَهْنِئُه», with kasra on the middle radical in the imperfect, i.e., I gave him. The derivation of al-hanīʾ is from al-hināʾ, which is the tar with which a camel is smeared against mange. He said:

1544 - مُتَبَذِّلاً تَبْدُو محاسِنُه ... يَضَع الهِناءَ مواضِعَ النُّقْبِ
(Working in his everyday clothes, his fine qualities showing, he puts the tar on the spots of mange.)

Al-marīʾ: what goes down easily and smoothly in the throat; and from this the passage of food from the gullet to the mouth of the stomach was called al-marīʾ (the oesophagus).

semin-durr:5-5.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَلاَ تُؤْتُواْ السفهآء أَمْوَالَكُمُ}: the underlying form of «تُؤتوا» is «تُؤْتِيُوا», like «تُكْرِموا». The ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt to be heavy, so it was dropped; two quiescent letters then met, the yāʾ and the wāw of the pronoun, so the yāʾ was dropped so that two quiescent letters would not meet.

«السُّفهاء» is the plural of «سفيه» (foolish). It is reported from Mujāhid: "What is meant by 'the foolish' is women." Some considered this weak, on the grounds that faʿīla is only pluralised as faʿāʾil or faʿīlāt; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. But some have reported that «سفيهة» is pluralised as «سُفَهاء», like the masculine, and on this basis Mujāhid's view is not weak. The pluralisation of faʿīla as an adjective on fuʿalāʾ, though rare, has been reported for this word in particular. And Ibn ʿAṭiyya's restricting the plural of faʿīla to faʿāʾil or faʿīlāt is not evident, because «فِعال» is also regular in it, as in كَريمة / كِرام and ظَرِيفة / ظِراف. Likewise his stating faʿīla without qualification: he ought to have restricted it to where it is not in the sense of mafʿūla (passive meaning), to guard against «قتيلة» (one slain), for that is not pluralised as faʿāʾil.

The majority read {التي جَعَلَ الله لَكُمْ} in the singular form, as an adjective of «الأموال», even though it is a plural; because it has been mentioned more than once that for a plural of what is non-rational in the plural of multitude, or one that has only a single plural form, it is best to treat it as a feminine singular. «الأموال» is of this kind, because it is the plural of something non-rational and is only pluralised on afʿāl; though it has the form of a plural of paucity, what is meant by it is multitude.

Al-Ḥasan and al-Nakhaʿī read: «اللاتي», agreeing with the plural form. By analogy, only that whose singular is described by «التي» should be described by «اللاتي», and the singular of «الأموال», namely «مال», is not described by «التي». Al-Farrāʾ said: "The Arabs say «اللاتي» of women more than they say «التي», and of possessions they say «التي» more than they say «اللاتي». Both are permissible in both." It was also read «اللواتي», which is the plural of «اللاتي», and so a plural of a plural, or the plural of «التي» itself.

His words: «قياماً»: if we say that «جَعَلَ» means "made (into)" (ṣayyara), then «قياماً» is a second object and the first is omitted, namely the pronoun referring back to the relative noun, the implied form being "which He made it," i.e., made it for you a means of support (qiyām). If we say that it means "created," then «قِياماً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from that omitted referring pronoun, the implied form being "He made it," i.e., created it and brought it into being, in the state of being a support.

Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read: «قِيَماً», and the rest of the Seven: «قِياماً». Ibn ʿUmar read «قِواماً» with kasra on the qāf, and al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar «قَواماً» with fatḥa on it, and it is also transmitted from Abū ʿAmr. It was also read «قِوَماً», on the pattern of «عِنَب».

As for the reading of Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir, there are three views about it. First: «قِيَماً» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like «القيام» and not shortened from it; al-Kisāʾī, al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said this. So it is a maṣdar in the sense of «القيام», by which firmness and permanence are meant.

This view was rejected on the grounds that the wāw ought to have remained sound, being protected by its medial position, just as the wāw of «عِوَض» and «حِوَل» remained sound. It was answered that it followed its verb in the weakening: just as its verb was weakened, so was it; and because it is in the sense of «القِيام», it was treated like it in the weakening. Al-Akhfash reported «قِيَماً» and «قِوَماً» and said: "Analogy requires the wāw to remain sound; it was weakened only irregularly, as in their saying «ثِيَرة» (bulls), and the Banū Ḍabba's saying «طِيال» as the plural of «طويل», and everyone's saying «جِياد» as the plural of «جَواد». And if they weakened «دِيَماً» because «دِيْمة» is weakened, then the weakening of a maṣdar because its verb is weakened is more fitting. Do you not see that the plural remains sound while its singular is weakened, in «معيشة» / «معايش» and «مقامة» / «مقاوِم», whereas they have not kept sound a maṣdar whose verb they weakened?"

Second: it is shortened from «قيام»; they dropped the alif for lightness, just as they said «خيَم» for «خِيام», and «مِخْيَط» and «مِقْول» for «مِخْياط» and «مِقْوال».

Third: it is the plural of «قِيمة» (value), like «دِيَم» as the plural of «دِيْمَة»; the meaning is that possessions are like the values of souls, because their survival depends on them. Al-Fārisī rejected this view — even though it is the view of the Basrans other than al-Akhfash — on the grounds that His words {دِيناً قِيَماً مِّلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ} [al-Anʿām: 161] and {البيت الحرام قِيَماً لِّلنَّاسِ} [al-Māʾida: 97] have been read [with this form], and the meaning of "value" is not valid in them. People answered him that it does not follow from its meaning not being valid in the two verses mentioned that it is not valid here, since its meaning here is fitting, while there another meaning fits the two verses mentioned, as will come.

As for the reading of the rest of the Seven, it is the maṣdar of «قام», its underlying form being «قِوام»; the wāw was changed to yāʾ according to the well-known rule. The meaning is: which Allah made the cause of the support (qiyām) of your bodies, i.e., their survival. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "I.e., you subsist by it and are revived."

As for the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, there are two views about it. First: it is the maṣdar of «قاوَمَ», like «لاوَذَ لِواذاً»; the wāw remained sound in the maṣdar just as it did in the verb. Second: it is a noun for that by which a thing subsists, not a maṣdar, as in their saying «هذا مِلاك الأمر» (this is the mainstay of the matter), i.e., that by which it is held together.

As for the reading of al-Ḥasan, there are two views about it. First: it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), like «الكَلام», «الدوام» and «السلام». Second: it is a dialect form of «القِوام» meaning stature (al-qāma), the meaning being: which Allah made the cause of the preservation of your statures. One says: «جارية حسنةُ القِوام والقَوام والقَامة» (a girl of fine stature), all with one meaning. Abū Ḥātim said: "«قَوام» with fatḥa is a mistake," saying: "because al-qawām is the extension of stature." The interpretation of that has been given above. Moreover, al-Kisāʾī said: "It is in the sense of «القِوام»," i.e., with kasra, meaning that it is a maṣdar.

As for «قِوَماً», it is a maṣdar that came in its original form, I mean with the middle radical kept sound, like «الحِوَل» and «العِوَض».

His words: «فيها»: there are two views about it. First: «في» has its usual sense of location, i.e., "make their provision in it." Second: it is in the sense of «مِنْ», i.e., "from part of it," and what is meant is: from its profits through trade.

semin-durr:39-39.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمَاذَا عَلَيْهِمْ}: the discussion of its counterpart has already preceded. This may mean that the speech is complete here, i.e. "and what [harm] would there be upon them in believing in Allah?", or: "and what would be upon them of evil consequence and punishment on the Day of Resurrection?"; then He resumed with His words {لَوْ آمَنُواْ}, its jawāb (apodosis) being omitted, i.e. "happiness would have come to them". It may also be that the speech is completed by «لو» and what follows it, that is by making «لو» maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming), according to those who affirm that function for it, i.e. "and what would be upon them in believing?"; in that case it has no jawāb. Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed {َمَاذَا عَلَيْهِمْ} to be the jawāb of «لو». If he means this in terms of meaning, it is granted; but if he means it in terms of grammatical technique, it is unsound, because the technical jawāb does not precede according to the Basrans; and furthermore «لو» is not answered with an interrogative. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «لو» to be in the sense of the conditional «إنْ», as in His words {وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 221], i.e. "and what would be upon them if they believed?"; but there is no need for that.

semin-durr:40-40.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ}: there are two views on it. The first: it is accusative (manṣūb) as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "He does not wrong anyone a wrong of the weight of an atom"; the object and the maṣdar were omitted and its adjective was put in its place. When Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this view he assumed an omitted muḍāf before it; he said: "Its implied form is: a wrong of the measure of the weight of an atom; the maṣdar and its adjective were omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi was put in their place." There is no need for that, because the mithqāl itself is one of the measures, made a standard for this specific measure. The second: it is accusative as the second object of «يَظْلم», the first being omitted, as though they made «يظلم» [Translator's note: printed «بظلم»] carry the meaning of «يغصب» [Translator's note: printed «بغضب»] and «ينقص» [Translator's note: printed «بنقص»], and so made it transitive to two objects; the underlying form is: "Allah does not wrong anyone the weight of an atom".
His words: {وَإِن تَكُ حَسَنَةً}: the nūn was omitted for lightness because of frequent usage. This is a general rule: it is permissible to omit the nūn of «يكون» when it is jussive (majzūm), on condition that no attached pronoun follows it, as in «لَم يَكُنْه», and that the nūn is not given a vowel because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, as in {لَمْ يَكُنِ الذين كَفَرُواْ} [al-Bayyina: 1] — contrary to Yūnus, who allowed that, citing as evidence the words of the poet:
1583 - فإنْ لم تَكُ المِرْآةُ أَبْدَتْ وَسامةً ... فقد أَبْدَتِ المرآةُ جَبْهَةَ ضَيْغَمِ
(If the mirror has not shown handsomeness, it has shown the brow of a lion.)
According to Sībawayh this is poetic licence. The nūn was omitted only because of its nasality and its quiescence, so that it resembled the wāw; this is unlike other verbs, such as «لم يَضِنَّ» and «لم يَهُنْ», because of the frequent usage of «كان». The wāw ought to have returned when this nūn was omitted, since it was only omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the second of them — the nūn — has gone; but the nūn is as though it were pronounced.
The majority read «حسنةً» in the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of the incomplete (nāqiṣa) «كان», its noun being latent (mustatir) in it and referring back to «مثقال». Its pronoun was made feminine only by construal according to the meaning, because it means: "and if the weight of an atom be a good deed"; or because of its annexation to a feminine noun, so that it acquired femininity from it. Ibn Kathīr and Nāfiʿ read «حسنة» in the nominative, taking it as the complete (tāmma) [kāna], i.e. "and if a good deed occurs or exists".
Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read «يُضَعِّفْها» with doubling [of the ʿayn], and the rest «يضاعفها». Abū ʿUbayda said: "«ضاعفه» implies many times, and «ضَعَّفَ» implies twice." This is the reverse of the speech of the Arabs, because muḍāʿafa (doubling) implies the addition of a like amount; and when you double the consonant the form indicates multiplicity, which entails repeating the doubling according to whatever number there is. Al-Fārisī said: "They are two dialectal forms with one meaning; this is indicated by His words {نُضَعِّفْ لَهَا العذاب ضِعْفَيْنِ} [al-Aḥzāb: 30] and {فَيُضَعِّفُهُ لَهُ أَضْعَافاً كَثِيرَةً} [al-Baqara: 245]." We have already discussed this more fully than here. Ibn Hurmuz read «نضاعِفْها» with nūn, and it has been read «يُضْعِفْها» with the lighter form, from «أضعفه», like «أكرم».
His words: {مِن لَّدُنْهُ}: there are two views on it. The first: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يُؤْتِ», and «من» is for the beginning [of the extent], figuratively. The second: it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أجراً», because it was originally an adjective of an indefinite noun that was placed before it, and so became accusative as a ḥāl.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَكَيْفَ}: there are three views on it. The first: it is in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "so how will their state, or their doing, be?"; and the governor of «إذا» is this implied element. The second: it is in the position of accusative through an omitted verb, i.e. "so how will you be, or what will you do?"; and both views apply here: the accusative by likening to the ḥāl, as is the doctrine of Sībawayh, or by likening to the adverbial (ẓarf), as is the doctrine of al-Akhfash; and that [verb] is also the governor of «إذا». The third, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya related from Makkī: it is governed by «جئنا»; and this is a gross error.
His words: {مِن كُلِّ}: there are two views on it. The first: it is attached to «جئنا». The second: it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «شهيد»; that is according to the opinion of those who allow the ḥāl of a noun made genitive by a preposition to precede it, and its precise treatment has preceded. The one witnessed against is omitted, i.e. "with a witness against its community".
Al-mithqāl is of the pattern mifʿāl, from al-thiql (weight); it is the weight of anything. Al-dharra is the small ant; it has also been said: its head; and it has been said: the mustard seed; and it has been said: a particle of dust. It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he put his hand in the dust, then blew on it and said: "Each one of these is a dharra." The first is the well-known view, because the ant is used proverbially for smallness, and it is at its smallest when a year has passed over it; they said this is because it then becomes very small. Ḥassān said:
1584 - لو يَدِبُّ الحَوْلِيُّ مِنْ وَلَدِ الذَّرْ ... رِ عليها لأنْدَبَتْها الكُلُومُ
(If a year-old offspring of the tiny ants crept upon her, wounds would scar her.)
And Imruʾ al-Qays said:
1585 - مِن القاصِراتِ الطَرْفِ لو دَبَّ مُحْوِلٌ ... من الذَرِّ فوق الإِتْبِ منها لأَثَّرا
(Of those who lower their gaze; were a year-old tiny ant to creep over her shift, it would leave a mark.)
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَجِئْنَا بِكَ}: there are three views on this clause. The most apparent: it is in the position of genitive by conjunction with the first «جئنا», i.e. "so what will you do at the time of the two comings?". The second: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, with «قد» intended along with it, the governor being the first «جئنا», i.e. "We brought from every community a witness, having brought [you]"; and this is questionable. The third: it is resumptive, so it has no grammatical position. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may be resumptive, the past being in the sense of the future." End of quotation. He needed that only because the coming has not yet occurred, so he claimed that; and Allah knows best. {على هؤلاء} is attached to «شهيداً», and «على» has its proper sense; it has also been said that it is in the sense of the lām, which is far-fetched. It has also been allowed that «على» is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «شهيداً», which is far-fetched. «شهيداً» is a ḥāl from the kāf in «بك».

semin-durr:42-42.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {يَوْمَئِذٍ}: there are three views on it. The first: it is governed by «يود», i.e. "those who disbelieved will wish, on the day when We bring…". The second: it is governed by «شهيداً»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and he said: "On this view «يود» is an adjective of «يوم», and the referent pronoun is omitted, its implied form being 'in it'; this has been mentioned at His words {واتقوا يَوْماً لاَّ تَجْزِي} [al-Baqara: 48]." What he said is obviously questionable.
The third: «يوم» is indeclinable (mabnī) because of its annexation to «إذ»; al-Ḥūfī said this. He said: "Because when an adverbial is annexed to a non-declinable word it may become indeclinable along with it. «إذ» here is a noun, because when adverbials are annexed to [other words], these leave for the meaning of nounhood, because they particularise what is annexed to them as nouns particularise, and because they deserve the genitive, and the genitive is not one of the marks of adverbials."
The tanwīn in «إذ» is the tanwīn of compensation, according to the correct view. It has been said that it compensates for the first clause in His words {جِئْنَا مِن كُلِّ}, i.e. "on the day when We bring from every community a witness, and bring you as a witness against these"; on this view «الرسول» (the Messenger) is a generic noun. It has also been said that it compensates for the last clause, namely «وجِئْنا بك», and that what is meant by the Messenger is Muhammad ﷺ; the [expected] wording would have been «وعَصَوْك» (and disobeyed you), but it was expressed overtly with the attribute of messengership in order to exalt his rank and nobility.
On His words {وَعَصَوُاْ} there are three views. The first: it is a clause conjoined to «كفروا», so it is part of the ṣila (relative clause), and they combine disbelief and disobedience. It has also been said: rather it is the ṣila of another relative noun, so they are two groups. And it has been said: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from [the subject of] «كفروا», with «قد» intended, i.e. "having disobeyed". Yaḥyā and Abū al-Sammāl read «وعَصَوِا الرسول» with a kasra on the wāw, according to the original rule.
His words: {لَوْ تسوى}: if it is said that «لو» has its proper sense, as is the view of the majority, then the object of «يود» is omitted, i.e. "those who disbelieved will wish the levelling of the earth [with them]", indicated by {لَوْ تسوى بِهِمُ الأرض}, and its jawāb (apodosis) is then omitted, i.e. "they would be glad of that". If it is said that it is maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming), then it and what follows it are in the position of the object of «يود», and it has no jawāb; the precise treatment of this has preceded at {يَوَدُّ أَحَدُهُمْ لَوْ يُعَمَّرُ} [al-Baqara: 96]. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«وعَصَوُا الرسول» is in the position of a ḥāl, with «قد» intended, and it is parenthetical between «يود» and its object, which is «لو تُسَوَّى», and «لو» is in the sense of the maṣdariyya «أَنْ»." End of quotation. His making the circumstantial clause parenthetical between the object and its governor is obviously questionable, because it is among the dependents of the governor that is the ṣila of the relative noun. This is like your saying «ضَرَبَ الذين جاؤوا مُسْرِعين زيداً» (those who came hurrying struck Zayd): just as it is not said that «مسرعين» is parenthetical, so too this clause.
Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr and ʿĀṣim read «تُسَوَّى» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and the sīn undoubled [Translator's note: the printed «تُسَوَّى» shows the wāw doubled; the reading meant is passive], as a passive. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «تَسَوَّى» with fatḥa on it and the lighter form, and Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir with the doubled form. As for the first reading, its meaning is that they wish that Allah the Exalted would level the earth with them: either in the sense that the earth splits and swallows them, the bāʾ being in the sense of «على»; or in the sense that they wish they had become dust like the beasts, the underlying form being "they wish that Allah would level them with the earth", which was inverted into this, like their saying «أدخلت القَلَنْسوة في رأسي» (I put the cap into my head); or in the sense that they wish they were buried in it, which is like the meaning of the first view. It has also been said: "would that the earth were made an equivalent for them", i.e. that what is on it be taken from them as a ransom.
As for the second reading, its underlying form is «تَتَسَوَّى» with two tāʾs, one of which was omitted. In the third, one of them was omitted [Translator's note: so in the source; in the doubled reading the tāʾ is assimilated into the sīn]. The meaning of the two readings is clear from what has preceded, for the views applying to the first reading apply to the other two readings; the most that can be said is that the verb is attributed overtly to the earth.
His words: {وَلاَ يَكْتُمُونَ}: there are six views on it. This wāw may be for conjunction or for the ḥāl. If it is for conjunction, it may be a conjunction of single words or a conjunction of clauses. Once this is established, {وَلاَ يَكْتُمُونَ} may be conjoined to the object of «يود», i.e. "they wish the levelling of the earth with them and the absence of concealing speech", «لو» on this view being maṣdariyya; and it is far-fetched to make it the particle of what would have occurred because of the occurrence of something else, with «ولا يكتمون» conjoined to the omitted object of «يَوَدُّ». So these are two views on the assumption that it is a conjunction of single words.
It may also be conjoined to the clause «يَوَدُّ»: Allah the Exalted informs about them with two pieces of information, the first being the wishing for such-and-such, the second that they are unable to conceal in some situations as opposed to others; «لو» on this view is maṣdariyya. «لو» may also be the particle of what would have occurred because of the occurrence of something else, its jawāb being omitted and the object of «يود» also omitted, with «ولا يكتمون» conjoined to «لو» and what is in its domain; Allah the Exalted then informs about them with three clauses: the wishing, the conditional clause with «لو», and the absence of concealment. So these too are two views on the assumption that it is a conjunction of clauses.
If it is for the ḥāl, it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «بهم», the governor being «تُسَوَّى»; «لو» may then be maṣdariyya or imtināʿiyya (expressing impossibility), the implied form being: "they wish the levelling of the earth with them, not concealing", or: "were it levelled with them, not concealing, that would be their desire". It may also be a ḥāl from {الذين كَفَرُواْ}, the governor being «يود», the ḥāl being a restriction on the wishing, «لو» on this view being maṣdariyya in the position of the object of the wishing; the meaning is: "on that day those who disbelieved will wish the levelling of the earth with them, not concealing any speech from Allah". On this view it is far-fetched for «لو» to be imtināʿiyya, because that would necessitate separating the ḥāl and its governor by a clause. «يكتمون» is transitive to two objects; the apparent view is that it reaches one of them through a preposition, the underlying form being «ولا يكتمون من الله حديثاً».

semin-durr:6-6.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {حتى إِذَا بَلَغُواْ}: concerning this «حتى» and those like it — I mean the one that comes before «إذا» — there are two views. The better known of them: it is a particle of limit (ghāya) that comes before the conditional sentence and its jawāb (apodosis), and the meaning is: "and test the orphans until the time of their maturity and their being entitled to have their property handed over to them, on condition that sound judgement is perceived." So it is a particle of inception (ḥarf ibtidāʾ), like the one that comes before other sentences, as in his words:

1545 - وما زالَتِ القَتْلى تَمُجُّ دماءها ... بِدَجْلَةَ حتى ماءُ دَجْلَةَ أَشْكَلُ
(The slain kept spewing out their blood into the Tigris, until the water of the Tigris was reddish.)

And the words of Imruʾ al-Qays:

1546 - سَرَيْتُ بهم حتى تَكِلَّ مَطِيُّهم ... وحتى الجيادُ ما يُقَدْنَ بِأَرْسانِ
(I travelled by night with them until their mounts grew weary, and until the steeds no longer needed leading by halters.)

The second — the view of a group including al-Zajjāj and Ibn Durustawayh — is that it is a preposition (ḥarf jarr), and what follows it is in the genitive through it. On this view «إذا» is purely adverbial (of time) and has no conditional meaning in it. On the first view, the governor of «إذا» is what is extracted from the meaning of its jawāb, the implied form being: "when they reach marriage(able age) with sound judgement, then hand over."

The apparent sense of the wording of one of them is that «إذا» is not conditional. He said: "«إذا» is not conditional, because what follows it is bound to happen. Sībawayh allowed it to be used as a conditional (with jussive) in poetry, and said: 'They did that under constraint.' It was used as a conditional only because it needs a jawāb, and because a verb follows it, overt or implied. Al-Khalīl argued that it is not conditional on the grounds that what follows it is bound to happen: do you not see that you say «أجيئك إذا احمرَّ البُسْر» (I will come to you when the unripe dates turn red), and you do not say «إنْ احمرَّ» (if they turn red)?" The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "His words indicate that it can be a mere adverb with no conditional meaning in it, which is contrary to the grammarians, for they are virtually agreed that it is an adverb usually carrying a conditional meaning. And if something is found in the wording of some of them denying that it is a conditional particle, they mean only that it does not make the verb jussive, not that it is not a condition." Some assumed an omitted muḍāf, saying: "Its implied form is: they reached the limit of marriage, or its time." The apparent view is that it is not needed, since the meaning is: they became fit for marriage. The fāʾ in His words {فَإِنْ آنَسْتُمْ} is the jawāb of «إذا», and in His words «فادْفَعُوا» the jawāb of «إنْ».

Ibn Masʿūd read: «فإن أحَسْتُم»; the underlying form is «أحْسَسْتُم», and one of the two sīns was dropped; it could be either the second or the third radical. Similar to it are the words of Abū Zubayd:

1547 - سِوى أنَّ العِتاقَ من المَطايا ... حَسِيْنَ به فهنَّ إليه شوسُ
(Except that the noble ones among the mounts sensed him, so they look at him askance.)

This is an elision that is not by regular analogy. Some reported that it is the dialect of Sulaym, and that it is regular in the second radical of every doubled verb to which the tāʾ or nūn of the pronoun is attached.

«رُشْداً» is made indefinite to indicate variety, the meaning being: whatever kind of sound judgement is attained is sufficient. The majority read «رُشْداً» with a ḍamma and a sukūn; Ibn Masʿūd and al-Sulamī with two fatḥas, and some with two ḍammas. Discussion of this will come in full in al-Aʿrāf, if Allah the Exalted wills.

«آنَسَ كذا»: he perceived it and sensed it. He said:

1548 - آنَسَتْ نَبْأَةً وأَفزعها القُن ... اصُ عَصْراً وقد دَنا الإِمساءُ
(She perceived a faint sound, and the hunters frightened her in the late afternoon, when evening had drawn near.)

It was also said: "found," from al-Farrāʾ; and it was said: "saw."

His words: {إِسْرَافاً وَبِدَاراً}: there are two views about them. First: they are accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e., for the sake of extravagance and haste. It is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "The guardians used to seize the opportunity of consuming the orphan's property before he grew up and took the property away from them." Second: they are two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e., being extravagant and hasty. «بِداراً» is the maṣdar of «بادرَ», and the mufāʿala here may be between two parties, in its usual sense, meaning that the guardian races the orphan to take his property while the orphan races towards growing up; or it may be from one party, meaning that fāʿala is in the sense of faʿala, as in «سافر» and «طارَقَ».

His words: {أَن يَكْبَرُواْ}: there are two views about it. First: it is an object of the maṣdar, i.e., "and hastening [against] their growing up," like His words {أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً} [al-Balad: 14-15]; and about the governing power of a maṣdar with tanwīn there is a well-known disagreement. Second: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi with an elision, i.e., "for fear that they grow up"; on this view the object of «بِداراً» is omitted. As for this prohibitive sentence, there are two views about it. The more correct: it is resumptive, and not conjoined to what precedes it. Second: it is conjoined to what precedes it, namely the jawāb of the condition with «إنْ», i.e., "then hand over, and do not consume it." This is corrupt, because the condition and its jawāb are consequent on reaching marriageable age, and that conflicts with His words {وَبِدَاراً أَن يَكْبَرُواْ}; it would entail its preceding that upon which it is consequent, and that is impossible.

His words: {وكفى بالله حَسِيباً}: about «كفى» there are two views. First: it is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl). Second — and this is the correct one — it is a verb. About its fāʿil (agent) there are two views. First — and it is the correct one — it is the noun in the genitive with the bāʾ, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in it and in the agent of its imperfect, as in {أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ} [Fuṣṣilat: 53], regularly. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It was added to indicate the meaning of command, since the implied form is: 'Be content with Allah'." Second: it is implied, the implied form being "the being-content sufficed," and «بالله» on this view is in the position of the accusative, because it is a direct object in meaning; this is the opinion of Ibn al-Sarrāj. This was rejected on the grounds that making an elided maṣdar govern is not permissible for the Basrans except under poetic necessity, as in his words:

1549 - هل تَذْكُرون إلى الدَّيْرَيْنِ هِجْرَتَكم ... ومَسْحَكم صُلْبَكُمْ رُحْمانَ قُرْبانا
(Do you remember your migration to the two monasteries, and your wiping your crosses [saying] "O Raḥmān!" as an offering?)

I.e., your saying "O Raḥmān." The Shaykh said: "It was said: the fāʿil is implied, namely the pronoun of 'the being-content,' i.e., 'it sufficed,' meaning the being-content, and the bāʾ is not redundant, so [«بالله»] is in the position of the accusative and is then attached to the fāʿil. This view is not admissible on the doctrine of the Basrans, because for them a maṣdar may not govern when it is a pronoun; and if by 'implied' he means 'elided,' it is also impossible for them for two reasons: the elision of the fāʿil, and making an elided maṣdar govern while keeping what it governs." There is something to consider in this, since someone may say: if we hold that the fāʿil of «كفى» is implied, we do not attach «بالله» to the fāʿil so that what he mentioned would follow; rather we attach it to the verb itself, as mentioned above. Makkī and al-Zajjāj preceded him in this view, for [al-Zajjāj] said: "The bāʾ entered on the fāʿil because the meaning of the speech is a command, i.e., 'be content with Allah'." This statement suggests that the bāʾ is not redundant, and it is an incorrect statement, because from the point of view of the meaning he assumed, the fāʿil would be those addressed, with «بالله» attached to it; while from the point of view of the bāʾ having entered on the fāʿil, the fāʿil would be Allah the Exalted — a contradiction.

In the words of Ibn ʿAṭiyya there is also something similar to his statement, for he said: "«بالله» is in the position of the nominative on the assumption that the preposition is redundant, and the benefit of its addition is to make clear the meaning of command in the form of a statement, i.e., 'be content with Allah'; so the bāʾ indicates what is intended by that." In this there is what was used to refute al-Zajjāj, plus making the particle both redundant and not redundant. Ibn ʿĪsā said: "The bāʾ entered «كفى بالله» only because it used to be connected as the fāʿil is connected, and by the entry of the bāʾ it became connected both as the muḍāf is connected and as the fāʿil is connected; because sufficiency from Him the Exalted is not like sufficiency from anyone else, so its wording was doubled to double its meaning." This needs reflection.

His words: {حسيباً}: there are two views about it. The more correct: it is a tamyīz (specification), as shown by the fact that «مِنْ» can be prefixed to it, which is the sign of the tamyīz. Second: it is a ḥāl.

«كفى» here is transitive to one object, which is omitted, the implied form being "and Allah sufficed you." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«كفى» is transitive to two objects which are omitted here, the implied form being 'Allah sufficed you against their evil,' as evidenced by His words {فَسَيَكْفِيكَهُمُ الله} [al-Baqara: 137]." The apparent view is that its meaning there is different from the meaning here. The Shaykh said, after mentioning that it is transitive to one object: "And it comes in a different meaning, transitive to two objects, as in His words: {فَسَيَكْفِيكَهُمُ الله}." This is open to consideration.

semin-durr:43-43.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لاَ تَقْرَبُواْ الصلاة}: there are two views on it. The first: there is an omitted muḍāf in the speech, its implied form being "the places of prayer", and what is meant by its places is the mosques; this is supported by His words after that, {إِلاَّ عَابِرِي سَبِيلٍ}, according to one of the two interpretations. The second: there is no omission, and the prohibition is against approaching the prayer itself in this state.
His words: {وَأَنْتُمْ سكارى}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «تقربوا». The majority read «سُكارى» with ḍamma on the sīn and an alif after the kāf, and there are two views on it. The first, which is the correct one: it is a broken plural; Sībawayh stated this explicitly, saying: "They sometimes give some of these a broken plural on the pattern fuʿālā, as in the saying of some of them «سُكارى» and «عُجالى»." The second: it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ); Ibn al-Bādhish claimed that this is the doctrine of Sībawayh, and said: "It is the analogical rule, because none of the plural patterns comes on this measure." Al-Sīrāfī mentioned the disagreement and preferred its being a broken plural.
Al-Aʿmash read «سُكْرى» with ḍamma on the sīn and sukūn on the kāf. Its justification is that it is an adjective on the pattern fuʿlā, like «حُبْلى», used as an adjective of a group, i.e. "while you are a drunken group". Janāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh reported «كُسْلى» and «كَسْلى» with ḍamma and fatḥa on the kāf; al-Zamakhsharī said this. Al-Nakhaʿī read «سَكْرى» with fatḥa on the sīn and sukūn on the kāf; this admits two views. The first: what was said about the preceding reading, namely that it is a singular adjective on the pattern faʿlā, as in «امرأةٌ سَكْرى» (a drunken woman), with which the group is described. The second: it is a broken plural like «جَرْحى», «مَوْتى» and «هَلْكى»; «سَكْران» was given a plural on «فَعْلى» only by analogy with these, because of the affliction it implies that befalls the doer. Something of this has preceded for you in al-Baqara at His words {وَإِن يَأتُوكُمْ أسارى} [verse: 85]. It has also been read «سَكارى» with fatḥa on the sīn and the alif; this is a broken plural like «نَدْمان» and «نَدامى», «عَطْشان» and «عَطاشَى».
Al-sukr in the language means blocking (al-sadd); from it is the name given to what befalls a person from drinking an intoxicant, because it blocks what is between a person and his intellect. Al-sukr is most often said of the removal of the intellect by an intoxicant, but it is sometimes said of its removal by anger and the like, such as passionate love and other things. The poet said:
1586 - سُكْرانِ سُكْرُ هوىً وسُكْرُ مُدامَةٍ ... أنَّى يُفيقُ فتىً به سُكْرانِ
(Two intoxications, the intoxication of love and the intoxication of wine: how can a youth recover who has two intoxications?)
Al-sakr, with fatḥa and sukūn on the kāf, is the damming of water; with kasra on the sīn it is the dammed place itself. As for «السَّكَر», with fatḥa on both, it is the drink by which one becomes intoxicated; from it is {سَكَراً وَرِزْقاً حَسَناً} [al-Naḥl: 67]. It has also been said: al-sukr, with ḍamma on the sīn and sukūn on the kāf, is the dam, i.e. the barrier between two things. The poet said:
1587 - فما زِلْنَا على السُّكْرِ ... نُداوي السُّكْرِ بالسُّكْرِ
(We remained in drunkenness, treating drunkenness with drunkenness.)
The upshot is that the root of the word indicates blockage; from it is «سَكِرتْ عينُ البازي» (the falcon's eye grew heavy) when sleep mingles with it, and «سَكِر النهرُ» (the river was blocked) when it does not flow, and «سَكَرْتُه أنا» (I dammed it).
His words: {حتى تَعْلَمُواْ}: «حتى» is a preposition in the sense of «إلى» (until), so it is attached to the verb of prohibition, and the verb after it is accusative through an implied «أَنْ»; its precise treatment has preceded.
In «ما» three views are possible: it may be in the sense of «الذي» (that which), or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective — the referent pronoun on these two views being omitted, i.e. "[what] you say it" — or maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming), in which case there is no omission, except according to the opinion of Ibn al-Sarrāj and those who followed him.
His words: {وَلاَ جُنُباً}: accusative as conjoined to the ḥāl before it, namely His words {وَأَنْتُمْ سكارى}; a single word was conjoined to a clause since the clause is interpreted as a single word. «لا» was repeated with it to point out that the prohibition against approaching the prayer applies with each of these two states separately; so the prohibition with the two states combined is more emphatic and more fitting.
Al-junub is derived from al-janāba, which is distance. The poet said:
1588 - فلا تَحْرِمَنِّي نائلاً عن جَنابَةٍ ... فإني امرؤٌ وَسْطَ القِبابِ غريبُ
(Do not deny me a gift on account of distance, for I am a stranger amid the tents.)
A man was called junub because of his distance from purity, or because he lay with his side (janb) and touched with it. The well-known view is that it is used in a single form for singular, dual and plural, masculine and feminine; from that is the noble verse. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because it is treated like the maṣdar, which is al-ijnāb." Some of the Arabs give it a dual, saying «جُنُبان», a sound plural, saying «جُنُبون», and a broken plural, saying «أَجْناب»; like it in that is «شُلُل». Its precise treatment has preceded.
His words: {إِلاَّ عَابِرِي}: there are two views on it. The first: it is accusative as a ḥāl, so it is an emptied (mufarragh) exception, the governor of it being the verb of prohibition; the implied form is: "do not approach the prayer in a state of janāba except in the state of travel or of passing through the mosque", according to the two views. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "{إِلاَّ عَابِرِي سَبِيلٍ} is an exception from the general states of those addressed, and its accusative is as a ḥāl. If you say: how did He combine this ḥāl with the ḥāl before it? I say: it is as though it were said: do not approach the prayer in a state of janāba unless you have another state with you in which you are excused, namely the state of travel; and 'passing along the way' is an expression for it." The second: it is accusative as an adjective of His word «جُنُباً», described by «إلا» in the sense of «غير» (other than), so the case-ending appeared on what follows it. More explanation of this will come at the words of Allah the Exalted {لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَآ آلِهَةٌ إِلاَّ الله لَفَسَدَتَا} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 22]. It is as though it were said: "do not approach it junub, not passing along the way", i.e. junub, residents, not excused; this is a clear meaning according to interpreting the passing as travel. As for those who assume "the places of prayer", the meaning according to them is: "do not approach the mosques junub except passing through, because there is no other path", or otherwise, according to the disagreement.
Al-ʿubūr is passing; from it is «ناقةٌ عُبْرُ الهَواجِر» (a she-camel that crosses the midday heats). The poet said:
1589 - عَيْرانَةٌ سُبُحُ اليدينِ شِمِلَّةٌ ... عُبْرُ الهواجرِ كالهِزَفِّ الخاضِبِ
(A sturdy she-camel, swimming with her forelegs, swift, crossing the midday heats like the ostrich with reddened legs.)
His words: {حتى تَغْتَسِلُواْ} are like His words {حتى تَعْلَمُواْ}: it is attached to the verb of prohibition. His words: {أَوْ على سَفَرٍ}: in the position of accusative by conjunction with the khabar of «كان», which is «مَرْضَى»; likewise His words {أَوْ جَآءَ أَحَدٌ} and {أَوْ لاَمَسْتُمُ}. In it there is evidence for the khabar of «كان» coming as a past verb without «قد», and claiming its omission is an unnecessary strain — so al-Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] argued from it. But there is no evidence in it, because «أو جاء» may be conjoined to «كنتم», its implied form being "or if anyone comes"; Abū al-Baqāʾ took this view, and it is more apparent than the first; and Allah knows best.
«منكم» is in the position of nominative because it is an adjective of «أحد», so it is attached to an omitted element; «من الغائط» is attached to «جاء», so it is its object. The majority read «الغائِط» on the measure fāʿil; it is the low-lying place in the ground, then it was used to express the act of relieving oneself itself, as a metonymy out of shame at mentioning it. The Arabs distinguished between the two verbs from it, saying «غاطَ في الأرض», i.e. he went far off to a place where none could see him except one who came upon him, and «تغوَّط» when he relieved himself. Ibn Masʿūd read «من الغَيْطِ», and there are two views on it. The first, which Ibn Jinnī held: it is lightened from fayʿil, like «هَيْن» and «مَيْت» from «هيّن» and «ميّت». The second: it is a maṣdar on the measure faʿl; they said «غاط يغيط غَيْطاً» and «غاط يَغُوط غَوطاً». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is the maṣdar of «يَغُوط», so the analogical form would have been «غَوْطاً», but the wāw was changed to yāʾ, even though it is quiescent and preceded by fatḥa, because of its lightness." It is as though he did not know that there is another dialectal form of it from the yāʾ-roots, and so claimed that. The two brothers [Translator's note: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read here and in al-Māʾida «لَمَسْتم», and the rest «لامستم». It has been said that «فاعَل» is in the sense of «فَعَل»; and it has been said that «لمَس» means having intercourse and «لامسَ» what is short of intercourse.
His words: {فَلَمْ تَجِدُواْ}: the fāʾ conjoins what follows it to the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "to «جاء»", because he made «جاء» conjoined to «كنتم», so it is a protasis according to him. The fāʾ in His words «فتيمَّموا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the pronoun in «تَيَمَّموا» is for all those previously mentioned — the sick, the traveller, the one who relieved himself, and the one who touched — and in it the second person is given precedence over the third person; that is because the third person preceded in His words {أَوْ جَآءَ أَحَدٌ} and the second person in «كنتم» and «لمستم», so the second person of His word «كنتم» and what follows it was given precedence over it. How excellent it is that the third person was used here, because it is a metonymy for something one is ashamed of, so He did not address them with it; this is one of the beauties of speech, and like it is {وَإِذَا مَرِضْتُ فَهُوَ يَشْفِينِ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 80]. «وَجَد» here is in the sense of «لَقِي» (to meet, find), so it is transitive to one object.
«صعيداً» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of His word «تَيمَّموا», i.e. "seek out". It has also been said that it is by dropping a preposition, i.e. «بصعيدٍ»; this is nothing, because it is not analogically applicable. «بوجوهكم» is attached to «امْسَحوا». This bāʾ may be redundant (zāʾida), which Abū al-Baqāʾ held, or it may be transitivising, because Sībawayh reported «مَسَحْتُ رأسَه» and «برأسِه», so it is of the type «نصحته» and «نصحت له». What one wipes with is omitted; it appears in the verse of al-Māʾida in His word «منه», and this one is construed accordingly.

semin-durr:44-44.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِّنَ الكتاب}: there are two views on it. The first: it is attached to an omitted element, since it is an adjective of «نصيباً», so it is in the position of accusative. The second: it is attached to «أوتوا», i.e. "they were given a portion of the Book". «يَشْتَرُون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and there are two views on the one it qualifies. The first: it is the wāw of «أوتوا». The second: it is the relative noun, and on this view it is an anticipated (muqaddara) ḥāl. What is given in exchange is omitted, i.e. "for guidance", as is stated explicitly in other places. «يريدون» is conjoined to «يشترون». Al-Nakhaʿī read «ويُريدون أَنْ تَضُلُّوا» with the tāʾ of address [Translator's note: so printed; the tāʾ of address presumably refers to «تَضُلُّوا», or the intended reading is «وتريدون»], the meaning being: "and you, O believers, want to abandon [Translator's note: printed «تَدَّعوا» (claim); probably «تَدَعوا» (abandon) is meant] what is right". Al-Ḥasan read «أن تُضِلُّوا» from «أضلَّ». It has also been read «أَنْ تُضَلُّوا السبيل» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the ḍād, as a passive. «السبيل» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), as when you say «أخطأ الطريق» (he missed the road), and not an adverbial. It has also been said that it is made transitive with «عَنْ»: you say «ضَلَلْتُ السبيل» and «عن السبيل».

semin-durr:45-45.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {وكفى بالله}: the discussion of this construction has preceded at the beginning of the sura, so there is no need to repeat it; likewise the discussion of the accusative word after it has preceded.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِّمَّا تَرَكَ الوالدان}: this prepositional phrase is in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ), because it is a naʿt (adjective) of the nominative word before it, i.e., "a share being (kāʾin) or settled (mustaqirr)." It may also be in the position of the accusative, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the word «نصيب», because it is part of its completion.

His words: {مِمَّا قَلَّ}: for this prepositional phrase too there are two views. First: it is a badal (substitute) from the latter «ما» in «مِمَّا ترك», with the preposition repeated in the badal, and the pronoun in «منه» refers back to the latter «ما». This badal is also intended in the first sentence and was omitted because it is indicated; and because what is intended by it is tawkīd (emphasis), since it is a detailing of the generality understood from His words {مِّمَّا تَرَكَ}; so this badal came detailing its two states of abundance and scarcity. Second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun omitted from «ترك», i.e., "of what he left, little or much," or "being settled, of what is little."

As for «نصيباً», there are several views about it. First: it is accusative as standing in the place of a maṣdar (verbal noun), its governor being the meaning of what precedes, since the implied form is "as a gift" or "as an entitlement"; this is the meaning of the statement of whoever says it is accusative as an emphatic maṣdar. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Like His words {فَرِيضَةً مِّنَ الله} [al-Nisāʾ: 11], as if it were said: 'an obligatory division'." Al-Farrāʾ preceded him in this, saying: "It is accusative because it was treated as a maṣdar, and that is why it is singular, as in your saying «له عليَّ كذا حقاً لازماً» (he has such-and-such from me as a binding due), and similarly {فَرِيضَةً مِّنَ الله}. Had it been a true noun it would not be accusative: you do not say «لك عليَّ حق درهماً» (you have a due from me, a dirham)."

Second: it is accusative as a ḥāl. The one described by the ḥāl may be the fāʿil (agent) in «قَلَّ أو كَثُر», or it may be «نصيب», even though it is indefinite, because it is specified either by the adjective or by its governing; the governor of the ḥāl is the "being settled" (al-istiqrār) contained in His words «للرجالِ». Al-Zajjāj and Makkī held that it is accusative as a ḥāl; they said: "The meaning is: these have shares, as we have mentioned, in the state of being obligatory."

Third: it is accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), in the sense of "I mean: a share"; al-Zamakhsharī said this. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "If he means the technical ikhtiṣāṣ, it is rejected because it is indefinite, and they have explicitly stipulated that it must be definite."

Fourth: accusative by an implied verb, i.e., "it was made obligatory," or "it was made for them, as a share." Fifth: it is an explicit maṣdar, i.e., "I allotted it as an allotment (naṣaba naṣīban)."

semin-durr:8-8.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {فارزقوهم مِّنْهُ}: concerning this pronoun there are three views. First: it refers back to the property, because the division indicates it by way of implication. Second: it refers back to «ما» in His words «مِمَّا ترك». Third: it refers back to the division itself, even though [the pronoun] is masculine, in regard to the meaning, since what is meant by "the division" is the thing divided. This is on the opinion of whoever holds that; as for whoever says that «القسمة» is from «الاقتسام» (sharing out), like «الخِبْرة» from «الاختبار», or is in the sense of «القَسَم», that is not possible.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَلْيَخْشَ الذين}: the majority read with a sukūn on the lām in the three verbs. It is the lām of command, and the verb after it is jussive (majzūm) through it. Al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read with kasra on the lām in the three verbs, which is the original; the sukūn is a lightening, treating what is separate as though it were joined, for they likened «وَلْيخش» to «كَتِف». This is like what was said earlier about «وهي» and «لَهْي» at the beginning of al-Baqara.

As for this «لو», there are two possibilities. First: it is in its usual sense of being a particle for what would have happened because something else happened, or a particle of impossibility because of impossibility, according to the two different formulations. Second: it is in the sense of conditional «إنْ». Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Zamakhsharī held the first possibility. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the meaning of «لو تركوا» and its jawāb (apodosis) occurring as the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين»? I say: its meaning is: let those fear whose description and state is that, were they on the point of leaving behind them weak offspring — and that is when death is approaching them — they would fear for them being lost after them, because of the departure of their provider and earner; as the poet said:

1550 - لقد زادَ الحياةَ إليَّ حُبَّاً ... بناتِي أنَّهن من الضِعافِ
أُحاذِرُ أن يَرَيْنَ البؤس بعدي ... وأن يَشْرَبْنَ رنْقاً بعد صافي
(My daughters have made life dearer to me, because they are among the weak; I fear they will see misery after me, and drink muddy water after clear.)"

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Its implied form is: 'if they left, they would fear (la-khāfū)'; and the lām may be dropped from the jawāb of «لو»." The point of relying on this wording is that he made the lām implied in its jawāb; had «لو» been in the sense of conditional «إنْ», that would not be permissible. Others besides them stated this explicitly, saying: "«لو تركوا»: «لو» is that by which a thing is impossible because of the impossibility of another, and «خافوا» is the jawāb of «لو»."

Abū al-Baqāʾ and Ibn Mālik held the second possibility. Ibn Mālik said: "«لو» here is conditional in the sense of «إنْ», so it turns the past into a future meaning, the implied form being: 'and let those fear who, if they leave…'. And if an imperfect verb occurs after this «لو», it is future, as it is after «إنْ»." And he recited:

1551 - لا يُلْفِكُ الرَّاجوك إلا مُظْهِراً ... خُلُقَ الكرامِ ولو تكونُ عَدِيما
(Those who hope in you will find you only displaying the character of the noble, even if you are destitute.)

I.e., even if you are destitute. Similar to this verse he recited is the words of another:

1552 - قومٌ إذا حارَبُوا شدَّوا مآزِرَهُمْ ... دونَ النساءِ ولو باتَتْ بأطْهارِ
(A people who, when they make war, tie fast their waist-wrappers against women, even if [the women] spend the night in a state of purity.)

What is fitting is that it be in its usual sense of a suspension in the past.

What led Ibn Mālik and Abū al-Baqāʾ to make it in the sense of «إنْ» was the supposition that, since He commanded fear, and the command is future and what the command concerns is a relative noun, it would not be valid for the ṣila to be past on the assumption that it indicates non-existence, which is incompatible with carrying out the command; so the wording «إنْ» was good in the place of «لو». Because of this supposition, al-Zamakhsharī did not put «لو» before a future verb; rather he brought a past verb attributed to the relative noun at the time of the command, saying: "let those fear whose description and state is that, were they on the point of leaving…"

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What they supposed does not follow, except if the ṣila were past in meaning and had actually happened, since the meaning of «لو تركوا من خلفهم» is 'they died and left behind them'; if it were so, the interpretation of «لو» as being in the sense of «إنْ» would be required, since the command to perform an act cannot go together with someone who has actually died. But if it is past on a supposition, it may validly occur as a ṣila, with the governor of the relative noun being the future verb, as in your saying: 'Let him visit us who, had he died yesterday, we would have wept for him'." End of quote.

As for the two verses mentioned above, it does not follow from the validity of making it in the sense of «إنْ» in them that it is so in the verse, because in the two verses we are compelled to that. As for the first verse, it is because the jawāb of «لو» is omitted and indicated by his words «لا يُلْفِك», which is a prohibition, and prohibition is future; that is why «لو» was a suspension in the future. As for the second verse, it is because what follows it falls within the scope of «إذا», and «إذا» is for the future.

The object of «وَلْيَخْشَ» is omitted, i.e., "and let them fear Allah." The case may also be one of tanāzuʿ (two governors competing for one word), for «وَلْيخش» seeks the name of Allah, and likewise «فليتقوا», and it would then be a case of making the second governor operate, given the omission from the first.

His words: {مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ}: there are two views about it. The more evident: it is attached to «تركوا» as an adverb of it. Second: it is attached to an omitted word, because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ذرية»; because it was originally an adjective of an indefinite noun, placed before it, and so made a ḥāl.

Ḥamza pronounced the alif of «ضِعافاً» with imāla (inclination), paying no heed to the elevated letter (ḥarf al-istiʿlāʾ) because it has kasra; there is thus a descent in it, so it is not incompatible with imāla.

Ibn Muḥayṣin read: «ضُعُفاً», with ḍamma on the ḍād and the ʿayn and tanwīn on the fāʾ. Al-Sulamī and ʿĀʾisha read «ضعفاء», with ḍamma on the ḍād, fatḥa on the ʿayn and a long vowel; it is a regular plural for faʿīl as an adjective, as in ظَريف / ظُرَفاء and كريم / كُرَماء. It was also read «ضَعافَى», with fatḥa and imāla, like «سَكارى». The apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's wording is that «ضُعافى» was read with ḍamma on the ḍād, like «سُكارى», for he said: "And it was read ضُعَفَاء, ضَعافى and ضُعافى, like سَكارى and سُكارى." It is possible that he means it was read with ḍamma on the ḍād and with fatḥa; and it is possible that he means it was read «ضَعافى» with fatḥa on the ḍād without imāla, and «ضَعافَى» with fatḥa and imāla, like «سَكارى» with fatḥa on the sīn without imāla and «سَكارى» with fatḥa and imāla. The apparent one is the first, and the most probable supposition is that it was not transmitted as a reading.

Ḥamza pronounced the alif of «خاف» with imāla because of the kasra implied in the alif, since the underlying form is «خَوِف» with kasra on the middle radical, as evidenced by its fatḥa in the imperfect, as in «يخاف». Abū al-Baqāʾ gave as the reason that kasra may occur in one of its states, namely when the verb is attributed to the first-person pronoun or one of its sisters, as in «خِفْت» and «خِفْنا». The sentence consisting of «لو» and its jawāb is the ṣila of «الذين».

semin-durr:10-10.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {ظُلْماً}: there are two views about it. First: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and the conditions for the accusative are present. Second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e., "they consume it, being wrongdoers." The sentence formed by His words {إِنَّمَا يَأْكُلُونَ} is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ». In that there is evidence for the khabar of «إنَّ» occurring as a sentence that begins with «إنَّ», and about that there is disagreement. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What made it good here is that the ism of «إنَّ» is a relative noun, so the speech was lengthened by the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; when it became distant, that was not minded. This is better than your saying «إنَّ زيداً إنَّ أباه منطلقٌ» (Zayd — his father is departing)." Someone might say: "There is no evidence in it for that, because it [«إنما»] is restrained by «ما» and its meaning is restriction, so it has become, in meaning, like your saying «إنَّ زيداً ما انطلق إلا أبوه» (Zayd — none departed but his father)." This is open to consideration.

His words: {فِي بُطُونِهِمْ}: there are two views about it. First: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يأكلون», i.e., their bellies are vessels for the fire — either literally, in that Allah creates for them a fire which they eat into their bellies, or figuratively, in that the effect is stated while the cause is meant. Second: it is attached to an omitted word, because it is a ḥāl from «ناراً»; it was originally an adjective of the indefinite noun, and when it was placed before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl.

Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this view from Abū ʿAlī in his «Tadhkira», and related from him that he rejected its being an adverb of «يأكلون», for he said: "{فِي بُطُونِهِمْ نَاراً}: something about it has been mentioned in al-Baqara. What is specific to this place is that «في بطونهم» is a ḥāl from «ناراً», i.e., a fire being in their bellies, and is not an adverb of «يأكلون»; he mentioned it in the «Tadhkira»." In his words "and what is specific to this place" there is something to consider, for just as «في بطونهم» may be a ḥāl from «نار» here, it may be a ḥāl from «النار» in al-Baqara, and showing a difference is difficult. Nor does any evident reason appear for Abū ʿAlī's rejection of «في بطونهم» being an adverb of the eating.

His words: {وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the lām; Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr [from ʿĀṣim] with ḍamma on the yāʾ, as a passive of the three-letter verb. It may also be from «أصلى», and when it was made passive the first object took the place of the fāʿil (agent). Ibn Abī ʿAbla read with ḍamma on both, as an active verb from the four-letter form; the underlying form on this reading is «سيُصْلِيُون», from «أصلى», like «يُكْرِمون» from «أكرم». The ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt to be heavy and was dropped, so two quiescent letters met; the first of them, the yāʾ, was dropped, and the letter before the wāw was given ḍamma so that it would remain sound.

«أَصْلَى»: the hamza in it may be for entering into a thing, so it is transitive to one object, namely «سعيراً»; or it may be for making transitive, in which case the object is omitted, i.e., they make themselves roast in a blaze.

Abū Ḥaywa read with ḍamma on the yāʾ, fatḥa on the ṣād and the lām doubled, as a passive of «صَلَّى» with doubling. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The doubling is for intensity."

Al-ṣilī: kindling with fire. One says «صَلِي بكذا», with kasra on the middle radical; and His words {لاَ يَصْلاَهَآ} [al-Layl: 15] mean "he roasts by it." Al-Khalīl said: "«صَلِي الكافرُ النارَ»: he suffered its heat. And another roasted him in the fire (ṣalāhu and aṣlāhu)." Al-Rāghib said thus, and the apparent sense of this wording is that faʿila and afʿala have the same meaning, being transitive to two objects, the second of them by a preposition, which may be dropped. Someone else said: "«صَلِيَ بالنارِ», i.e., he warmed himself by being near it"; on this view «سعيراً» is accusative by removal of the preposition. What shows that the original of «يَصْلاها» is «يَصْلَى بها» is the poet's words:

1553 - إذا أَوْقَدُوا ناراً لحربِ عَدُوِّهم ... فقد خابَ مَنْ يَصْلَى بها وسعيرِها
(When they kindle a fire for war against their enemy, whoever roasts in it and its blaze has failed.)

It was also said: one says «صَلَيْتُه النارَ»: I brought him near to it; so it may be accusative without removal of a preposition. Al-saʿīr is originally the blazing embers; «سَعَرْتُ النارَ»: I kindled it. From this comes «مُسْعِرُ حربٍ» (kindler of war), by way of likeness. Al-misʿar: the instrument with which the fire is stirred.

semin-durr:46-46.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِّنَ الذين هَادُواْ يُحَرِّفُونَ}: there are seven views on it. The first: «مِن الذين» is a fronted khabar (predicate), and «يُحَرِّفون» is a clause in the position of nominative as an adjective of an omitted qualified noun which is the mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: «من الذين هادوا قومٌ يُحَرِّفون» (among those who are Jews are people who distort). The omission of the qualified noun after partitive «مِنْ» is permissible, even if the adjective is a verb, as in their saying «منا ظَعَن ومنا أَقام» (of us [some] departed and of us [some] stayed), i.e. a party departed.
