This is the doctrine of Sībawayh and al-Fārisī; and like it is:
1590 - وما الدهرُ إلا تارتانِ فمِنْهما ... أموتُ وأُخْرى أبتغي العيشَ أكدحُ
(Time is nothing but two turns: of them [one in which] I die, and another in which I seek a living, toiling.)
i.e. "of them is a turn in which I die".
The second is the view of al-Farrāʾ: the preposition and its genitive noun are also a fronted khabar, but he assumes the omitted mubtadaʾ to be a relative noun, its implied form being: «من الذين هادوا مَنْ يحرفون» (among those who are Jews are those who distort), and he would have construed «يُحَرِّفون» according to the meaning. Al-Farrāʾ said: "And like it is:
1591 - فَظَلُّوا ومنهم دَمْعُه سابقٌ له ... وآخرُ يَثْني دمعةً العينِ باليدِ
(They remained, and of them [one] whose tears outran him, and another holding back the eye's tear with his hand.)
He said: "Its implied form is: «ومنهم مَنْ دمعُه سابقٌ له»." The Basrans do not allow the omission of the relative noun because it is part of a word; according to them this is interpreted as the omission of a qualified noun, as preceded. Their interpretation is more fitting, because an indefinite noun is conjoined to it, namely «آخر», and «أخرى» in the verse before it; so there is in that an indication of what was omitted, and the implied form is: "of them is a lover whose tears outrun him, and another".
The third: «مِن الذين» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are those who are Jews", and on this view «يُحَرِّفون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of «هادوا». On these three views the speech is complete at His word «نصيراً».
The fourth: «من الذين» is a ḥāl from the agent of «يريدون»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and he disallowed its being a ḥāl from the pronoun in «أوتوا» and from «الذين», I mean in His words {أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الذين أُوتُواْ}; he said: "Because there are not [several] ḥāls for one thing unless some are conjoined to others." I say: this is a disputed question; some grammarians disallow it and some allow it, and that is the correct view.
The fifth: «مِن الذين» is an explication of the relative noun in His words {أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الذين أُوتُواْ}, because they are Jews and Christians, so He explained them as the Jews; al-Zamakhsharī said this. This is questionable in that the two have been separated by three clauses, namely «والله أعلم» to the end; and if al-Fārisī disallowed parenthesis by two clauses, then what of three! Al-Shaykh said this. But this is questionable, for the clauses here are conjoined to one another, and conjunction makes two things one thing.
The sixth: it is an explication of «أعدائكم», what is between them also being a parenthesis; and what is in that has been learned.
The seventh: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نصيراً», and this root is made transitive with «من». Allah the Exalted said: {وَنَصَرْنَاهُ مِنَ القوم} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 77] and {فَمَن يَنصُرُنَا مِن بَأْسِ الله} [Ghāfir: 29], according to one of two interpretations: either by making help (naṣr) carry the meaning of protection (manʿ), i.e. "We protected him from the people", and likewise: "Allah suffices as one who protects, through His help, from those who are Jews"; or by making «مِنْ» in the sense of «على»; the first is the doctrine of the Basrans. If we make «من الذين» an explication of what precedes it, to what is it attached? The apparent view is that it is attached to an omitted element; that is indicated by their saying, about «سُقيْاً لك» (may you be watered), that «لك» is attached to an omitted element because it is an explication.
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It has also been said that it is a ḥāl from «أعدائكم», i.e. 'Allah knows best your enemies, being among those who are Jews'; and the separation between them is well-founded [Translator's note: printed «مُسَدِّد»], so it does not prevent the ḥāl." This statement of his implies that it is an explication of «أعدائكم», while he parses it as a ḥāl, so it is attached to an omitted element — but not according to that omission intended in explication.
It has become clear from what preceded that «يُحَرِّفون» either has no grammatical position, or has the position of nominative or accusative, according to what preceded. Abū Rajāʾ and al-Nakhaʿī read «الكلام», and it has been read «الكِلْم» with kasra on the kāf and sukūn on the lām, the plural of «كِلْمة», lightened from «كَلِمة»; their meanings are close.
{عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِ} is attached to «يُحَرِّفون». The pronoun in «مواضعه» was made masculine by construal with «الكَلِم», because it is a generic noun.
Here came {عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِ}, and in al-Māʾida {مِن بَعْدِ مَوَاضِعِهِ} [verse: 41]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "As for «عن مواضِعه», it is according to what we explained, namely removing it from its places in which Allah's wisdom required it to be placed, by substituting something else in its place as their desires demanded. As for {مِن بَعْدِ مَوَاضِعِهِ}, the meaning is that it had places in which it was fit to be, and when they distorted it they left it like a stranger with no place after its places and abodes. The two meanings are close." Al-Shaykh said: "It may be said that they are equivalent, but here, and in the first [passage] of al-Māʾida, {مِن بَعْدِ مَوَاضِعِهِ} [verse: 41] [Translator's note: so in the source; the first passage of al-Māʾida (5:13) has «عن مواضعه», and 5:41 has «من بعد مواضعه»] was omitted, because His words «عَنْ مَّواضِعِه» indicate that it had settled places; and in the second [passage] of al-Māʾida «عن مواضِعِه» was omitted, because distortion after its places indicates that it is distortion away from its places. So the underlying form is: 'they distort the words from after their places away from them'; here the 'after' was omitted, and there 'away from them', as an extension of expression. The starting point here was His words «عن مواضعه» because it is more concise, and there [Translator's note: printed «وفي»; probably «وفيه», 'in it'] is an explicit statement in the wording of «عن» and of the places, and an allusion to the 'after'."
He also said: "The apparent view is that where they are described with extreme rebelliousness and transgression, open enmity, buying error and breaking the covenant, there came {يُحَرِّفُونَ الكلم عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِ}, as though they distorted them at the very first moment, before they settled in their places, and hastened to do that; for that reason the first [passage] of al-Māʾida came like this verse, where He describes them with breaking the covenant and hardness of hearts. And where they are described with softness and referring judgement to the Messenger, there came {مِن بَعْدِ مَوَاضِعِهِ}, as though they did not hasten to distortion, but it occurred to them after the words had settled in their places. So they are two different contexts."
His words: {وَيَقُولُونَ} is conjoined to «يُحَرِّفون», as preceded, and what follows it is in the position of accusative through it. His words: {غَيْرَ مُسْمَعٍ}: there are two views on its accusative. The first: it is a ḥāl. The second: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the meaning being: "hear, without being made to hear speech that you would be pleased with, for your hearing shuns it". Al-Zamakhsharī, after relating its accusative as a ḥāl and mentioning the preceding meaning, said: "On this view «غيرَ مُسْمَع» may be the object of «اسمَعْ», i.e. hear speech that does not make you hear, because your ear does not take it in, shunning it." This speech is two-faced, meaning that it can bear praise and blame: intending praise, you assume "not made to hear anything disliked", so the second object has been omitted, because the first has taken the place of the agent; and intending blame, you assume "not made to hear any good", the second object also being omitted.
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It has also been said: they meant 'not heard [i.e. accepted] from you'." Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted this view from al-Ṭabarī and said: "It is reported from al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Morphology does not support it", meaning that the Arabs do not say «أَسْمَعْتُك» in the sense of "I accepted from you"; rather they say «أسْمَعْتُه» in the sense of "I insulted him", and «سمعت منه» in the sense of "I accepted from him": they express acceptance figuratively with hearing (samāʿ), not with making-hear (ismāʿ). The discussion of {رَاعِنَا} [verse: 104] in al-Baqara has preceded.
His words: {لَيّاً بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ وَطَعْناً}: there are two views on them. The first: they are mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), governed in the accusative by «ويقولون». The second: they are two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "twisting and reviling". The origin of «لَيّاً» is «لَوْيٌ», from «لوى يَلْوي»; the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ after being changed into yāʾ, so it is like «طَيّ», the maṣdar of «طَوَى يَطْوي». «بألسنتِهم» and «في الدين» are attached to the two maṣdars before them. As for {لَوْ أَنَّهُمْ قَالُواْ}, the discussion of that has preceded in al-Baqara in the fullest terms.
His words: {لَكَانَ خَيْراً}: there are two views on it. The more apparent: it is in the sense of afʿal (the elative), the thing over which it is preferred being omitted, i.e. "had they said these words, it would have been better than those words". The second: there is no comparison in it; rather it is in the sense of "good" and "excellent", so there is no omission then. The bāʾ in «بكفرِهم» is causal.
His words: {إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً}: there are three views on it. The first: it is accusative as excepted from «لَعَنَهم», i.e. "Allah cursed them, except a few of them", for they believed, so He did not curse them. The second: it is excepted from the pronoun in «فلا يؤمنون», and what is meant by the few is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and those like him. Makkī did not approve of these two views: as for the first, he said: "Because whoever disbelieves is cursed; no one is excepted from them." As for the second: "Because the proper form is the nominative as a badal (substitute), since the speech is not affirmative." The third: it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "except a little faith"; its rationale is that they believed in the divine unity but disbelieved in Muhammad ﷺ and his law.
Al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya expressed this "littleness" as non-existence, meaning that they do not believe at all, like his words:
1592 - قليلٌ التشكِّي للمُهِمِّ يُصيبه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Seldom complaining of a grave matter that befalls him…)
Al-Shaykh said: "What they mentioned — that littleness may be meant as non-existence — is correct, except that this exceptive construction rejects it. If you say «لم أقم إلا قليلاً» (I did not stand except a little), the meaning is the negation of standing except for the little, which exists on your part; it does not indicate the negation of standing altogether. This is unlike «قَلَّما يقولُ ذلك أحدٌ إلا زيدٌ» (seldom does anyone say that except Zayd) and «قَلَّ رجلٌ يفعل ذلك» (few a man does that), for that can bear the littleness opposed to muchness and can bear pure negation. But that you negate, then affirm, then by the affirmation after the negation intend a negation — no; because it would entail «إلاَّ» and what follows it being superfluous without benefit, since the negation of standing has already been understood from your saying «لم أقم»; so what benefit is there in an affirmed exception by which is meant a negation understood from the preceding clause? Furthermore, it would lead to what follows «إلا» agreeing in meaning with what precedes it, whereas exception requires that what follows «إلاَّ» differ from what precedes it in that."

semin-durr:47-47.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِّن قَبْلِ أَن نَّطْمِسَ}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) the imperative in His word «آمنوا». «نَطْمِس» may be transitive — and from that is this verse, and likewise {فَإِذَا النجوم طُمِسَتْ} [al-Mursalāt: 8], since it is made passive without a preposition — and it may be intransitive; one says «طمس المطرُ الأعلامَ» (the rain effaced the landmarks) and «طَمَست الأعلامُ» (the landmarks were effaced). Kaʿb said:
1593 - من كلِّ نَضَّاخةِ الذِّفْرى إذا عَرِقَتْ ... عُرْضَتُها طامِسُ الأعلامِ مجهولُ
(Of every she-camel whose nape gushes with sweat when she sweats; her aim is a [desert] with effaced landmarks, unknown.)
The majority read «نَطْمِس» with kasra on the mīm, and Abū Rajāʾ with ḍamma; they are two dialectal forms in the imperfect. Some assumed a muḍāf, i.e. "the eyes of faces"; this is strengthened by the fact that effacing pertains to eyes; Allah the Exalted said: {لَطَمَسْنَا على أَعْيُنِهِمْ} [Yā Sīn: 66].
His words: {على أَدْبَارِهَآ}: there are two views on it. The more apparent: it is attached to «نَرُدَّها». The second: it is attached to an omitted element, because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object in «نردَّها»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and it is not clear.
His words «أو نلعَنهم» are conjoined to «نَطْمِسَ». The pronoun in «نلعنهم» refers back to the faces "by omission of a muḍāf ilayhi", i.e. "the faces of a people", or on the basis that by them are meant the notables and chiefs; or it refers back to those who were given the Book, in which case it is a shift (iltifāt) from second to third person; and in it there is an inducement for them to believe, since He did not confront them with the curse after having honoured them by their being People of the Book. His words: {وَكَانَ أَمْرُ الله}: a single "command" by which the commands are meant. It has also been said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) occurring in the place of a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. what is commanded by Him, that is, what He brings into existence is bound to be.

semin-durr:48-48.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ}: resumptive, and not conjoined to the first «يَغْفر», because the meaning would be corrupted. The agent in «يشاء» is a pronoun referring back to Allah the Exalted. It is understood from the words of al-Zamakhsharī that it is a pronoun referring back to «مَنْ» in «لِمَنْ»; the meaning according to him is: "Allah does not forgive association (shirk) for one who does not will that He forgive him, by his having died upon shirk without repenting of it; and He forgives what is less than that for one who wills that He forgive him, by his having died repentant of shirk". «لِمَنْ يشاء» is attached to «يغفر».

semin-durr:49-49.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَلَمْ تَرَ}: its like has preceded. «بل» is a turning away (iḍrāb) from their declaring themselves pure. Abū al-Baqāʾ assumed a clause before this iḍrāb; he said: "Its implied form is: they erred; rather Allah purifies whom He wills."
His words: {وَلاَ يُظْلَمُونَ} may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from what preceded, or resumptive. The pronoun in «يُظْلمون» may refer back to «مَنْ يشاء», i.e. nothing is diminished of their purification — the pronoun was made plural only by construal according to the meaning of «مَنْ» — or it may refer back to those who declare [themselves] pure, or to both parties, the one who declared himself pure and the one whom Allah declared pure: for the former nothing is diminished of his punishment, and for the latter nothing is diminished of his reward. The first is more apparent, because «مَنْ» is the nearest thing mentioned, and because «بل» is an iḍrāb whose sequel is cut off from what precedes it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may be resumptive, i.e. [referring to] the one who declared himself pure and the one whom Allah declared pure." End of quotation. So he made the pronoun's referring back to the two parties based on the resumptive view; this is not necessary, rather it may refer back to both while the clause is circumstantial.
{فَتِيلاً} is a second object, because the first has taken the place of the agent. It may also be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), as was established at {مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ} [al-Nisāʾ: 40]. Al-fatīl is a fine thread in the cleft of the date-stone, used proverbially for littleness. It has also been said: it is the dirt that comes out from between your fingers or palms when you roll them, so it is faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl. The Arabs used four things found together in the date-stone as proverbs for trifling littleness: al-fatīl; al-naqīr, the small pit on the back of the date-stone; al-qiṭmīr, the thin skin over it — these three occur in the Mighty Book — and al-thufrūq, which is what is between the date-stone and the calyx at the top of the date, like a link between them.

semin-durr:50-50.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {انظُرْ كَيفَ يَفْتَرُونَ}: «كيف» is accusative through «يَفْتَرون», and the disagreement about it has preceded. The clause is in the position of accusative after the dropping of the preposition, because it is suspended (muʿallaqa) as the complement of «انظر», and «انظر» is made transitive with «في», because here it is not visual. «على الله» is attached to «يفترون». Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الكذب», placed before it; he said: "It may not be attached to «الكذب», because the dependent of a maṣdar does not precede it [Translator's note: printed «يقتدَّم»; read «يتقدَّم»]; but if it is taken as explication (tabyīn), it is permissible." Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed «كيف» to be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the clause of His word «يفترون» as the khabar (predicate). This is unsound, because «كيف» is not put in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; and even assuming that, where is the link between it and the clause occurring as its khabar? It is not the mubtadaʾ itself, so as to dispense with a link. «إثْماً» is a tamyīz (specification). The pronoun in «به» refers back to «الكذب»; it has also been said: to the fabrication; and al-Zamakhsharī made it refer back to their claim, meaning in terms of the implied sense.

semin-durr:51-51.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {يُؤْمِنُونَ}: there are two views on it. The first: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from «الذين» or from the wāw of «أُوتوا». «بالجِبْتِ» is attached to it, «ويقولون» is conjoined to it, and «للذين» is attached to «يقولون»; the lām is either for conveying [speech] or for cause, like its counterparts. «وهؤلاء أَهْدَى» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of accusative through the verb of saying. «سبيلاً» is a tamyīz (specification). The second: «يؤمنون» is resumptive, as though He expressed wonder at their state, since one who has been given a portion of the Book ought not to do any of what has been mentioned; so it is an answer to an implied question, as though it were said: "Do you not wonder at the state of those who were given a portion of the Book?" And it was said: "And what is their state?" And He said: "They believe … and they say …", and these two contradict their state.
Al-jibt is al-jibs, with the undotted sīn, changed into tāʾ, as in «النات», «الأكيات» and «ست» for «الناس», «الأكياس» and «سِدْس». The poet said:
1594 -. . . . . . . . . . . ... شرارُ الناتِ ليسوا بأجوادٍ ولا أَكْياتِ
(… the worst of people, neither generous nor shrewd.)
Al-jibs is one in whom there is no good; one says «رجلٌ جِبْسٌ» and «جِبْتٌ», i.e. base. It has been said: the change of sīn to tāʾ was only claimed because the root j-b-t is unused; this is the view of Quṭrub, while others make it an independent root. It has also been said: al-jibt is the sorcerer in the language of Abyssinia. Al-jibt is applied to everything worshipped besides Allah, and for that reason they named a particular idol with it. Al-ṭāghūt: its explanation and morphology have preceded.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الأنثيين}: this is a sentence made of a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). It may be in the position of the accusative through «يُوصي», because the meaning is "He prescribes for you" or "He legislates concerning your children"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. This is close to the doctrine of al-Farrāʾ, for he treats whatever is in the sense of "saying" like "saying" in reporting the sentences after it. Al-Farrāʾ said: "«يُوصيكم» did not govern «مِثْل», since it was treated like 'saying' in reporting sentences; so the sentence is in the position of the accusative through «يُوصيكم»." Makkī said: "«للذَّكَرِ مثلُ حظ» is a subject and predicate in the position of the accusative, a clarification and explanation of the injunction." Al-Kisāʾī said: "«مثل» is nominative on the elision of «أنَّ», its implied form being «أنَّ للذكرِ مثلَ حظ»." And Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it so [i.e., «مثلَ»].

It may also have no grammatical position, but rather have been brought for clarification and explanation; so it is a sentence explaining the injunction. This is better and in line with the doctrine of the Basrans, and it is the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's wording, for he said: "This is a summary whose detail is {لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الأنثيين}." As for His words «للذَّكر», there must be in this sentence a pronoun referring back to «أولادكم». It may be omitted, i.e., "for the male of them," as in «السَّمْنُ مَنَوانِ بدرهم» (ghee: two manās for a dirham [i.e., of it]); al-Zamakhsharī said this. Or the definite article may have taken its place, for those who hold that view, the underlying form being "for their male."

«مثلُ» is an adjective of an omitted noun it describes, i.e., "for the male of them is a share like the share of two females." As for {في أَوْلاَدِكُمْ}, it was said that there is an omitted muḍāf there, i.e., "concerning the children of your dead." They said: because a living person cannot be addressed with the division of the inheritance among his own children and have that imposed upon him. Some said: "If we say that the meaning of «يُوصيكم» is 'He makes clear to you,' this assumption is not needed." Some assumed a muḍāf before «أولادكم», i.e., "concerning the matter of your children" or "concerning the affair of your children."

Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read: «يُوَصِّيكم», with doubling; it was mentioned earlier that «أوصى» and «وصَّى» are two dialect forms.

His words: {فَإِن كُنَّ نِسَآءً}: the pronoun in «كُنَّ» refers back to the females comprised in His words {في أَوْلاَدِكُمْ}, for the implied form is "concerning your children, male and female"; so the pronoun refers back to one of the two categories of children. And if the pronoun refers back to a broken plural of rational beings meaning purely males — in his words, upon him be peace, «وربَّ الشياطين ومَنْ أَضْلَلْن» (and Lord of the devils and those they [fem. pl.] have led astray) — just as it refers back to a group of females, then all the more and more fittingly does it so refer to a broken plural that includes females. This is the meaning of the Shaykh's [Abū Ḥayyān's] statement. There is something to consider in it, because its referring there like the feminine pronoun was only for a reason absent here, namely seeking symmetry, because before it is «اللهم ربََّ السماوات ومَنْ أَظْلَلْنَ، وربَّ الأرضين وما أَقْلَلْنَ» (O Allah, Lord of the heavens and what they have shaded, and Lord of the earths and what they have carried); the grammarians mentioned that.

It was also said: the pronoun refers back to the females left behind (al-matrūkāt), i.e., "if the ones left are…," the mention of children indicating it; Abū al-Baqāʾ and Makkī said this. Al-Zamakhsharī gave its implied form as: "if the daughters, or the female offspring, are…"

When this is established, «كُنَّ» is kāna with its ism, «نساءً» is its khabar, and «فوق اثنتين» is an adverb in the position of the accusative as an adjective of «نساء». It is by this adjective that the khabar becomes informative; had it been restricted to it [i.e., «نساء»], it would not be informative. Do you not see that if it were said «إن كان الزيدون رجالاً كان كذا» (if the Zayds are men, such-and-such), there would be no information in it?

Al-Zamakhsharī allowed two unusual views in this verse. First: the pronoun in «كنَّ» is a vague pronoun, and «نساءً» is accusative as explaining it, meaning as a tamyīz (specification); he said the same about the pronoun in «كانت» in His words «وإنْ كانت واحدة», on the view that «كان» is complete (tāmma). The other view: that «فوق اثنتين» is a second khabar of «كُنَّ». The Shaykh rejected both of them. As for the first, because «كان» is not among the verbs whose fāʿil (agent) can be an implied pronoun explained by what follows it; rather, among verbs this is specific to «نعم» and «بئس» and what is treated like them, and to the chapter of tanāzuʿ (two governors competing) when the second governor is made to operate. As for the second, because of the need for this adjective mentioned above, since the khabar must by itself carry the information of the predication; and it was mentioned above that had He restricted Himself to His words {فَإِن كُنَّ نِسَآءً}, it would convey nothing, because it is known.

Al-Ḥasan and Nuʿaym ibn Maysara read «ثُلْثا», «الثلْث», «النصْف», «الرُّبْع» and «الثُّمْن», all with sukūn on the middle letter; the majority with ḍamma, which is the dialect of the Ḥijāz and Banū Asad. Al-Naḥḥās said: "From al-thulth to al-ʿushr (from a third to a tenth)." Al-Zajjāj said: "It is a single dialect form, and the sukūn is a lightening."

His words: {وَإِن كَانَتْ وَاحِدَةً}: Nāfiʿ read «واحدةٌ» in the nominative, on the view that «كان» is complete (tāmma), i.e., "if one [daughter] exists"; the rest read «واحدة» in the accusative, on the view that «كانت» is incomplete (nāqiṣa), its ism being latent in it and referring back to the female heir or the female left behind, and «واحدةً» is accusative as the khabar of «كان». It was mentioned above that al-Zamakhsharī allowed that there be in «كان» a vague pronoun explained by the accusative word after it.

Al-Sulamī read «النُّصف» with ḍamma on the nūn, and it is the reading of ʿAlī and Zayd ibn Thābit, may Allah be pleased with them both. Something of that was mentioned in al-Baqara on His words {فَنِصْفُ مَا فَرَضْتُمْ} [verse 237].

His words: {وَلأَبَوَيْهِ لِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِّنْهُمَا السدس}: «السدس» is a mubtadaʾ and «لأبويه» a fronted khabar, and «لكلِّ واحدٍ» is a badal (substitute) from «لأبويه». This is what al-Zamakhsharī stated explicitly, for he said: "«لكلَّ واحد منهما» is a badal from «لأبويه», with the governor repeated. The benefit of this badal is that had it been said «ولأبويه السدسُ» (and to his parents the sixth), its apparent sense would be their sharing in it; and had it been said «لأبويه السدسان» (to his parents the two sixths), it would suggest dividing the two sixths between them equally or unequally.

"If you say: then why was it not said «ولكلِّ واحدٍ من أبويه السدس» (and to each one of his parents the sixth), and what benefit is there in mentioning the parents first and then substituting from them? I say: because in substitution and detailing after summary there is emphasis and reinforcement, like what you see in combining the thing explained and the explanation. «السدس» is a mubtadaʾ, its khabar is «لأبويه», and the badal is placed between them for clarification." End of quote.

The Shaykh disputed with him over his making «لأبويه» the khabar rather than his words «بكلِّ واحد» [Translator's note: so in the text; read «لكلِّ واحد»]. He said: "Because the badal ought to be the khabar rather than what it substitutes for," meaning that the badal is what is relied upon, while what it substitutes for has taken the status of what is discarded. He compared it to your saying «إنًَّ زيداً عينُه حسنة» (Zayd — his eye is beautiful): just as «حسنة» is a khabar about «عينه» rather than «زيد», because [Zayd] has the status of what is discarded, so too this. He also compared it to your saying «أبواك كلُّ واحد منهما يَصنع كذا» (your parents — each one of them does such-and-such): «يَصنع» is a khabar about «كل واحد» of them, and had you said «أبواك كلُّ واحدٍ منهما يَصْنعان كذا» (… each one of them do [dual] such-and-such), it would not be permissible.

There is something to consider in this dispute, because if you were asked, "What is the grammatical position of «لأبويه»?", we would be compelled to say: "In the position of the nominative as a fronted khabar"; but he transferred the attribution of being the khabar to «لكلِّ واحدٍ منهما» rather than «لأبويه». He said: "One of them said: «السدسُ» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, «لكلِّ واحدٍ» is the khabar, «لكلِّ» is a badal from the parents, and «منهما» is an adjective of «واحد». This badal is a part-for-whole substitution, which is why a pronoun was brought with it. It should not be imagined that it is a thing-for-thing substitution, with both referring to one and the same entity, because «أبواك يَصْنعان كذا» (your parents do such-and-such) is permissible while «أبواكَ كلُّ واحدٍ منهما يصنعان كذا» is impossible; rather you say «يَصْنع»." End of quote.

The pronoun in «لأبويه» refers back to what the pronoun in «ترك» refers back to, namely the deceased, indicated by the force of the speech. The dual in «أبويه» is by way of predominance (taghlīb); the underlying form is "to his father and his mother," and the masculine was given predominance over the feminine, as in their saying «القَمَران» (the two moons: the sun and the moon) and «العُمَران» (the two ʿUmars: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar). It is a dual that is not formed by regular analogy.

His words: «فلأِمه»: the majority read «فلإِمه» [Translator's note: so in the text; the context requires that the majority read «فلأُمه» with ḍamma on the hamza, as stated below], and His words {في أُمِّ الكتاب} [verse 4] in Sūrat al-Zukhruf, His words {حتى يَبْعَثَ في أُمِّهَا} [verse 59] in al-Qaṣaṣ, His words {فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ} in [al-Naḥl: 78] and [al-Zumar: 6], His words {أَوْ بُيُوتِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ} [verse 61] in al-Nūr, and {فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ} [verse 32] in al-Najm, with ḍamma on the hamza of «أُمّ», which is the original. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read all of that with kasra on the hamza, and Ḥamza alone added kasra on the mīm of «أمَّهات» in the places mentioned. All this is in continuous recitation; as for beginning with the hamza of «الأم» and «الأمهات», there is no disagreement about its ḍamma.

As for the reason for the majority's reading, it is evident, because it is the original, as mentioned. As for Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī's reading with kasra on the hamza, they said: it is for harmony with the kasra or the yāʾ before the hamza; the hamza was given kasra in harmony with what precedes it, and because they found it heavy to pass from a kasra or something like it to a ḍamma. That is why, when the two of them begin with the hamza, they give it ḍamma, because the kasra or yāʾ is gone. As for Ḥamza's kasra on the mīm of «أمهات» in the places mentioned, it is for harmony (itbāʿ): he made the vowel of the mīm follow the vowel of the hamza, so the kasra of the mīm is a follower of a follower. That is why, when he begins with it, he gives the hamza ḍamma and the mīm fatḥa, because the cause of that is gone, as mentioned. The kasra of the hamza of «أم» after a kasra or a yāʾ was reported by Sībawayh as a dialect form of the Arabs, and al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ attributed it to Hawāzin and Hudhayl.

His words: {فَإِن كَانَ لَهُ إِخْوَةٌ}: «إخوة» is more general than their being males or females or some males and some females, and this would be by way of predominance (taghlīb). Some claimed that «الإِخوة» is specific to males, and that sisters do not reduce the mother from the third to the sixth; they said: because «إخوة» is the plural of «أخ». The majority hold that «الإِخوة», though plural in form, applies to two, so two brothers also reduce the mother from the third to the sixth — contrary to Ibn ʿAbbās, for he does not hold that she is reduced by two, and the apparent sense is with him.

His words: {مِن بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ}: there are three views about it. First: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to what precedes it of the division of all the inheritances, not to what immediately adjoins it alone, as if it were said: "the division of these shares is after a bequest"; al-Zamakhsharī said this, meaning that it is attached to His words {يُوصِيكُمُ الله} and what follows. Second, mentioned by the Shaykh: it is attached to an omitted word, i.e., "they are entitled to that, as detailed, after a bequest." Third: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السدس», its implied form being "being due, after a bequest," the governor being the adverb; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. He also allowed another view, saying: "[It may be an adverb], i.e., that becomes settled for them after the bequest is taken out; and an elided muḍāf must be assumed, because the bequest here is the property bequeathed; and the bequest may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), like «الفريضة»." No evident reason appears for these two views. As for his words "the governor being the adverb," he means by "the adverb" the prepositional phrase in His words {فَلأُمِّهِ السدس}, for it resembles an adverb, and it governed the ḥāl because of the verb it contains, through occurring as a khabar. «يوصي» is an imperfect verb by which the past is meant, i.e., "a bequest which he made"; «بها» is attached to it, and the sentence is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of «وصية».

Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read «يُوصَى» as a passive in both places, and Ḥafṣ agreed with them in the latter; the rest read it as active. It was read anomalously (shādhdh) «يُوَصَّى», with doubling, as a passive. So «بها», in the reading with the active, is in the position of the accusative, and in the reading with the passive in the position of the nominative, because it takes the place of the fāʿil.

His words: {أَوْ دَيْنٍ}: «أو» here is for one of two things. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It does not indicate order, since there is no difference between your saying «جاءني زيد أو عمرو» (Zayd or ʿAmr came to me) and your saying «جاءني عمرو أو زيد» (ʿAmr or Zayd came to me), because «أو» is for one of two things, and in one thing there is no order. By this the statement of whoever said '[it means] after a debt or a bequest' is invalidated; order occurs only when both are present together, in which case the debt is put before the bequest."

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the meaning of «أو»? I say: its meaning is permission (ibāḥa), and that if one or both of them exist, it is put before the division of the inheritance, as in your saying «جالسِ [الحسنَ] أو ابنَ سيرين» (sit with al-Ḥasan or Ibn Sīrīn). If you say: why was the bequest put before the debt, when the debt comes before it in the Sharia? I say: since the bequest resembles inheritance in being taken without compensation, taking it out is something burdensome for the heirs, unlike the debt, for their souls are at ease with paying it; so it was put before the debt to urge its obligatoriness and hastening to take it out together with the debt. For that reason the word «أو» was brought, to make them equal in obligatoriness."

His words: {آبَآؤُكُمْ وَأَبناؤُكُمْ}: a mubtadaʾ, and «لا تَدْرُون» with what is in its scope is in the position of the nominative as its khabar. As for «أيُّهم», there are two views about it. The better known among the grammatical analysts: «أيُّهم» is a mubtadaʾ, being an interrogative noun, and «أقربُ» is its khabar; the sentence made of this mubtadaʾ and its khabar is in the position of the accusative through «تَدْرون», because it is one of the verbs of the heart, and the interrogative noun suspended it (taʿlīq) from governing its wording, because an interrogative is not governed by what precedes it, except in a request for confirmation (istithbāt).

Second: «أيُّهم» may be a relative noun in the sense of «الذي», and «أقربُ» the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ which is the pronoun referring back to the relative noun. Its omission is permissible because that is permissible with «أي» without restriction, i.e., whether the ṣila is long or not; the implied form is «أيُّهم هو أقربُ». This relative noun and its ṣila are in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), governed by «تَدْرون». It is indeclinable (mabnī) only because the two conditions for indeclinability are present, namely «أي» being in a genitive construct in its wording and the first part of its ṣila being omitted. This verse would then be parallel to the other verse, namely {ثُمَّ لَنَنزِعَنَّ مِن كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ} [Maryam: 69]. So the implied form becomes: "you do not know the one who is nearer." The Shaykh said: "I have not seen them mention it," meaning this view. I say: there is nothing to prevent it, neither from the side of meaning nor from the side of grammatical technique. On the first view the sentence fills the place of the two objects, and there is no need to assume an elision; on the second the relative noun is in the position of the accusative as a first object, and the second is omitted. Because there is no need to omit a second object, the first view is preferred.

Then this sentence — I mean His words {آبَآؤُكُمْ وَأَبناؤُكُمْ لاَ تَدْرُونَ} — has no grammatical position, because it is a parenthetical sentence. Al-Zamakhsharī said, after relating several views on its meanings and choosing the first of them: "Because this sentence is parenthetical, and it is the right of a parenthesis to emphasise that between which it is interposed and what is fitting to it." By "parenthesis" he means that it occurs within the account of the inheritances. However, this parenthesis is not what the grammarians intend, because by "parenthesis" in their technical usage they mean only what is between two inseparable things, such as a parenthesis between a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, a condition and its consequence, an oath and its answer, and a ṣila and its relative noun. Then he mentioned several views on its meanings. First — and it is the one he chose — he made it connected to the bequest, saying: "Then He emphasised that" — meaning concern for the bequest — "and encouraged it by His words {آبَآؤُكُمْ وَأَبناؤُكُمْ}, i.e., you do not know which of your fathers and sons who die is more beneficial to you: the one of them who made a bequest or the one who did not. That is, the one who bequeathed part of his property, and so exposed you to the reward of the Hereafter by carrying out his bequest, is nearer to you in benefit and more readily profitable than the one who left off the bequest and so left you more of the goods of this world. He made the reward of the Hereafter nearer and more present than the goods of this world, going by the reality of the matter; for the goods of this world, though near and immediate in appearance, are perishing, and so in reality are the farthest and remotest; while the reward of the Hereafter, though deferred, is lasting, and so in reality is the nearest and closest."

«نفعاً» is accusative as a tamyīz from «أقرب»; it is transferred from the position of fāʿil, and must be accusative. For whenever a tamyīz occurs after an elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl): if it is valid to form from it a verb attributed to that tamyīz as its fāʿil, the accusative is required, as in this verse, since it is valid to say «أيُّهم قَرُبَ لكم نَفْعُه» (which of them, his benefit is near to you); and if that is not valid, it must be genitive, as in «زيد أحسنُ فقيه» (Zayd is the best jurist), unlike «زيد أحسنُ فقهاً» (Zayd is best in jurisprudence). This is a useful rule. «لكم» is attached to «أقرب».

His words: {فَرِيضَةً}: there are three views about it. The most evident: it is a maṣdar emphasising the content of the preceding sentence about the injunction, because the meaning of «يوصيكم» is "Allah has made obligatory upon you," so the meaning becomes "Allah enjoins you with an injunction of obligation"; so it is a maṣdar not from the verb's own root. Second: it is a maṣdar in the accusative by an omitted verb from its own root. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«فريضةً» is a maṣdar of an omitted verb, i.e., 'Allah has made that obligatory as an obligation'." Third — Makkī and others said it — it is a ḥāl, because it is not a maṣdar. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording can bear the first two views, for he said: "«فريضة» is in the accusative of the emphatic maṣdar, i.e., 'He has made that obligatory as an obligation'."

semin-durr:53-53.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَمْ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ}: this «أم» is disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa), because the condition of connection is lacking, as has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara; so it is rendered as «بل» plus the hamza intended for disapproval. Likewise it is in His words {أَمْ يَحْسُدُونَ الناس} [al-Nisāʾ: 54]. His word «فإذَنْ» is a particle of answer and requital, and its nūn is radical. Makkī said: "The skilled grammarians write its nūn as a nūn, and al-Farrāʾ allowed it to be written as an alif." What al-Farrāʾ said is the analogical rule of the script, because [the script] is based on the pause, and the pause on its nūn is with alif. It is a particle that puts the imperfect in the accusative under conditions that have preceded; but when it occurs after a conjunction it is better to leave it ungoverning. Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them, read it here with it governing, so they omitted the nūn of His words «لا يؤتون». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It does not govern here because of the conjunction, which is the fāʾ; outside the Qur'an it may govern with the fāʾ. What annuls it is not «لا», because the governor passes over «لا»." The apparent sense of this statement at first is that the obstacle is the conjunction; but that is not so — rather the obstacle is the recitation [as transmitted], and that is why he said at the end "outside the Qur'an". The reading of ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: i.e. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās] has preceded.

semin-durr:55-55.t: The pronoun in His words {فَمِنْهُمْ مَّنْ آمَنَ بِهِ} refers back to Ibrāhīm, or to the Qur'an, or to the Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, or to what Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, was given. The majority read «صَدَّ» with fatḥa on the ṣād; Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿIkrima read «صُدَّ» with ḍamma on it; and Abū Rajāʾ and Abū al-Jawzāʾ read it with kasra. Both of these readings are passive, except that the doubled triliteral is like the hollow (weak-middle) one, so three dialectal forms are permissible in its first letter: pure ḍamma, pure kasra, and ishmām (a ḍamma tinged with kasra). «سعيراً» is a tamyīz (specification). If it is in the sense of blazing and burning, a muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. "the blaze of Hell suffices as a blaze", except that its kindling and blazing are not itself [Translator's note: the text here is elliptical]; and if it is in the sense of «مُسْعِر» (blazing fire), no omission is needed.

semin-durr:56-56.t: The majority read {نُصْلِيهِمْ} with ḍamma on the nūn, from «أصلَى»; Ḥumayd with fatḥa on it, from the triliteral «صَلَيْتُ»; and Sallām and Yaʿqūb «نُصْلِيهُم» with ḍamma on the hāʾ, which is the dialect of the Ḥijāz, and its establishment has preceded. His words: {كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتْ}: the discussion of «كلما» has preceded, and that it is an adverbial of time whose governor is «بَدَّلْناهم». The clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the accusative pronoun in «نُصْليهم»; it may also be an adjective of «ناراً», with the referent pronoun omitted, but this is not strong. «وليذوقوا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «بَدَّلناهم».

semin-durr:57-57.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {والذين آمَنُواْ}: there are three views on it. The most apparent: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is «سَنُدْخِلُهم». The second: it is in the position of accusative by conjunction with the noun of «إن», which is «الذين كفروا», the khabar also being «سندخلهم جناتٍ»; this becomes like your saying «إنَّ زيداً قائمٌ وعمراً قاعدٌ» (Zayd is standing and ʿAmr sitting), where you conjoined the accusative to the accusative and the nominative to the nominative. The third: it is in the position of nominative by conjunction with the position of the noun of «إنَّ», because its position is nominative; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this. It is questionable in terms of verbal ugliness, in that one would say «والذين آمنوا» is in the position of accusative by conjunction with «الذين كفروا». [Translator's note: so in the source.] He brought the clause of threat emphasised with «إنَّ» to point out the severity of that, and the clause of promise free of it because of its certainty and that there is no denial of it; and He brought in it the particle of postponement (tanfīs) of short duration [i.e. the sīn] to point out the nearness of the promise.
{تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا الأنهار} is in the position of accusative as an adjective of «جنات». Al-Nakhaʿī read «سَيُدْخِلُهم», and likewise «ويُدْخِلُهم ظِلاًّ», with the yāʾ of the third person, referring back to His words {إِنَّ الله كَانَ عَزِيزاً}; the majority read with nūn, referring back to His words {سَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِمْ}. In «خالدين» three views are possible. The first: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the accusative pronoun in «سَنُدْخِلُهم». The second, which Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed: it is a ḥāl from «جنات»; he said: "Because there is a pronoun in it for each of them", meaning that it may be a ḥāl from the object of «سندخلهم», as preceded, or from «جنات», because in the ḥāl there are two pronouns: one latent in «خالدين», referring back to those who believed, and the other made genitive by «في», referring back to «جنات»; so it is valid to make it a ḥāl from each of them because of the existence of the link, which is the pronoun. What he said is obviously questionable from two angles. First: the meaning would become that the gardens are eternal in themselves, because the pronoun in «فيها» refers back to them, as though it were said: "gardens eternal in the gardens themselves". Second: the condition of this plural [in -īn] is rationality, and if that were intended it would have been said «خالدات». The third: it is also an adjective of «جنات». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "According to the opinion of the Kufans", meaning that the adjective has been applied to something other than what it belongs to in meaning, without the pronoun being made overt. This is the doctrine of the Kufans: when [the adjective] is applied to something other than what it belongs to, and confusion is safely avoided, the pronoun need not be made overt, as in this verse. The doctrine of the Basrans is that it must be made overt absolutely, so according to their doctrine it ought to have been said «خالدين هم فيها»; and since it was not said so, that indicates the unsoundness of this view. Its precise treatment has preceded for you.
If you say: then let the first question be likewise, I mean that if you make «خالدين» a ḥāl from «جنات», it would be a ḥāl from it verbally while belonging to something else in meaning, and the pronoun not be made overt according to the opinion of the Kufans, and so Abū al-Baqāʾ's statement would be valid — the answer is that if this were held it would be good, but it does not ward off the rebuttal from Abū al-Baqāʾ, because he restricted the doctrine of the Kufans to the adjective view, not the ḥāl. His words {لَّهُمْ فِيهَآ أَزْوَاجٌ} are a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the position of this clause is either accusative or nominative: accusative either as a ḥāl from «جنات» or from the pronoun in «سندخلهم», or as an adjective of «جنات» after an adjective; and nominative as a khabar after a khabar.

semin-durr:58-58.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَن تُؤدُّواْ}: in the position of accusative, either by dropping the preposition — because its omission is regular with «أنْ» when confusion is safely avoided, because of their length with the ṣila — or because «أَمَر» is transitive to the second object by itself, as in «أمرتك الخير» (I commanded you the good). On the first view, the disagreement about its position applies: is it in the position of accusative or genitive? On the second, it is in the position of accusative only. It has also been read «الأمانةَ».
The apparent view is that His words {أَن تَحْكُمُواْ} are conjoined to «أَنْ تُؤَدُّوا», i.e. "He commands you to render trusts and to judge with justice"; He would thus have separated the conjunction and the conjoined element by the adverbial. This is a disputed question: al-Fārisī held it to be disallowed except in poetry, and others held it permissible absolutely. Let us first refine the point of disagreement, so I say: when the conjunction consists of a single letter, like the wāw and the fāʾ, is it permissible to separate it from what it conjoins by the adverbial and the like, or not? Al-Fārisī held it disallowed, arguing that when it consists of a single letter it is weak, so nothing intervenes between it and what it conjoins except in poetic necessity, as in his words:
1595 - يوماً تَراها كشِبْه أَرْدِيَةِ ال ... عَضْب ويوماً أَدِيمَها نَغِلا
(One day you see her like the likeness of striped cloaks, and another day her skin putrid.)
Its implied form is: "and you see her skin putrid one day", so he separated with «يوماً». Others held it permissible, arguing from His words {رَبَّنَآ آتِنَا فِي الدنيا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الآخرة حَسَنَةً} [al-Baqara: 201], {فَبَشَّرْنَاهَا بِإِسْحَاقَ وَمِن وَرَآءِ إِسْحَاقَ يَعْقُوبَ} [Hūd: 71], {وَجَعَلْنَا مِن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدّاً ومِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدّاً} [Yā Sīn: 9], {الله الذي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سموات وَمِنَ الأرض مِثْلَهُنّ} [al-Ṭalāq: 12], and {أَن تُؤدُّواْ الأمانات. . . . .} the verse.
The holder of this view said: "When the element conjoined to is made genitive by a preposition, that preposition is repeated with the conjoined element, as in «امرُرْ بزيدٍ وغداً بعمروٍ» (pass by Zayd, and tomorrow by ʿAmr)." These pieces of evidence prove nothing. As for «في الدنيا حسنةً وفي الآخرةِ حسنةً» and His words «وجَعَلْنَا من بينِ أيديهم», that is because two things were conjoined to two things: «الآخرة» was conjoined to «الدنيا» with repetition of the preposition, and the second «حسنةً» was conjoined to the first «حسنةً»; likewise «مِنْ خلفهم» was conjoined to «من بين», and «سداً» to «سداً». Likewise in the verse, «أَدِيمَها» was conjoined to the first object of «تَراها», and «نَغِلا» to the second, which is «كشِبْه», and the second «يوماً» to the first «يوماً»; so there is no separation in it. It may then be said: Abū ʿAlī ought to disallow it absolutely and not except poetic necessity, since what he cited as evidence is interpreted as I mentioned. If it is said: Abū ʿAlī did not make it of that type only because it would lead to the second adverbial being restricted by what occurred in the first, namely that you see her like striped cloaks on the first day and the second, because the rule for the conjoined element is the rule for what it is conjoined to — it is like your saying «ضربت زيداً يوم الجمعة ويوم السبت» (I struck Zayd on Friday and Saturday), where Saturday is restricted by the striking of Zayd as Friday is restricted by it; but the intent is that the second day in the verse is restricted by another restriction, namely seeing her skin putrid — the answer is: if we were left with the apparent sense, without the second adverbial being restricted by another meaning, the rule would be as you mentioned, because it is the apparent sense, as you mentioned in your example «ضربت زيداً يوم الجمعة ويوم السبت»; but when you restrict it by something else, that apparent sense is abandoned for this explicit statement. Do you not see that you say «ضربت زيداً يوم الجمعة وعمراً يوم السبت» (I struck Zayd on Friday and ʿAmr on Saturday)? So too this; and it is a point that needs reflection.
As for «فبشَّرناها بإسحاق», «يعقوب» is not genitive by conjunction with «إسحاق»; rather it is accusative through an implied verb, i.e. "and We granted [Translator's note: printed «ووهبا»; read «ووهبنا»] her Yaʿqūb". This is indicated by the reading in the nominative, for it signals its being cut off from the good tidings. How [could it be otherwise], when it has preceded that this proponent says that whenever the element conjoined to is genitive, the preposition is repeated with the conjoined element? As for {أَن تُؤدُّواْ الأمانات}, there is no evidence in it either, because «إذا» is an adverbial that must have a governor, and its governor is either «أَنْ تَحْكُموا» — which is the apparent one in terms of meaning — or «يأمُركم». The first is impossible, even though the meaning is based on it, because what is in the domain of the relative [particle] does not precede it according to the Basrans; the Kufans, however, allow that, and the verse is an instance of it according to them. They argued from his words:
4596 [Translator's note: so printed; in sequence this is verse 1596] - كان جَزائي بالعصا أَنْ أُجْلَدا
(My reward was that I be beaten with the stick.)
And that has occurred with the explicit object, in his words:
1597 -. . . . . . . . . . . . ... وشفاءُ غَيِّك خابراً أَنْ تَسْألي
(… and the cure of your error, as one informed, is that you ask.)
So how much more the adverbial and the like? The second is also impossible, because the command does not occur at the time of judging; so said al-Shaykh, and this is questionable. Since these two are invalid, its governor is implied, explained by what follows it, its implied form being: "and that you judge, when you judge, [that you judge…]", the latter «أن تحكموا» indicating the former.
His words: {بالعدل}: two views are possible on it. The first: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تحكموا», the bāʾ being transitivising. The second: it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «تَحْكُموا», the bāʾ being for accompaniment, i.e. "clothed with justice, accompanied by it". The two meanings entail each other.
His words: {إِنَّ الله نِعِمَّا يَعِظُكُمْ بِهِ}: the discussion of «ما» attached to «نعم» and «بئس», and what people have said about it, has preceded, so refer back to it. However, Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted something here that is not far from a slip, so it must be mentioned. He said: "The «ما» appended to «نِعْم» is only the preparatory [particle] for the verb's connection to it, as it is in «ربما», and «مِمَّا» in the saying 'and the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, was among those who [i.e. would often] move his lips', and as in his words:
1598 - وإنَّا لَمِمَّا نضربُ الكبشَ ضربةً ... على رأسِه تُلْقي اللسانَ من الفم
(And we are of those who strike the ram [i.e. the chief] a blow on his head that casts the tongue out of the mouth.)
In this it is in the position of «ربما», though it differs from it in meaning, because «ربما» is for paucity and «مِمَّا» for multiplicity. And while «ما» is a preparatory particle, it is in the sense of «الذي»; it only prepared while being a noun, but the intent is only for the meaning in the verb that follows it." Al-Shaykh said: "This is self-contradictory, because insofar as he made it a preparatory particle it is not a noun, and insofar as he made it in the sense of «الذي» it must be a noun; so the two clash."

semin-durr:12-12.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِن كَانَ رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ كَلاَلَةً}: this verse is one about which the discussion ought to be lengthened, because of its difficulty and the confusion of people's views about it. Before touching on the i'rab, one must mention the meaning of al-kalāla, its derivation and people's disagreement about it; then we shall return after that to its i'rab, because that depends on what we have mentioned. So we say, and with Allah is the help:

There is disagreement about the meaning of al-kalāla. The majority of lexicographers and others said: it is the deceased who has neither child nor parent. It was also said: the one who has no parent only. And it was said: the one who has no child only. And it was said: it is one who is inherited by neither father nor mother. On all these views al-kalāla applies to the deceased. It was also said: al-kalāla is the heirs other than the parents and the child; Quṭrub said this. They were called that because, when the deceased's two ends are gone, the heirs encircle him (takallalahu), i.e., they surround him on all sides. This view is supported by the fact that the verse was revealed concerning Jābir, and on the day it was revealed he had neither father nor son. It was also said: al-kalāla is the inherited property. It was said: al-kalāla is kinship. And it was said: it is inheritance. So it is summarised from the above that it is either the inherited deceased, or the heir, or the inherited property, or the inheritance, or kinship.

As for its derivation, it was said: it is derived from «تَكَلَّله الشيء», i.e., the thing surrounded it. That is because when he leaves neither child nor parent, his two ends — the two pillars of his lineage — are cut off, and his inherited property remains for those whose lineage surrounds him, i.e., encircles him like a crown (iklīl). From this comes «الروضة المُكَلَّلة» (the garden crowned), i.e., with flowers. On this is the statement of al-Farazdaq:

1554 - وَرِثْتُمْ قناةَ المجدِ لا عن كَلالةِ ... عن ابنَيْ منافٍ عبدِ شمس وهاشمِ
(You inherited the spear-shaft of glory, not through distant kinship, from the two sons of Manāf, ʿAbd Shams and Hāshim.)

It was also said: its derivation is from al-kalāl, which is exhaustion, as if the inheritance came to the heir after exhaustion. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-kalāla is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of al-kalāl, which is the departure of strength from exhaustion. Al-Aʿshā said:

1555 - فآليْتُ لا أَرْثي لها مِنْ كَلالةٍ ... ولا مِنْ وَحَىً حتى تُلاقِي مُحَمَّدا
(I swore I would not pity her [my camel] for weariness, nor for sore feet, until she meets Muḥammad.)

So it was borrowed for kinship other than through child and parent, because, compared with their kinship, it is as if it were weary and weak." He also allowed it to be an adjective on the pattern faʿāla, saying: "Like al-hajāja and al-faqāqa, for the fool."

When this is established, let us return to the i'rab. We say, and help is with Allah: «كان» admits two views. First: it is incomplete (nāqiṣa), and «رجلٌ» is its ism. For the khabar (predicate) there are two possibilities. First: it is «كلالة», if it is said that it means the deceased; and if it is said that it means the heir or something else, you assume an elided muḍāf, i.e., "one with kalāla." «يُورثُ» is then in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «رجل». It is a passive verb, originally transitive to two objects: the first, the pronoun of the man, was made to take the place of the fāʿil (agent), and the second is omitted, the implied form being "he is inherited from, [in respect of] his property."

Is this verb from three-letter «وَرِث» or four-letter «أورث»? There is disagreement about it. However, al-Zamakhsharī, when he took it from the three-letter verb, made it transitive to the first of the two objects with «مِنْ», for he said: "«يُوْرَثُ» is from «ورث», i.e., 'he is inherited from (yūrathu minhu)'," meaning that it is originally transitive with «مِنْ», which may be dropped: you say «وَرِثْتُ زيداً مالَه» (I inherited Zayd his property), i.e., from Zayd. And when he took it from «أورث», he made the man an heir, not one inherited from, for he said: "If you say: if you take «يورَث» as a passive of «أورث», what is its sense? I say: the man is then the heir, not the one inherited from." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "It is from four-letter «أورث», in the passive," and did not restrict it with the meaning with which al-Zamakhsharī restricted it.

The second possibility: the khabar is the sentence «يُورَث». The accusative of «كلالة» then has four views. First: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يُورَث», if by it is meant the deceased or the heir; however, in taking it in the sense of the heir, it needs the assumption of a muḍāf, i.e., "he is inherited from, being one with kalāla"; because al-kalāla is then not the pronoun latent in «يُورث» itself. Abū al-Baqāʾ said, taking it in the sense of the deceased: "Had «كلالةٌ» been read in the nominative, as an adjective or as a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in «يُورث», it would have been permissible; but I know of no one who read it so, so it must not be read except as it has been transmitted." By its being an adjective he means that it is an adjective of «رجل».

Second: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), if it is said to mean kinship, i.e., "he is inherited from on account of kalāla." Third: it is a second object of «يورث», if it is said to mean the inherited property. Fourth: it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, if it is said to mean inheritance, i.e., "he is inherited from with a kalāla inheritance." Makkī assumed in this view an elided muḍāf, saying: "Its implied form is 'one possessing kalāla'." Some, taking it in the sense of inheritance, allowed it to be a ḥāl.

The second of the two views about «كان»: it is complete (tāmma), so the nominative suffices, i.e., "and if a man exists"; «يُورَثُ» is in the position of the nominative as an adjective of «رجل», and «كلالة» is accusative according to what was mentioned — ḥāl, object of purpose, direct object, or adjective of an omitted maṣdar — according to the meanings established for it. Specific to this view is another one mentioned by Makkī, namely that «كلالة» is accusative as an explanation (tafsīr). Makkī said: "«كان», i.e., occurred; «يورث» is an adjective of the man; «رجل» is nominative through «كان»; and «كلالة» is accusative as an explanation. It was also said: it is accusative as a ḥāl, on the view that al-kalāla is the deceased, in both these views." In making it an explanation, i.e., a tamyīz (specification), there is something to consider which is not hidden.

The majority read «يُورَثُ» as a passive, and its explanation has been given.

Al-Ḥasan read «يُورِثُ» as active, and the same is transmitted from him and from Abū Rajāʾ, except that the two of them doubled the rāʾ. The explanation of the two readings is clear from what has been said. That is: if by al-kalāla the deceased is meant, the two objects are omitted and «كلالةً» is accusative as a ḥāl, i.e., "and if a man bequeaths to his heir or his family his property while being kalāla." If kinship is meant by it, it is accusative as an object of purpose, and the two objects are again omitted, as established above. If the property is meant by it, it is a second object and the first is omitted, i.e., "he bequeaths [as inheritance] to his family his property." If the heir is meant by it, then it is the reverse, i.e., "he bequeaths his property to his family."

His words: {أَو امرأة} are conjoined to «رجلٌ», and what is stated in the word it is conjoined to was omitted from it because it is indicated; the implied form is "or a woman who is inherited from as kalāla." Even though restricting the word conjoined to does not entail restricting the conjoined word, nor the reverse, this is the apparent sense.

His words: {وَلَهُ أَخٌ}: a sentence of mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; the wāw before it is the wāw of the ḥāl. The one described by the ḥāl is either «رجل», if «يورَثُ» is its adjective, or the pronoun latent in «يورَث». The pronoun in His words «وله» is singular because the conjunction is with «أو»; whatever came contrary to that is interpreted by the majority, as in His words {إِن يَكُنْ غَنِيّاً أَوْ فَقَيراً فالله أولى بِهِمَا} [al-Nisāʾ: 135]. It was brought as masculine only because, when two words conjoined with «أو» precede, a masculine and a feminine, you have the choice of regarding the earlier or the later, so you say «زيدٌ أو هند قام» (Zayd or Hind stood [masc.]), or, if you wish, «قامت» [fem.]. Abū al-Baqāʾ answered regarding its masculine with three views. First: it refers back to the man, who is masculine and mentioned first. Second: it refers back to "one of the two," and the word «أحد» is masculine singular. Third: it refers back to the deceased or the one inherited from, because what indicates it precedes.

As for the pronoun in His words {فَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِّنْهُمَا}, there are two views about it. First: it refers back to the brother and the sister. Second: it refers back to the man and to his brother or sister, if by the man in His words {وَإِن كَانَ رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ} it is meant that he is an heir and not one inherited from, as related above from al-Zamakhsharī. Al-Zamakhsharī said, after what we related from him: "If you say: to whom then does the pronoun in His words {فَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِّنْهُمَا} refer? I say: to the man and to his brother or sister; and on the first view, to the two of them [the brother and sister]. If you say: if the pronoun refers to the two of them, it conveys their equality in taking the sixth without preference of male over female; does this benefit remain on this view? I say: yes, because when you say 'the sixth is his, or for one of the brother or sister,' by way of alternative, you have made male and female equal." End of quote.

Ubayy read: «أخ أو أخت من الأم» (a brother or a sister from the mother).

Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ read «من أم» without the definite article. People are agreed that what is meant by the brother and sister is from the mother, in accordance with the reading of the two of them, and because what is at the end of the sūra indicates that, namely that the sister has a half, the two sisters two thirds, and for siblings male and female the male has the like of the share of two females.

His words: {فَإِن كانوا}: the wāw is the pronoun of the siblings from the mother indicated by His words {أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ}, and males and females are meant. He brought the masculine pronoun in His words «كانوا» and «فهم» by giving predominance (taghlīb) to the masculine over the feminine. «ذلك» points to the one, i.e., more than the one, meaning: if those who inherit exceed one; because one cannot validly say "this is more than one" except in this sense, since the meanings of "many" and "one" are incompatible; otherwise, there is no multiplicity in one.

His words: {مِن بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يوصى}: the i'rab of this has been given above, and this is like it.

His words: {غَيْرَ مُضَآرٍّ}: «غيرَ» is accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil in «يوصَى», which is a pronoun referring back to the man in His words {وَإِن كَانَ رَجُلٌ}; this is if by the man the one inherited from is meant. If the heir is meant, as mentioned above, it refers back to the deceased inherited from, who is indicated by the heir by way of implication, just as He indicated him in His words {فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثَا مَا تَرَكَ}, i.e., what the one inherited from left; so the implied form becomes "which the one inherited from bequeaths." Thus people — al-Zamakhsharī and others — parsed it, making it a ḥāl.

However, the Shaykh rejected that on the grounds that it leads to separating this ḥāl from its governor by something foreign to both. That is because its governor is «يوصَى», as established, and His words {أَوْ دَيْنٍ} are foreign, since they are conjoined to «وصية», which is described by the governor of the ḥāl. He said: "Had it been according to the i'rab they gave, the construction would have been «مِنْ بعد وصيةٍ يُوصَى بها غيرَ مُضارٍّ أو دينٍ». This reason is an obstacle in both readings — I mean the verb as active or passive — and the reading with the passive adds another reason, namely that the one described by the ḥāl is not mentioned, because it is originally a fāʿil which was dropped and the object put in its place. Do you not see that if you said «تُرْسَلُ الرياح مبشِّراً بها» (the winds are sent, [He] bringing good tidings by them), with kasra on the shīn, meaning 'Allah sends the winds, bringing good tidings by them,' having dropped the fāʿil, put the object in its place and brought a ḥāl from the fāʿil, it would not be permissible; so too this." Then he explained it in one of two ways: either by a verb indicated by the meaning of what precedes, being general for the sense of what has power over the property by bequest or debt, its implied form being "he binds that on his property," or "he makes it obligatory in it, not causing harm to his heirs by that binding or making obligatory"; or by an active verb, because the passive indicates it, i.e., "he bequeaths, not causing harm." It then becomes parallel to His words {يُسَبَّحُ لَهُ فِيهَا بالغدو والآصال رِجَالٌ} [al-Nūr: 36-37] in the reading of whoever gives fatḥa to the bāʾ.

His words: {وَصِيَّةً}: in its accusative there are four views. First: it is an emphatic maṣdar, i.e., "Allah enjoins you with that as an injunction." Second: it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, its governor being «يُوصيكم»; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. Third: it is accusative by "going out" (al-khurūj), either from His words {فَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِّنْهُمَا السدس} or from His words {فَهُمْ شُرَكَآءُ فِي الثلث}; this is a formulation resembling the formulation of the Kufans. Fourth: it is accusative through the active participle, namely «مُضارّ». Harm does not fall upon the injunction but upon the heirs; but since Allah the Exalted made an injunction about the heirs, He made the harm falling upon them as if it fell upon the injunction itself, by way of hyperbole. This explanation is supported by the reading of al-Ḥasan: «غيرَ مُضارِّ وصيةٍ», with the active participle in genitive construct with it, according to the figurative usage we mentioned. It becomes parallel to their saying «يا سارقَ الليلةِ» (O thief of the night), the implied form being "O one who steals in the night"; but he put the active participle in construct with its adverb, figuratively and by extension of usage. So too this: its underlying form is "not causing harm in an injunction from Allah," and usage was extended in this until it was made transitive by itself without an intermediary, for the purpose of hyperbole I mentioned to you.

This is a better explanation than that of Abū al-Baqāʾ, for he mentioned two views in explaining al-Ḥasan's reading. First: it is on the elision of «أهل» or «ذي», i.e., "not causing harm to the people of the bequest" or "to the one with the bequest." Second: on the elision of "time," i.e., "the time of the bequest." He said: "It is a case of putting an adjective in construct with a time. Close to that is their saying «هو فارسُ حربٍ» (he is a horseman of war), i.e., a horseman in war; and you say «هو فارسُ زمانه» (he is the horseman of his age), i.e., in his age. So too the implied form of the reading: not causing harm at the time of the bequest."

The object of «مُضارّ» is omitted if «وصيةً» is not made its object, i.e., "not causing harm to his heirs by a bequest."

semin-durr:59-59.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِنْكُمْ}: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أُولي الأمر», so it is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "and those in authority, being from among you"; «مِنْ» is partitive. His words «إنْ كنتم» are a protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) whose apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted according to the majority of the Basrans, i.e. "then refer it to Allah"; according to others it precedes. «تأويلاً» is accusative as a tamyīz (specification).

semin-durr:60-60.t:
{يَزْعُمُونَ}: like «ظنَّ» and its sisters, on condition that it is not in the sense of "to guarantee", "to lie", "to grow fat" or "to grow lean"; «أنَّ» fills the place of its two objects. The majority read «أُنْزل إليك وما أُنْزل من قبلك» as passives, and they have been read as actives, the agent being Allah the Exalted. Al-zaʿm — with fatḥa, ḍamma and kasra on the zāy — is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «زَعَم»; it is speech accompanied by a conjectural belief. The poet said:
1599 - فإنْ تَزْعُميني كنتُ أجهلُ فيكُمُ ... فإني شَرَيْتُ الحِلْمَ بعدَك بالجَهْل
(If you claim that I used to be foolish among you, I have since bought forbearance in exchange for folly.)
Ibn Durayd said: "It is mostly applied to what is false." The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "What a bad mount for a man is 'they claimed'." Al-Aʿshā said:
1600 - ونُبِّئْتُ قيساً ولم أَبْلُه ... كما زعموا خيرَ أهلِ اليمنْ
(I was told — and I had not tested him — that Qays, as they claimed, was the best of the people of Yemen.)
The one praised said: "It is nothing but a claim", and denied him and gave him nothing. [The author of «al-ʿAyn» mentioned that it mostly applies to «أنَّ»; he said: "It may occur in poetry applied to a noun", and he cited the verse of Abū Dhuʾayb, and the words of another:]
1601 - زَعَمَتْني شيخاً ولستُ بشيخٍ ... إنما الشيخُ مَنْ يَدِبُّ دبيباً
(She claimed me an old man, and I am not an old man; the old man is only he who creeps along.)
«زعم» may be in the sense of «ظَنَّ», and is then transitive to two objects; in the sense of «كفِل» (to guarantee), and is then transitive to one, and from that is {وَأَنَاْ بِهِ زَعِيمٌ} [Yūsuf: 72]; and in the sense of «رَأس» (to be chief) and in the sense of «سَمِن» (to grow fat) and «هَزَل» (to grow lean), and it is then intransitive.
His words: {يُرِيدُونَ} is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يَزْعُمون» or from «الذين يزعمون». His words {وَقَدْ أمروا} are a ḥāl from the agent of «يريدون», so they are two overlapping ḥāls. «أن يكفروا» is in the position of accusative only, if you assume that «أمر» is transitive to the second object by itself; otherwise the well-known disagreement applies to it. The pronoun in «به» refers back to al-ṭāghūt; it has preceded that it is masculine and feminine, and what people said about it in al-Baqara. ʿAbbās ibn al-Faḍl read «ان يكفُروا بهنَّ» with the feminine plural pronoun.
His words: {أَن يُضِلَّهُمْ ضَلاَلاً}: on «ضلالاً» there are three views. The first: it is a maṣdar not on the form of the verb [Translator's note: printed «الصدر»; read «المصدر» or «الصدر» as "the verb's form"], like {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17] [Translator's note: the source prints «نوح: 3»]; the original being «إضلال» and «إنبات», so it is a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar), not a maṣdar. The second: it is the maṣdar of the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of «أَضلَّ», i.e. "He led them astray, so they strayed a straying". The third: it is a case of putting one of two maṣdars in the place of the other. The discussion of «تعالوا» in Āl ʿImrān, what people said about it, and the reading of al-Ḥasan and its justification have preceded, so turn your attention to that.

semin-durr:61-61.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {رَأَيْتَ}: there are two views on it. The first: it is from visual seeing, i.e. openly and explicitly. The second: it is from mental seeing, i.e. "you knew". So «يصدُّون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) on the first view, and in the position of the second object on the second. On «صدوداً» there are two views. The first: it is a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar), the maṣdar being only «الصدّ»; this is the choice [Translator's note: printed «اختبار»; read «اختيار»] of Ibn ʿAṭiyya, and Makkī attributed it to al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad. The second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in itself; one says «صد صَدًّاً وصُدوداً». Some said: "«الصُّدود» is the maṣdar of intransitive «صَدَّ», and «الصَّدُّ» the maṣdar of transitive «صد», as in {فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ السبيل} [al-Naml: 24]; the verb here is transitive by the preposition, not by itself, so its maṣdar came on «فُعُول», because fuʿūl is mostly for the intransitive." This is questionable, since someone may say: it is transitive here, the most that can be said being that the object has been omitted, i.e. "they turn others away — or those seeking judgement before you — a turning away". As for fuʿūl, it has come [Translator's note: printed «فاء»; read «فجاء»] in the transitive, as in «لزمه لُزوماً» and «فتنة فُتوناً».

semin-durr:62-62.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَكَيْفَ}: two views are possible on «كيف». The first: it is in the position of accusative; this is the view of al-Zajjāj, who said: "Its implied form is: so how do you see them?" The second: it is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "so how will their doing be at the time when the calamity befalls them?"; «إذا» is governed by that element implied after «كيف». The bāʾ in «بما» is causal, and «ما» may be maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming) or nominal, in which case the referent pronoun is omitted. His words: {يَحْلِفُونَ} is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «جاؤوك». «إنْ» is negative, i.e. "we did not intend", and «إحسانا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) or an excepted element, according to the two views on the question.

semin-durr:63-63.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {في أَنْفُسِهِمْ}: there are several views on it. The most sound: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قل», and there are two meanings in it. The first: "speak to them in private, with no one else with them", because that is more conducive to the acceptance of advice. The second: "speak to them concerning their souls that harbour hypocrisy, words that reach in them what will restrain them from returning to hypocrisy". The second view: it is attached to «بليغاً», i.e. "words that affect their hearts, by which they are greatly distressed and which they deeply feel"; al-Zamakhsharī stated its meaning. Al-Shaykh rebutted him on the ground that this is the doctrine of the Kufans, since it involves placing the dependent of an adjective before the qualified noun: if you said «جاء زيداً رجلٌ يضربُ» (a man came striking Zayd), it would not be allowed according to the Basrans, because the dependent precedes only where the governor may precede, and here the governor may not precede, because the adjective does not precede the qualified noun; while the Kufans allow the dependent of the adjective to precede the qualified noun. As for the Basrans' saying that the dependent precedes only where the governor precedes, it is open to discussion: we have found this rule broken in His words {فَأَمَّا اليتيم فَلاَ تَقْهَرْ وَأَمَّا السآئل فَلاَ تَنْهَرْ} [al-Ḍuḥā: 9-10], for «اليتيم» is governed by «تقهر» and «السائل» by «تنهر», and they precede the prohibitive «لا», while their governor may not be placed before it, since the jussive verb does not precede what makes it jussive; so the dependent has preceded where the governor does not precede. Likewise what they said about his words:
1602 - قنافِذُ هَدَّاجون حولَ بيوتِهم ... بما كان إيَّاها عطيَّةُ عَوَّدا
(Hedgehogs creeping about their houses [at night], because of what ʿAṭiyya accustomed them to.)
They explained this verse on the basis that in «كان» there is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), «عَطِيَّةُ» being a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «عَوَّدَ» its khabar (predicate), so that the dependent of its khabar — which is neither an adverbial nor the like — does not follow «كان» directly. This obliged them to place the dependent, which is «إياهم» [Translator's note: so here; the verse has «إيَّاها»], before where the governor does not precede, because when the khabar is a verb governing a latent pronoun in the nominative, its placement before the mubtadaʾ is disallowed lest it be confused with the agent, as in «زيد ضرب عمراً». The original source of this discussion is the placing of the khabar of «ليس» before it, which the majority allowed because of the words of Allah the Exalted {أَلاَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمْ لَيْسَ مَصْرُوفاً عَنْهُمْ} [Hūd: 8]; the point of evidence is that «يوم» is governed by «مصروفاً» and has preceded «ليس», and the precedence of the dependent signals the [possible] precedence of the governor. They were then countered with what I have mentioned to you. There is scope for examination in this discussion that this is not the place for; I have treated it thoroughly in my book «al-Sharḥ al-Kabīr: Sharḥ Tashīl al-Fawāʾid», so refer to it. The third: it has been transmitted from Mujāhid — and I do not think it is authentic from him — that it is attached to «مصيبة», so it is a case of advancing and postponing [word order]; the Qur'an is to be kept free of that, and I have only mentioned it to point out its weakness.

semin-durr:64-64.t:
