The words of Allah the Exalted: {لِيُطَاعَ}: this is the lām of purpose (lām kay), and the verb after it is accusative through an implied «أن». This is an emptied (mufarragh) exception from the mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), the implied form being: "We did not send any messenger for anything at all except for obedience". On «وبإذن الله» there are three views. The first: [it is] attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يُطاع», the bāʾ being causal; Abū al-Baqāʾ took this view, and he said: "It has also been said: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. by reason of Allah's command." The second: it is attached to «أرسلنا», i.e. "We did not send [him except] by Allah's command", i.e. with His law. The third: it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يطاعَ»; Abū al-Baqāʾ began with this. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "On both attachments — i.e. its attachment to «يُطاعَ» or to «أَرْسلنا» — the speech is general in wording and specific in meaning, because we know for certain that Allah the Exalted willed from some of them that they not obey him; for that reason some interpreted the permission (idhn) as knowledge, and some as guidance." Al-Shaykh said: "There is no need for that, because his saying 'general in wording' is not granted: «يُطاع» is passive, so that omitted agent is assumed to be specific, its implied form being: 'except that he be obeyed by those whose obedience Allah willed'."
His words: {وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ}: the discussion of «أنَّ» occurring after «لو» has preceded. «إذ» is an adverbial governed by the khabar (predicate) of «أنَّ», which is «جاؤوك». He said {واستغفر لَهُمُ الرسول} and did not say «واستغفرت» (and you sought forgiveness), shifting from the second person to the third, because of the honour and exaltation by the attribute of messengership that this overt noun contains. «وجَد» here may be the cognitive one, in which case it is transitive to two objects, the second being «تواباً»; or it may be non-cognitive, in which case it is transitive to one object and «تواباً» is a ḥāl. As for «رحيماً», it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun of «تَوَّاباً», or a badal (substitute) from «تواباً»; or it may originally be a second khabar, based on the multiplicity of the khabar, which is correct; then when the abrogating word (nāsikh) came in, the multiple khabar was put in the accusative. You say «زيدٌ فاضلٌ شاعرٌ فقيه عالم» (Zayd is excellent, a poet, a jurist, learned), then you say «علمتُ زيدا فاضلاً شاعراً فقيهاً عالماً» (I knew Zayd to be excellent, a poet, a jurist, learned); however, it is not good to say here: "«شاعراً» is a third object, «فقيهاً» a fourth, and «عالماً» a fifth".

semin-durr:13-13.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {يُدْخِلْهُ}: He went by the wording of «مَنْ» and so made the pronoun singular in His words «يُطِعْ» and «يُدْخِلْه», and by its meaning and so made it plural in His words «خالدين». This is the better of the two ways of construing — I mean construing by the wording and then by the meaning. The reverse is permissible, even though Ibn ʿAṭiyya forbade it; [his view] is of no account, because it is established from the Arabs. This has been mentioned more than once; there is detail to it, and it has conditions mentioned in the books of grammar.

In the accusative of «خالدين» there are two views. The more evident: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the accusative pronoun in «يُدْخِلُه». The mismatch between the ḥāl and the one it describes — in that it is plural while the one it describes is singular — does no harm, because of the regard for wording and meaning mentioned above. It is an anticipated ḥāl (muqaddara), because the eternal abiding comes after the entering.

Second: it is a naʿt (adjective) of «جنات», of the type that runs on its described noun in wording while belonging to something else in meaning, as in «مررت برجلٍ قائمةٍ أمه» (I passed by a man whose mother was standing) and «بامرأة حسنٍ غلامُها» (by a woman whose servant-boy was handsome): «قائمة» and «حسنٍ», although they run on what precedes them in wording, belong in meaning to what follows them. Al-Zajjāj allowed that in the noble verse, and al-Tibrīzī followed him. However, when an adjective runs on someone other than the one it belongs to, the pronoun must be made overt without restriction on the doctrine of the Basrans, whether it causes ambiguity or not. The Kufans, however, distinguish, saying: when the adjective runs on someone other than the one it belongs to, if it causes ambiguity the pronoun must be made overt, as is the doctrine of the Basrans, as in «زيدٌ عمروٌ ضاربُه هو» (Zayd — ʿAmr is the one he [Zayd] strikes), when the striking is done by Zayd to ʿAmr; and if it does not cause ambiguity, making it overt is not required, as in «زيدٌ هندٌ ضاربُها» (Zayd — Hind is the one he strikes). When this is established, al-Zajjāj's doctrine on the verse works only on the opinion of the Kufans, and it is a good doctrine.

Those who supported the doctrine of the Kufans argued from what is heard (samāʿ). Among it is the reading of whoever read {إلى طَعَامٍ غَيْرِ نَاظِرِينَ إِنَاهُ} [al-Aḥzāb: 53] with «غير» in the genitive, without the pronoun being made overt; had he made it overt, he would have said «غيرِ ناظرين إناه أنتم». And among it is the words of the other:

1556 - قَوْمي ذُرا المجدِ بانُوها وقد عَلِمَتْ ... بكُنْهِ ذلك عدنانٌ وقَحْطانُ
(My people — the summits of glory, they are their builders; and ʿAdnān and Qaḥṭān know the truth of that.)

He did not say «بانُوها هم». Some explained the verse as an elided mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being «هم بانوها»: so «قومي» is a first mubtadaʾ, «ذرا» a second mubtadaʾ, «هم» a third mubtadaʾ, «بانوها» the khabar (predicate) of the third; the third with its khabar is the khabar of the second, and the second with its khabar is the khabar of the first.

Al-Zamakhsharī rejected «خالدين» and «خالداً» being adjectives of «جنات» and «ناراً», because the pronoun is not overt. He said: "If you say: may they be adjectives of «جنات» and «ناراً»? I say [Translator's note: the text has «قتل», a misprint for «قلت»]: no, because they run on something other than the one they belong to, so the pronoun is necessary, in your saying «خالدين هم فيها» and «خالداً هو فيها»."

Abū al-Baqāʾ also rejected that because the pronoun is not overt, but with «خالداً», and he did not address that with «خالدين», though there is no difference between them; then he related its permissibility from the Kufans. This rejection is on the doctrine of the Basrans, as mentioned above.

Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read here «نُدْخِلْه» in both places, and in Sūrat al-Taghābun, al-Ṭalāq and al-Fatḥ, with the nūn of majesty; the rest with the yāʾ, the pronoun being for Allah the Exalted. «خالدين» was made plural only for the obedient, and «خالداً» singular for the disobedient. They said: because the people of obedience are the people of intercession, so since they enter together with those for whom intercession is made, the plural suited that; while the disobedient one brings no one else into the Fire with him, so the singular suited that.

The sentence formed by His words {تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا الأنهار} is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of «جنات». It has been mentioned more than once [that there is a question about] the accusative after «دخل» among adverbs: is its accusative that of adverbs, or that of the mafʿūl bihi (direct object)? The first is the view of the majority, and the second the view of al-Akhfash. So too «جنات» and «ناراً».

semin-durr:15-15.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {واللاتي}: «اللاتي» is the plural of «التي» in meaning, not in form, because these are forms coined for the dual and plural, not true duals or plurals. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«اللاتي» is the plural of «التي», irregularly; and it was said: it is a form coined for the plural." Something like this should not be counted as a disagreement. It has many plurals, thirteen words: «اللاتي», «اللواتي» and «اللائي», and [the same] without the yāʾs — these are six; «اللاي» with the yāʾ without hamza; «اللا» with neither yāʾ nor hamza; «اللَّواء» with the long vowel; «اللَّوا» with the short vowel; and «الأُلى», as in his words:

1557 - فأمَّا الأُلى يَسْكُنَّ غَوْرَ تهامةٍ ... فكلُّ فتاةٍ تترُكُ الحِجْلَ أَفْصَما
(As for those [women] who dwell in the lowland of Tihāma, every girl leaves her anklet broken open.)

— though most often it is the plural of «الذي»; and «اللاءاتِ», with kasra in all cases, or inflected like the sound feminine plural, as in his words:

1558 - أولئك إخواني الذين عَرَفْتُهُمْ ... وأخْدانُك اللاءاتُ زُيِّنَّ بالكَتَمْ
(Those are my brothers whom I have known, and your companions are those [women] who are adorned with katam dye.)

with «اللاءات» in the nominative.

As for the grammatical position of «اللاتي», there are two views. First: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). There are then two views about the khabar (predicate). First: the sentence formed by His words «فاسْتَشْهدوا». The entry of the fāʾ, as redundant (zāʾida), into the khabar is permissible — even though its addition is not permissible in the like of «زيدٌ فاضرِبْ» (Zayd — then strike [him]) in the opinion of the majority — because the mubtadaʾ resembles a condition in being a general relative noun whose ṣila (relative clause) is a future verb, and the khabar is merited by the ṣila.

The second view: the khabar is omitted, the implied form being "among what is recited to you is the ruling of those [women] who…"; so the khabar and the muḍāf of the mubtadaʾ were omitted because they are indicated, and the muḍāf ilayhi was put in its place. This is parallel to what Sībawayh did in the like of {الزانية والزاني فاجلدوا} [al-Nūr: 2] and {السارق والسارقة فاقطعوا} [al-Māʾida: 38], i.e., "among what is recited to you is the ruling of the fornicatress"; and His words «فاستشهِدوا» and «فاجْلدوا» indicate that omitted ruling, because they are an explanation of it.

The second view: its position is accusative, and there are two views about it. First: it is accusative through an implied verb, because the context indicates it, not by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb with a pronoun), for a reason we shall mention; the implied form is "aim at those [women] who commit…" or "intend…". It may not be accusative through an implied verb explained by His words «فاستشهدوا», making the case one of ishtighāl, because this relative noun resembles a conditional noun, as established above, and a conditional noun may not be accusative by ishtighāl, because it is not governed by what precedes it; so if we made it accusative by an implied verb, it would follow that it is governed by what precedes it. This is what some said. Close to it is what Abū al-Baqāʾ said, for he said: "Since it is so" — i.e., its being in the status of a condition — "the accusative is not good, because assuming the verb before the conditional particle is not permissible, and assuming it after the ṣila needs the implication of a verb other than His words «فاستشهدوا», because «استشهدوا» cannot validly put «اللاتي» in the accusative." In his wording there is something to dispute, the mention of which would lengthen the book.

Second: it is accusative by ishtighāl. And their rejection of that on the grounds that it entails its being governed by what precedes it is answered by our assuming the verb after it, not before it. This is a well-known disagreement about conditional and interrogative nouns: does ishtighāl apply to them or not? Some forbade it for the reason mentioned above, and others allowed it, assuming the verb after the conditional and interrogative. Its being accusative by ishtighāl is the apparent sense of Makkī's words, for he mentioned that on His words {واللذان يَأْتِيَانِهَا مِنكُمْ فَآذُوهُمَا} [al-Nisāʾ: 16], and the two verses are of one kind. We must cite his text so that his view becomes clear to you. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "«واللذانِ يأتيانِها»: the preferred option for Sībawayh in «اللذان» is the nominative, even though the meaning of the speech is a command, because when it is connected with a verb [as its ṣila], the meaning of condition becomes established in it, since it does not apply to a specific thing. When the meaning of condition and vagueness became established, it was treated like a condition in that it is not governed by what precedes it, just as a condition is not governed by what precedes it, whether implied or overt." Then he said: "The accusative is permissible by implying a verb, because it only resembles a condition, and what resembles a thing is not like the thing in its ruling." End of quote. And no one may say: "What he means is the accusative by implying a verb of the accusative, not by ishtighāl, but by an indicated verb," as related above from some; because then his giving the reason "because it only resembles a condition…" to the end would have no benefit, since an accusative of that kind does not need this justification.

His words: {مِن نِّسَآئِكُمْ} is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يِأْتِين», so it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted word, i.e., "they commit, being of your women." As for His words «منكم», there are two views about it. First: it is attached to His words «فاستشهدوا». Second: it is attached to an omitted word as an adjective of «أربعة», so it is in the position of the accusative, its implied form being "then call to witness against them four being from among you."

His words: «حتى»: «حتى» is in the sense of «إلى» (until), so the verb after it is accusative by an implied «أن», and it is attached to His words «فأمسكوهن» as its limit. As for His words «أو يجعلَ», there are two views about it. First: «أو» is a conjunction, so the making [of a way] is also a limit for confining them, and «يجعلَ» is accusative by being conjoined to «يتوفَّاهن». Second: «أو» is in the sense of «إلا» (unless), like the one in their saying «لألزَمَنَّك أو تقضيَني حقي» (I will stick to you until / unless you pay me my due), on one of the two meanings; and the verb after it is likewise accusative by an implied «أن», as in his words:

1559 - فَسِرْ في بلادِ اللهِ والتمسِ الغِنَى ... تَعِشْ ذا يَسارٍ أو تموت فَتُعْذَرا
(So travel in Allah's lands and seek wealth: you will live in ease, unless you die and so are excused.)

I.e., unless you die. The difference between this view and the one before it is that the making [of a way] is not a limit for confining them in the houses.

His words: «لهن»: there are two views about it. The more evident: it is attached to «يَجْعَلَ». Second: it is attached to an omitted word, because it is a ḥāl from «سبيل», since it is originally an adjective of an indefinite noun placed before it and so made accusative as a ḥāl. This is if the making is taken in the sense of legislating or creating. If it is taken in the sense of "making into" (taṣyīr), then «لَهُنَّ» is a second object placed before the first, which is «سبيل»; and placing it first here is obligatory, because if the two were resolved into a mubtadaʾ and khabar, placing this khabar first would be obligatory, since it is a prepositional phrase and the mubtadaʾ is an indefinite noun with nothing else to justify it.

semin-durr:125-125.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِمَّنْ أَسْلَمَ} are attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أَحْسَنُ», so this is the «مِنْ» that governs the genitive and introduces the one surpassed in the comparison; and «لله» is attached to «أَسْلَم». Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «وجهه», and there is an evident objection to this. «وهو مُحْسِنٌ» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «أَسْلم». As for «اتَّبع», it may be conjoined to «أسلم», which is the apparent view, or it may be a second ḥāl from the fāʿil of «أسلم» with an implied «قد», according to those who require that. The discussion of {حَنِيفاً} has already preceded in al-Baqara [verse 135], except that here it may also be a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «اتّبع».
His words: {واتخذ الله إِبْرَاهِيمَ خَلِيلاً} — there are two views on it, namely that if we make «اتَّخذ» take two objects, [«خليلاً»] is the second object; otherwise it is a ḥāl. This clause is conjoined to the interrogative clause whose meaning is declarative; it draws attention to the nobility of the one followed and that he is worthy of being followed because Allah chose him for intimate friendship (al-khulla). It is not permissible to conjoin it to what precedes it, because it is not fit to be a ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. Al-Zamakhsharī made it a parenthetical clause; he said: "If you ask: what is the position of this clause? I say: it has no grammatical position, because it is one of the parenthetical clauses, like what comes in poetry in their saying «والحوادثُ جَمَّةٌ» ('and events are many'); its benefit is to emphasise the obligation of following his religion, because one who reached such nearness to Allah that He took him as an intimate friend is worthy of being followed." If he means by "parenthesis" the technical sense, then there is no parenthesis here, since parenthesis comes between two inseparable elements, such as a verb and its fāʿil, a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), a condition and its apodosis, an oath and its answer. If he means something other than that, it is possible; except that his comparing it with their saying «والحوادثُ جَمَّةٌ» suggests the technical parenthesis, for the saying «والحوادث جمة» occurs in two verses, one of which is between a verb and its fāʿil, as in the poet's words:
1656 - وقد أَدْرَكَتْني والحوادثُ جَمَّةٌ ... أَسِنَّةُ قومٍ لا ضعافٍ ولا عُزْلِ
(The spearheads of a people neither weak nor unarmed overtook me — and events are many.)
And the other allows that, on the view that the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the fāʿil, as in his words:
1657 - ألا هل أتاها والحوادثُ جَمَّةٌ ... بأنَّ امرأ القيس بنَ تَمْلِكَ بَيْقَرا
(Has it reached her — and events are many — that Imruʾ al-Qays son of Tamlik has gone wandering abroad?)
It is also possible that the fāʿil is a pronoun indicated by the context, i.e. "Has the news reached her that Imruʾ al-Qays…", so it would be a parenthesis between the verb and what it governs.
And «الخليل» is derived from al-khalla (with fatḥa), which is need; or from al-khulla (with ḍamma), which is pure affection; or from al-khalal (a gap). Thaʿlab said: "He was called khalīl because his affection permeates (tatakhallalu) the heart," and he recited:
1658 - قد تَخَلَّلْتَ مسلكَ الروحِ مني ... وبه سُمِّي الخليلُ خليلا
(You have permeated the passage of the spirit within me — and by this the intimate friend was named khalīl.)
Al-Rāghib said: "Al-khalla — i.e. with fatḥa — is the disturbance (ikhtilāl) that befalls the soul, either through its desire for something or its need of it; that is why al-khalla was explained as need. And al-khulla — i.e. with ḍamma — is affection: either because it permeates the soul, i.e. lies in its midst; or because it pierces (tukhillu) the soul and affects it as the arrow affects the game; or because of the extreme need for it."

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِّن نَّفْسٍ}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خَلَقكم», so it is in the position of the accusative; and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent. Likewise «منها زوجَها» and «بَثَّ منهما». Ibn Abī ʿAbla [read]: «واحدٍ» without the tāʾ, and it has two analyses. The first: regard for the meaning, because what is meant by the soul is Adam, upon him be peace. The second: that نفس is treated as both masculine and feminine; and upon this is:
1524 - ثلاثةُ أنفُسٍ وثلاثُ ذَوْدٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Three persons and three camels …)

His saying: «وخَلَقَ»: there are three analyses in it. The first: it is conjoined to the meaning of «واحدة», because of the meaning of the verb in it, as if it were said: «مِنْ نفسٍ وَحُدتْ» (from a soul that was alone), i.e. was single; one says «وَحُد، يَحِد، وَحْداً وحِدَة» in the sense of being single. The second: it is conjoined to something omitted. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "As if it were said: from a single soul which He brought into being, or originated, and created from it …; it was only omitted because the meaning indicates it. The meaning is: He branched you out from a single soul whose description is this" — with a description that is an explanation and detailing of the manner of their creation from it. What led al-Zamakhsharī and the one who spoke before him to that is only regard for the order of existence, because the creation of Eve, who is expressed by "the mate", was before our creation. There is no need for that, because the wāw does not require order, on the correct view.

The third: it is conjoined to «خَلَقَكم», so it is included within the scope of the ṣila (relative clause), and no heed is paid to the wāw, since it does not require order. However, al-Zamakhsharī restricted this analysis to the address in {ياأيها الناس} being to the contemporaries of the Messenger, upon him be peace, for he said: "The second: that it be conjoined to «خلقكم», and the address is to those to whom the Messenger was sent; and the meaning is: He created you from the soul of Adam, because they are among the totality of the genus branched from him; and He created from it your mother Eve." The apparent sense of this is the restriction of the second analysis to the address being to the contemporaries; and this is open to question. Some implied a muḍāf in «منها», i.e. «مِنْ جنسِها زوجَها» (from its kind its mate); this is according to whoever holds that Eve was not created from Adam, but was only created from clay left over from Adam's clay; and this is a view that is turned away from.

It was read: «وخالِقٌ وباثٌّ», in the form of the active participle. Al-Zamakhsharī analysed it as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. and He is creator and disperser. One says بَثَّ and أَبَثَّ in the sense of «فَرَّق» (to disperse), as triliteral and quadriliteral.

His saying: {كَثِيراً}: there are two analyses in it. The more evident of them: it is a naʿt (adjective) of «رجالاً». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "He did not make it feminine, treating it according to the meaning, because «رجالاً» is a number, a genus or a plural, just as He made masculine the verb attributed to a feminine group, as in His saying {وَقَالَ نِسْوَةٌ} [Yūsuf: 30]."

The second: it is a naʿt of a maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: and He dispersed from them a great dispersing. It has preceded that Sībawayh's view in the like of it is the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). If it is said: why did He single out the men for the description of multitude and not the women? There are two answers. The first: He deleted their [the women's] description because what precedes it indicates it, [i.e.]: and many women. [Translator's note: the bracketed «[أي]» is in the printed source.]

The second: that the men, because of their prominence, are suited to that, unlike the women, for what is more fitting for them is obscurity and concealment.

His saying: {تَسَآءَلُونَ}: the Kufans read: «تَساءلون» with the sīn lightened, on the deletion of one of the two tāʾs for lightness, the original being «تَتَساءلون»; the disagreement whether the deleted one is the first or the second has preceded for us. The rest read with doubling, on the assimilation of the tāʾ of tafāʿul into the sīn, because it is close to it in voicelessness (hams); hence it is substituted for the sīn: they said «ست» (six), the original being «سِدْسٌ».

ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read: «تَسْأَلون», from the triliteral سأل. And it was read «تَسَلون», by transferring the vowel of the hamza to the sīn.

«تَساءلون», on [the pattern of] tafāʿul, has two analyses. The first: participation in asking. The second: it is in the sense of faʿala, and the reading of ʿAbd Allāh indicates it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The preposition entered on the object because the meaning is: you swear to one another." He means: the original was to make «تسألون» transitive to the pronoun by itself; but when it was made to imply the meaning of «تتحالفون», it was made transitive as that is.

His saying: {والأرحام}: the majority read the mīm of «والأرحام» in the accusative, and there are two analyses in it. The first: it is conjoined to the Majestic Name, i.e. and fear [Allah regarding] the wombs (ties of kinship), i.e. do not sever them. Some implied a muḍāf, i.e. the severing of the wombs. And it is said: "This is in reality of conjoining the specific to the general; that is because the meaning of 'fear Allah' is 'fear opposing Him', and severing the ties of kinship is included in it." The second: it is conjoined to the position of the genitive in «به», as in «مررت بزيد وعمراً» (I passed by Zayd and ʿAmr): since it could not share with it in following on the wording, it followed on the position. This is supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «وبالأرحام». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "[i.e.] you venerate Him and the wombs, because swearing by Him is venerating Him."

Ḥamza read «والأرحامِ» in the genitive, and there are two views of it. The first: it is conjoined to the genitive pronoun in «به» without repeating the preposition. The Basrans do not permit this; the verification of the discussion of this question has preceded, [namely] that there are three schools on it, and the argumentation of each party, at His saying, the Exalted: {وَكُفْرٌ بِهِ والمسجد} [al-Baqara: 217].

A group attacked this reading, such as al-Zajjāj and others; so much so that it is related of al-Farrāʾ, whose view is that this is permissible, that he said: "Sharīk ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to me from al-Aʿmash from Ibrāhīm that he said: «والأرحامِ», with the genitive of الأرحام, is like their saying: «أسألك بالله والرحمِ» (I ask you by Allah and by the womb)." He said: "And this is ugly, because the Arabs do not join a genitive noun back onto a genitive that has been expressed by a pronoun."

The second: it is not conjoined to the genitive pronoun; rather the wāw is for the oath, and it is a genitive by the particle of oath, sworn by, and the answer to the oath is: «إنَّ الله كان عليكم رقيباً». This was declared weak on two grounds. The first: the two readings — with the accusative and with the overt preposition in «بالأرحام» — prevent that, and the default is that readings agree. The second: it is forbidden to swear by other than Allah the Exalted, and the ḥadīths are explicit about that.

Some implied a muḍāf, fleeing from that, and said: "Its implied form is: and by the Lord of the wombs." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "What precedes it has made this unnecessary", meaning the swearing by Allah the Exalted. Someone may [say]: "Allah the Exalted may swear by whatever He wills, as He swore by His creatures, like the sun, the star and the night, even though we are forbidden that." [Translator's note: the bracketed «[أن يقول:]» is in the printed source.] However, what is intended in terms of meaning is not an oath; so the more fitting is to take this reading as conjunction to the pronoun, and no attention is paid to the attack of whoever attacked it; and Ḥamza is of an exalted rank that prevents him from transmitting a weak reading.

ʿAbd Allāh also read: «والأرحامُ» in the nominative, which is as a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar omitted. Ibn ʿAṭiyya implied it as: "worthy to be joined"; and al-Zamakhsharī implied it as: "and the wombs are among what is to be feared, or among what is asked by"; and this is better, because of the verbal and semantic indication, unlike the first, which is by semantic indication only. Abū al-Baqāʾ implied it as: "and the wombs are inviolable", i.e. their sanctity is obligatory.

His saying: {إِنَّ الله كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيباً} runs in the course of giving the reason (taʿlīl). And الرقيب: faʿīl for intensity, from رَقَبَ يَرْقُب رَقْباً ورُقوباً ورِقْباناً, when one sharpens one's gaze at a matter one wants to ascertain; and its use among the attributes of Allah the Exalted is in the sense of الحفيظ (the Preserver). [Translator's note: the printed text reads «صافت», a misprint for «صفات».] The poet said:
1525 - كمقاعِد الرُّقباءِ للضُّرَبَاءِ أيديهم نواهِدْ
(Like the seats of the watchers [in the game of maysir] over the players, their hands raised.)
And الرقيب is also a kind of snake. And الرقيب is the third arrow of the arrows of maysir (the game of chance), and these have preceded in al-Baqara. And الارتقاب is waiting.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بالطيب}: it is the second object of «تتبدَّلوا». It has preceded in al-Baqara, at His saying, the Exalted, {فَبَدَّلَ الذين ظَلَمُواْ} [verse 59], that what is genitive by the bāʾ is what is abandoned, and the accusative is what is obtained. And tafaʿʿala here is in the sense of istafʿala, which is frequent, as in تَعَجَّل and تأخر in the sense of استعجل and استأخر. Among the instances of تبدّل in the sense of استبدل is the saying of Dhū al-Rumma:
1526 - فياكرَمَ السَّكْنِ الذين تَحَمَّلوا ... عن الدارِ والمُسْتَخْلِفِ المُتَبَدِّلِ
(O the noble dwellers who departed from the abode, and the one who took their place, the substituting one!)
i.e. the one taking in exchange (المستبدل).

His saying: {إلى أَمْوَالِكُمْ}: there are three analyses in it. The first: «إلى» is in the sense of «مع» (with), as in His saying {إِلَى المرافق} [al-Māʾida: 6]; this is the view of the Kufans. The second: it is in its proper sense, and it, with its genitive noun, is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. joined or added to your wealth. The third: that «تأكلوا» be made to imply the meaning of «تَضُمُّوا» (to join), as if it were said: and do not join it to your wealth, consuming [it]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: He has forbidden them to consume the wealth of orphans alone and together with their own wealth, so why did the prohibition come against consuming it together with it? I say: because if they were in no need of the orphans' wealth, owing to the lawful provision Allah had given them, and they nevertheless coveted it, the ugliness would be more extreme and the blame more fitting; and because they used to do so, so He denounced their act and decried them, so that it would be a stronger deterrent for them."

His saying: {إِنَّهُ كَانَ حُوباً}: regarding the hāʾ there are three analyses. The first: it refers to the consuming understood from «لا تأكلوا». The second: to the exchanging understood from «لا تَتَبدَّلوا». The third: to both of them, taking it in the manner of a demonstrative, as in {عَوَانٌ بَيْنَ ذلك} [al-Baqara: 68], and from it:
1527 - كأنَّه في الجِلْدِ تَوْليعُ البَهقْ
(As if it were, on the skin, the blotching of vitiligo.)
That has preceded in al-Baqara. The first is preferable, because it is the nearest thing mentioned.

The majority read: «حُوباً» with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, al-Ḥasan with fatḥa, and some: «حَاباً» with alif; these are dialectal forms of the maṣdar (verbal noun), and the fatḥa is the dialect of Tamīm. Parallel to الحَوْب and الحاب are القول and القال, and الطُّرد and الطَّرْد. And it [الحوب] is sin. It is also said: the form with ḍamma is a noun of the maṣdar, and the form with fatḥa is a maṣdar. Its origin is from حَوْب of camels, which is driving them on with a cry; so sin was named by it, because one is rebuked by it; and it is also applied to a fault, because one is rebuked away from it. And from it is his saying, upon him be peace: "Divorcing Umm Ayyūb would be a ḥawb", i.e. a great sin. One says: حابَ يَحُوب حَوْباً وحُوباً وحاباً وحَوُوباً وحِيابة. Al-Mukhabbal al-Saʿdī said:
1528 - فلا يَدْخُلَنَّ الدهرَ قبرك حُوبٌ ... فإنَّك تلقاهُ عليك حَسِيبُ
(Let no sin ever enter your grave [with you], for you will meet it as a reckoner against you.)
And another said:
1529 - وإنَّ مهاجِرَيْنِ تَكَنَّفاه ... غداتئذٍ لقد خَطِئا وحابا
(Two emigrants who flanked him on that morning have surely erred and sinned.)
And الحَوْبة is need; from it in supplication: «إليك أرفع حَوْبتي» (to You I raise my need); and "Allah inflicted الحَوْبة upon him". And تحوَّب فلان when he gets out of sin, like تحرَّج and تأثَّم; so the doubling in it is for privation (salb).

semin-durr:159-159.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَإِن مِّنْ أَهْلِ الكتاب}: «إنْ» here is negating, in the sense of «ما», and «من أهل» admits two analyses. The first: it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is the omitted oath clause together with its response; the implied form is: "And there is no one of the People of the Book but — by Allah — he will surely believe in him." So it is like His saying: {وَمَا مِنَّآ إِلاَّ لَهُ مَقَامٌ [مَّعْلُومٌ]} [al-Ṣāffāt: 164], i.e. "there is no one of us", and like His saying: {وَإِن مِّنكُمْ إِلاَّ وَارِدُهَا} [Maryam: 71], i.e. "there is no one of you but he will come to it". This is the apparent analysis. The second — held by al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ — is that it is in the position of the khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The clause «ليؤمِنَنَّ به» is an oath clause standing as the adjective of an omitted qualified noun, its implied form being: 'And there is not, of the People of the Book, anyone but he will surely believe in him'; and similar to it are: {وَمَا مِنَّآ إِلاَّ لَهُ مَقَامٌ مَّعْلُومٌ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 164] and {وَإِن مِّنكُمْ إِلاَّ وَارِدُهَا} [Maryam: 71]; and the meaning is: there is not, of the Jews, anyone but he will surely believe."

Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is a gross error, since he claimed that «ليؤمنن به» is an oath clause [قسيمة] standing as the adjective of an omitted qualified noun, and so on; whereas the adjective of the omitted «أحد» is only the preposition and its genitive noun, as we have construed it. As for his saying «ليؤمنن به», it is neither an adjective of a qualified noun nor an oath clause [قسيمة]; it is only the clause of the response to the oath, the oath being omitted, and the oath together with its response is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, since no predication (isnād) can be formed from «أحد» and the genitive phrase, because that would convey no information; the predication is formed only by the oath clause and its response, and that is where the information lies. Likewise the khabar is «إلاَّ له مقام», and likewise «إلا واردها», since no predicative construction can be formed from what precedes «إلا»." «[Translator's note: the text reads «قسيمة» in both places in this quotation, apparently for «قسمية» "oath clause"; translated as written in sense.]»

This man — as you see — has spoken ill of al-Zamakhsharī in claiming that it is an error, whereas it is sound and correct. Would that I knew how a predication cannot be formed from «أحد», qualified by the clause after it, and the preposition-phrase before it! Its parallel is your saying: «ما في الدار رجلٌ إلا صالحٌ» ("There is not in the house a man but a righteous one"): just as «في الدار» is a fronted khabar, «رجل» a postponed mubtadaʾ, and «إلا صالحٌ» its adjective — and it is meaningful, sound speech — so it is here; the most that can be said is that «إلا» has entered upon the adjective to convey restriction (ḥaṣr). As for his objection to him for saying "an oath clause" when it is only the response to the oath, he need not be excused for that; such objections suffice to show their worth.

The lām in «ليؤمِنَنَّ» is the response to an omitted oath, as has preceded. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«ليؤمِنَنَّ» is the response to an omitted oath; and it is said: he emphasized with it outside the oath, as it occurs in negation and interrogation." His saying "and it is said …" is only sound if we refer the disagreement to the nūn of emphasis, because emphasis with the nūn of emphasis is known to occur regularly in interrogation, and in negation with disagreement over it; but emphasis with the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ) in negation and interrogation is not known at all.

He also said before that: "[The implied form is] 'and there is not, of the People of the Book, anyone (أحد)'; and it is said that the omitted word is «مَنْ», and its parallel has passed, except that construing «مَنْ» here is far-fetched, because the exception comes after the noun is complete, and «مَنْ», whether relative or indefinite-qualified, is not complete." He means that some made the omitted word the word «مَنْ», construing: "وإنْ مِنْ أهل مَنْ إلا ليؤمِنَنَّ", putting the word «مَنْ» in place of «أحد». His saying "and its parallel has passed" refers to His saying, Exalted is He: {وَإِنَّ مِنْ أَهْلِ الكتاب لَمَن يُؤْمِنُ بالله} [Āl ʿImrān: 199]; the point of the parallel is that there the «مَنْ» that is implied here is stated explicitly.

Ubayy read: {ليؤمِنُنَ به قبل موتهم} with ḍamma on the first nūn, out of regard for the meaning of the omitted «أحد», for although its wording is singular its meaning is plural. The pronoun in «به» refers to ʿĪsā; and it is said: to Allah the Exalted; and it is said: to Muḥammad, upon him be peace. The pronoun in «موته» refers to ʿĪsā; and it is related in the exegesis that when he descends to earth everyone will believe in him, until the whole religion becomes Islamic. And it is said: it refers back to the implied «أحد», i.e. no scripturist dies until he believes in ʿĪsā; this is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, whereupon ʿIkrima said to him: "What do you think if he falls from a house, or is burned, or a wild beast eats him?" He said: "He does not die until he moves his lips with it", i.e. with belief in ʿĪsā. Al-Fayyāḍ ibn Ghazwān read: «وإنَّ من أهل الكتاب» with «إنَّ» doubled; and it is a rejected reading because of its difficulty.

His saying: {وَيَوْمَ القيامة}: what governs it is «شيهداً» «[Translator's note: so in the text, for «شهيداً».]». In it is evidence for the permissibility of fronting the khabar of «كان» before it, because fronting the governed word signals [the permissibility of] fronting the governing word. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted that it be in the accusative by «يكون»; this is according to the view of those who allow «كان» to govern the adverb and what resembles it. The pronoun in «يكون» refers to ʿĪsā; and it is said: to Muḥammad, upon him be peace.

semin-durr:160-160.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {فَبِظُلْمٍ}: this preposition-phrase is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «حَرَّمنا», and the bāʾ is causal. It was only fronted before its governing word to draw attention to the ugliness of the cause of the prohibition. It has preceded that someone said «فبظلمِ» is a badal (substitute) from His saying {فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ مَّيثَاقَهُمْ}, and the refutation of the one who said it has also preceded, so there is no need to repeat it. «من الذين» is an adjective of «ظلم», i.e. a wrongdoing issuing from those who were Jews. And it is said: there is an adjective of «الظلم» omitted because it is understood, i.e. "for a wrongdoing — what a wrongdoing!", or "for a great wrongdoing", as in the poet's saying:

167 - 3- فلا وأبى الطيرِ المُرِبَّةِ بالضحى ... على خالدٍ لقد وقَعْتِ على لَحْمِ
(No, by the father of the birds that settle in the forenoon over Khālid — you have surely alighted upon flesh!)

i.e. great flesh.

His saying: {أُحِلَّتْ لَهُمْ}: this clause is an adjective of «طيبات», so its position is accusative. The meaning of describing them thus is: by virtue of the lawfulness they had been in; this is made clear by the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās: {كانت أُحِلَّتْ لهم}.

His saying: «كثيراً»: there are three analyses. The most apparent: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "by their turning away many people", or "a large party", or "a large group". And it is said: its accusative is as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a great turning away". And it is said: as an adverb of time, i.e. "for a long time". The first is preferable, because the maṣdars after it put their objects in the accusative, so the whole section runs on one pattern.

The bāʾ was repeated only in His saying {وَبِصَدِّهِمْ}, and was not repeated in His saying «وأَخْذِهم» and what follows, because between the maʿṭūf (conjoined) and what it is conjoined to there has intervened something that is not governed by the conjoined-to word, namely its governing word «حَرَّمْنا» and what is attached to it. So when the conjoined word became distant from what it is conjoined to by the intervention of what is not governed by the conjoined-to word, the bāʾ was repeated for that reason. As for what follows, nothing intervened in it except what is governed by the conjoined-to word, namely «الربا».

semin-durr:161-161.t: The clause in His saying, Exalted is He: {وَقَدْ نُهُواْ عَنْهُ}: is in the position of the accusative because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The parallel to this in repeating the particle and not repeating it is what preceded in His saying: {فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ مَّيثَاقَهُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 155], the verse. «بالباطل» may be attached to «أَكْلِهم», the bāʾ being causal, or to an omitted word, as a ḥāl from «هم» in «أكلهم», i.e. "being involved in falsehood".

semin-durr:16-16.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {واللذان}: the discussion of it is like the discussion of «اللاتي», except that in the words of Abū al-Baqāʾ there is what suggests that ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb with a pronoun) is permissible in it, for he said: "The discussion of «اللذان» is like the discussion of «اللاتي», except that whoever allows the accusative may validly assume a verb of the same kind as the one mentioned, its implied form being 'harm the two who…'. What is after the fāʾ may not govern what is before it here, even if it were free of the pronoun, because the fāʾ here has the status of the fāʾ occurring in the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis), and that cuts off what is after it from what is before it." His words "whoever allows the accusative" may mean whoever allows the accusative mentioned earlier for «اللاتي», by implying a verb not by way of ishtighāl, as he himself assumed it with the like of «اقصِدوا» (aim at); or it may mean whoever allows the accusative by ishtighāl in general. But this is unlikely, because the two verses are of one kind, so it is not to be supposed of him that he forbids it in one of them and allows it in the other. Nor does it help that in the first verse the verb that explains [the implied verb] is transitive by a preposition, while the verb in this verse is transitive by itself and so stronger, since that has no effect in the chapter of ishtighāl. The accusative pronoun in «يأتِيانها» is for the indecency (al-fāḥisha).

ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read: «يأتينَ بالفاحشةِ» (they [fem.] commit [lit. bring] the indecency), i.e., they come with it; and the meaning of the majority's reading is "they approach it and engage in it."

The majority read «واللذانِ» with the nūn light, and Ibn Kathīr read «واللذانِّ» here, and «اللذينِّ» in Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda [Fuṣṣilat], with the nūn doubled. Its explanation is that one of the two nūns was made a compensation for the dropped yāʾ, which ought to have remained; for «الذي» is like «القاضي», and the yāʾ of «القاضي» remains in the dual, so the yāʾ of «الذي» and «التي» ought by right to have remained in the dual. But they dropped it, either because this is an irregular dual — since vague words (mubhamāt) are not truly made dual, for only what can be made indefinite is made dual, and vague words are not made indefinite, so they made the dropping a pointer to this — or because the speech is lengthened by the ṣila (relative clause). Ibn ʿUṣfūr claimed that the doubling of the nūn is only permissible with the alif, as in this verse, and not with the yāʾ in the genitive and accusative; but Ibn Kathīr's reading in Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda, {أَرِنَا اللذيْنِّ أَضَلاَّنَا} [verse 29], is an argument against him.

It was also read: «اللَّذَأَنِّ», with a hamza and the nūn doubled. Its explanation is that when he doubled the nūn, two quiescent letters met, and he escaped from that by changing the alif into a hamza. The verification of that was given in al-Fātiḥa.

ʿAbd Allāh read: «والذين يَفْعَلُونه منكم» (and those [pl.] of you who do it). This is a difficult reading, because it is in the plural form and after it is a dual pronoun. An explanation may be contrived for it: since «الذين» comprises the two categories of males and females, the pronoun referring back to it is dual with regard to what is included under it; just as a plural pronoun refers back to a dual that comprises many individuals included under it, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِن طَآئِفَتَانِ مِنَ المؤمنين اقتتلوا} [al-Ḥujurāt: 9] and {هذان خَصْمَانِ اختصموا} [al-Ḥajj: 19]. So the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said; but there is something to consider in it, for the difference stands: «الطائفة» is a noun for a group, and likewise «خصم», because it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) which was applied to the plural.

The underlying form of «فآذُوهما» is «فآذِيُوهما»; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt to be heavy, so the yāʾ, which is the third radical, was dropped, and the letter before the wāw was given ḍamma so that it would remain sound.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِنَّمَا التوبة عَلَى الله}: the discussion of «إنما» and what has been said about it was given at the beginning of al-Baqara. «التوبة» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and about its khabar (predicate) there are two views. The more evident: it is «على الله», i.e., "repentance rests upon the bounty of Allah," and «للذين» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to what the khabar is attached to. Abū al-Baqāʾ, when mentioning this view, allowed «للذين» to be attached to an omitted word as a ḥāl (circumstantial). He said: "On this view «للذين يعملون السوء» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in the adverbial phrase, namely «على الله», the governor of it being the adverbial phrase or the 'being settled' (al-istiqrār), i.e., 'being for those who…'. The governor of the ḥāl may not be «التوبة», because it has been separated from it by the khabar." What he said here is contrived and unnecessary.

Second: the khabar is «للذين», and «على الله» is attached to an omitted word as a ḥāl from something omitted, the implied form being "repentance [Translator's note: the text has «إما», a misprint for «إنما»], when it is, or since it is, upon Allah, is for those who do…"; so «إذا» and «إذ» are governed by «الذين» [i.e., «للذين»], because an adverb may precede its abstract (maʿnawī) governor. This «كان» is the complete (tāmma) one, and its fāʿil (agent) is the one described by the ḥāl. «على الله» may not be a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in «للذين» with «للذين» governing it, because it is an abstract governor, and a ḥāl does not precede its abstract governor. This is what Abū al-Baqāʾ said, and he compared this question to their saying «هذا بُسْراً أطيبُ منه رُطَباً» (this, as unripe dates, is better than it as ripe dates), meaning that the implied form there is "when it was unripe it is better than it when it was ripe." On this question there are many confused views which this book cannot bear. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] assumed two muḍāfs omitted from the mubtadaʾ and the khabar, saying: "The implied form is: the acceptance of repentance is consequent upon the bounty of Allah; so «على» remains in its usual sense," meaning of superiority (istiʿlāʾ).

His words: {بِجَهَالَةٍ}: there are two views about it. First: it is attached to an omitted word as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «يعملون», and its meaning is accompaniment, i.e., they do evil while involved in ignorance, i.e., accompanied by it. It may also be a ḥāl from the object, i.e., "[the evil] being involved with ignorance," but there is remoteness and laxity in this.

Second: it is attached to «يعملون», being the bāʾ of causation. The Shaykh said: "I.e., what drives them to doing evil is ignorance; since had they known what follows from disobedience, remembering it at the time of doing it, they would not have embarked on it, as in his ﷺ words: 'The fornicator does not fornicate, at the time when he fornicates, while he is a believer'; because the intellect is then overcome or taken away."

His words: {مِن قَرِيبٍ}: there are two views about it. First: «من» is for the beginning of extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), i.e., the repentance begins from a time near to the time of the disobedience, so that he does not fall into persistence. This is only possible on the view of the Kufans; the Basrans do not allow «مِنْ» to be for the beginning of extent in time, and they interpret whatever occurs of it. The implied sense (mafhūm) of the verse would be that, had he repented after a distant time, he would not be among those singled out for the honour of acceptance of repentance by Allah mentioned in this verse; rather he would be among those of whom He said «فأولئك عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم» (as for those, perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness).

Second: it is partitive, i.e., "part of a near time," meaning: in whatever part of the parts of this time he makes repentance, he is one who repents soon. On both views «مِنْ» is attached to «يتوبون», and «قريب» is an adjective of an omitted [noun] "time," as established above. However, omitting this described noun and putting this adjective in its place is not according to regular analogy, since the omission is regular only in certain cases: among them that the adjective has come to be treated like non-derived nouns, such as «الأبطح» (the broad watercourse) and «الأبرق» (the mixed stony ground); or that it is specific to the genus of the described noun, as in «مررت بكاتبٍ» (I passed by a writer); or that its described noun has been mentioned before, as in «اسقِني ماءً ولو بارداً» (give me water to drink, even cold). What we are dealing with is none of these.

In His words {ثُمَّ يَتُوبُونَ} there is an indication of the vastness of His pardon, since He brought the particle of delay (thumma). The fāʾ in His words «فأولئك» signals that Allah's acceptance of their repentance is caused by their repenting soon. «يتوب» was made to include the meaning of "inclining with favour" (yaʿṭifu), which is why it was made transitive with «على». As for His words {إِنَّمَا التوبة عَلَى الله}, He had regard to the omitted muḍāf, since the implied form is "the acceptance of repentance is upon Allah." So the Shaykh said, and there is something to consider in it.

semin-durr:65-65.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَلاَ وَرَبِّكَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}: there are four views on this question. The first, which is the view of Ibn Jarīr: the first «لا» is a rejection of speech that preceded it, its implied form being: "No, you do not understand", or: "the matter is not as they claim, that they believe in what was sent down to you"; then He began an oath after that. On this view the pause on «لا» is complete. The second: the first «لا» was placed before the oath out of concern for the negation, then repeated for emphasis. It would have been valid to drop the first and the [meaning of] negation would remain, but the indication of the said concern would be lost; and it would have been valid to drop the second and the meaning of concern would remain, but the indication of negation would be lost; so both were combined for that reason. The third: the second is redundant (zāʾida), and the oath is parenthetical between the particle of negation and what is negated, as though the implied form were: "So they do not believe, by your Lord". The fourth: the first is redundant and the second is not redundant; this is the choice of al-Zamakhsharī, for he said: "«لا» is added to emphasise the meaning of the oath, as it was added in {لِّئَلاَّ يَعْلَمَ} [al-Ḥadīd: 29] to emphasise the necessity of knowing; and «لا يؤمنون» is the answer to the oath. If you say: why did you not claim that it was added to support the «لا» in «لا يؤمنون»? I say: that is rejected by the equal status of negation and affirmation in it; that is His words {فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِمَا تُبْصِرُونَ وَمَا لاَ تُبْصِرُونَ إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 38]" — meaning that «لا» has come before the oath where there is no «لا» in the answer. So al-Zamakhsharī holds that the «لا» in the words of Allah the Exalted {فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِمَا تُبْصِرُون} [al-Ḥāqqa: 38] is also redundant, to emphasise the meaning of the oath; this is one of two views, the other being like the view of al-Ṭabarī already mentioned. Like the verse, according to the explanations mentioned, are the words of another:
1603 - فلا واللَّهِ لا يُلْفَى لِما بي ... ولا لَلِما بهم أبداً دواءُ
(No, by Allah, no remedy is ever found for what afflicts me, nor for what afflicts them.)
His words {حتى يُحَكِّمُوكَ}: «حتى» is [a particle of] limit attached to His words «لا يؤمنون», i.e. faith is negated of them up to this limit, which is their making you judge, their not finding distress, and their submitting to your command. There is a shift (iltifāt) in His word «ربِّك» from the third person in His words {واستغفر لَهُمُ الرسول}, returning to His words «ثم جاؤوك». Abū al-Sammāl read «شَجْر» with sukūn on the jīm, to escape the succession of vowels; this is weak, because fatḥa is the sister of sukūn [i.e. light enough already]. «بينهم» is an adverbial made accusative by «شجر»; this is the correct view. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a ḥāl (circumstantial), and gave two possibilities for the one qualified by this ḥāl. The first: it is a ḥāl from the relative «ما». The second: it is a ḥāl from the agent of «شجر», which is also the relative noun itself in meaning; on this view it is attached to an omitted element. «ثم لا يجدوا» is conjoined to what follows «حتى». «يَجِدُوا» may be the one transitive to two objects, the first being «حرجاً» and the second the preposition-phrase before it, which is then attached to an omitted element; or it may be the one transitive to one object, in which case two views are possible on «في أنفسهم». The first: it is attached to «يجدوا», in the way supplementary elements (faḍalāt) are attached.
The second: it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «حَرَجاً», because the adjective of an indefinite noun, when placed before it, becomes accusative as a ḥāl.
On {مِّمَّا قَضَيْتَ} there are two views. The first: it is attached to «حرجاً» itself, because you say «حَرِجْتُ من كذا» [Translator's note: printed «خَرَجْتُ» (I went out); the context requires «حَرِجْتُ» (I felt distress)]. The second: it is attached to an omitted element, so it is in the position of accusative because it is an adjective of «حرجاً». «ما» may be maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming), or in the sense of «الذي», i.e. "distress from your judgement" or "from that which you judged"; or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective; on these two [latter] views the referent pronoun is omitted.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {حتى إِذَا}: «حتى» is a particle of inception (ḥarf ibtidāʾ), and the conditional sentence after it is a limit for what precedes it, i.e., repentance is not for a people who do evil deeds, and the limit of their doing is that when death comes to them they say such-and-such. This is a good view. «حتى» may not be a preposition putting «إذا» in the genitive, i.e., "they do evil deeds until the time when death comes," because it is conditional and a condition is not governed by what precedes it; and if we made «حتى» a preposition, it would be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يعملون», while conditional particles are not governed by what precedes them. Do you not see that «بمَنْ تمرر أمرر» (by whomever you pass, I will pass) is permissible, while «مَرَرْتُ بمن يَقُمْ أكرمْه» (I passed by whoever stands, I will honour him) is not, because it [the conditional] has the right to head the sentence? And because «إذا» is not freely inflected (lā tataṣarraf) according to the well-known view, as was established at the beginning of al-Baqara. Ibn Mālik argued for its being freely inflected on several grounds, among them its being put in the genitive by «حتى», as in {حتى إِذَا جَآءُوهَا} [al-Zumar: 71] and {حتى إِذَا كُنتُمْ} [Yūnus: 22]; and there is in this the difficulty I have mentioned to you. This was established above at His words {حتى إِذَا بَلَغُواْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 6].

His words: {وَلاَ الذين يَمُوتُونَ}: «الذين» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to His words «للذين يعملون», i.e., repentance is neither for these nor for those. So He made equal, in the non-acceptance of repentance, the one who dies an unbeliever and the one who does not repent until he sees death with his own eyes. What is meant by those who do evil deeds is the hypocrites.

Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «الذين» to be in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being «أولئك» and what follows it, believing that the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ) and not «لا» of negation. What he said about the lām being the lām of inception is not valid unless a lām had been written in the Muṣḥaf prefixed to «الذين», so that it would become «وللذين»; but the written form is not so: it is only a lām and an alif [i.e., «لا»], and the alif and lām of the definite article prefixed to the relative noun; its written form is «ولا الذين».

His words: «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ and «أَعْتَدْنا» its khabar. «أولئك» may point to «الذين يموتون وهم كفار» (those who die while they are unbelievers), because the demonstrative is treated like the pronoun and so refers back to the nearest thing mentioned; or it may point to both descriptions: those who do evil deeds and those who die while they are unbelievers. «أعتدنا», i.e., We have made ready.

semin-durr:66-66.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَنِ اقتلوا}: there are two views on «أن». The first: it is explicative (mufassira), because it came after what has the meaning of saying but not its letters; this is more apparent. The second: it is maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming), the imperative verb after it being its ṣila; and there is a difficulty in this, in that when a maṣdar is formed from it and what follows it, the indication of command is lost. Do you not see that when you say «كتبت إليه أَنْ قم» (I wrote to him: stand), there is in it an indication of requesting standing by way of command that is not in your saying «كتبت إليه القيامَ» (I wrote to him the standing)? But they allowed it, arguing from their saying «كتبت إليه بأَنْ قم», the point of evidence being that the preposition is not suspended. The thorough treatment of the discussion of this is in «al-Sharḥ al-Kabīr li-l-Tashīl».
Abū ʿAmr read with kasra on the nūn of «أَنْ» and ḍamma on the wāw of «أو»; Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim gave both kasra, and the rest of the Seven gave both ḍamma. The kasra is according to the original rule for the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the ḍamma is for harmonising with the third [letter], since it carries a necessary ḍamma. Abū ʿAmr distinguished only because the wāw is the sister of the ḍamma. The precise treatment of this has preceded in al-Baqara at His words {فَمَنِ اضطر} [verse: 173].
His words: {مَّا فَعَلُوهُ}: the hāʾ may be the pronoun of the maṣdar of «اقتلوا» or of «اخرجوا», i.e. "they would not have done the killing" or "they would not have done the going out". Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī went far in claiming that it refers back to both together, because grammatical technique shuns that. [Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed a fourth view]: that it refers back to what was prescribed, indicated by «كتبنا».
His words: {إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ}: its nominative is from two angles. The first: it is a badal (substitute) from the agent of «فَعَلوه», and this is preferred over the accusative because the speech is not affirmative. The second: it is conjoined to that nominative pronoun, «إلاَّ» being a conjunction; this is the opinion of the Kufans, and this question has another place. Ibn ʿĀmir and a group read «إلا قليلاً» in the accusative, and there are two views on it. The better known: it is accusative as an exception, even though the preferred form is the nominative, because the meaning is present with it [i.e. the nominative] just as it is present with the accusative, and it exceeds it by agreeing with the wording. The second: it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "except a little doing"; al-Zamakhsharī said this, and it is [Translator's note: printed «وفي»; read «وفيه»] questionable, since the apparent view is that «منهم» is an adjective of «قليلاً», and whenever «القليل» is taken to refer to something other than persons this construction becomes awkward, since there would then be no benefit in mentioning «منهم».
His words: {وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ فَعَلُواْ}: the discussion of the counterpart of this question has preceded in several places. «ما» in «ما يوعظون» is a nominal relative. The bāʾ in «به» may be the transitivising one, entering on the thing they are admonished with; on this view what they are admonished with is the obligations, commands and prohibitions — the commands and prohibitions of Allah the Exalted are called admonitions because they are accompanied by promise and threat. Or it may be causal, the implied form being: "what they are admonished on account of", i.e. on account of abandoning it, the omitted "abandoning" being indicated by His words «ولو أنهم فعلوا». The noun of «كان» is a pronoun referring back to the doing understood from His words {وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ فَعَلُواُْ}, i.e. "doing what they are admonished with would have been [better]"; «خيراً» is its khabar (predicate), and «تثبيتاً» is a tamyīz (specification) of «أشد».

semin-durr:67-67.t: {وَإِذاً}: a particle of answer and requital. Are these two meanings necessary to it, or is it sometimes an answer only? There are two views. The first is the view of al-Shalawbīn, following the apparent sense of Sībawayh's statement. The second is the view of al-Fārisī: if someone says «أزورُك غداً» (I will visit you tomorrow) and you say «إذن أكرمَك» (then I will honour you), it is according to him an answer and requital; but if you say «إذاً أظنَّك صادقاً» (then I think you truthful), it is a particle of answer only; it is as though he took this from the circumstantial context. It has preceded that it is one of the particles that put the imperfect in the accusative, under conditions mentioned. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«إذَنْ» is an answer, rendered ungoverning (mulghāh)." The apparent sense of this statement agrees with al-Fārisī's view, but it is questionable, because al-Fārisī does not say of a verse like this one that it is an answer only; and its being an answer needs something implied. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«وإذن» is an answer to an implied question, as though it were said: and what will they have, after the strengthening, besides? And it was said: had they been made firm, We would have given them; because «إذَنْ» is answer and requital." On «مِنْ لَدُنّا» there are two views. The more apparent: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «آتيناهم». The second: it is attached to an omitted element because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أجراً», because it was originally an adjective of an indefinite noun placed before it. «أجراً» is the second object of «آتيناهم».

semin-durr:69-69.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِّنَ النبيين}: there are four views on it. The most apparent: it is an explication of «الذين أَنْعَم الله عليهم» (those whom Allah has favoured). The second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive pronoun in «عليهم». The third: it is a ḥāl from the relative noun, which is in meaning like the first; on these two views it is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "being among the prophets". The fourth: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يُطِعِ». Al-Rāghib said: "I.e. whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, among the prophets and those after them; and His words {فأولئك مَعَ الذين أَنْعَمَ الله عَلَيْهِم} are an allusion to the Highest Assembly; then He said {وَحَسُنَ أولئك رَفِيقاً}; this is made clear by his words, peace be upon him, at death: 'O Allah, join me to the Highest Companion.' This is apparent." End of quotation. Al-Shaykh showed it to be unsound in terms of meaning and in terms of grammatical technique. In terms of meaning: the Messenger here is Muhammad ﷺ, and Allah the Exalted has informed that whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger will be with those mentioned; if «مِن النبيين» were made attached to «يُطِع», «من النبيين» would be an explanation of the conditional «مَنْ», which would entail that in his time, peace be upon him, or after him, there are prophets who obey him; and this is not possible because of the words of Allah the Exalted {وَخَاتَمَ النبيين} [al-Aḥzāb: 30] [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse is al-Aḥzāb: 40] and his words, peace be upon him: "There is no prophet after me." In terms of technique: what precedes the fāʾ occurring as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) does not govern what follows it; if you said «إنْ تضرب يقم عمروٌ زيداً», it would not be allowed. Are these four descriptions for one class of people or for different classes? There are two views.
His words: {وَحَسُنَ أولئك رَفِيقاً}: on the accusative of «رفيقاً» there are two views. The first: it is a tamyīz (specification). The second: it is a ḥāl. On the assumption that it is a tamyīz, there are two possibilities [Translator's note: printed «في احتمالان»; read «ففيه احتمالان»]. The first: it is transferred from the agent position, its implied form being «وحَسُنَ رفيقُ أولئك» (and excellent is the companionship of those); on this view the companion is other than the thing specified, and «مِنْ» may not enter on it.
The second: it is not transferred, so it is the specified thing itself, and «مِنْ» may enter on it. It was brought here in the singular for one of two reasons: either because «الرفيق» is like «الخليط» (associate) and «الصديق» (friend) in applying to singular, dual and plural with one form; or by sufficing with the singular in place of the plural because the meaning is understood — and its being a verse-ending (fāṣila) made that good. «أولئك» may point to the prophets and those after them, or to whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, being made plural only according to its meaning. On this view it may be said that He observed the wording of «مَنْ», so made it singular in His word «رفيقاً», and its meaning, so made it plural in His word «أولئك»; except that beginning with construal according to the wording is better in that. On this view He would have combined in it construal according to the wording in «يُطِعْ», then according to the meaning in «أولئك», then according to the wording in «رفيقاً».
The majority read with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and ḍamma on the sīn of «حَسُن». Abū al-Sammāl read with fatḥa on it and sukūn on the sīn, for lightness, like «عَضْد» for «عَضُد»; this is the dialect of Tamīm. «وحُسْن» with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the sīn is also permissible, as though they transferred the vowel of the ʿayn to the fāʾ after stripping it of its vowel; this is the dialect of some of Qays.
Al-Zamakhsharī made this of the type of exclamation (taʿajjub), for he said: "In it is the meaning of exclamation, as though it were said: how excellent are those as companions! Because of its independence in the meaning of exclamation, «وحَسْنَ» has been read with sukūn on the sīn; one who exclaims says «حَسُنَ الوجهُ وجهُك» and «حَسْن الوجهُ وجهك» (how fine a face is your face!), with fatḥa and ḍamma along with the sukūn." Al-Shaykh said: "This is confusion and the grafting of one doctrine onto another. We say: they disagreed about «فَعُل» intended for praise. Al-Fārisī and most grammarians held that it may be attached only to the category of «نعم» and «بئس», so its agent can only be what can be an agent for them. Al-Akhfash and al-Mubarrad held that it may be attached to the category of «نعم» and «بئس», its agent being treated like theirs — that is when the meaning of exclamation does not enter it — and that it may be attached to the verb of exclamation, in which case it is not treated like «نعم» and «بئس» either in the agent or in the rest of their rules; so you say «لَضَرُبَتْ يَدُكَ» (how [skilled] your hand is at striking!) and «لَضَرُبَتِ اليدُ». He took the exclamation from the doctrine of al-Akhfash and the example from the doctrine of al-Fārisī, so he followed neither of the two doctrines. As for his making the sukūn and the transfer [of the vowel] evidence of its being independent in exclamation, that is not granted, because al-Farrāʾ reported that as a dialectal form in what is not intended for exclamation."

semin-durr:70-70.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {ذلك الفضل مِنَ الله}: «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and there are two views on the khabar (predicate). The first: it is «الفضلُ», and the preposition-phrase is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the governor of it being the meaning of pointing. The second: it is the preposition-phrase, and «الفضلُ» is an adjective of the demonstrative. «الفضل» and the preposition-phrase after it may also be two khabars of «ذلك», according to the opinion of those who allow that. His words: {وكفى بالله عَلِيماً}. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "For that reason the bāʾ entered on the name of Allah, to indicate the command." [Translator's note: the text appears elliptical here.] The discussion of this question has preceded in full.

semin-durr:127-127.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمَا يتلى} — there are seven views on it, namely that the position of «ما» may be nominative, accusative or genitive.
The nominative is from three views. The first: that it is nominative, conjoined to the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «يُفتيكم» which refers to Allah the Exalted; this is permissible because of the separation by the object and the preposition with its genitive noun, although separation by one of them is sufficient. The second: that it is conjoined to the word of majesty alone; this is how Abū al-Baqāʾ and others mentioned it, and there is an objection to it, because either it is made a conjoining of a single word to a single word, in which case the khabar (predicate) would have to be dual, even if it stands between the two conjoined items, so that one would say «يُفْتِيانكم» — but that is not permissible, and whoever claims it is permissible needs attested usage from the Arabs, so that one could say «زيد قائمان وعمرو», and the like of this is not permissible; or it is made a conjoining of clauses, meaning that the khabar of the second is omitted, i.e. "and what is recited to you gives you a ruling", so this would be the third view — and they have mentioned it — and repetition would then follow. The third of the nominative views: that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and there are two possibilities for the khabar. One of them: that it is the preposition with its genitive noun after it, namely «في الكتاب», what is recited being the Quran and "the Book" being the Preserved Tablet; this clause would then be parenthetical between the badal (substitute) and the one substituted for, as its explanation will come. The benefit of informing of this is to magnify what is recited and raise its standing, and similar to it is: {وَإِنَّهُ في أُمِّ الكتاب لَدَيْنَا لَعَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ} [al-Zukhruf: 4]. The second possibility: that the khabar is omitted, i.e. "and what is recited to you in the Book gives you a ruling", or "makes clear to you their rulings". These then are four views. Al-Zamakhsharī's words allow all the views, for he said: "«ما يُتْلى» is in the position of the nominative, i.e. Allah gives you a ruling, and so does what is recited in the Book concerning the orphans, meaning His words: {وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلاَّ تُقْسِطُواْ فِي اليتامى} [al-Nisāʾ: 3]; and it is like your saying «أعجبني زيدٌ وكرمه» ('Zayd and his generosity pleased me')." End of quotation. He means that it is of the type of tajrīd (abstraction), since what is intended is to inform that Zayd's generosity pleased, and Zayd was mentioned only to convey this specific meaning; likewise the intended point is that the one who gives them the ruling is what is recited in the Book, and the word of majesty was mentioned for the meaning indicated. The examination of tajrīd has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara, at His words {يُخَادِعُونَ الله} [verse 9].
The genitive is from two views. The first: that the wāw is the wāw of the oath, Allah swearing by what is recited concerning women, magnifying it, as though it were said: "and I swear by what is recited to you in the Book"; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it. The second: that it is conjoined to the pronoun made genitive by «في», i.e. "He gives you a ruling concerning them and concerning what is recited"; this is reported from Muḥammad ibn Abī Mūsā, who said: "Allah gave them a ruling concerning what they asked about and what they did not ask about." However, this is weak from the standpoint of grammatical craft, because it is a conjoining to the genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition, which is the opinion of the Kufans. I have already set out fully the positions of the scholars and their proofs on this at His words: {وَكُفْرٌ بِهِ والمسجد الحرام} [al-Baqara: 217], so refer to it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is not sound to conjoin it to the genitive in «فيهنَّ», because of its defect in wording and meaning." Abū Isḥāq preceded him in this; he said: "This is far-fetched in relation to the wording and to the meaning. As for the wording, it entails conjoining an overt noun to a pronoun; as for the meaning, it is not intended that Allah gives you a ruling concerning what is recited to you in the Book, and that is not permissible, just as it was not permissible in His words {تَسَآءَلُونَ بِهِ والأرحام} [al-Nisāʾ: 1]" — he means without repeating the preposition. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] answered what al-Zamakhsharī and al-Zajjāj rejected it with, saying that the implied meaning is: "He gives you a ruling concerning what is recited regarding them, and concerning what is recited to you in the Book about the orphan women", and it was omitted because His words {وَمَا يتلى عَلَيْكُمْ} indicate it; and annexing «متلوّ» to the pronoun «هُنَّ» is acceptable, since annexation occurs with the slightest connection: since it is recited concerning them, annexing it to them is valid, as in His words: {مَكْرُ الليل والنهار} [Sabaʾ: 33] — since the scheming occurs in them, annexing it to them is valid. And like it is the saying of another:
1659 - إذا كوكبُ الخَرْقاءِ لاحَ بِسُحْرَةٍ ... سهيلٌ أذاعَتْ غَزْلَها في الغرائب
(When the clumsy woman's star — Suhayl — appears before dawn, she scatters her spun yarn among the strange women.)
There is an objection to this answer.
The accusative is by an implied verb, i.e. "and He makes clear to you what is recited", because «يُفْتيكم» means "He makes clear to you". The Shaykh chose the view of the genitive by conjoining to the pronoun, choosing the position of the Kufans, and on the ground that all the other views lead to emphasis (taʾkīd), whereas the view of conjoining to the pronoun makes it a new statement (taʾsīs); he said: "When the matter turns between the two, a new statement is preferable." There is an evident objection to his making this view alone a new statement, to the exclusion of the other views.
His words: {فِي الكتاب} — three views are possible in it. The first: that it is attached to «يُتْلى». The second: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in «يتلى». The third: that it is the khabar of «ما يتلى» on the view that holds «ما يتلى» to be a mubtadaʾ, so it is also attached to an omitted element, except that its position on this view is nominative, and on the one before it accusative.
His words: {فِي يَتَامَى} — there are five views on it. The first: that it is a badal from «الكتاب», a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), and a muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. "concerning the ruling of the orphan women", and there is no doubt that the Book includes mention of their rulings. The second: that it is attached to «يتلى». If it is asked: how is it permissible for two prepositions with one wording and one meaning to be attached [to one verb]? The answer is that their meanings differ, because the first is for location in its proper sense, and the second has the meaning of the bāʾ, for causation, either figuratively or literally according to those who hold [prepositions] to be polysemous. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "As you say: «جئتُك في يوم الجمعة في أَمْرِ زيد» ('I came to you on Friday about Zayd's affair')." The third: that it is a badal from «فيهن» with repetition of the governing element, and this would be a badal of part from whole. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: to what is His saying «في يتامى النساء» attached? I say: on the first view it is connected to «يُتْلى», i.e. it is recited to you concerning them; and «في يتامى» may be a badal from «فيهنَّ». As for the last two views, it is a badal and nothing else." End of quotation.
By "the first view" he means that «ما يتلى» is in a nominative position. The Shaykh said: "As for what he permitted on the nominative view, that it is connected to «يتلى», this is not permissible unless it is a badal from «في الكتاب», or «في» is for causation, lest two prepositions with one wording and one meaning be attached to one governing element, which is prohibited except in badal and conjunction. As for his allowing it to be a badal from «فيهن», the apparent position is that it is not permissible, because of the separation between the badal and the one substituted for by the conjoined element; this would become analogous to your saying «زيدٌ يقيمُ في الدار وعمروٌ في كِسْرٍ منها» ('Zayd stays in the house, and ʿAmr, in a corner of it'), where you have separated «في الدار» from «في كِسْر» by «عمرو»; what is customary in such a construction is: «زيدٌ يقيمُ في الدار في كِسْرٍ منها وعمروٌ»." The fourth: that it is attached to «الكتاب» itself, i.e. "in what He wrote concerning the ruling of the orphans". The fifth: that it is a ḥāl, so it is attached to an omitted element, and the one to whom the ḥāl refers is the nominative of «يُتْلى», i.e. "being concerning the ruling of the orphan women". The annexation of «يتامى» to «النساء» is of the type of annexing the specific to the general, because women divide into orphans and others. The Kufans said: it is of the type of annexing the adjective to what it qualifies, since the original is "concerning the orphan women"; according to the Basrans this is not permissible, and they interpret whatever occurs of it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the annexation of «اليتامى» to «النساء»? I say: it is an annexation with the meaning of «مِنْ», like «سُحْقِ عمامةٍ» ('a worn-out piece of a turban')." The Shaykh said: "What the grammarians mentioned of this is the annexation of a thing to its genus, such as «خاتمُ حديدٍ» ('a ring of iron'); and separation is allowed either by apposition, as in «خاتمٌ حديدٌ», or by making it accusative as a tamyīz (specification), as in «خاتمٌ حديداً», or by making it genitive with «مِنْ», as in «خاتم من حديد»." He said: "The apparent view is that the annexation in «سُحْق عمامةٍ» and «يتامى النساء» has the meaning of the lām, and the meaning of the lām is specification (ikhtiṣāṣ)." This rebuttal is worthless, for they stated the criterion of annexation with the meaning of «مِنْ» as being the annexation of a part to a whole, on condition that the name of the whole applies to the part; and there is no doubt that «يتامى» are some of the women, and «النساء» applies to them. By our phrase "on condition that the name of the whole applies to the part" we exclude something like «يد زيد» ('Zayd's hand'), for "Zayd" does not apply to the hand alone. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«في يتامى النساء», i.e. concerning the orphans among them" — and this is an explanation of meaning, not of i'rab.
The majority read «يتامى», the plural of «يتيمة». Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Madanī read «ييامى» with two yāʾs [dotted] beneath, and Ibn Jinnī explained it as originally «أَيامى», the hamza being replaced by a yāʾ, as they said «فلانٌ ابنُ أعصر ويَعْصر», where the hamza is original; he was named that because of his saying:
