1660 - أبْنَيَّ إنَّ أباكَ غَيَّر لونَه ... كَرُّ الليالي واختلافُ الأعْصُرِ
(My little sons, your father's colour has been changed by the return of the nights and the alternation of the ages.)
They replace the yāʾ with hamza, as in their saying «قطع الله أَدَاهُ», meaning «يَده» ('his hand'), and therefore they also replace it [the hamza] with a yāʾ. And «أيامى» is the plural of «أَيِّم», on the pattern fayʿil; it was then given a broken plural «أيايم», like «سيِّد» and «سيايد»; then the lām was transposed to the place of the ʿayn and the ʿayn to the place of the lām, so the word became «أَيامي»; then the kasra was changed to a fatḥa for its lightness, so the yāʾ was vowelled with the letter before it having fatḥa, and it was changed to an alif, giving «أيامى», whose pattern is fayāliʿ. Abū al-Fatḥ also said: "If it were said that «أيِّم» was given a broken plural on faʿlā, like «سَكْرى», and then a second broken plural «أيامى», that would be a good view." The examination of this word will come at His words: {وَأَنْكِحُواْ الأيامى مِنْكُمْ} [al-Nūr: 32], if Allah the Exalted wills. And it was read: «ما كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لهنَّ», with the agent named.
His words: {وَتَرْغَبُونَ} — there are several views on it. The first — and it is the apparent one — that it is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause), a conjoining of an affirmative clause to a negative clause, i.e. "those to whom you do not give, and those whom you desire to marry", as in your saying «جاء الذي لا يَبْخَلُ ويكرم الضيفان» ('the one who is not stingy and honours guests came'). The second: that it is conjoined to the verb negated by «لا», i.e. "you do not give them and you do not desire". The third: that it is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «تؤتونهن», i.e. "you do not give them while you desire to marry them". Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned these two views, and there is an objection to both: as for the first [of them], because it is contrary to the apparent sense; as for the second, because it is an affirmative imperfect verb, so the wāw does not enter it except by an interpretation for which we have no need here.
And {أَن تَنكِحُوهُنَّ} is with omission of the preposition, so there is the well-known disagreement about it: is it in the position of the accusative or the genitive? There is also disagreement about which preposition is implied. It was said it is «في», i.e. "you desire to marry them for their beauty and their wealth"; and it was said it is «عن», i.e. "you are averse to marrying them because of their ugliness and poverty". The guardians were like that: if they saw her beautiful and wealthy, her guardian married her; otherwise he turned away from her. The first opinion is narrated from ʿĀʾisha and a large group. Here there is a question: the scholars of Arabic stated that the omission of the preposition is regularly permissible with «أَنْ» and «أنَّ» on condition of security from ambiguity, meaning that the preposition is determinate, as in «عجبت أن تقوم», i.e. «من أن تقوم», unlike «مِلْتُ إلى أن تقوم» or «عن أن تقوم»; and the verse is of this [ambiguous] kind. The answer: both meanings are valid, as indicated by what I mentioned to you of the occasion of revelation, so each of the two prepositions is intended alternatively.
His words: {والمستضعفين} — there are three views on it. The first — and it is the apparent one — that it is conjoined to «يتامى النساء», i.e. "what is recited to you concerning the orphan women and concerning the oppressed"; what was recited to them concerning them is His words: {يُوصِيكُمُ الله في أَوْلاَدِكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 11]; that is because they used to say: "We give inheritance only to one who protects the territory and defends the sanctuary," so they deprived the woman and the minor, and it was revealed. The second: that it is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the pronoun in «فيهن», and this is a Kufan opinion. The third: that it is accusative, conjoined to the position of «فيهن», i.e. "and He makes clear the state of the oppressed". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "This implied form fits into the position of the Basrans without strain" — meaning that it is better than the position of the Kufans, where one conjoins to the genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition.
His words: {وَأَن تَقُومُواْ} — there are five views on it: the three mentioned for what precedes it, so it is the same, being conjoined to what precedes it; what was recited to them in this sense is His words: {وَلاَ تأكلوا أَمْوَالَهُمْ إلى أَمْوَالِكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 2] and the like. The fourth: the accusative by an implied verb. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be accusative by an implied «يأمركم», meaning: and He commands you to stand; this is an address to the leaders, that they look after them, secure their rights in full, and let no one wrong them." This view of the accusative is other than the view I mentioned earlier. The fifth: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "and your standing for the orphans with justice is better for you". The first of the views is the most sound.

semin-durr:162-162.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {لكن الراسخون}: «لكن» was brought here because it stands between two opposites, namely the disbelievers and the believers. «الراسخون» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and there are two possibilities for its khabar (predicate). The more apparent of them: it is «يؤمنون»; the second: it is the clause in His saying «أولئك سنؤتيهم». «في العلم» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «الراسخون». «منهم» is attached to an omitted word, because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun latent (mustakinn) in «الراسخون».

His saying: «المؤمنون» is conjoined to «الراسخون», and for its khabar there are the two analyses mentioned for the khabar of «الراسخون». But if we make the khabar «أولئك سنُؤتيهم», then what is the position of «يؤمنون»? What appears is that it is a parenthetical clause, because it contains emphasis and reinforcement of the speech, and «يؤمنون» then refers to «الراسخون» and «المؤمنون» together. It may also be a ḥāl from the two of them; in that case it cannot be said that it is an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida) because a governing word sharing its wording precedes it, since the belief in it is restricted while the first belief is unrestricted, so it contains information that was not in its governing word. It may also be said: it is emphatic relative to His saying «يؤمنون», not emphatic relative to His saying «الراسخون».

His saying: «والمقيمين»: the reading of the majority is with yāʾ. A large group read «والمقيمون» with wāw, among them Ibn Jubayr; Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ in the transmission of Yūnus and Hārūn from him; Mālik ibn Dīnār; ʿIṣma from al-Aʿmash; ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd; al-Jaḥdarī; ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar; and a great many others.

As for the reading with yāʾ, the opinions of the grammarians on it have been confused, and there are six views. The most apparent of them «[Translator's note: the text has the dual «أظهرهما» "the more apparent of the two" although six views are listed.]» — al-Makkī attributed it to Sībawayh, and Abū al-Baqāʾ to the Basrans — is that it is accusative by severance (qaṭʿ), meaning the severance that conveys praise, as in the severance of adjectives. This severance serves to show the excellence of prayer, so the speech in the description was amplified by putting it in another clause; and likewise the severance in His saying {والمؤتون الزكاة}, as will come, is also to show the excellence of [zakāt]. But on this analysis the khabar must be His saying «يؤمنون», and it cannot be His saying {أولئك سَنُؤْتِيهِمْ}, because severance only occurs after the speech is complete. Al-Makkī said: "Whoever makes the accusative of «المقيمين» one of praise makes the khabar of «الراسخين» 'يؤمنون'; if he makes the khabar 'أولئك سنؤتيهم', the accusative of «المقيمين» as praise is not permissible, because that only occurs after the speech is complete." Al-Shaykh said: "Whoever makes the khabar 'أولئك سنؤتيهم', his view is weak." I say: this does not necessarily follow, because this proponent does not, in that case, make «المقيمين» accusative by severance; but it is weak in respect of his having adopted a weak analysis in explaining «المقيمين», as will come.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported from some people a prohibition of its accusative by severance because of the conjunction, since severance does not occur in conjunction, only in adjectives. And when people adduced as evidence for the permissibility of severance the saying of al-Khirniq:

167 - 4- لا يَبْعَدَن قومي الذين همُ ... سُمُّ العُداةِ وآفَةُ الجُزْرِ
النازلين بكلِّ معتَركٍ ... والطيبون معاقدَ الأزْرِ
(May my people not perish, who are poison to enemies and the bane of slaughter-camels; who alight at every battlefield, and are pure where the waist-wrappers are tied.)

this proponent distinguished it by saying that the verse contains no conjunction, because she severed «النازين» «[Translator's note: so in the text, for «النازلين».]» and put it in the accusative, and «الطيبون» and put it in the nominative, from her word «قومي». This distinction has no effect, because outside this verse severance is established together with a conjunction. Sībawayh recited:

167 - 5- ويَأْوي إلى نِسْوةٍ عُطَّلٍ ... وشُعْثاً مراضيعَ مثلَ السَّعالِي
(And he takes refuge with women bare of ornaments, and dishevelled ones, nursing mothers like ghouls.)

so he put «شعثاً» in the accusative, though it is conjoined.

The second: that it is conjoined to the pronoun in «منهم», i.e. "but those firmly grounded in knowledge among them and among those who establish prayer". The third: that it is conjoined to the kāf in «إليك», i.e. "they believe in what was sent down to you and to those who establish prayer", who are the prophets. The fourth: that it is conjoined to «ما» in «بما أُنْزِل», i.e. "they believe in what was sent down to Muḥammad ﷺ and in those who establish [prayer]"; this is attributed to al-Kisāʾī. These differed in their account of «المقيمين»: it is said they are the angels — al-Makkī said: "and they believe in the angels whose attribute is establishing prayer, as in His saying: {يُسَبِّحُونَ الليل والنهار لاَ يَفْتُرُونَ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 20]"; and it is said they are the prophets; and it is said they are the Muslims, and it is then by the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "and in the religion of those who establish [prayer]". The fifth: that it is conjoined to the kāf in «قبلك», i.e. "and before those who establish [prayer]", meaning by them the prophets as well. The sixth: that it is conjoined to the adverb itself, by the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "and from before those who establish [prayer]"; the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place. This is the full extent of what is said in explaining this reading.

Some people of no account have claimed that it is a solecism (laḥn), and they transmitted from ʿĀʾisha and Abān ibn ʿUthmān that it is a mistake arising from an error of the scribe of the Muṣḥaf. They said: moreover, it is in the Muṣḥaf of Ibn Masʿūd with wāw only — al-Farrāʾ transmitted this — and likewise in the Muṣḥaf of Ubayy. This is not authentic from ʿĀʾisha nor from Abān. How excellent is the saying of al-Zamakhsharī, may Allah have mercy on him: "No attention is to be paid to what they claimed about its occurring as a solecism in the writing of the Muṣḥaf. Perhaps one who has not looked into the Book [of Sībawayh] «[Translator's note: the text has «الكتاب الكتاب» repeated.]», and who does not know the ways of the Arabs and the variety they display in the accusative of specification (al-naṣb ʿalā al-ikhtiṣāṣ), would pay attention to it; and it escaped him that the foremost first ones, whose likeness is in the Torah and whose likeness is in the Gospel, were far too high-minded in their zeal for Islam and in repelling attacks from it to leave a breach in the Book of Allah for those after them to close, or a tear for those who came after them to mend." As for the reading with the nominative, it is clear.

His saying: {والمؤتون}: there are also seven analyses. The most apparent: that it is by an implied mubtadaʾ, and it is of the category of praise mentioned for the accusative. The second: that it is conjoined to «الراسخون»; there is weakness in this, because when a follower has been severed from what it follows, what comes after it may not return to the case of the followed word; one does not say «مررت بزيدٍ العاقلَ الفاضلِ» with «العاقل» accusative and «الفاضل» genitive, and so it is here.

The third: that it is conjoined to the pronoun latent in «الراسخون», this being permissible because of the separation. The fourth: that it is conjoined to the pronoun in «المؤمنون». The fifth: that it is conjoined to the pronoun in «يؤمنون». The sixth: that it is conjoined to «المؤمنون». The seventh: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «أولئِك سنؤتيهم», «أولئك» being a mubtadaʾ and «سنؤتيهم» its khabar, and the clause being the khabar of the first. «أولئك» may also be accusative by an omitted verb explained by what follows, making it a case of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb). But this analysis is outweighed, in that «زيدٌ ضربته» «[Translator's note: the text has «ضرتبه», a misprint.]» in the nominative is better than its accusative, because it does not require an implied word; and because there is disagreement among us over fronting the governed word of a verb accompanied by a particle of futurity (ḥarf al-tanfīs) in the like of «سأضربُ زيداً»: some forbade «زيداً سأضرب»; and the condition for ishtighāl is that the governing word can act on what precedes it. So it is better to take it on what involves no disagreement.

Ḥamza read: «سيؤتيهم» with yāʾ, in keeping with the overt [third person] in His saying {والمؤمنون بالله}; the rest read with nūn, by way of iltifāt (shift of person) for majesty, and to correspond with His saying «وأعتدْنا». Both are clear.

semin-durr:163-163.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {كَمَآ أَوْحَيْنَآ}: the kāf is the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a revelation like Our revealing"; or it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from that omitted maṣdar, construed as definite, i.e. "We revealed it", i.e. the revelation, while it resembles Our revelation to those mentioned. This is the school of Sībawayh, and its verification has preceded. «ما» admits two analyses: that it is maṣdariyya, in which case it needs no returning pronoun according to the correct view; and that it is in the sense of «الذي», in which case the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "like that which We revealed to Nūḥ". «من بعده» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أوْحينا»; «من» may not be explicative [here], because the ḥāl is a predicate in meaning, and an adverb of time is not predicated of a concrete being except by an interpretation for which this is not the place. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted that it be attached to «النبيين» itself, meaning that it is in the sense of the verb, as if it were said "and those who became prophets after him"; and it is a good meaning.

In «يونس» there are six dialectal forms. The most eloquent: a pure wāw and nūn with ḍamma; it is the dialect of the Ḥijāz. Kasra on the nūn after the wāw is reported, and Nāfiʿ read with it in the transmission of Ḥibbān. Fatḥa on it with the wāw is also reported; al-Nakhaʿī read with it, and it is the dialect of some of ʿUqayl. Some made these two readings transferred from the verb, active or passive, making this name derived from «الأنس» (intimacy), the hamza having been changed to wāw only because it is vowelless and preceded by ḍamma; evidence for this is its occurrence with hamza on the original pattern in some dialects, as will come. But there is a reservation about this, because this name is foreign. All three vowels on the nūn are reported with the wāw pronounced as hamza, as though they changed the wāw to hamza because of the ḍamma before it, as in:

167 - 6- أَحَبُّ المُؤْقِدينَ إليَّ موسى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(The dearest of fire-kindlers to me is Mūsā …)

and its explanation has preceded. It is reported that ḍamma on the nūn with the hamza is the dialect of some of Banū Asad «[Translator's note: the text has «بضع» "a few", apparently for «بعض» "some".]», though I do not know that any of the hamza dialects was read. This is if we say that this name is not transferred from a verb, active or passive, in the case of kasra or fatḥa on the nūn. But if we say that, then the hamza is original, not changed from wāw, since it is derived from «الأنس». As for [the form] with ḍamma on the nūn, it should be said that the hamza is a substitute for the wāw, since verbality is excluded with ḍamma on the nūn.

His saying: {زَبُوراً}: the majority read with fatḥa on the zāy, and Ḥamza with ḍamma. On it there are three analyses. The first: that it is the plural of «زَبْر». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "the plural of «زَبْر», which is a writing", and he mentioned nothing else; he means that it is originally a maṣdar on the pattern faʿl, then pluralized on the pattern fuʿūl, as in «فَلْس» and «فُلوس», «قَلْس» and «قُلُوس». Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī preceded him in this view, in one of the two explanations reported from him. Abū ʿAlī said: "It may be a plural of «زَبْر» applied to what is written, as they said 'the striking of the emir' and 'the weaving of Yemen', just as what is written is called «كتاب»." Abū ʿAlī means that it is a maṣdar standing in place of the mafʿūl bihi (object), as he illustrated.

The second: that it is the plural of «زَبُور» in the reading of the generality, but with deletion of the augments, i.e. the wāw was deleted from it so the word became «زَبُر»; this is Abū ʿAlī's second explanation. Abū ʿAlī said: "As they said «ظريف» and «ظُروف», «كَرَوان» and «كَرْوان», «وَرَشان» and «وِرْشان», on the supposition of deleting the yāʾ and the alif." There is nothing wrong with this, for the broken plural and the diminutive mostly run along the same course, and we have seen them form diminutives by deleting the augments, as in «زُهَيْر» and «حُمَيْد» from «أزهر» and «محمود»; the grammarians call it "the diminutive of truncation" (taṣghīr al-tarkhīm). So it is with the broken plural.

The third: that it is a singular noun, namely a maṣdar coming on the pattern fuʿūl, like «الدُّخول», «القُعود» and «الجُلوس»; Abū al-Baqāʾ and others said this. There is a reservation about it, in that fuʿūl is a maṣdar of the intransitive, and is not one of the transitive except in memorized words such as «اللُّزوم» and «النُّهوك»; and «زَبَر», as you see, is transitive, so making fuʿūl its maṣdar is weak. The meaning of this root has preceded.

semin-durr:71-71.t:
(والحَذَر والحِذْر) are two dialectal forms with one meaning. It has been said that in this construction only «خُذْ حِذْرك», with kasra, has been heard, not «حَذَرك». His words: «ثُباتٍ» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise [«جميعاً»; the meaning is: "go forth in groups, dispersed, detachment after detachment, or assembled as a single troop"]. Al-Shaykh said: "As far as I know it has only been read with kasra on the tāʾ." End of quotation. This is the most eloquent dialectal form. Some Arabs put the sound feminine plural in the accusative with fatḥa when it is weak in its final radical and the feminine tāʾ compensates for it; al-Farrāʾ recited:
1604 - فلمَّا جَلاها بالأُيام تَحيَّزَتْ ... ثباتاً عليها ذُلُّها واكتئابُها
(When he drove them out with smoke, they gathered in groups, humiliation and dejection upon them.)
It has been read, irregularly, «ويَجْعلون لله البناتَ» with fatḥa; and «سمعتُ لغاتَهم» (I heard their dialects) has been reported. Al-Fārisī claimed that what has come of that is a singular whose final radical has been restored, because the original is «لُغَوَة», and when the final radical was restored it was changed into alif. Al-Fārisī was rebutted on the ground that this obliges him to combine the compensation and what it compensates for; he is also refuted by the reading mentioned earlier in «البناتَ», because its singular has kasra on the first radical. I have clarified this question as fully as possible in my book «Sharḥ al-Tashīl».
«ثباتٍ» is the plural of «ثُبَة», whose original measure is fuʿala, like «حُطَمة»; its final radical was omitted and compensated for by the feminine tāʾ. Is its final radical wāw or yāʾ? There are two views. The argument for the first view is that it is derived from «ثَبا يَثْبو», like «خلا يَخْلو», i.e. to gather. The argument for the second is that it is derived from «ثَبَيْتُ على الرجل» when you praised him, as though you gathered his good qualities. It is given a plural with alif and tāʾ and with wāw and nūn; when it is pluralised as «ثُبين», its first radical may have ḍamma or kasra, and likewise everything resembling it, such as «قُلة» and «بُرة», as long as it is not given a broken plural. Al-thuba is a group of men above ten; it has also been said: two and three. Its diminutive is «ثُبَيَّة», with restoration of what was omitted. As for «ثُبَةُ الحوضِ», which is the middle of the basin, what is omitted from it is its middle radical, because it is from «يَثُوب الماءُ», i.e. the water returns; its diminutive is «ثُوَيْبة», as you say in the diminutive of «سَنَة»: «سُنَيْهة».
Al-nafar is hastening in alarm; one says «نَفَر إليه», i.e. he hastened to him in alarm. In its imperfect there are two dialectal forms: ḍamma and kasra on the middle radical. It has also been said: one says «نَفَر الرجل يَنْفِر» with kasra, and «نَفَرت الدابةُ تنفُر» with ḍamma, so they distinguished the two in the imperfect; this distinction is refuted by the reading of al-Aʿmash «فانفُروا» and «أو انفُروا» with ḍamma in both. The maṣdar is «النَّفير», «النُّفور» and «النَّفْر»; and «النَّفَر» is a group, like «القوم» and «الرهط».
His words: {وَإِنَّ مِنْكُمْ لَمَن لَّيُبَطِّئَنَّ}: «منكم» is the fronted khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ», and its noun is «لَمَنْ»; the lām entered on the noun for emphasis since it was separated from «إنَّ» by the khabar. «مَنْ» may be a relative noun or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective. On the lām in «لَيُبَطِّئَنْ» there are two views. The more correct: it is the answer to an omitted oath, its implied form being "Allah swore: he will surely lag behind"; and the two clauses — I mean the oath and its answer — are the ṣila (relative clause) of «مَنْ» or an adjective of it [Translator's note: printed «هلا»; read «لها»], according to the two views mentioned. The referent pronoun on both assumptions is the pronoun put in the nominative by «ليبطِّئن», the implied form being: "and among you is one who — or a party that — by Allah, will surely lag behind".
Some grammarians argued from this verse that it is permissible to complete the relative noun with an oath-clause and its answer when the oath-clause is devoid of a pronoun referring back to the relative noun, as in «جاء الذي أحلفُ باللَّهِ لقد قام أبوه» (there came the one who — I swear by Allah — his father stood up), and made it a rebuttal of the early grammarians, who claimed it was disallowed. But there is no evidence in that, since someone may say: I only assume that omitted oath to contain a pronoun referring back to the relative noun.
The second view — Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted it from some — is that it is the lām of emphasis after emphasis; this is an error on the part of whoever said it. The majority read «لَيُبَطِّئَنْ» with the ṭāʾ doubled, and Mujāhid with it undoubled. On both readings the verb may be intransitive or transitive. One says «أَبْطَأَ» and «بَطَّأَ» in the sense of «بَطُؤَ», i.e. to be sluggish and hold back; these two are intransitive. If one assumes they are transitive, their object is omitted, i.e. "he will surely hold back others", i.e. discourage them and make them cowardly about fighting. «إذا لم أكن» is an adverbial governed in the accusative by «أنعم الله».

semin-durr:73-73.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لَيَقُولَنَّ}: the majority read the lām of «ليقولَنَّ» with fatḥa, because it is a verb attributed to the pronoun of «مَنْ», indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because of the nūn of emphasis. Al-Ḥasan read it with ḍamma, attributing the verb also to the pronoun of «مَنْ», but construing it according to its meaning; the original form is «ليقولونَنَّ», and its morphology has preceded.
His words: {كَأَن لَّمْ تَكُنْ}: this is «كَأَنْ» lightened from the heavy form, and its governing remains according to the Basrans. The Kufans claimed that when lightened it does not govern, just as «لكن» lightened does not govern according to the majority. Its governing according to the Basrans is mostly on the pronoun of the matter and the affair (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn), which must be omitted; according to them it does not govern another pronoun or an overt noun except in poetic necessity, as in his words:
1605 - وصدرٍ مشرقِ النَّحْرِ ... كَأَنْ ثَدْيَيْهِ حُقَّانِ
(And a bosom bright of throat, as if its two breasts were two small round boxes.)
And the words of another:
1606 - ويوماً تُوافينا بوجهٍ مُقَسَّمٍ ... كأنْ ظبيةٍ تَعْطُوا إلى وارِق السَّلَمْ
(And one day she meets us with a beautiful face, as though [she were] a gazelle stretching toward the leafy salam-tree.)
in one of the transmissions. The apparent sense of Sībawayh's statement is that it governs other than the pronoun of the matter outside poetic necessity; his text may be consulted in his Book. The negated clause after it is in the position of nominative as its khabar (predicate). If the clause after it is verbal, it is introduced by «قد» [Translator's note: printed «قدر»] as in his words:
1607 - لا يَهُولَنْكَ اصطلاُؤكَ للحَرْ ... بِ فمحذورُها كَأَنْ قد أَلَمَّا
(Let not your exposure to the heat of war frighten you, for what is feared of it is as though it has already come.)
or by «لم», as in this verse and His words {كَأَن لَّمْ تَغْنَ بالأمس} [Yūnus: 24]. It has been introduced by «لَمَّا» in the words of ʿAmmār al-Kalbī:
1608 - بَدَّدَتْ منها الليالِي شَمْلَهمْ ... فكأنْ لمَّا يكونوا قبلُ ثَمّْ
(The nights scattered their gathering from it, so it is as though they had not been there before.)
Al-Shaykh said: "The like of this needs to be heard from the Arabs." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«كَأَنْ» contains the meaning of likening, but it is not like the heavy form in needing a noun and a khabar; only clauses come after it." The apparent sense of this statement is that it does not govern when lightened; it has preceded that this is the view of the Kufans, not the Basrans. He may have meant by that that the clause after it is not affected by it in its wording, because its noun is omitted and the clause is its khabar.
Ibn Kathīr and Ḥafṣ read «يَكُنْ» with yāʾ, because «المودة» has the meaning of «الودّ», and because it has been separated from its verb; the rest read with tāʾ, taking account of its wording. «يكون» may be complete (tāmma), in which case the adverbial is attached to it, or to an omitted element because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مودة», since it was originally an adjective of an indefinite noun placed before it; or it may be incomplete (nāqiṣa), in which case the adverbial is attached to an omitted element as its khabar.
People disagreed about this clause, with three views. The first: it has no grammatical position, being parenthetical. On this view, between what is it interposed? There are two views. The first of them: it is interposed between the conditional clause, which is «فإنْ أصابَتْكم», and the oath clause, which is «ولَئِنْ أصابَتْكم», the implied form being: "If a calamity befalls you, he says: Allah has favoured me in that I was not present with them — as though there had been no affection between you and him — and if bounty befalls you…"; so the parenthetical clause, I mean His words {كَأَن لَّمْ تَكُنْ بَيْنَكُمْ}, was postponed while its intended place is in the middle. This is the view of al-Zajjāj, and al-Māturīdī followed him.
Al-Rāghib al-Iṣfahānī rejected this view on the ground that it is ugly, because one does not separate between part of a clause and part of what is connected to another clause. I say: this from al-Zajjāj seems to be an explanation of meaning, not of grammatical analysis; this is indicated by what I shall mention from him in explanation of the analysis. The second of the two views: it is interposed between the verb of saying and its object, the original being: "he will surely say: would that I had been with them — as though there had not been…". Most people hold this, but their expressions about it differ, and the meaning only becomes clear by transmitting their texts, so let us transmit them. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a parenthesis between the verb, which is «ليقولَنَّ», and its object, which is «ياليتني»; the meaning is: as though no affection had previously existed between him and you, because the hypocrites used to show affection to the believers outwardly, even though they sought calamities for them inwardly. The apparent view is that it is sarcasm, because they were the most hostile of enemies to the believers and the most envious of them; so how could they be described with affection except by way of inversion and sarcasm?" Al-Zajjāj said: "This clause is a parenthesis; Allah the Exalted informed of that because they used to show affection to the believers." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The hypocrite offers the believers affection and pledges to commit to the obligations of Islam, then stays behind out of hypocrisy, doubt and disbelief in Allah and His Messenger; then, when the unseen is revealed, he wishes for the victory of the believers [Translator's note: so in the source]. On this view the words of Allah the Exalted {كَأَن لَّمْ تَكُن} come as an eloquent turning aside and a parenthesis between the saying and what is said, in wording that shows additional ugliness of their deed." Al-Rāzī said: "It is a parenthesis of the utmost beauty, because whoever loves a person rejoices at his joy and grieves at his grief; so when he reverses the case, that is a display of enmity. Allah the Exalted related the hypocrite's pleasure at the misfortune of the Muslims, then wished to relate his grief at the Muslims' success because of his missing the spoils; so before mentioning the speech in full He put forward His words «كأن لم تكن», the intent being wonder, as though He says: look at what this hypocrite says, as though there were never any affection or association at all between you and him. What made parenthesis with this clause good — even though its place is later — is that what follows it is a verse-ending (fāṣila), whereas it is not a verse-ending." Al-Fārisī said: "This clause is part of the speech of the hypocrites to those whom they made stay behind from jihad while they themselves went out: 'as though there had been no [affection] between you and him', i.e. between [you and] the Messenger, peace be upon him, so that he would take you out with him to take some of the spoils — in order to make the Messenger hateful to them thereby." So he made the pronoun in «بينه» refer back to the Prophet, peace be upon him.
Al-Fārisī followed Muqātil in that. Muqātil said: "Its meaning is: as though he were not of the people of your religion and there were no affection between you", meaning that the one who lags behind said to those who stayed behind from the campaign — the hypocrites, the weak among the believers, and those who stayed behind with permission: "as though there had been no affection between you and Muhammad, so that he would take you out to jihad and you would win [Translator's note: printed «فتفوزا»; read «فتفوزوا»] what he won."
The second of the views: it is in the position of accusative through the verb of saying, so Allah the Exalted has related through the saying two clauses: the clause of likening and the clause of wishing. This is apparent according to the view of Muqātil and al-Fārisī, since they claimed that the pronoun in «بينه» is for the Messenger, peace be upon him.
The third: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «ليقولَنَّ», as you say «مررت بزيدٍ وكأَنْ لم يكنْ بينك وبينه معرفةٌ فضلاً عن مودةٍ» (I passed by Zayd, and it was as though there were no acquaintance between you and him, let alone affection). This has been transmitted from al-Zajjāj, and Abū al-Baqāʾ followed him in it. I have spoken at length on this verse only because I saw people's views on it scattered, so I gathered them.
On «يا» there are two views. The first — the view of al-Fārisī — is that it is merely for drawing attention, so no omitted addressee is assumed; for that reason it is directly followed by the particle. The second: the addressee is omitted, its implied form being "O these, would that I…". This disagreement applies to it whenever it is directly followed by a particle or a verb, as in the reading of al-Kisāʾī «ألا يا اسْجُدوا», and his words:
1609 - ألا يا اسقياني قبل غارةِ سنجالِ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O, give me drink, you two, before the raid of Sinjāl…)
and his words:
1610 - يا حبَّذا جَبَلُ الريَّانِ من جبلٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O how excellent is the mountain of al-Rayyān as a mountain…)
according to the view that «حَبَّذا» is verbal. That is done only with «يا» specifically, not with the other vocative particles, because it is the principal one of the category; and it is frequently followed directly by «ليت», unlike the other particles.
His words: {فَأَفُوزَ}: the majority hold that it is accusative in answer to the wish. The Kufans claim that it is accusative by divergence (khilāf), and al-Jarmī claims that it is accusative by the fāʾ itself. The first is correct, because the fāʾ conjoins this maṣdar, interpreted from «أن» and the verb, to an imagined maṣdar, since the implied form is: "would that I had being with them, or their company, and so winning". These doctrines have another place for their verification and refutation, to which I have drawn attention more than once. Al-Ḥasan read «فأفوزُ» in the nominative, on one of two views: either as resumptive, i.e. "so I would win", or conjoined to «كنت», so that it too enters the domain of the wish; then being with them and the great winning are both wished for.

semin-durr:128-128.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِنِ امرأة}: «امرأةٌ» is the fāʿil (agent) of an implied verb whose implication is obligatory; this is of the type of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb). It may not be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), because the conditional particle is followed only by a verb according to the majority of the Basrans, in contrast to al-Akhfash and the Kufans. The implied form is: "and if a woman fears, [if she] fears", and similar to it is: {وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِّنَ المشركين استجارك} [al-Tawba: 6]. The Basrans argued for their position that the verb has come in the jussive (majzūm) after the noun that follows the conditional particle, in the words of ʿAdī:
1661 - ومتى واغِلٌ يَنُبْهُمْ يُحَيُّو ... هُ وتُعْطَفْ عليه كأسُ الساقي
(And whenever an uninvited guest drops in on them, they greet him, and the cup-bearer's cup is turned towards him.)
And {مِنْ بعلها} may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «خافت», which is the apparent view; or it may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «نُشوزاً», since it is originally an adjective of an indefinite noun, and when it was placed before it, making it an adjective became impossible, so it was made accusative as a ḥāl. And «فلا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
His words: {أَن يُصْلِحَا} — the Kufans read «يُصْلِحا», from «أصلح»; the rest of the Seven read «يَصَّالحا», with a doubled ṣād followed by an alif; ʿUthmān al-Battī and al-Jaḥdarī read «يَصَّلِحا», with a doubled ṣād and no alif; ʿUbayda al-Salmānī read «يُصالِحا», with ḍamma on the yāʾ and an undoubled ṣād followed by an alif, from the pattern mufāʿala; and Ibn Masʿūd and al-Aʿmash read «أن اصَّالحا». The reading of the Kufans is clear. The reading of the rest of the Seven is originally «يتصالحا»; assimilation was intended for lightness, so the tāʾ was replaced by a ṣād and assimilated. The reading of ʿUthmān is originally «يَصْطَلِحا»; it was lightened by replacing the ṭāʾ — which is itself a replacement for the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl pattern — with a ṣād and assimilating them into what follows. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its origin is «يَصْتَلِحا»; the tāʾ was replaced with a ṣād and the first was assimilated into it." This is not good, because the tāʾ of iftiʿāl must be changed to a ṭāʾ after the four letters, as its examination preceded in al-Baqara, so there is no need to posit it as a tāʾ, because if the verb were pronounced without assimilation, the tāʾ would not be pronounced in it except to show its origin. The reading of ʿUbayda is clear, because it is from muṣālaḥa. And the reading «يصطلحا» is clearer still. There was no disagreement over «صُلْحاً», despite their disagreement over its verb.
There are several views on its accusative. On the reading of the Kufans, it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), and what makes it accusative is either the preceding verb — it being a maṣdar with the augment letters dropped, and some express this by saying it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), like «العطاء» and «النبات» — or an implied verb, i.e. "so that the state between them is set right with a settlement". On these two implied forms there are two views about the object. One of them: that it is «بينهما», the adverb being treated broadly and made a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The second: that it is omitted, and «بينهما» is an adverb, or a ḥāl from «صلحا», since it is originally its adjective. «صلحاً» may also be accusative as a mafʿūl bihi if you make it a name for the thing agreed upon, like «العَطاء» meaning "what is given" and «النبات» meaning "what is grown". On the other readings, it may be a maṣdar on one of the two implied forms mentioned above — I mean its being a noun of the maṣdar, or its being with the augments dropped — so it stands in the place of «تصالحا», «اصطلاحاً» or «مصالحةً», according to the readings mentioned above; and it may be accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. «بصلح», i.e. by something that comes about through the reconciliation, if we make it a name for the thing agreed upon.
In sum, on the other readings the view of the mafʿūl bihi mentioned for the Kufans' reading is excluded, and the remaining views stay permissible in all the readings.
His words: {والصلح خَيْرٌ} are a mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate). Al-Zamakhsharī said of this clause and the one after it: "They are both a parenthesis," and he did not explain that. It is as though he means that His words «وإنْ يَتفَرَّقا» are conjoined to His words «فلا جناح», so the two clauses came between them as a parenthesis — this is what the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said, and there is an objection to it, for after them come other clauses, so al-Zamakhsharī ought to have said of all of them that they are a parenthesis, and not restricted it to «والصلح خير» and «وأُحْضِرَت الأنفسُ». Rather, al-Zamakhsharī means by that the parenthesis between His words {وَإِنِ امرأة} and His words {وَإِن تُحْسِنُواْ}, for they are two conjoined conditions; this is indicated by his explanation of it in terms that convey this meaning, for he said: "And if you do good by remaining with your wives even though you dislike them and love others, and guard against ill-treatment and turning away." End of quotation. The alif and lām in «الصلح» may be for the genus, or for prior reference (ʿahd) because it was mentioned before, as in: {فعصى فِرْعَوْنُ الرسول} [al-Muzzammil: 16]. And «خير» may be for comparison in its proper sense, with what it is compared to omitted; it was said its implied form is "than ill-treatment and turning away", and it was said "better than separation"; the first implied form is preferable because of the verbal indication. It may also be a mere adjective, i.e. "and settlement is a good among goods", just as dispute is an evil among evils.
His words: {وَأُحْضِرَتِ الأنفس الشح}: «حَضَر» takes one object, and with the hamza it acquired a second object; when it was made passive, one of them stood in place of the fāʿil and the other remained accusative. What stands in place of the fāʿil here may be one of two things. The more apparent of them — and it is the well-known position among the grammarians — is that it is the first, namely «الأنفس», for it is the fāʿil originally, since the original is: «حضرت الأنفسُ الشحَّ» ("the souls were present to avarice"). The second: that it is the second object, the original being "and avarice was present to the souls", then "Allah made avarice present to the souls"; when the verb was made passive, the second — namely «الأنفس» — was put in place of the fāʿil, and the first was placed after and remained accusative. On this view one may say «أُعْطِي درهمٌ زيداً» and «كُسِي جبةً عمراً» [sic]; the reverse is the well-known [usage], as has preceded. [Translator's note: the second example appears in the source as «كُسِي جبةً عمراً», with both nouns accusative; it is translated as written.] Al-Zamakhsharī's words allow that the second is what stands in place of the fāʿil, for he said: "The meaning of making avarice present to the souls is that avarice was made present to them, never absent from them nor separate" — meaning that they are innately disposed to it; so he attributed the presence to avarice, as you see. It is also possible that he made it of the type of inversion (qalb), attributing the presence to avarice while in reality it is attributed to the souls. Al-ʿAdawī read «الشِحَّ» with kasra on the shīn, which is a dialectal form. «الشُّحُّ» is stinginess combined with greed, so it is more specific than stinginess.

semin-durr:129-129.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {كُلَّ الميل}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), it being established that «كل» takes the character of what it is annexed to: if it is annexed to a maṣdar it is [a maṣdar], and likewise if annexed to an adverb or something else. His words: {فَتَذَرُوهَا} — there are two views on it. The first: that it is accusative by an implied «أَنْ» in answer to the prohibition. The second: that it is jussive (majzūm), conjoined to the verb before it, i.e. "and do not leave her". In the first, there is a prohibition of combining the two; in the second, a prohibition of each separately, and that is more eloquent. The pronoun in «تَذَروها» refers to the one from whom [the husband] turns away, as the context indicates her. His words: {كالمعلقة} are a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ها» in «تَذَروها», so it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted element, i.e. "and leave her resembling one suspended". In my view it may also be a second object, because your saying «تذر» means «تترك», and «تَرَكَ» takes two objects when it means "to make".

semin-durr:131-131.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِيَّاكُمْ} is conjoined to «الذين أُوتوا», and here it must be separate because attachment is impossible. Some argued from this verse that when the attached pronoun is possible, one may turn to the detached pronoun, because it would have been possible to say «ولقد وَصَّيْناكم والذين أوتوا». Likewise they argued from the words of Allah the Exalted: {يُخْرِجُونَ الرسول وَإِيَّاكُمْ} [al-Mumtaḥana: 1], since one could say «يخرجونكم والرسولَ». This does not prove it. As for the first verse, because the speech in it came in the order of actual occurrence, for the injunction to those before us preceded the injunction to us; since this meaning was intended, it was impossible — in this case — for the attached pronoun to be possible. As for the second verse, because in it the prior mention of the Messenger was intended, to honour him and to censure those who dared such a heinous act; so it was impossible — in this case — to bring it as attached. «ومِنْ قبلكم» may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أوتوا», and may be attached to «وَصَّيْنا»; the first is more apparent.
His words: {أَنِ اتقوا} — two views are possible regarding «أن». The first: that it is maṣdariyya (infinitival), with omission of the preposition, its implied form being «بأن اتَّقوا»; when the preposition was omitted, the well-known disagreement applied to it. The second: that it is the explicative [«أن»], because it comes after something that has the meaning of speech but not its letters, namely "injunction". The apparent view is that His words {وَإِن تَكْفُرُواْ} are a resumptive clause informing of this state, not included in what the injunction governs. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«وإنْ تكفروا فإن لله» is conjoined to «اتقوا», because the meaning is: We commanded them and commanded you with piety, and We said to them and to you: if you disbelieve." There is an objection to his words, because his positing "saying" negates the conditional clause's being included within the scope of the injunction with respect to grammatical craft, and he did not intend only an explanation of meaning; rather he intended that and an explanation of the i'rab, as shown by his saying: "conjoined to «اتقوا»", and «اتقوا» is within the scope of the injunction, whether you make «أن» maṣdariyya or explicative.

semin-durr:133-133.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {بِآخَرِينَ}: «آخرين» is the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted noun qualified by it, of the same kind as what preceded it, its implied form being "by other people who worship Allah". The omitted noun may also be of a different kind from what preceded it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It may be a threat to all the children of Adam, and the others would be of a different kind from them, as it was narrated that there were angels on earth worshipping Allah." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or other creatures than humans," and others said likewise. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected this view on the ground that the sense of «آخر» and «أخرى», and their duals and plurals, is like the sense of «غير», except that it is specific to the kind of what preceded it. So if you say «اشتريت فرساً وآخرَ» ('I bought a horse and another'), or «ثوباً وآخر», or «جارية وأخرى», or «جاريتين وأُخْريين», or «جواري وأُخَرَ», all of that can only be of the kind of what preceded, so that if you meant "and another donkey" in the preceding examples it would not be permissible. This is unlike «غير», for it may be of the kind of what preceded or of another kind: you say «اشتريت ثوباً وغيره», and if you meant "and a horse other than it", it would be permissible. He said: "Few know this difference." This difference that he mentioned, and by which he rebutted these great scholars, is not agreed upon; he did not base it on transmitted usage. But this may be rebutted against them by another route, namely that «آخرين» is an adjective of an omitted noun, and the adjective does not stand in place of the noun it qualifies unless it is specific to it, as in «مررت بكاتبٍ» ('I passed by a writer'), or some evidence indicates it; here it is not specific, so it must be of the kind of the first, so that thereby the indication of the omitted noun is obtained.

semin-durr:134-134.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {مَّن كَانَ يُرِيدُ}: two views are possible for «مَنْ». The more apparent of them: that it is conditional, and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is His words {فَعِندَ الله}; there must be an implied pronoun in this apodosis referring back to the conditional noun, for the reason established before; the implied form is: "then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter for him, if he wants it"; this is al-Zamakhsharī's implied form. He said: "so that the apodosis is connected with the condition." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] permitted — and made it the apparent view — that the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being: "whoever wants the reward of this world, let him not restrict himself to it, and let him seek both rewards, for with Allah is the reward of both abodes." The second: that it is a relative noun, and the fāʾ entered the khabar (predicate) because of its resemblance to the conditional noun; this is made unlikely by the verb after it being past tense [and the returning pronoun is omitted, as its illustration has been established].

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ}: a condition, and regarding its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) there are two analyses. The first: it is His saying {فانكحوا}. That is because they used to marry eight and ten [wives] and not fulfil their rights; so when {وَلاَ تأكلوا أَمْوَالَهُمْ} was revealed, they began to feel uneasy about the guardianship of orphans. So it was said to them: if you fear injustice regarding the rights of orphans, then fear also injustice regarding the rights of women, and marry this number; because a large number leads to injustice, and repentance from a sin does not avail while committing its like.

The second: the apodosis is His saying «فواحدةً». The meaning: a man among them used to marry the orphan girl who was under his guardianship; so when the verse containing the threat for consuming the orphan's wealth was revealed, they felt uneasy about that. So it was said to them: if you fear [injustice] in marrying orphan women, then marry what is good [to you] of unrelated women, i.e. those not under your guardianship. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «فانحكوا», a misprint for «فانكحوا».] On this, a muḍāf must be implied, i.e. in marrying the orphans among women. If it is said: «فواحدةً» is the apodosis of His saying {فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلاَّ تَعْدِلُواْ}, so how can it be the apodosis of the first? It was answered that He repeated the second condition, because it is like the first in meaning, since the separation between the first and its apodosis grew long. There is in this a question not hidden from one who reflects on it.

The fear here is in its proper sense, what is meant by it being caution. Abū ʿUbayda said that it is in the sense of certainty, and cited:
1530 - فقلتُ لهم خافوا بألفَي مُدَجَّجٍ ... سَراتُهُم في الفارسي المُسَرَّدِ
(I said to them: be sure of two thousand fully armed men, their chiefs clad in close-woven Persian mail.)
i.e. be certain. The verification of that and the refutation of him has preceded, and that there are three views on the question, at His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلاَّ يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ الله} [al-Baqara: 229].

His saying: {أَلاَّ تُقْسِطُواْ}: if you imply that it is on the omission of a preposition, i.e. «مِنْ أن لا», then the well-known disagreement applies to it: is it in the position of the accusative or the genitive? But if you do not imply that, but the verb reaches it by itself, as if you had said «فإن حذرتم» (if you are wary of), then it is in the position of the accusative only, as preceded in al-Baqara.

The majority read «تُقْسطوا» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, from «أقسط» when one acts justly; so «لا» on this reading is negating, the implied form being: and if you fear the absence of iqsāṭ, i.e. justice. Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it with fatḥa, from «قسط»; and there are two interpretations of it. The first: that «قَسَط» is in the sense of «جار» (to act unjustly); this is the well-known [usage] in the language — I mean that the quadriliteral is in the sense of acting justly and the triliteral in the sense of acting unjustly, as though the hamza in it were for privation (salb), so the meaning of «أقسط» is: he removed the qasṭ, which is injustice. On this view «لا» is redundant (zāʾida) and nothing else; otherwise the meaning would be corrupted; as it is in His saying {لِّئَلاَّ يَعْلَمَ} [al-Ḥadīd: 29]. The second: al-Zajjāj related that the triliteral «قسط» is used as the quadriliteral «أقسط» is used; on this «لا» is not redundant, as in the well-known reading; however, the distinction is what is known in the language.

Al-Rāghib said: "القِسْط is that one takes another's share (qisṭ), and that is injustice; and الإِقساط is that one gives another his share, and that is fairness. Hence it is said: قَسَط الرجل when he acts unjustly, and أقسط when he acts justly. He, the Exalted, said: {وَأَمَّا القاسطون فَكَانُواْ لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَباً} [al-Jinn: 15], and He, the Exalted, said: {وأقسطوا إِنَّ الله يُحِبُّ المقسطين} [al-Ḥujurāt: 9]."

Among the strange things related is that when al-Ḥajjāj had the famous scholar Saʿīd ibn Jubayr brought before him, he said to him: "What do you say about me?" He said: "قاسط عادل" (qāsiṭ, ʿādil), which pleased those present. So al-Ḥajjāj said to them: "Woe to you! You did not understand him. He has made me an unjust man and an unbeliever. Have you not heard His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَمَّا القاسطون فَكَانُواْ لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَباً}, and His saying, the Exalted: {ثْمَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ} [al-Anʿām: 1]?" [Translator's note: the printed text reads «تسعموا», a misprint for «تسمعوا». The point is that «عادل» can mean one who sets up equals to his Lord, from «يعدلون» in that verse.] The full discussion of this root has preceded at His saying {قَآئِمَاً بالقسط} [Āl ʿImrān: 18].

His saying: {مَا طَابَ}: regarding this «ما» there are [several] analyses. The first: it is in the sense of «الذي»; that is according to whoever holds that «ما» may be used for rational beings, which is a well-known question. Someone said: "What made its occurrence here good is that it falls on women, and they are deficient in intellect." Some say: it is for the attributes of rational beings. Some say: for the kind of rational beings, as if it were said: the good kind of women. These are close expressions; hence we did not count them as [separate] analyses.

The second: it is an indefinite qualified noun (nakira mawṣūfa), i.e. marry a good kind, or a good number.

The third: it is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and that maṣdar (verbal noun) occurs in the place of an active participle, its implied form being: so marry the good [ones]. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said here: "The maṣdar here is implied by the active participle, and the meaning is: so marry with the marrying that is good for you"; and the first is more evident.

The fourth: it is temporal (ẓarfiyya), and the temporal entails the infinitival; the implied form being: so marry for the period in which marrying is good for you. When this is established: if we say that it is a nominal relative, or an indefinite qualified noun, or infinitival with the maṣdar occurring in the place of the active participle, then «ما» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «انكحوا». And «من النساء» then has two analyses. The first: it is to explain the vague genus in «ما», according to those who affirm that [function] for it. The second: it is partitive, i.e. some of the women, and it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ما طاب». But if we say it is infinitival-temporal, or purely infinitival, and the maṣdar is not put in the place of an active participle, as was related earlier from the Shaykh, then the object of «فانكحوا» is His saying «من النساء», as in your saying «أكلت من الرغيف، وشربت من العسل» (I ate of the loaf and drank of the honey), i.e. something of the loaf and something of the honey. [Translator's note: the printed text has «من نساء» here; the verse reads «من النساء».] If it is said: why not make, on this, «مَثْنى» and what follows it the object of «فانكحوا», i.e. so marry this number? The answer: these deflected words (maʿdūla) do not immediately follow governors.

Ibn Abī ʿAbla read: «مَنْ طاب», and this supports «ما» being in the sense of «الذي» for rational beings. In the codex of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: «طِيب» with yāʾ; this is not passive, because it is intransitive; it was only written so to indicate the imāla (inclination of the vowel), and it is the reading of Ḥamza.

His saying: {مَثْنى}: accusative as a ḥāl from «ما طاب». Abū al-Baqāʾ made it a ḥāl from «النساء»; and he and Ibn ʿAṭiyya permitted that it be a badal (substitute) of «ما». These two analyses are weak. As for the first, because what is spoken about is only the relative noun, and His saying «من النساء» came as a kind of clarification. As for the second, because the badal is on the intention of repeating the governor, and it has preceded that these words do not directly follow governors.

Know that there is disagreement about these deflected words: is analogy (qiyās) permissible in them, or are they restricted to what is heard? Two views: the view of the Basrans is no analogy, and the view of the Kufans and Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] is that it is permissible. What has been heard of them is eleven words: أُحاد and مَوْحَد, ثُناء and مَثْنى, ثُلاث and مَثْلَث, رُباع and مَرْبع, and مَخْمس — خُماس was not heard — and عُشار and مَعْشر. They also disagreed about their being declined (taking tanwīn) or not: the majority of grammarians hold that they are not [they are diptotes]; al-Farrāʾ permitted declining them, although not declining was preferable in his view. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «منعة», a misprint for «منعه».]

They also disagreed about the cause of their being diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf), on four positions. The first is the position of Sībawayh, namely that they are diptote because of deflection (ʿadl) and being descriptive (waṣf). As for the description, it is evident; as for the deflection, it is because they are deflected from one form to another; that is, they are deflected from a repeated number. So when you say «جاء القوم أحادَ أو مَوْحَدَ، أو ثُلاثَ أو مَثْلَثَ», it is equivalent to your saying «جاؤوا واحداً واحداً وثلاثةً ثلاثة» (they came one by one, and three by three). What is deflected from is not intended for emphasis; it is only intended for the repetition of the number, as in their saying «عَلَّمْتُه الحسابَ باباً باباً» (I taught him arithmetic chapter by chapter).

The second: the position of al-Farrāʾ, which is deflection and definiteness through the intention of the alif and lām; hence their annexation is barred in his view because of the implied alif and lām, and the overt appearance of the alif and lām is barred in his view because they are intended as annexed.

The third: the position of Abū Isḥāq: their deflection from a repeated number, and their deflection from the feminine.

The fourth, reported by al-Akhfash from some: that it is a repetition of deflection. That is, it is deflected from the wording of «اثنين اثنين» and from its meaning, because it is not used in a place where the non-deflected numbers are used: you say «جاءني اثنان وثلاثة» (two and three came to me), but you do not say «جاءني مَثْنى وثلاث» unless a plural precedes it, because this chapter was made to explain the order of the action. So when you say «جاء القوم مَثْنَى», it conveys that their coming occurred two by two, unlike the non-deflected, which conveys information about the quantity of what is counted and nothing else. So the difference between them in meaning has become clear by what we mentioned; hence it was permissible for the [one] cause to stand in place of two causes, because it necessitates two different rulings. End. These positions have proofs, objections and answers, and this is not their place.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "They are diptote only because of the deflection in them: their deflection from their form, and their deflection from their repetition. They are indefinites that are made definite by the lām of definiteness; one says: «فلان ينكح المَثْنى والثُلاث» (so-and-so marries in twos and threes)." The Shaykh said: "As for what he held — their being diptote for that reason — I do not know anyone who said it; rather there are four positions on it", and he mentioned them as preceded. It may be said: this is the fourth position, and he expressed the deflection in meaning as their deflection from their repetition.

The Shaykh also disputed with him about his example «ينكح المثنى» on two counts. The first: the entry of «أل» upon them. He said: "No one has held this; indeed they have only been used in the language of the Arabs as indefinites." The second: that he made them directly follow governors, whereas they do not directly follow governors; rather something precedes them [in place of them] that follows the governors, and they occur only as khabars (predicates), as in his saying, upon him be peace: «صلاةُ الليلِ مَثْنى مثنى» (the night prayer is two by two), or as ḥāls, as in this noble verse, or as naʿts (adjectives), as in His saying, the Exalted: {أولي أَجْنِحَةٍ مثنى وَثُلاَثَ وَرُبَاعَ} [Fāṭir: 1], and the poet's saying:
1531 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ذئابٌ تَبَغَّى الناسَ مَثْنَى ومَوْحَدُ
(… wolves seeking out the people, in twos and singly.)
[Translator's note: the printed text has «يتقدمهما» (dual) and «صلاةٌ الليلِ»; translated according to the evident sense.] Their annexation has occurred rarely, as in the poet's saying:
1532 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
بمَثْنى الزُّقاقِ المُتْرَعات وبالجُزُرْ
(… with pairs of brimming wineskins and with slaughtered camels.)
Some have cited, as proof of their directly following governors on a small scale, the poet's saying:
1533 - ضربْتُ خُماسَ ضربةَ عبشمِيٍّ ... أدارُ سداسَ أن لا يستقيما
(I struck [them] five by five with the blow of an ʿAbshamite; six by six were made to turn so that they would not stand upright.)
It can be interpreted as the omission of the object because the meaning is understood, its implied form being: I struck them five by five.

Among the rulings of these words is that they are not made feminine with the tāʾ: you do not say «مَثْناة» nor «ثُلاثَة»; rather they run alike for the masculine and the feminine.

Al-Nakhaʿī and Ibn Waththāb read: «ورُبَعَ» without alif. Al-Zamakhsharī added from al-Nakhaʿī: «وثُلَثَ» also, and others from him: «ثُنَى», shortened from «ثُناء». They deleted the alif from all of that for lightness, as another deleted it in his saying:
1534 - وصِلِّيانا بَرِدا ...
(… and cool ṣilliyān [a desert pasture plant].)
meaning «بارداً».

His saying: {فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ}: a condition whose apodosis is «فواحدة». It has preceded that some made «فواحدة» the apodosis of the first, and [held that] the second was repeated because the separation grew long, and made His saying {فانكحوا} a parenthetical clause; this is attributed to Abū ʿAlī [al-Fārisī], and perhaps it is not authentic from him. The Shaykh said: "Because when what is concluded is concluded from the two verses — this one and His saying {وَلَن تستطيعوا} [al-Nisāʾ: 129] — it would entail that it is not permissible to marry more than one, or [else] to take concubines from what one's right hand possesses; and the separation by the parenthetical clause would remain without benefit; indeed it would be void (laghw) on his claim."

The majority read «فواحِدةً» in the accusative by an implied verb, i.e. so marry one, and have intercourse with what your right hands possess. We implied another governor of the accusative for what the right hand possesses only because marriage (nikāḥ) does not occur in what the right hand possesses — unless one intends by it intercourse in this and marriage in the first; then it would require using a homonym in both its meanings, or combining the literal and the figurative, and both are views that have been held. This is close to the poet's saying:
1535 - عَلَفْتُها تِبْناً وماءً بارداً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I fed her straw, and cold water …)
and its chapter. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «فليزم», a misprint for «فيلزم».]

Al-Ḥasan and Abū Jaʿfar read: «فواحدةٌ» in the nominative, and there are three analyses of it. The first: the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); what permitted beginning with an indefinite is its reliance on the fāʾ of requital; and the khabar is omitted, i.e. then one is sufficient. The second: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. then what suffices is one. The third: it is a fāʿil (agent) of an implied verb, i.e. then one suffices.

And «أو» is in its proper sense of being for permission or for choice. And «ما» in «ما مَلَكَتْ» is like it in His saying «ما طابَ».

He annexed possession to the right hand because it is the seat of good qualities, and with it the banners of glory are received. [Translator's note: the printed text has «راياتُ» (banners), an allusion to the well-known verse «تلقّاها عرابةُ باليمين».] It is narrated from Abū [ʿAmr]: «فما ملكت أيمانكم», and the meaning is: if he does not act justly in living with one [wife], then what his right hand possesses. [Translator's note: the bracketed «[عمرو]» is in the printed source.] Ibn Abī ʿAbla read: «أو مَنْ ملكت أيمانكم».

His saying: {ذلك أدنى}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar. «ذلك» points to choosing one [wife] or taking a concubine. «أَدْنى» is an elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl) from دنا يدنو, i.e. to be near; i.e. nearer to not deviating. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «عَدِم», evidently for «عَدَم».]

And {أَن لاَ تَعُولُواْ} is in the position of the accusative or the genitive, according to the well-known disagreement about «أن» after the deletion of the preposition. Regarding that deleted preposition there are three analyses. The first: «إلى», i.e. nearer to your not deviating. The second: «اللام», the implied form being: nearer so that you do not deviate. The third, which al-Zamakhsharī implied: «مِنْ أن لا تميلوا» (than that you deviate), because the elative runs in the manner of its verb, so whatever its verb is made transitive by, it is made transitive by; and أَدْنى is from دنا, and «دنا» is made transitive by إلى, the lām and مِنْ; you say: دَنَوْت إليه وله ومنه (I drew near to him).

The majority read: «تَعُولوا», from عالَ يَعُول when one inclines and acts unjustly; the maṣdar is العَوْل and العِيالة; and عالَ الحاكم, i.e. the judge acted unjustly. Abū Ṭālib said about the Prophet ﷺ:
1536 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... له حاكمٌ من نفسِه غيرُ عائِل
(… he has a judge from within himself that does not deviate.)
And عالَ الرجل عيالَه يَعُولهم, i.e. he provided for them their sustenance; and from it: «ابدَأْ بنفسك ثم بمن تعول» (begin with yourself, then with those you support). Ibn al-Aʿrābī related: عال الرجل يعول: his dependants became many; and عالَ يَعِيل: he became poor and had a family [to support]. The upshot: «عال» is intransitive and transitive. The intransitive is in the sense of inclining and acting unjustly — and from it «عال الميزانُ» (the balance tilted) — and in the sense of his dependants becoming many, and in the sense of a matter becoming serious; the imperfect of all of this is يعولُ. And عالَ الرجل: he became poor; and عالَ في الأرض: he went off in the land; the imperfect of these two is يَعِيل. The transitive is in the sense of burdening, in the sense of providing sustenance, and in the sense of overcoming — and from it «عيل صبري» (my patience was overcome) — and the imperfect of all this is يَعُول; and in the sense of disabling: you say أعالني الأمر, i.e. the matter disabled me, and the imperfect of this is يَعيل, and the maṣdar is عَيْل and مَعِيل. So it has been summarised from this that intransitive «عال» is sometimes of the wāw-roots and sometimes of the yāʾ-roots according to the difference of meaning; and likewise transitive «عال» too. [Translator's note: so in the text; «أعالني» is quoted with the hamza though listed under «عال».]

Al-Shāfiʿī explained «تَعُولوا» in the sense of: your dependants become many. A group rejected this view, such as Abū Bakr ibn Dāwūd al-Rāzī, al-Zajjāj and the author of «al-Naẓm». Al-Rāzī said: "This is a mistake in meaning and in wording. As for the first, because of the permission of concubines, although that is an occasion for many dependants, like marriage. As for the wording, because the root «عال» in the sense of having many dependants is of the yāʾ-roots, since it is from العَيْلَة, while «عال» in the sense of acting unjustly is of the wāw-roots; so the two roots differ. Also, he contradicted the exegetes." The author of al-Naẓm said: "He said first «ألاَّ تعدلوا», so its opposite must be injustice."

People have replied to these. As for their saying that taking concubines also increases dependants while it is permitted, that is not conceded; that is because the slave woman is not like the married wife; hence he may practise withdrawal (ʿazl) with her without her permission, hire her out and take her wages, spending them on himself, on her and on her children. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its justification is to make it from your saying «عالَ الرجل عِياله يعولهم», like your saying «مانَهم يَمُونهم», i.e. he spent on them; because whoever has many dependants must support them, and in that there is what makes it hard for him to preserve earning the lawful and taking from good provision." Then he praised al-Shāfiʿī with fine praise, and said: "But scholars have ways and methods, and in explaining this word he took the way of metonymy (kināya)." End.

As for their saying "he contradicted the exegetes", that is not correct; rather Zayd ibn Aslam and Ibn Zayd said it. As for their saying "the two roots differ", that is not correct either, because Ibn al-Aʿrābī's report from the Arabs has preceded: «عال الرجل يَعُول»: his dependants became many. Al-Kisāʾī related it too; he said: "One says عال الرجل يَعُول and أعال يُعيل: his dependants became many." Al-Dūrī the reciter also transmitted it as a dialect of Ḥimyar, and cited:
1537 - وإنَّ الموتَ يأخذُ كلَّ حَيٍّ ... بلا شك وإنْ أَمْشى وعَالا
(Death takes every living being, without doubt, even if he has grown rich in livestock and has many dependants.)
أمشى: his livestock became many; and عال: his dependants became many. [Translator's note: so in the text; the following sentence appears to state an objection to this proof.] There is no proof in this, because of the possibility that «عال» is of the yāʾ-roots; and they do not deny that «عال» may be in the sense of having many dependants. It is also narrated from him [al-Shāfiʿī] that he explained «تَعُولوا» in the sense of becoming poor; he does not mean by it that تَعولوا and تَعيلوا are of one meaning, but intended metonymy as well, because many dependants are a cause of poverty.

Ṭalḥa read: «تَعيلوا», with fatḥa on the tāʾ of the imperfect, from عالَ يعيل: to become poor. The poet said:
1538 - وما يَدْري الفقيرُ متى غِناه ... وما يَدْري الغنيُّ متى يَعِيل
(The poor man does not know when his wealth will come, nor does the rich man know when he will become poor.)
Ṭāwūs read: «تُعيلوا», with ḍamma on it, from أعال: to have many dependants; and this supports al-Shāfiʿī's explanation given earlier, in terms of meaning. Al-Rāghib said: "عاله and غاله are close, but الغَوْل is in what destroys, and العَوْل in what burdens; and عالت الفريضة (the inheritance share was increased) when it exceeded in the division the shares named by the text for their owners."

semin-durr:164-164.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَرُسُلاً قَدْ قَصَصْنَاهُمْ}: the majority read «رسلاً» in the accusative, and there are three analyses. The first: that it is accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), since its conditions are present, i.e. "and We narrated messengers", the meaning being by the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "We narrated their stories"; so «قد قصصناهم» has no grammatical position, because it explains that implied governing word. Strengthening this analysis is the reading of Ubayy «ورسل» in the nominative in both places; and the accusative here is preferable to the nominative because the conjunction is onto a verbal clause, namely «وآتينا داودَ زبوراً». The second: that it is accusative by conjunction onto the meaning of «أوحينا إليك كما أوحينا إلى نوح», i.e. "We sent and made prophets Nūḥ and messengers"; on this, «قد قَصَصْناهم» is in the position of the accusative, because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «رسلاً». The third: that it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "and We sent messengers"; that is because the verse was revealed as a refutation of the Jews in their denial of the sending of messengers and the sending down of revelation, as Allah reported of them in His saying: {مَآ أَنزَلَ الله على بَشَرٍ مِّن شَيْءٍ} [al-Anʿām: 91]; and the clause is also in the position of an adjective.

Ubayy read: «ورسلٌ» in the nominative in both places, and there are two explanations of it. The more apparent: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows is its khabar (predicate); beginning with an indefinite noun is permissible here for one of two reasons: either the conjunction, as in the poet's saying:

167 - 7- عندي اصطبارٌ وشكوى عند قاتلتي ... فهل بأعجبَ مِنْ هذا امرؤٌ سَمِعا
(With me is patience, and complaint is with her who slays me — has any man heard of anything stranger than this?)

or the detailing (tafṣīl), as in his saying:

167 - 8- فأقبلتُ زحفاً على الركبتينِ ... فثوبٌ لَبِسْتٌ وثوبٌ أَجُرّْ
(So I came crawling on my knees: one garment I wore and one garment I dragged.)

and as in his saying:

167 - 9- إذا ما بكى مِنْ خلفِها انصرفَتْ له ... بشقٍ وشِقٌّ عندنا لم يُحَوَّلِ
(Whenever [the child] behind her cried, she turned to him with one half, while a half with us was not turned away.)

The second — Ibn ʿAṭiyya inclined to it — is that it is nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and they are messengers"; this is not clear. On this analysis the clause after «رسل» is in the position of the nominative, since it stands as an adjective of the indefinite noun before it.

His saying: {وَرُسُلاً لَّمْ نَقْصُصْهُمْ} is like the first.

His saying: {وَكَلَّمَ الله موسى}: the majority read the Majestic Name in the nominative, and it is clear. «تكليماً» is an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun) that removes [the possibility of] metaphor; this is a question the legal theorists (uṣūliyyūn) discuss, admitting much discussion for which this is not the place — although emphasis with the maṣdar has occurred in reinforcing (tarshīḥ) a metaphor, as in the saying of Hind bint al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr about her husband Rawḥ ibn Zinbāʿ, the minister of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān:

168 - 0- بكى الخَزُّ مِنْ رَوْحٍ وأنكَر جِلْدَه ... وعَجَّتْ عجيجاً مِنْ جُذامَ المطارِفُ
(The silk wept because of Rawḥ and disowned his skin, and the embroidered cloaks cried out loudly against Judhām.)

She says: her husband Rawḥ — the silk garments wept at his wearing them, because he is not one of the people of silk; and likewise the embroidered cloaks cried out loudly against Judhām — Rawḥ's tribe — meaning that they are not people of such garments. Her saying «عَجَّت المطارف» is a metaphor, because garments do not cry out; then she reinforced it with her saying «عجيجاً». Thaʿlab said: "Were it not for the emphasis with the maṣdar, it would be possible for it to be as when you say: 'I spoke to so-and-so for you', i.e. I sent to him, or wrote him a note." Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Nakhaʿī read: «وكَلَّم اللَّهَ موسى» with the Majestic Name in the accusative, and it is also clear.

semin-durr:74-74.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {الذين يَشْرُونَ الحياة}: the fāʿil (agent) of His words {فَلْيُقَاتِلْ}. «يَشْرون» admits two views. The first: it is in the sense of «يشترون» (they buy). If it is said: you have established that the bāʾ enters only on what is given up, and the apparent case here is that it has entered on what is taken — the answer is that what is meant by those who buy is the hypocrites who lag behind from jihad; they were commanded to change the hypocrisy in them, make their faith in Allah and His Messenger sincere, and fight in the way of Allah; so it has entered only on what is given up, because the hypocrites give up the Hereafter and take this world. The second: «يشرون» is in the sense of «يَبيعون» (they sell), and what is meant by those who sell is the believers who stay behind from jihad [Translator's note: so in the source], preferring the deferred to the immediate. The counterpart of this verse, in that «شرى» can bear buying and selling according to two perspectives, is the words of Allah the Exalted {وَشَرَوْهُ بِثَمَنٍ بَخْسٍ} [Yūsuf: 20], which will come. Something of this has preceded for you at the beginning of al-Baqara.
The majority read the lām of «فَلْيقاتل» with sukūn, because it occurs after the fāʾ, so that the word resembles «كتف» [i.e. it is lightened like katif to katf]. It has been read with kasra, which is the original. The majority read «فيُقْتل» as passive, and Muḥārib ibn Dithār as active; the first is more apparent, because of His words «أو يَغْلِب». «يُقْتَلْ» and «يُغْلِب» are conjoined to the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʾ in «فسوف» is its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); it may not be omitted. The well-known [reading] is to pronounce this bāʾ distinctly before the fāʾ; Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, Hishām and Khallād — with a variant from him — assimilated it. The majority read «نُؤْتيه» with the nūn of majesty, and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif and al-Aʿmash with the yāʾ of the third person; both are clear.
He put His words {فَيُقْتَلْ} first because it is the rank of martyrdom, which is greater than any other; and He put second the overcoming, which comprises two kinds: killing the enemies of Allah and gaining the spoils, the first being greater than the second.

semin-durr:165-165.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {رُّسُلاً مُّبَشِّرِينَ}: there are four analyses. The first: that it is a badal (substitute) from the first «رسلاً» in the reading of the majority; al-Zamakhsharī expressed this as its being accusative by repetition (takrīr) — so al-Shaykh understood him. The second: that it is accusative as a preparatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa), as in your saying «مررت بزيدٍ رجلاً صالحاً» ("I passed by Zayd, a righteous man"); the meaning of "preparatory" is that it is not itself intended, only its adjective is intended — do you not see that manhood is understood from your saying «بزيد», and what is intended is only describing him as righteous? The third: that it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "We sent messengers". The fourth: that it is accusative by way of praise; Abū al-Baqāʾ construed it with «أعني» ("I mean"), whereas he ought to have construed it as a verb indicating praise, such as «أمدح» ("I praise"). Al-Zamakhsharī preferred this last, saying: "The better analysis is that «رسلاً» is accusative by way of praise."

His saying: {لِئَلاَّ}: this is the lām of kay (purpose). It is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «منذرين» according to the preferred view of the Basrans, and to «مبشِّرين» according to the preferred view of the Kufans, for the question is one of tanāzuʿ (two governors competing for one governed word). Had it been a case of the first governing, a pronoun would have been implied in the second without omission, and it would have been said: "bringers of good tidings and warners for it, so that …"; but He did not say so «[Translator's note: the text has «يَقُلُّ», a misprint for «يَقُلْ».]», which indicates the school of the Basrans. It has parallels in the Qurʾān, a good number of which have preceded. And it is said: the lām is attached to an omitted word, i.e. "We sent them for that".

«حُجَّةٌ» is the noun of «كان», and for the khabar (predicate) there are two analyses. The first: it is «على الله», and «للناس» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The second: that the khabar is «للناس» and «على الله» is a ḥāl. Each of the two prepositional phrases may also be attached to what the other is attached to, when we make it the khabar. «على الله» may not be attached to «حجة», even though the meaning is upon that, because the governed word of a maṣdar does not precede it. «بعد الرسل» is attached to «حجة»; it may also be attached to an omitted word as an adjective of «حُجَّة», because events (aḥdāth) are qualified by adverbs [of time] just as they are predicated by them, as in «القتالُ يوم الجمعة» ("The fighting is on Friday").

semin-durr:75-75.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمَا لَكُمْ لاَ تُقَاتِلُونَ}: this is an interrogative by which incitement and the command to jihad are meant. «ما» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «لكم» its khabar (predicate), i.e. "what is it that is established for you?" On the clause of His words «لا تقاتلون» there are two views.
