The more apparent: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "what is with you, not fighting?" — He disapproved of their being in anything other than this state. The ḥāl has been stated explicitly after this construction in His words {فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ التذكرة مُعْرِضِينَ} [al-Muddaththir: 49]. They have said of such a ḥāl that it is necessary, because the speech is not complete without it; and this is questionable. The governor of this ḥāl is the implied "being established", as in your saying «ما لك ضاحكاً؟» (what is with you, laughing?). The second view: the original is «وما لكم في ألا تقتلوا» (and what is with you in not fighting); «في» was omitted, leaving «أَنْ لا تقاتلوا», so the well-known disagreement applies to it; then the accusative-making «أَنْ» was omitted, so the verb after it became nominative, as in their saying «تَسْمَعُ بالمُعَيْدِيّ خيرٌ من أن تراه» (that you hear of al-Muʿaydī is better than that you see him), and his words:
1611 - ألا أيُّهذا الزاجري أحضُرُ الوغى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O you who rebuke me for attending battle…)
in one of the two transmissions. This supports the ḥāl's not being necessary.
His words: {والمستضعفين}: there are three views on it. The most apparent: it is genitive by conjunction with the name of Allah the Exalted, i.e. "and in the way of the oppressed". The second, which al-Zajjāj and al-Mubarrad held: it is genitive by conjunction with «سبيل» itself. Abū al-Baqāʾ, after relating it from al-Mubarrad alone, said: "It is nothing." It is as though its rationale did not become clear to Abū al-Baqāʾ; its rationale is that its implied form is: "and in the deliverance of the oppressed". The third, which al-Zamakhsharī held: it is accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), its implied form being: "and I specify, of the way of Allah, the deliverance of the oppressed", because the way of Allah is general in every good, and the deliverance of the oppressed Muslims from the hands of the disbelievers is among the greatest of goods. The majority read «والمستضعفين» with the conjunctive wāw, and Ibn Shihāb read «في سبيل الله المستضعفين»; there are two explanations of it. The first: the conjunction is implied, as in their saying «أكلت لحماً تمراً سمكاً» (I ate meat, dates, fish). The second: it is a badal (substitute) from «سبيل الله», i.e. "in the way of Allah, the way of the oppressed", because their way is the way of Allah the Exalted.
His words: {مِنَ الرجال}: there are two views on it. The first: it is a ḥāl from «المستضعفين».
The second: «مِنْ» is for explaining the genus. «الوِلْدان»: it has been said, the plural of «وليد»; and it has been said, the plural of «وَلَد», like «وَرَل» and «وِرْلان». What is meant by them is the boys; it has also been said: male and female slaves — the male slave is called «وليد» and the female slave «وليدة» — and the masculine was given precedence over the feminine because the latter is included in it. On «الذين يقولون» there are two views. The first: it is genitive as an adjective, either of «المستضعفين» or of «الرجال» and those after them, the masculine being given precedence over the feminine. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«الذين يقولون» is in the position of genitive as an adjective of those of the mentioned who are rational." It is as though he imagined that the «وِلْدان» [are] the boys, and boys are not rational, so he made it an adjective of those of the mentioned who are rational, namely the men and women, excluding the children, because rationality is a condition of the sound masculine plural, and «الذين» is treated like it. This is an oversight, because what the grammarians mean by rational is what is of the genus of rational beings, even if deprived of reason; this is indicated by the words of Allah the Exalted:
{أَوِ الطفل الذين لَمْ يَظْهَرُواْ} [al-Nūr: 31] — what is meant here by «الطفل» is small boys, and nevertheless He described them with «الذين». The second: it is accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ).
His words: {الظالم أَهْلُهَا}: «الظالم» is an adjective of «القرية», and «أهلُها» is nominative through it as its agent. The «أل» in «الظالم» is a relative in the sense of «التي», i.e. "whose people did wrong"; so the wrongdoing is applied to the town verbally, while in meaning it belongs to what follows it; like it is «مَرَرْتُ برجلٍ حسن غلامُه» (I passed by a man whose servant is handsome). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was «الظالم» made masculine when what it qualifies is feminine? I say: it is an adjective of the town, except that it is predicated of its people; so it was given the case of «القرية» because it is its adjective, and made masculine because of its being predicated of the people, as you say: from this town whose people did wrong. Were it made feminine, so that it were said «الظالمةُ أهلُها», it would be permissible — not because of the femininity of the qualified noun, but because «الأهل» may be masculine and feminine. If you say: is «من هذه القريةِ الظالمين أهلُها» permissible? I say: yes, as [you say] «التي ظَلَموا أهلها», according to the dialect of «أكلوني البراغيث» (the fleas ate me, with plural agreement); and from it is {وَأَسَرُّواْ النجوى الذين ظَلَمُواْ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 3]." End of quotation. This is a general rule: when the adjective is applied to something other than what it belongs to — whether it is a khabar, an adjective or a ḥāl — it agrees with what precedes it in two out of five: one of the case designations, and one of indefiniteness and definiteness; as for masculine and feminine, singular and its two opposites, what it puts in the nominative is reckoned as with the verb. The precise treatment of that has preceded more than once. It is also necessary to make the pronoun overt from it absolutely, I mean whether there is ambiguity or not. As for when what it puts in the nominative is an overt noun, there is no need for it to put a pronoun in the nominative, but there must be a referent element referring back to the noun qualified by it verbally, as in this verse. I have clarified and explained that in this book and in my commentary on the Tashīl. This is unlike the verb when it is used as an adjective, a khabar, or a ḥāl of something verbally while belonging to something else in meaning, for the pronoun is not made overt from it but remains latent, as in «زيدٌ هندٌ يضرُبها» (Zayd — Hind, he strikes her) and «هند زيدٌ تضربه» (Hind — Zayd, she strikes him), without an overt pronoun, because of the strength of the verb and the weakness of the noun in governing; and this whether there is no ambiguity, as in the example given, or there is ambiguity, as in «زيدٌ عمروٌ يضربه» when you intend that Zayd is the one striking ʿAmr. This is what the doctrine of the Basrans entails; Makkī and others stated it explicitly. However, he said before that: "Except that the active participle, when it is a khabar, an adjective or a ḥāl of other than what it belongs to, no pronoun remains latent in it and it must be made overt; likewise if it is conjoined to other than what it belongs to." I say: this addition was not mentioned by the grammarians, and exemplifying it is difficult. As for Ibn Mālik, he treated the verb and the descriptive alike, meaning that if there is ambiguity, overtness is necessary even with the verb, as in «زيدٌ عَمْروٌ يضربه هو», and if there is no ambiguity it is permissible [to leave it latent], as in «زيد هند يضربها». This is what the doctrine of the Kufans entails, for they gave ambiguity as the reason. In sum, there is disagreement on the question.

semin-durr:166-166.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {لكن الله يَشْهَدُ}: this corrective (istidrāk) clause is not begun with, so there must be an omitted clause from which this clause is a correction. The omitted clause is what is related about the occasion of revelation: when {إِنَّآ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ} [al-Nisāʾ: 163] was revealed, they said: "We will never bear witness to you for this", and then {لكن الله يَشْهَدُ} was revealed. Al-Zamakhsharī did well here in construing a clause other than the one I mentioned, namely: "If you say: a correction must have something corrected, so where is it in His saying {لكن الله يَشْهَدُ}? I say: when the People of the Book asked for the sending down of a book from the sky «[Translator's note: the text has «المساء» "the evening", a misprint for «السماء» "the sky".]» and were obstinate about it, and He argued against them with His saying 'We have revealed to you', He said: 'But Allah bears witness', meaning that they do not bear witness, but Allah bears witness." Then he mentioned the first analysis.

The majority read «لكن» without doubling and the Majestic Name in the nominative; al-Sulamī and al-Jarrāḥ al-Ḥakamī read it with doubling and the Majestic Name in the accusative; these are like the two readings in {ولكن الشياطين}, whose ruling has preceded. The majority read «أَنْزله» in the active, the agent being Allah the Exalted; al-Ḥasan read it «أُنزل» in the passive; and al-Sulamī read «نَزَّله بعلمه» with doubling. The bāʾ in «بعلمه» is of accompaniment, i.e. "bound up with His knowledge", so the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Regarding the one it describes there are two analyses: the first, the hāʾ in «أنزله»; the second, the agent in «أنزله», i.e. "He sent it down knowing it".

«والملائكةُ يشهدون» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); it may also be a ḥāl from the object in «أنزله», i.e. "while the angels bear witness to its truth"; or it may have no grammatical position, its ruling then being that of the corrective clause before it. Discussion has preceded on the like of His saying {كفى بالله} [al-Nisāʾ: 6], and on His saying {لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 168], and that the verb with this lām is more emphatic than without it. The majority read «وصَدُّوا» in the active; ʿIkrima and Ibn Hurmuz read «وصُدُّوا» in the passive; both are clear, and both were read in the mutawātir readings in His saying {وَصُدُّواْ} [verse 33] in al-Raʿd, and {وَصُدَّ عَنِ السبيل} [verse 37] in Ghāfir.

semin-durr:169-169.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {إِلاَّ طَرِيقَ جَهَنَّمَ}: there are two views. The first: that it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), because what is meant by the first "path" is the general, so the second is of its kind. The second: that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), if by "path" something specific is meant, namely the righteous deeds by which one reaches Paradise. «خالدين» is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara, circumstantial).

semin-durr:170-170.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {بالحق}: there are two analyses. The first: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted word, the bāʾ being for the ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "the Messenger has come to you bound up with the truth" or "speaking it". The second: that it is attached to «جاءكم» itself, i.e. "he has come to you for the sake of establishing the truth". «من ربكم» has two analyses. The first: that it is attached to an omitted word, as a ḥāl also, from «الحق». The second: that it is attached to «جاء», i.e. "he came from Allah", i.e. he is sent, not a fabricator.

His saying: {خَيْراً لَّكُمْ}: there are four analyses of its accusative. The first — the school of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh — is that it is accusative by an omitted verb that must be implied, its implied form being "and bring about what is better for you", because when He commanded them to believe, He wants to take them out of one matter and bring them into what is better than it. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else; he said: "That is because when He urged them to believe and to desist from the trinity, it was known that He was impelling them toward a matter, so He said 'خيراً لكم', i.e. aim at and bring about a matter better for you than the disbelief and trinity «[Translator's note: the text has «التثلث».]» you are in."

The second — the school of al-Farrāʾ — is that it is the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "so believe with a belief that is better for you". There is a reservation about this, in that it suggests that belief is divided into good and otherwise, for otherwise there would be no point in restricting it by the adjective. But it may be said that he may not hold to the implied meaning of the adjective (mafhūm al-ṣifa); and also the adjective sometimes comes for emphasis and other than that.

The third — the school of al-Kisāʾī and Abū ʿUbayd — is that it is accusative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied «كان», its implied form being "belief will be better". Some rejected this school on the ground that «كان» is not omitted together with its noun without its khabar except where it is indispensable. What makes it weaker still is that the implied «يكن» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an omitted condition, so what is omitted becomes the condition together with its apodosis; that is, the implied form is "if you believe, belief will be better": you have omitted the condition, «إنْ تؤمنوا», and its apodosis, «يكن الإِيمان», and kept the governed word of the apodosis, «خيراً». But it may be said that there is no need to imply a formal condition, even though the meaning is upon it, because we claim that the jussive in the implied «يكن» is only by the imperative clause itself that precedes it, namely His saying {فَآمِنُواْ}, without implying a conditional particle or its verb. This is the correct view regarding responses occurring after one of the seven things: you say «قم أكرمْك» ("Stand, and I will honour you"), so «أكرمك» is a response in the jussive by «قم» itself, because this request contains the meaning of a condition without implying a formal condition.

The fourth — and its unsoundness is apparent — is that it is accusative as a ḥāl. Al-Makkī transmitted it from some of the Kufans and said: "It is far-fetched"; Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted it too without attributing it.

semin-durr:135-135.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {شُهَدَآءِ} — there are two views on it. The first: that it is a second khabar (predicate) of «كان», and there is a disagreement about this whose mention has passed. The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «قَوَّامين», so what governs it is «قَوَّامين». The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected this view on the ground that it entails restricting their being upholders [of justice] to the state of bearing witness, whereas they are commanded to do so absolutely. This rebuttal is worthless, for Ibn ʿAbbās inclined to this meaning; he — may Allah be pleased with him — said: "Be upholders of justice in testimony against whomever it may be," and this is the meaning of the view that makes «شهداء» a ḥāl.
His words: {وَلَوْ على أَنْفُسِكُمْ} — this «لو» may be in its proper sense, being a particle for what would have happened because of the happening of something else, and its answer is omitted, i.e. "and even if you were witnesses against yourselves, it would be obligatory upon you to bear witness against them". The Shaykh permitted it to have the meaning of the conditional «إن», with His words «على أنفسكم» attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted element, its implied form being: "and if you are witnesses against yourselves, then be witnesses for Allah" — "this is the implied form of the speech, and the omission of «كان» after «لو» is frequent; you say: «ائتِني بتمر ولو حَشَفاً» ('bring me dates, even if poor dry ones'), i.e. and if the dates are poor and dry, bring them to me." End of quotation. Nothing compels this, and the use of «لو» in the meaning of «إنْ» is something that some affirmed as rare, so the Quran should not be interpreted according to it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«على أنفسكم» is attached to «شهداء»." The Shaykh said: "If he means by «شهداء» the one actually pronounced, it is not correct; if he means by it what we have posited, it is correct" — meaning his own positing of «لو» as meaning «إنْ» and the omission of «كان», its noun and its khabar after «لو»; it has preceded that this is rare, so it remains only that Ibn ʿAṭiyya means an omitted «شهداء», as I posited for you first, i.e. "and if you were witnesses against yourselves, it would be obligatory upon you to bear witness". [Translator's note: the source has «ولم كنتم شهداء», evidently a slip for «ولو كنتم شهداء»; translated per the latter.]
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And even if the testimony is against yourselves," so he made «كان» implied, and in his implied form it may be complete (tāmma) or incomplete (nāqiṣa). If you posit it as complete, His words «على أنفسكم» are attached to "the testimony" itself, and the meaning is: "and even if testimony against yourselves exists". If you posit it as incomplete, «على أنفسكم» may be attached to an omitted element as its khabar, or may be attached to "the testimony" itself, in which case the khabar is implied, and the meaning is: "and even if testimony against yourselves exists" — except that making «على أنفسكم» attached to "the testimony" entails omitting the maṣdar (verbal noun) while keeping what it governs, which is rare or prohibited. He also said: "The meaning may be: and even if the testimony is a calamity upon yourselves." The Shaykh rejected these two views of his, saying: "His implied form 'and even if the testimony is against yourselves' is not good, because the omitted element is only of the kind of what is pronounced, so that it indicates it. If you say «كن محسناً ولو لمَنْ أساء إليك» ('be good-doing, even to one who did you wrong'), the implied form is 'even if you are good-doing to one who did wrong'; if you posited it as 'even if your good-doing is…', it would not be good, because you would be omitting something for which there is no indication by a matching word." This rebuttal is worthless, for the verbal indication is present, since the omitted and the pronounced share the root, and their differing in type does no harm.
And he said regarding the second view: "This is not permissible, because what the adverbial phrase is attached to is a restricted being (kawn muqayyad), and a restricted being may not be omitted — only an absolute one. If you said «[كان] زيدٌ فيك», meaning 'loving for your sake', it would not be permissible." This rebuttal is also worthless, because he intended an explanation of the meaning; the basics of grammar are not hidden from the least of students, so how much less from the master of the craft?
His words: {فالله أولى بِهِمَا} — when conjoining is with «أو», the rule in the pronoun's reference, the predicate and other things is for one of the two or more things, and agreement [with both] is not permissible: you say «زيد أو عمرو أكرمته» ('Zayd or ʿAmr — I honoured him'), and if you said «أكرمتها» it would not be permissible. On this basis it is asked: how did He make the pronoun dual in the noble verse, when the conjoining is with «أو»? Necessarily, the grammarians disagreed in answering this, in five views. The first: that the pronoun in «بهما» does not refer to the rich and the poor mentioned first, but to the two genera of rich and poor indicated by the two mentioned, its implied form being: "and if the one testified against is rich or poor, let him bear witness against him, for Allah is more entitled to the two genera, rich and poor"; this is indicated by the reading of Ubayy: «فالله أوْلَى بهم», i.e. the rich and the poor, in consideration of the genus as I established for you. His words {فالله أولى بِهِمَا} would then not be the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); rather its apodosis is omitted, as you have learned, and this indicates it. The second: that «أو» means the wāw; this is attributed to al-Akhfash, and I mentioned earlier at the beginning of al-Baqara that it is the opinion of the Kufans and that it is weak. The third: that «أو» is for detailing, i.e. for detailing what was left vague. Abū al-Baqāʾ clarified this, saying: "That is because each of the one testified against and the one testified for may be rich or may be poor; both may be rich, both may be poor, or one may be rich and the other poor. Since the divisions upon detailing were thus, «أو» was used to indicate the detailing. On this view the pronoun in «بهما» refers to the one testified for and the one testified against, in whatever state they are." End of quotation. However, his saying "or one may be rich and the other poor" is repetitive, because his saying "That is because each of …" to the end makes it unnecessary. The fourth: that the pronoun refers to the two litigants, its implied form being: "if the two litigants are rich or poor, then Allah is more entitled to those two litigants".
The fifth: that the pronoun refers to wealth and poverty, indicated by the words "rich" and "poor"; the implied form is: "then Allah is more entitled to the wealth of the rich and the poverty of the poor". Ibn ʿUṣfūr expressed this badly here, as may be seen in his words. On the last four views, the apodosis is pronounced, namely His words {فالله أولى بِهِمَا}, unlike the first, where it is omitted. ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd] read «إن يكنْ غنيٌ أو فقيرٌ», with both nominative; the apparent view is that «كان» in his reading is complete, i.e. "and if there is someone rich or poor", as in: {وَإِن كَانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ} [al-Baqara: 280].
His words: {أَن تَعْدِلُواْ} — there are three views on it. The first: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being: "so do not follow desire out of love of deviating", or "wishing to deviate", i.e. that you deviate from the truth and act unjustly. Abū al-Baqāʾ said about the omitted muḍāf: "its implied form is: for fear that you deviate from the truth." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Its meaning may be: for fear that you deviate, justice (ʿadl) here meaning deviation (ʿudūl) from the truth; and its meaning may be: out of love of being just, ʿadl meaning equity, as though He says: desist for fear of acting unjustly, or out of love of being equitable. If you make the governing element «تتبعوا», the meaning may be: out of love of acting unjustly." End of quotation. So we obtain two views about the governing element: the apparent one of them is that it is «تتبَّعوا» itself; the second is that it is implied, a verb derived from the meaning of the prohibition, as Ibn ʿAṭiyya posited, as though he claims that the speech is complete at His words {فَلاَ تَتَّبِعُواْ الهوى} and then a governing element is implied; and there is no need for this.
The second: that it is by removal of the preposition and omission of the negating «لا», the original being: "so do not follow desire in not being just", i.e. in abandoning justice; «لا» was omitted because the meaning indicates it, and when the preposition was omitted from «أن», the two well-known opinions applied. The third: that it is with omission of the lām of cause, its implied form being: "so do not follow desire in order that you be just". The proponent of this opinion said: "The meaning is: do not follow desire so as to be just in following it — drawing attention [to the fact] that following desire and seeking justice are mutually exclusive and do not combine." This is weak in meaning.
His words: {وَإِن تَلْوُواْ} — Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamza read «تَلُوا», with a lām bearing ḍamma and a quiescent wāw; the rest read it with a quiescent lām followed by two wāws, the first of which bears ḍamma.
The reading with two wāws is clear, because it is from «لَوَى يَلْوي», and the meaning is: "and if you twist your tongues away from true testimony or just judgment". The original is «تَلْوِيُون», like «تَضْرِبون»; the ḍamma was found heavy on the yāʾ and was dropped, so two quiescent letters met: the yāʾ and the wāw of the pronoun; the first of them — the yāʾ — was dropped, and the wāw with kasra, which is the ʿayn [of the root], was given ḍamma because of the wāw of the pronoun, so it became «تَلْوُون», and its inflection is like the inflection of «تَرْمُون».
As for the reading of Ḥamza and Ibn ʿĀmir, there are three opinions about it. The first — the opinion of al-Zajjāj, al-Farrāʾ, and al-Fārisī in one of the two narrations from him — is that it is from «لَوَى يَلْوي», like the reading of the majority, except that the wāw bearing ḍamma was changed to a hamza, as it is changed in «أُجوه» and «أُقِّتتْ»; then the vowel of this hamza was transferred to the quiescent letter before it and the hamza dropped, so it became «تَلُون», as you see.
The second: that it is also from «لَوَى يَلْوي», except that the ḍamma was found heavy on the first wāw and was transferred to the quiescent lām for lightness; then two quiescent letters met — namely the two wāws — and the first of them was dropped. This is attributed to al-Naḥḥās. There is an objection to these two explanations, namely that the lām [radical] of the word was dropped first, as I established, so its pattern became «تَفْعُوا» with the lām dropped; then the ʿayn was dropped second, so its pattern became «تَفُوا», and that is an excessive mutilation of the word. The third — attributed to a group including al-Fārisī — is that this reading is taken from al-wilāya (charge, authority), meaning: "and if you are put in charge of giving testimony", or "put in charge of the matter, and you deviate from it". The original is «تَوْلِيُوا»; the first wāw was dropped because it falls between the imperfect prefix and a kasra, so it became «تَلِيُوا», like «تَعِدُوا» and its class; then the ḍamma was found heavy on the yāʾ, and what was described for «تَلْوُوا» was done to it. Some criticised the reading of Ḥamza and Ibn ʿĀmir — among them Abū ʿUbayd — saying: because the meaning of wilāya does not suit this place. Abū ʿUbayd said: "The reading in our view is with two wāws, taken from «لَوَيْتُ»; its verification is in the exegesis of Ibn ʿAbbās: it is the judge whose twisting and turning away is from one of the two litigants in favour of the other." This criticism is worthless, because it is a mutawātir (mass-transmitted) reading and its meaning is sound: if we take it from al-wilāya, the meaning is as preceded; and if we take it from al-layy (twisting), the original is «تَلْوُوا», like the other reading, and what preceded was merely done to it — changing the wāw to a hamza and transferring its vowel, or transferring its vowel without changing it — so the two readings agree in meaning.

semin-durr:136-136.t:
And the words of Allah the Exalted: {يَا أَيُّهَا الذين آمَنُواْ آمِنُواْ}, i.e. persevere in faith; or by "those who believed" all people are meant, and that was on the day He took the covenant from them. Nāfiʿ and the Kufans read «والكتابِ الذي نَزَّل على رسوله والكتاب الذي أَنْزل من قبل», with both verbs in the active, the agent being Allah the Exalted; the rest read them both in the passive, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being the pronoun of "the Book". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why did He say «نَزَّل على رسوله» and «أَنْزل من قبل»? I say: because the Quran was sent down in instalments, piecemeal, over twenty years, unlike the books before it." The [discussion] with him on this has preceded, and that the doubling in «نَزَّل» is for transitivity, synonymous with the hamza, not for multiplicity.
And His words «فقد ضَلَّ ضلالاً» are not the apodosis for [all] the three things [together]; rather the meaning is: and whoever disbelieves in any one of them.

semin-durr:137-137.t: And the words of Allah the Exalted: {لَّمْ يَكُنْ الله لِيَغْفِرَ} are like His words: {مَّا كَانَ الله لِيَذَرَ المؤمنين} [Āl ʿImrān: 179]. The examination of this, the positions of the scholars, the fact that the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd) conveys emphasis, and the difference between your saying «ما كان زيدٌ يقوم» and «ما كان ليقومَ» have already preceded.

semin-durr:139-139.t: The fāʾ in the words of Allah the Exalted: {فَإِنَّ العزة} is because of the sense of condition in the speech, since the meaning is: "if you seek might from these". And «جميعاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in His words «لله», because it occurs as a khabar (predicate). His words: {الذين يَتَّخِذُونَ} — both the accusative and the nominative are possible in it. The accusative is from two views. The first: its being a naʿt (adjective) of «المنافقين». The second: that it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "I censure those who…". The nominative is as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are those who…".

semin-durr:171-171.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: «[Translator's note: the quoted Quranic words are missing in the text here; the discussion concerns {لاَ تَغْلُواْ فِي دِينِكُمْ}.]» «الغُلُوُّ» is exceeding the limit; from it come «غَلْوة السهم» (the arrow's flight-distance) and «غَلاء السعر» (high price).

His saying: {إِلاَّ الحق}: this is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), and there are two analyses of its accusative. The first: that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because it contains the meaning of speech, as in «قلت خطبةً» ("I spoke a sermon"). The second: that it is the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "except the true saying"; it is close in meaning to the first.

Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad read: «المِسِّيح» on the pattern of «السِّكِّيت», as though he made it an intensive form, as in «شِرِّيبٌ العسلَ» ("a great drinker of honey"). «المسيح» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) after the restrained (makfūfa) «إنَّ»; «عيسى» is a badal (substitute) from it or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); «ابن مريم» is its adjective; «رسول الله» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; and «كلمتُه» is conjoined to it.

«ألقاها» is a past-tense clause in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), with «قد» implied with it. Regarding what governs the ḥāl there are three analyses, which Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted: "The first: that it is the meaning of «كلمة», because the meaning of describing ʿĪsā as the word is: the one brought into being by the word without a father; so it is as if He said: 'and His creation and His originated one'. The second: that the implied form is 'when (إذ) He had cast it', «إذا» «[Translator's note: so in the text, after «إذ» above.]» being an adverb of future time, «كان» complete, its agent the pronoun of Allah the Exalted, and «ألقاها» a ḥāl from that agent; it is like their saying «ضربني زيداً قائماً» «[Translator's note: so in the text here; below it is quoted as «ضربي زيدا قائماً», the well-known example.]». The third: that it is a ḥāl from the genitive hāʾ, what governs it being the meaning of the iḍāfa (genitive construct), its implied form being: 'and the word of Allah, casting it'." End of quotation.

As for his making the governing word the meaning of «كلمة», it is correct; but in this analysis he did not explain who the one described by the ḥāl is. The one described by the ḥāl is the pronoun latent in «كَلِمتُه», referring to ʿĪsā, because of the derived-word meaning it contains, such as "brought into being" and "originated". As for his making the governing word the meaning of the iḍāfa, it is a weak thing that some grammarians adopted. As for his construing the verse on the like of «ضربي زيدا قائماً» ("my striking Zayd standing"), it is unsound in meaning. And Allah knows best.

«روحٌ» is conjoined to «كلمة», «منه» is an adjective of «روح», and «من» is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), figuratively, and is not partitive. Among the strange things that are related is that a certain Christian debated with ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid al-Marwazī and said: "In the Book of Allah there is what testifies that ʿĪsā is a part of Allah", and recited «وروح منه». Ibn Wāqid countered him with His saying, Exalted is He: {وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمْ مَّا فِي السموات وَمَا فِي الأرض جَمِيعاً مِّنْهُ} [al-Jāthiya: 13], and said: "It would follow that those things are a part of Allah the Exalted, which is impossible by agreement." So the Christian was silenced and embraced Islam.

«ثلاثةٌ» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, and the clause made of this mubtadaʾ and khabar is in the position of the accusative by the verb of saying, i.e. "and do not say: our gods are three"; His saying after that indicates it: {إِنَّمَا الله إله وَاحِدٌ}. And it is said: its implied form is "the hypostases (aqānīm) are three" or "the one worshipped is three".

Al-Fārisī said: "Its implied form is: Allah is the third of three; then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place." By that he wants agreement with His saying: {لَّقَدْ كَفَرَ الذين قالوا إِنَّ الله ثَالِثُ ثَلاَثَةٍ} [al-Māʾida: 73].

His saying: {انتهوا خَيْراً لَّكُمْ}: the accusative of «خيراً» here is like its accusative in what preceded, in all its analyses, with their attribution to those who held them. «أن يكون له ولد» — its implied form is "from its being" or "away from its being", because the meaning of «سبحان» is declaring transcendent (tanzīh); so it is as if it were said: "declare Him transcendent above having a child" or "from having a child"; so the two well-known analyses come in for the position of «أن». «واحد» is an adjective by way of emphasis. The apparent sense of al-Makkī's words is that it is an adjective not by way of emphasis, for he said: "«الله» is a mubtadaʾ, «إله» its khabar, «واحد» an adjective, its implied form being: Allah is only unique in His divinity." And it is said: «واحدٌ» is an emphasis, on a par with {لاَ تَتَّخِذُواْ إلهين اثنين} [al-Naḥl: 51]. «إله» may also be a badal from «الله» and «واحد» its khabar, its implied form being: the one worshipped is only one. His saying {أَن يَكُونَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ} — its parallel has preceded. Al-Ḥasan read: «إنْ يكونُ» with kasra on the hamza and «يكون» in the nominative, «إنْ» being negating, i.e. "there will not be a child for Him"; on his reading this speech consists of two clauses, and on the reading of the generality it is one clause.

semin-durr:172-172.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {لَّن يَسْتَنكِفَ المسيح أَن يَكُونَ عَبْداً}: ʿAlī read «عُبَيْداً» in the diminutive, which suits the context. His saying {وَلاَ الملائكة} is conjoined to «المسيح», i.e. "nor will the angels disdain to be servants of Allah".

Al-Shaykh said, in his words: "In the speech there is an omission, the implied form being: nor the angels brought near [disdain] to be servants of Allah. If «عبداً» is made to contain the meaning of 'owned by Allah', this construal is not needed, and «ولا الملائكة» is then of the category of conjoining single words; unlike when the meaning of oneness is regarded in «عبد», for then His saying «ولا الملائكة» is of conjoining clauses, because of the difference in the predicate. And if in His saying «ولا الملائكة» the meaning 'nor each one of the angels' is regarded, it is of the category of conjoining single words."

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: to what is «والملائكة» conjoined? I say «[Translator's note: the text has «قتل», a misprint for «قلت».]»: either it is conjoined to «المسيح», or to the noun of «يكون», or to the pronoun latent in «عبداً» because of the descriptive meaning in it, since it indicates worship — as in your saying «مررت برجلٍ عبدٍ أبوه» ('I passed by a man whose father is a servant'). Conjunction to «المسيح» is the apparent one, because the others lead to something of a deviation from the purpose, namely that the Messiah does not disdain that he, nor «[Translator's note: the text has «هو لا مَنْ», apparently for «هو ولا مَنْ».]» those above him, be described by servitude, or that he and those above him worship Allah."

Al-Shaykh said: "The deviation from the purpose he alluded to is that the disdaining would be restricted to the Messiah, whereas the complete meaning is the inclusion of the angels with the Messiah in the negation of disdain for servitude. The outweighed status of the two [other] analyses also appears from the entry of «لا», since if conjunction to the pronoun in «يكون» or in «عبدا» were intended, «لا» would not have entered; rather the construction would have been without it. You say: «ما يريد زيدٌ أن يكونَ هو وأبوه قائمين» ('Zayd does not want that he and his father be standing') and «ما يريد زيد أن يصطلح هو وعمرو» ('Zayd does not want that he and ʿAmr be reconciled'); these two constructions are not a place where [lā] is expected to enter, and if anything of the sort is found it is interpreted." End of quotation. So there result three analyses for the nominative of «الملائكة», the most sound being the first.

«الاستنكاف» is the istafʿala form of «النَّكْف», and «النَّكْف» is that something bad be said of him; from it comes «وما عليه في هذا الأمر نَكْفٌ ولا وَكْف» ("There is no blame or fault on him in this matter"). Abū al-ʿAbbās said: "Istafʿala here means to repel blame from himself." Another said: "It is disdain and haughtiness." From it comes «نَكَفْتُ الدَّمعَ بإصبعي» ("I wiped the tear away with my finger"), when you prevent it from running down your cheek. The poet said:

168 - 1- فبانوا فلولا مَا تَذَكَّرُ منهمُ ... من الحِلْفِ لم يُنْكَفْ لعَيْنَيْك مَدْمَعُ
(So they departed; and were it not for the alliance you remember with them, no tear of your eyes would be wiped away.)

His saying {فَسَيَحْشُرُهُمْ}: the fāʾ may be the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition in His saying {وَمَن يَسْتَنْكِفْ}. If it is said: the apodosis of conditional «إنْ» and its sisters other than «إذا» must be something that may occur or not occur, whereas their being gathered to Him all together is inevitable, so how did it occur as its apodosis? — two answers have been given. The first — and it is the more correct — is that this is speech containing promise and threat, because their gathering entails their recompense with reward or punishment; this is indicated by the detailing after it in His saying «فأمَّا الذين …» to the end. So the implied form is: "whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant, He will punish him when He gathers him to Himself; and whoever does not disdain and is not arrogant, He will reward him."

The second: that the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "He will requite him", then He informed with His saying {فَسَيَحْشُرُهُمْ إِلَيهِ جَمِيعاً}; this is not evident. This passage may be one in which regard was paid at one time to the wording of «مَنْ», in His saying «يستنكف» and «يستكبر», which is why the pronoun is singular, and at another time to its meaning, in His saying «فسيحشرهم», which is why it is plural. Or it may be that He referred the pronoun in «فسيحشرهم» to «مَنْ» and others, so that the one who disdains is included in it, the link of this clause to the conditional noun being the generality alluded to. And it is said: rather, a conjoined word was omitted because the meaning is understood, the implied form being "He will gather them", i.e. those who disdain and others, as in His saying {سَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الحر} [al-Naḥl: 81], i.e. "and the cold".

«جميعاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), or an emphasis according to those who made it like «كل», which is correct. Al-Ḥasan read «فسنحشرهم» with the nūn of majesty, and «فيعذبهم» with the bāʾ undoubled. And it was read «فسيحشِرهم» with kasra on the shīn, which is a dialectal form in the imperfect of «حَشَر».

semin-durr:173-173.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {فَأَمَّا الذين}: discussion of its parallel has preceded. But here there is a good question that al-Zamakhsharī raised, namely: "If you say: the detailing does not correspond to what is detailed, because it includes the two parties while what is detailed includes one party — I say: it is like your saying: 'The imam gathered the Khārijites: whoever had not rebelled against him he clothed with a robe, and whoever had rebelled against him he made an example of.' Its soundness is for two reasons. The first: that mention of one of the two parties is omitted because the detailing indicates it, and because mention of one of them indicates mention of the second, just as He omitted one of them in the detailing in His saying right after this: {فَأَمَّا الذين آمَنُواْ بالله واعتصموا بِهِ}. The second: that kindness to others than them is something that grieves them, so it was included among the making an example of them; so it is as if it were said: whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant, He will punish them with regret when they see the rewards of those who did [good], and with what befalls them of Allah's punishment." End of quotation. By the detailing he means His saying «فأما» and «أما», which includes two parties, i.e. those rewarded and those punished; and by what is detailed, His saying before that, «ومَنْ يستنكف», which includes only one party, namely those punished.

semin-durr:174-174.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ}: there are two analyses. The more apparent: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted word, because it is an adjective of «برهان», i.e. "a proof that is from your Lord"; «مِنْ» may be for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), figuratively, or partitive, i.e. "of the proofs of your Lord". The second: that it is attached to «جاء» itself, «مِنْ» being for the beginning of the extent, as has preceded.

semin-durr:175-175.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {صِرَاطاً}: it is the second object of «يهدي», because it takes two objects, as its verification has preceded. A group, among them al-Makkī, said: it is the object of an omitted verb indicated by «يهديهم», the implied form being «يُعَرِّفهم» ("He makes them know"). Abū al-Baqāʾ said something close to this, except that he did not imply a verb, but made it accusative by «يهدي» according to the sense, because the meaning is "He makes them know". Al-Makkī said in the second analysis: "It may be a second object of «يَهْدي», i.e. He guides them on a straight path to His reward and recompense." I do not know why they singled out this place, rather than the one in al-Fātiḥa, and needed to imply a verb or make it contain the meaning of «يُعَرِّفهم».

Abū ʿAlī permitted that it be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from an omitted word, for he said: "The hāʾ in «إليه» refers back to the name of Allah that preceded, and the meaning is: and He guides them to His path; so if we make «صراطاً مستقيماً» accusative as a ḥāl, the ḥāl is from this omitted word." End of quotation.

So there result four analyses of its accusative. The first: that it is an object of «يهدي» without its containing the meaning of another verb. The second: that it is on its containing the meaning of «يُعَرفهم». The third: that it is accusative by an omitted verb. The fourth: that it is accusative as a ḥāl; on this construal that al-Fārisī made, it comes close to the emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), yet it is not like your saying «تبسَّم ضاحكاً» ("he smiled, laughing"), because it differs from what it describes by the additional adjective, even if it agrees with it in wording.

The hāʾ in «إليه» either refers to «الله», by the implied omission of a muḍāf as preceded, such as «ثوابه» (His reward) or «صراطه» (His path); or to the bounty and the mercy, because they are in the sense of one thing; or it refers to the bounty, because by it is meant the way to the Gardens.

semin-durr:140-140.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ} — the majority read «نُزِّل», in the passive; ʿĀṣim read it in the active; Abū Ḥaywa and Ḥumayd read «نَزَل», undoubled, in the active; and al-Nakhaʿī read «أُنْزِل», with the hamza, in the passive. What stands in place of the fāʿil (agent) in the reading of the majority and of al-Nakhaʿī is «أَنْ» and what falls within its scope, i.e. "and there has been sent down to you the prohibition of sitting with them when you hear disbelief in the signs and mockery of them". In the reading of ʿĀṣim, «أَنْ» with what follows it is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «نزَّل», and the fāʿil is the pronoun of Allah the Exalted, as preceded. In the reading of Abū Ḥaywa and Ḥumayd, its position is nominative as the fāʿil of the undoubled «نزل». So its position is either accusative, in the reading of ʿĀṣim, or nominative, in the reading of the others — but the nominative differs [in kind]. This «أن» is the one lightened from the heavy [«أنّ»], and its noun is the pronoun of the matter and the affair (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), i.e. "that the matter and the affair is: when you hear disbelief and mockery, do not sit". The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What Abū al-Baqāʾ posited in his saying «أنكم إذا سمعتم» ('that you, when you hear') is not good, because the lightened «أن» governs only the pronoun of the affair, except in poetic necessity, as in his words:
1662 - فلو أَنْكِ في يومِ الرخاءِ سَأَلْتِني ... طلاقَك لم أبخَلْ وأنتِ صديقُ
(Had you asked me for your divorce on a day of ease, I would not have withheld it, while you remained a friend.)"
So he said; but I did not see it in the i'rab of Abū al-Baqāʾ except with the hāʾ, not with the kāf and mīm. The conditional clause formed from «إذا» and its answer is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «أَنْ». An instance of the conditional clause coming as the khabar of the lightened «أنْ» is his saying:
1663 - فعلمْتُ أَنْ ما تَتَّقُوه فإنه ... جَزْرٌ لِخامعةٍ وفَرْخِ عقابِ
(And I knew that whatever you guard against, it becomes slaughter-meat for the limping hyena and the eagle's chick.)
So «ما» is conditional, «فإنه» is its answer, and the clause is the khabar of the lightened «أن».
His words: {يُكَفَرُ بِهَا} are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الآيات», and «بها» is in the position of the nominative because it stands in place of the fāʿil; likewise in His words {وَيُسْتَهْزَأُ بِهَا}. The original is "someone disbelieves in them"; when the fāʿil was omitted, the preposition with its genitive noun stood in its place; that is why this omitted fāʿil was taken into account, and the pronoun in His words «معهم» and «حتى يخوضوا» refers to it, as though it were said: "when you hear the signs of Allah being disbelieved in by the polytheists and mocked by the hypocrites, do not sit with them until they engage in some other talk", i.e. other than the talk of disbelief and mockery; so the pronoun in «غيره» refers to what the meaning indicates. It was also said: the pronoun in «غيره» may refer to the disbelief and mockery understood from His words «يكفر بها» and «يستهزأ بها»; the pronoun was made singular, although two things are meant by it, for one of two reasons: either because disbelief and mockery are one thing in meaning, or because the pronoun is treated like the demonstrative, as in: {عَوَانٌ بَيْنَ ذلك} [al-Baqara: 68], and [his words]:
1664 - كأنَّه في الجِلْدِ توليعُ البَهَقْ
(As if it were, on the skin, the blotching of leucoderma.)
Its examination has preceded in al-Baqara. And «حتى» is the limit of the prohibition; the meaning is that sitting with them is permissible when they engage in something other than disbelief and mockery.
And His words: {إِنَّكُمْ إِذاً مِّثْلُهُمْ}: «إذنْ» here is rendered inoperative because it falls between a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar. The majority read the lām of «مثلُهم» with ḍamma, as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. It was read anomalously with fatḥa, and there are two explanations of it. The first — the opinion of the Basrans — is that it is also a khabar, and it was given fatḥa only because it is annexed to something not fully declinable, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: {إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ مِّثْلَ مَآ أَنَّكُمْ تَنطِقُونَ} [al-Dhāriyāt: 23] with fatḥa on the lām, and the words of al-Farazdaq:
1665 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . وإذما مثلَهم بشرُ
(… and since no human being is their like.)
on one of the views. The second — the opinion of the Kufans — is that «مثل» may be accusative as an adverbial position, i.e. as an adverb; they permit «زيد مثلك» in the accusative by position, i.e. "Zayd is in a state like yours". «مثل» was made singular even though it is predicated of a plural, and it was not made to agree as what was before it agreed in His words: {ثُمَّ لاَ يكونوا أَمْثَالَكُم} [Muḥammad: 38] and His words {وَحُورٌ عِينٌ كَأَمْثَالِ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 22–23]. Abū al-Baqāʾ and others said: "because here the maṣdar (verbal noun) is intended by it, so it was made singular, as it was made singular in His words: {أَنُؤْمِنُ لِبَشَرَيْنِ مِثْلِنَا} [al-Muʾminūn: 47]." The precise meaning is that the implied form is: "your disobedience is like their disobedience"; however, positing the maṣdar sense in His words «لبشر مثلنا» is awkward.

semin-durr:141-141.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {الذين يَتَرَبَّصُونَ} — there are six views on it. The first: that it is a badal (substitute) from His words {الذين يَتَّخِذُونَ}, so the views mentioned there apply to it. The second: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of «المنافقين» according to the wording, so its position is genitive. The third: that it follows them according to position, so its position is accusative; it is established that when an operative active participle is annexed to what it governs, what it governs may be followed [by an appositive] according to wording and according to position: you say «هذا ضاربٌ هندٍ العاقلةِ والعاقلةَ» ('this one is striking Hind, the sensible'), with «العاقلة» in the genitive or the accusative. The fourth: that it is accusative by way of censure. The fifth: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are those who…". The sixth — mentioned by Abū al-Baqāʾ — is that it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is His words «فإنْ كان لكم فتحُ»; this is weak because the meaning is at odds with it, and because of the addition of the fāʾ in a place not its own, since this relative noun does not clearly resemble a conditional noun.
His words: {وَنَمْنَعْكُمْ} — the majority read it in the jussive (majzūm), conjoined to what precedes it. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with fatḥa on the ʿayn, and this is clear, for it is by an implied «أن» after the wāw that requires combination, in answer to the question, as in the words of al-Ḥuṭayʾa:
1666 - ألم أكُ جارَكمْ ويكونَ بيني ... وبينكمُ المودةُ والإخاءُ
(Was I not your neighbour, with affection and brotherhood being between me and you?)
Ibn ʿAṭiyya used the expression of the Kufans, saying: "with fatḥa on the ʿayn by ṣarf (diversion)", and by ṣarf they mean the verb's not sharing the i'rab of what precedes it. Ubayy read «ومنعناكم», a past verb, and this too is clear, because it is construed according to the meaning, for the meaning of «ألم نستحوذ» is "we have indeed prevailed", because when the interrogative enters upon a negation it affirms it; similar to it is: {أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ وَوَضَعْنَا} [al-Sharḥ: 1–2] — since «ألم نشرح» has the meaning of "We have expanded", «ووضَعْنا» was conjoined to it.
«نستحوذ» and «استحوذ» are among the words that are anomalous by analogy but eloquent in usage, because by right the vowel of its weak letter should be transferred to the quiescent letter before it and it should be changed to an alif, like «استقام» and «استبان» and their class. I have set out the examination of this at His words {نَسْتَعِينُ} [verse 5] in al-Fātiḥa. Other words are anomalous along with it, such as «أَغْيَمت» and «أَغْيلت المرأة» and «أَخْيلت السماء»; the grammarians restricted them to attested usage, while Abū Zayd treated them as a basis for analogy. [Translator's note: the source prints «أَغْمَيتْ», apparently a misprint for «أغْيَمَتْ» (the sky became cloudy); translated per the latter.] Al-istiḥwādh is gaining mastery over something and taking possession of it; from it is: {استحوذ عَلَيْهِمُ الشيطان} [al-Mujādila: 19]. One says «حاذَ» and «أحاذ» with the same meaning, and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is «الحَوْذ».
And His words: {يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ} — it was said that there is an omitted conjoined element here, i.e. "and between them", as in his words:
1667 - فما كانَ بين الخيرِ لو جاء سالماً ... أبو حُجُرٍ إلا ليالٍ قلائِلُ
(Had Abū Ḥujur come back safe, there would have been between good fortune [and me] only a few nights.)
i.e. "and me". The apparent view is that there is no need for that, because the address in «بينكم» includes all, those addressed and those absent being meant; the address merely predominated, for what you know of the usage of the Arabs. His words: {عَلَى المؤمنين} may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to "making" (al-jaʿl), or may be attached to an omitted element, because it is originally an adjective of «سبيلا»; when it was placed before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it.

semin-durr:142-142.t:
And the words of Allah the Exalted: {يُخَادِعُونَ}: its derivation and the meaning of the mufāʿala pattern in it have preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. His words: {وَهُوَ خَادِعُهُمْ} — there are three views on it. The first — mentioned by Abū al-Baqāʾ — is that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The second: that it is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ». The third: that it is a resumptive statement informing of that. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«خادِع» is the active participle of «خادَعْتُه فَخَدَعْتُه» ('I tried to deceive him and outwitted him'), when you overcame him and were more cunning than he." His words «وإذا قاموا» are conjoined to the khabar of «إنَّ»; He informs of them by these blameworthy traits. And «كُسالى» is accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun of «قاموا», which occurs as the answer [of «إذا»]. The majority read it with ḍamma on the kāf, which is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz; al-Aʿraj read it with fatḥa, which is the dialect of Tamīm and Asad; and Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «كَسْلى», describing them with what describes a single feminine, in consideration of the meaning of "group", as in His words: {وتَرَى الناسَ سَكْرى}. Al-kasal is languor and sluggishness; and «أَكْسَل» is said when one has intercourse and slackens without ejaculating.
His words: {يراؤون} — there are three views on this clause. The first: that it is a ḥāl from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «كُسالى». The second: that it is a badal (substitute) from «كُسالى», mentioned by Abū al-Baqāʾ, so it would be a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «قاموا»; there is an objection to this, because the second is neither the first, nor part of it, nor included in it. The third: that it is resumptive, informing of them thus. The original of «يُراؤُون» is «يُرائِيوُن», and it underwent weakening like its counterparts. The majority read «يُراؤُون», from the mufāʿala pattern. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the meaning of murāʾāt, which is mufāʿala from seeing? I say: it has two aspects. The first: that the one who shows off makes them see his deed, and they make him see approval. The second: that it is mufāʿala in the sense of tafʿīl; one says «نعَّمه» and «ناعمه», «فَنَّقه» and «فانَقَه», and «عيش مُفَانِق» ('a pampered life'); Abū Zayd narrated: «رأَّت المَرْأةُ المِرْآة» ('the woman held up the mirror'), when she held it for him so that he could see his face. This is indicated by the reading of Ibn Abī Isḥāq: «يُرَؤُّونهم», with a doubled hamza, like «يُدَعُّونهم», i.e. they make them see, and «يُرَاؤُوْنهم» is likewise." He means that the reading «يُرَؤُّونَهم», without an alif but with a doubled hamza bearing ḍamma, makes clear that the mufāʿala here has the meaning of tafʿīl. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It — meaning this reading — is stronger than «يراؤون» in meaning, because its meaning is that they induce people to see them, and they make a show of prayer before them while concealing hypocrisy." This from him is not good, because if the mufāʿala is in its proper sense it is more emphatic, for what has been known more than once; and if it has the meaning of tafʿīl, it fully conveys the meaning he intended. It is as though he did not know that mufāʿala may come with the meaning of tafʿīl. The object of the showing-off is omitted so that it covers everything by which one shows off. The best is to posit: "they show off to people with their deeds".
And His words: {قَلِيلاً} are a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) or of an omitted time, i.e. "a little remembrance" or "a little time"; "littleness" here is in its proper sense. Al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya permitted it to have the meaning of non-existence, but its being excepted rules this out; the rebuttal of them on this has preceded. And His words: {وَلاَ يَذْكُرُونَ} may be conjoined to «يُراؤُون», or may be a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «يُراؤون»; the latter is weak, because the imperfect negated by «لا» is like the affirmative, and the affirmative, when it occurs as a ḥāl, is not joined with the wāw; but if one makes it [the wāw] a conjunction, it is permissible.

semin-durr:143-143.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مُّذَبْذَبِينَ} — there are three views on it. The first: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يُراؤون». The second: that it is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «ولا يَذْكُرُون». The third: that it is accusative by way of censure. The majority read «مذبذَبين» with a mīm bearing ḍamma and two dotted dhāls, the second with fatḥa, as a passive participle, from «ذبذبته فهو مُذَبْذَب», i.e. perplexed. Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid read it with kasra on the second dhāl, as an active participle, and there are two possibilities in it. The first: that it is from the transitive «ذَبْذَبَ», so its object is omitted, i.e. "wavering themselves, or their religion", or the like. The second: that it has the meaning of tafaʿlala, as in «صَلْصَلَ», so it is intransitive; this second is indicated by the reading of Ubayy and what is in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh: «مُتَذَبْذِبين»; therefore the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās may have the meaning of «متذبذبين». Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read «مَذَبْذَبِين», with fatḥa on the mīm. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is rejected," and by my life he spoke the truth; it should not be held authentic from him. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] excused it, because of al-Ḥasan's eloquence and people's citing his speech as evidence, [saying] that the fatḥa of the mīm is to make it harmonise with the vowel of the dhāl. He said: "Since they made the vowel of the mīm in «مِنْتِن» harmonise with the vowel of the tāʾ despite the barrier between them, and in the like of «منحدُر» made the vowel of the dāl harmonise with the vowel of the rāʾ in the nominative state, even though the case vowel is not permanent, it is all the more fitting that they harmonise in the like of «مَذَبذبين»." This is invalid, because harmonisation in the examples he cited and their counterparts occurs only when the vowel is strong, namely the ḍamma and the kasra; the fatḥa is light, so they did not harmonise for its sake. [Translator's note: the source prints «منحدْر» with sukūn on the dāl; the argument requires «منحدُر» harmonised to «منحُدُر»; translated per the argument.] Ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read it with two undotted dāls, from al-dubba, which is "the way"; one says «خَلَّني ودُبَّتي», i.e. my way. He said:
1668 - طَها هُذْرُبانٌ قَلَّ تغميضُ عيِنِه ... على دُبَّةٍ مثلِ الخَنيفِ المُرَعْبَلِ
(A prattler went off, his eye seldom closing, on a way like a tattered linen garment.)
And in the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās: "Follow the dubba of Quraysh", i.e. their way. The meaning on this reading is that He takes them at one time on one way and at another time on another way, so they follow perplexed, not proceeding on a single path.
«مُذَبْذَب» and the like, such as «مُكَبْكَب» and «مُكَفْكَف» — words whose first and second [radicals] are repeated and whose meaning remains valid with the third dropped — there are several positions on them. The first — the opinion of the majority of the Basrans — is that all are radicals, because the minimum structure is three radicals, and neither of the two repeated elements is more entitled to be augmentative than the other. The second — attributed to al-Zajjāj — is that what may validly be dropped is augmentative. The third — the opinion of the Kufans — is that the third is a replacement for the doubling of the second; they claim that the origin of «كفكف» is «كَفَّفَ» with three fāʾs, and of «ذبذب» «ذَبَّب» with three bāʾs; the succession of three identical letters was found heavy, so they replaced the third with one of the kind of the first. These positions have a place other than this, where I have set out their discussions in detail. As for where the meaning is not valid with the third dropped, as in «سِمْسم», «يُؤْيؤ» and «وعْوَع», all hold that all [the letters] are radicals. Al-dhabdhaba is originally agitation and wavering between two states. Al-Nābigha said:
1669 - ألم تَرَ أنَّ اللهَ أَعْطاك سُورةً ... تَرَى كُلَّ مَلْكٍ دونَها يَتَذَبْذَبُ
(Do you not see that Allah has given you a rank, below which you see every king wavering?)
And another said:
1670 - خيالٌ لأمِّ السَّلْبيل ودونَها ... مسيرةُ شهرٍ للبعيرِ المُذَبْذِبِ
(A phantom of Umm al-Salbīl, while short of her lies a month's journey for the restless camel.)
with kasra on the second dhāl. Ibn Jinnī said: "i.e. the restless one that does not settle." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The real meaning of al-mudhabdhab is one who is driven off (yudhabbu) from both sides, i.e. repelled and pushed away, so he does not settle on one side, as is said: 'So-and-so is tossed about by the two millstones'; except that dhabdhaba contains a repetition not found in dhabb, as though the meaning were: whenever he inclines to a side, he is driven off from it."
And «بين» is governed by His words «مُذَبْذَبين», and «ذلك» points to disbelief and faith, indicated by the mention of the disbelievers and the believers, as in:
1671 - إذا نُهِي السفيهُ جَرَى إليه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(When the fool is forbidden, he runs towards it …)
i.e. towards folly, because the word "fool" indicates it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It was pointed to even though there was no mention of it, because the speech implies it, as in: {حتى تَوَارَتْ بالحجاب} [Ṣād: 32] and {كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ} [al-Raḥmān: 26]" — meaning the sun was hidden, and everyone on the earth. The Shaykh said: "It is not so; rather, something indicating it has preceded," and he mentioned what I set out earlier. «ذلك», which is singular, was used to point to two things for the reason that preceded at His words {عَوَانٌ بَيْنَ ذلك} [al-Baqara: 68]. His words: {لاَ إلى هؤلاء وَلاَ إِلَى هؤلاء}: «إلى» in both places is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted element, and that omitted element is a ḥāl, omitted because the meaning indicates it; the implied form is: "wavering, attributed neither to these nor to those", so what governs the ḥāl is «مُذَبْذَبين» itself. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The position of «لا إلى هؤلاء» is accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مذبذبين», i.e. they waver, changing colour." This is an explanation of meaning, not of i'rab.

semin-durr:144-144.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {سُلْطَاناً}: «السلطان» is treated as masculine and as feminine; its masculine is in consideration of "proof" (burhān), and its feminine in consideration of "argument" (ḥujja), except that the feminine is more frequent among the eloquent — so said al-Farrāʾ, and he related: «قَضَتْ عليك السلطان» and «أَخَذَتْ فلاناً السلطانُ». On this basis, how was its adjective made masculine, so that «مبيناً» was said and not «مبينة»? The answer is that the adjective here is at the end of a verse-ending (fāṣila), so for that reason it turned to the masculine rather than the feminine. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said something contrary to what al-Farrāʾ related, for he said: "The masculine is better known, and it is the usage of the Quran wherever it occurs." And «عليكم» may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to the "making", or to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «سلطانا», because it is originally its adjective; its like has preceded.

semin-durr:176-176.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {فِي الكلالة}: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يُفْتيكم», by giving government to the second [verb], which is the choice of the Basrans; had He given government to the first, He would have implied a pronoun in the second. It has parallels in the Qurʾān: {هَآؤُمُ اقرؤا كِتَابيَهْ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 19], {آتوني أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْراً} [al-Kahf: 96], {وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعَالَوْاْ يَسْتَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ رَسُولُ الله} [al-Munāfiqūn: 5], {والذين كَفَرواْ وَكَذَّبُواْ بِآيَاتِنَآ} [al-Baqara: 39]. Discussion of it, more fully than this, has preceded in Sūrat al-Baqara, so let it be consulted. The derivation of «الكلالة» has also preceded at the beginning of this sūra.

His saying: {إِن امرؤ} is like His saying {وَإِنِ امرأة} [al-Nisāʾ: 128]. «هلك» is a verbal clause in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «امرؤ».

«ليس له ولدٌ» is also a clause in the position of the nominative, as a second adjective. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted that this clause be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «هلك», and mentioned nothing else. And al-Zamakhsharī prohibited «[Translator's note: the text has «ومع», apparently a misprint for «ومنع» "prohibited"; translated accordingly.]» that it be a ḥāl, without explaining the reason for that, nor explaining who the one described by the ḥāl would be: is it «امرؤ» or the pronoun in «هلك»?

Al-Shaykh said: "Al-Zamakhsharī prohibited that His saying «ليس له ولد» be a ḥāl clause from the pronoun in «هلك», saying: 'The position of «ليس له ولد» is the nominative as an adjective, not the accusative as a ḥāl'." End of quotation. But al-Zamakhsharī did not say that, i.e. he did not prohibit its being a ḥāl from the pronoun in «هلك»; rather he prohibited its being a ḥāl in general, as is the apparent sense of his words. He may have meant to prohibit its being a ḥāl from «امرؤ» because it is indefinite; but the indefinite here has been specified by the adjective; and in any case the ḥāl from an indefinite is rarer than from a definite. What ought to be held is that its being a ḥāl is prohibited absolutely, as is the apparent sense of his wording. That is because this clause that explains the omitted verb has no grammatical position, so it resembles emphasizing clauses; and when you add a follower or a predicate, you intend only that noun which came first in the previous, emphasized clause, not the noun repeated in the second clause that came as emphasis, because the first clause is the one intended by the statement. So if you say «ضربتُ زيداً ضربت زيداً الفاضلَ» ("I struck Zayd, I struck Zayd, the excellent"), «الفاضل» is the adjective of the first «زيداً», because it is in the emphasized clause that is intended by the statement; and the separation between the adjective and what it qualifies by the emphasizing clause does no harm. This sense excludes its being a ḥāl from the pronoun in «هلك». What excludes its being a ḥāl from «امرؤ» is what I mentioned to you: the rarity of the ḥāl coming from an indefinite, in general.

In this verse, according to what they chose — «ليس له ولد» being an adjective — there is evidence for separating the adjective and what it qualifies by the clause that explains the omitted [verb] in the chapter of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb). Its parallel is: «إنْ رجلٌ قام عاقلٌ فأكرمْه» ("If an intelligent man stands, honour him"): «عاقل» is an adjective of «رجل», separated from it by «قام», which explains the explained «قام» «[Translator's note: so in the text: «المفسِّرٍ ل» قام المفسَّر», i.e. the overt «قام» explains the implied «قام».]».

His saying: {وَلَهُ أُخْتٌ} is like His saying {لَيْسَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ}, and the fāʾ in «فلها» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of «إنْ». His saying: {وَهُوَ يَرِثُهَآ}: this clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive; it indicates the apodosis and is not the apodosis — contrary to the Kufans and Abū Zayd. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "This clause has taken the place of the apodosis", meaning that it indicates it, as has preceded; this is as the grammarians say: when a condition and an oath come together, the first of them is answered, and that answer is made to take the place of the answer of the other.

The two pronouns in His saying «وهو يرثها» refer back to the wording of «امرئ» and «أخت», not their meaning; so it is of the category of the poet's saying:

168 - 2- وكُلُّ أناسٍ قاربوا قيدَ فَحْلِهمْ ... ونحن خَلَعْنا قيدَه فَهْوَ سارِبُ
(Every people has shortened the hobble of its stallion, but we have taken off his hobble, so he roams freely.)

and their saying «عندي درهمٌ ونصفه» ("I have a dirham and half of it"), and His saying, Exalted is He: {وَمَا يُعَمَّرُ مِن مُّعَمَّرٍ وَلاَ يُنقَصُ مِنْ عُمُرِهِ}. This was needed only because a living woman is not inherited from, and the one who has perished does not inherit; so the meaning is: and another man, other than the one who perished, inherits from another sister of his.

His saying: {فَإِن كَانَتَا اثنتين}: regarding the alif in «كانتا» there are several views. The first «[Translator's note: the text has the dual «أحدُهما».]»: that it refers to the two sisters, as indicated by His saying «وله أخت», i.e. "if the sisters are two". The grammarians have been accustomed to raise a question here, namely: the khabar (predicate) must convey what the mubtadaʾ (subject) does not, otherwise it is not meaningful speech; that is why they prohibited «سيدُ الجارية مالكُها» ("The slave-girl's master is her owner"), because the predicate added nothing to what the subject conveyed. Here the predicate indicated a number, [but] that number is already conveyed by the alif in «كانتا». They have answered this with several answers. Among them is what Abū al-Ḥasan and al-Akhfash «[Translator's note: so in the text; Abū al-Ḥasan is himself al-Akhfash's kunya, so «و» "and" appears to be an error.]» mentioned, namely that His saying «اثنتين» indicates mere duality, without restriction to young or old or other such descriptions; i.e. the two-thirds are due by virtue of this number alone, without regard to any other restriction, and so the speech becomes informative thereby. This is not clear, because the alif in «كانتا» also indicates mere duality without restriction to young or old or other descriptions; so the matter returns to the predicate conveying nothing other than what the subject conveyed.

Among them is what al-Makkī mentioned, also from al-Akhfash, and al-Zamakhsharī and others followed him, namely construing it on the meaning of «مَنْ». Its explanation is what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned; he said, may Allah have mercy on him: "If you say: to whom do the dual and plural pronouns refer in His saying {فَإِن كَانَتَا اثنتين، وَإِن كانوا إِخْوَةً}? I say: its origin is: 'if those (مَنْ) who inherit through brotherhood are two [females], and if [those] who inherit through brotherhood are males and females'. It was said 'فإن كانتا' and 'وإن كانوا' just as it is said «مَنْ كانت أمَّك» ('who was your mother?'): just as the pronoun of «مَنْ» was made feminine because of the femininity of the predicate, so He made the pronoun of 'those who inherit' dual and plural in «كانتا» and «كانوا» because of the duality and plurality of the predicate." And it is a good answer.

But al-Shaykh objected to it, saying: "This explanation is not sound, and it is not a parallel of «مَنْ كانت أمَّك», because there «مَنْ» is stated explicitly, and it has wording and meaning; whoever makes it feminine pays regard to the meaning, because the implied form is 'which mother was your mother?', and what the predicate denotes in this differs from what the noun denotes — unlike the verse, where the two denotations are one. Nor was it made feminine in «مَنْ كانت أمك» because of the femininity of the predicate; it was only made feminine because of the meaning of «من», since a feminine was intended by it. Do you not see that you say «مَنْ قامت» ('who [fem.] stood?'), making it feminine out of regard for the meaning when you mean to ask about a female, and there is no predicate here for «قامت» to be made feminine on its account?" End of quotation. This is a prejudiced attack from him, as is his habit; al-Zamakhsharī and others did not deny that the word «مَنْ» is not stated explicitly in the verse, so that he should distinguish for them with this obscure distinction. This explanation mentioned is the second view on the alif.

The apparent view is that the pronoun in «كانتا» refers to the two female heirs, «اثنتين» is its khabar, and «له» «[Translator's note: so in the text; perhaps «لها» "it has" was intended, i.e. «اثنتين» has an omitted adjective.]» is an omitted adjective by which the difference between the noun and the predicate is obtained, the implied form being: "if the two female heirs are two of the sisters". This is a good answer, and the omission of an adjective because the meaning is understood is not objectionable, even if it is rarer than the reverse. It is also possible that the khabar of «كان» is omitted, and the alif refers to the two sisters indicated by His saying «وله أخت», as was mentioned from al-Akhfash and others; in that case His saying «اثنتين» is an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), the implied form being "and if the two sisters are his", «له» having been omitted because His saying «وله أخت» indicates it. So these are four views.

«وإنْ كانوا»: regarding this pronoun there are three analyses. The first: that it refers to the meaning of the implied «مَنْ», its implied form being "if those who inherit are brothers", as its explanation preceded from al-Zamakhsharī and others. The second: that it refers to the brothers, the predicate having conveyed [information] by the detailing, for «الإخوة» includes males and females; even if it is apparent in males specifically, the predicate has conveyed what the noun did not. If it refers to the heir, it has conveyed what the noun did not convey in a clear way; this is the third analysis. His saying «فللذكرِ» means "of them", which was omitted because the meaning indicates it.

His saying: {أَن تَضِلُّواْ}: there are three analyses. The most apparent: that the object of the making-clear is omitted, and «أن تَضِلُّوا» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) by the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being: "Allah makes clear the matter of the kalāla out of dislike that you go astray in it", i.e. in its ruling; this is al-Mubarrad's construal. The second — the view of al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ and others of the Kufans — is that «لا» is omitted after «أن», the implied form being "lest you go astray". They said: "The omission of «لا» is widespread and common, as in the poet's saying:

168 - 3- رأينا ما رأى البُصَراءُ فيها ... فآلينا عليها أَنْ تُباعَا
(We saw in her what the discerning saw, so we swore concerning her that she [not] be sold.)

i.e. that she not be sold." Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj said: "It is like His saying, Exalted is He: {إِنَّ الله يُمْسِكُ السموات والأرض أَن تَزُولاَ} [Fāṭir: 41], i.e. lest they cease." Abū ʿUbayd said: "I narrated to al-Kisāʾī the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar, namely: 'Let none of you supplicate against his child, lest (أن) it coincide with an answer from Allah', and he found it good", i.e. "lest it coincide". Al-Fārisī preferred al-Mubarrad's view on the ground that omission of the muḍāf is more widespread than omission of negating «لا». The third: that it is the object of «يبين», the meaning being: Allah makes clear to you misguidance so that you avoid it, because when evil is made clear it is avoided, and when good is made clear it is undertaken.

semin-durr:145-145.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {فِي الدرك}: the Kufans — with a divergent narration from ʿĀṣim — read it with a quiescent rāʾ, and the rest with fatḥa on it. There are two opinions on this. The first: that «الدَّرْك» and «الدَّرَك» are two dialectal forms with one meaning, like «الشَّمْع» and «الشَّمَع», «القَدْر» and «القَدَر». The second: that «الدَّرَك» with fatḥa is the plural of «دَرَكة», in the manner of «بَقَر» and «بَقَرة». Abū ʿUbayd chose the fatḥa; he said: "because the mention of «الدَّرَك» in the reports has come only with fatḥa." This is not binding, since ḥadīths come with one of the two dialectal forms. Some chose the fatḥa because of its plural on afʿāl. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The proper form is with the vowel, because of their saying «أدراك جهنم»" — meaning that afʿāl is regular for faʿal with fatḥa, not for faʿl with sukūn; however, afʿāl has come for faʿl with sukūn, as in «فَرْخ» and «أَفْراخ», «زَنْد» and «أَزْناد», «فَرْد» and «أَفْراد». Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Fāsī said in his commentary on al-Qaṣīda: "Someone else — meaning other than ʿĀṣim — said, arguing for the reading with fatḥa: their saying «أَدْراك» for its plural indicates that it is «دَرَك» with fatḥa. What he said is also not binding, because faʿal with the vowel has been given the plural afʿāl, like «قَلَم» and «أَقْلام», «جَبَل» and «أَجبال»." End of quotation. [Translator's note: the source prints «أَفْعاله», evidently a slip for «أَفْعال».] This is an oversight on his part, because what is disputed is only faʿl with sukūn: does it take the plural afʿāl or not? As for faʿal with the vowel, afʿāl is its regular pattern. It is as though he intended to rebut al-Zamakhsharī and fell into error; he should have said: faʿl with sukūn has been given the plural afʿāl, as in «فَرْخ» and «أَفْراخ», as I mentioned to you. It is related that ʿĀṣim said: "If «الدرَك» were with fatḥa, it ought to have been said «السُّفْلى», not «الأسفل»." One of the grammarians said: "He means that «الدرَك» with fatḥa is the plural of «دَرَكة», as «بَقَر» is the plural of «بَقَرة», and the plural is treated as feminine." This is not binding, because a generic noun whose singular is distinguished from its plural by the feminine tāʾ may be treated as masculine or feminine, except those excepted as obligatorily masculine or feminine, and «الدرك» is not among them, so both treatments are permissible in it — and this is after granting that «الدرك» is the plural of «دَرَكة» with sukūn, as preceded. [Translator's note: the source says "«دَرَكة» with sukūn", whereas the view stated above is that «الدَّرَك» with fatḥa is the plural of «دَرَكة»; translated as written.] «الدَّرَك» is taken from al-mudāraka, which is following in succession; the levels of the Fire were called «دَرَكات» because some of them follow upon others, i.e. are successive. His words: {مِنَ النار} are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and there are two views about the one it refers to. The first: that it is «الدرك», and what governs it is the [implied] "being settled". The second: that it is the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «الأسفل», because it is an adjective and so carries a pronoun.

semin-durr:146-146.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِلاَّ الذين} — there are three views on it. The first: that it is accusative as an exception from His words {إِنَّ المنافقين}. The second: that it is excepted from the genitive pronoun in «لهم». The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is the clause of His words {فأولئك مَعَ المؤمنين}. It was said: "The fāʾ entered the khabar because the mubtadaʾ resembles a conditional noun." Abū al-Baqāʾ, Makkī and others said: "«مع المؤمنين» is the khabar of «أولئك», and the clause is the khabar of «إلا الذين», the implied form being: then those are believers with the believers." This implied form is not required by grammatical craft; rather, what grammatical craft requires is that the khabar to which this adverbial is attached be posited as something fitting it, namely "then those are accompanying", or "being", or "settled", and the like; so you posit it as an absolute being (kawn muṭlaq) or something close to it.
His words: {وَسَوْفَ يُؤْتِ الله}: «يؤت» was written without a yāʾ, although it is a nominative imperfect verb, so its yāʾ ought by right to be retained in pronunciation and in writing; however, it was dropped in pronunciation in connected speech because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, so the orthography followed the pronunciation; it has counterparts, some of which have preceded.
