The Readers pause on it without a yāʾ, following the noble script, except Yaʿqūb, who pauses with the yāʾ in view of the original; this is also narrated from al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza. Abū ʿAmr said: "One should not pause on it, because if one pauses on it as in the script, without a yāʾ, one contradicts the grammarians; and if one pauses with the yāʾ, one contradicts the script of the codex." There is no harm in what he said, because pausing is not necessary; if one who pauses is compelled to it, by running out of breath and the like, he should follow the script, because word-endings are frequently dropped. Something resembling this place is His words: {وَمَن تَقِ السيئات يَوْمَئِذٍ} [Ghāfir: 9], for «تَقِ» was written with a qāf without the hāʾ of pause; according to the grammarians, when something is dropped from a verb until only one letter of it remains and one pauses on it, the hāʾ of pause must be brought at its end to compensate it, as in «قِهْ», «لم يقه», «عِه» and «لم يَعِه»; the imperfect prefix is not counted, because it is additional to the structure of the word. Once this is established, we say: one should not pause on it, because if one pauses without the hāʾ of pause, one contradicts grammatical craft, and if one pauses with the hāʾ, one contradicts the script of the codex.

semin-durr:147-147.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {مَّا يَفْعَلُ الله بِعَذَابِكُمْ} — there are two views on «ما». The first: that it is interrogative, so it is in the position of the accusative governed by «يفعل»; it was placed first only because it has the right to the head of the sentence. On this view the bāʾ is causal and attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يفعل». The interrogative here means negation, and the meaning is that Allah does nothing by punishing you, because He brings Himself no benefit by punishing you and wards off no harm from Himself by it — so what need has He of punishing you? The second: that «ما» is negating, as though it were said: Allah does not punish you; on this view the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) and is not attached to anything. In my view these two views are one thing in meaning, so it [the bāʾ] should be causal in both places or redundant in both, because the interrogative has the meaning of negation, so there is no difference. The maṣdar (verbal noun) here is annexed to its object. And His words: {إِن شَكَرْتُمْ} — its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because what precedes indicates it, i.e. "if you are grateful and believe, then what will He do by punishing you?"

semin-durr:148-148.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لاَّ يُحِبُّ الله الجهر بالسوء}: «بالسوء» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «الجهر», which is a maṣdar (verbal noun) made definite by «أل»; al-Fārisī used it as evidence that a maṣdar made definite by «أل» may govern. It was said: there is no proof in it, because an adverbial and a preposition [with its noun] are governed even by the faint scent of verbs. The fāʿil (agent) of this maṣdar is omitted, i.e. "someone's speaking openly"; it has preceded that the omission of the fāʿil is regular in certain forms, among them the maṣdar. «الجهر» may also be taken from a passive verb — with disagreement over that — so the preposition with its noun after it would be in the position of the nominative, standing in place of the fāʿil, because if you said "Allah does not love that evil be spoken openly", «بالسوء» would stand in place of the fāʿil and would not then be attached to it. And «من القول» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السوء».
His words: {إِلاَّ مَن ظُلِمَ} — there are two opinions about this exception. The first: that it is connected (muttaṣil). The second: that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ). If it is said to be connected, it was said: it is excepted from the implied «أحد» which is the fāʿil of the maṣdar, so «مَن» may be in the position of the accusative on the basic rule of exception, or of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from «أحد» — and this is the preferred view. If it were made explicit, it would be said: "Allah does not love that anyone speak evil openly except the wronged", with «المظلوم» nominative or accusative. Makkī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and others mentioned this. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is the position of al-Farrāʾ, who permitted in «ما قام إلا زيدٌ» that «زيد» be a badal from «أحد». On the position of the majority, it is of the excepted for which the governing element is left free (mufarragh), so it is nominative as the fāʿil of the maṣdar; this is made good by «الجهر» being within the scope of negation, as though it were said: no one speaks evil words openly except the wronged." End of quotation. The difference between the position of al-Farrāʾ and this verse is clear, for the grammarians did not accept the position of al-Farrāʾ, they said, because the omitted element has become utterly forgotten; whereas the fāʿil of the maṣdar here is like something pronounced, not forgotten. So their permitting exception from this implied fāʿil does not entail their following the position of al-Farrāʾ, given the evident difference. It was also said: it is an unfilled (mufarragh) exception, so «مَنْ» is in the position of the nominative as fāʿil, as set out in the Shaykh's words; the unfilled exception occurs only in a negation or what resembles it, but since «الجهر» is the object of the love that falls within the scope of negation, that became acceptable. It was also said: it is excepted from «الجهر» with the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being "except the speaking openly of one who was wronged". These are three views on the assumption that it is connected, from which four views on the position of «مَنْ» are obtained: the nominative from two views, namely as a badal from the implied «أحد», or as fāʿil on its being unfilled; and the accusative on the basic rule of exception from the implied «أحد», or from «الجهر» with the omission of a muḍāf.
The second: that it is a disconnected exception, its implied form being: "but one who has been wronged may obtain redress from his wrongdoer with what equals his grievance"; so «مَنْ» is in the position of the accusative only, as a disconnected exception.
The majority read «إلاَّ مَنْ ظُلِمَ» in the passive; a large group, among them Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn Jubayr and al-Ḥasan, read «ظَلَم» in the active, and it is a disconnected exception, so it is in the position of the accusative on the basic rule of the disconnected exception. The scholars' expressions differed in positing this exception, and the upshot comes back to one of three implied forms: either it refers back to the first clause, as though it were said: "Allah does not love speaking evil openly, but the wrongdoer loves it, so he does it"; or it refers back to the fāʿil of «الجهر», i.e. "Allah does not love that anyone speak evil openly, but the wrongdoer speaks it openly"; or it refers back to the object of «الجهر», namely "the one to whom evil is spoken openly and to whose face it is said", i.e. "Allah does not love that evil be spoken openly to anyone, but evil is spoken openly to the wrongdoer", i.e. his evil traits are mentioned to his face, that perhaps he may desist. That this excepted element in this reading is in the position of the accusative as disconnected is the correct view. Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Zamakhsharī permitted it to be in the position of the nominative as a badal, but their reasoning differed. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The i'rab of «مَنْ» in some of these interpretations may be the accusative, and it may be the nominative as a badal from the implied «أحد»" — meaning the «أحد» implied in the maṣdar, as its examination preceded. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«مَنْ» may be nominative, as though it were said: Allah does not love speaking evil openly except the wrongdoer, according to the dialect of those who say «ما جاءني زيدٌ إلا عمروٌ» ('Zayd did not come to me, except ʿAmr'), meaning: none came to me but ʿAmr; and from it is {لاَّ يَعْلَمُ مَن فِي السماوات والأرض الغيب إِلاَّ الله} [al-Naml: 65]." The Shaykh rebutted them both, saying: "What he — meaning Ibn ʿAṭiyya — mentioned of the permissibility of the nominative as a badal is not correct, because the disconnected [exception] is of two kinds. One kind is that to which the governing element can be directed, as in «ما فيها أحدٌ إلا حمار» ('there is no one in it except a donkey'); in this there are two dialects: the dialect of the Ḥijāz requires the accusative, and the dialect of Tamīm permits the badal. If the governing element cannot be directed to it, its accusative is obligatory for all, as in «المالُ ما زاد إلا النقصَ» ('the wealth did not increase, except decrease'), i.e. but decrease befell it; the badal is not permissible in it, because if you directed the governing element to it, it would not be valid." He said: "The verse is of this kind, because if you said «لا يحبُّ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَجْهَرَ بالسوءِ إلا الظالمُ», making «يجهر» govern «الظالم», it would not be valid." And he said: "What he — meaning al-Zamakhsharī — permitted is not permissible, because the fāʿil cannot be void (laghw), and «الظالم» cannot be a badal from «الله», nor «عمرو» a badal from «زيد», because the badal in this chapter comes back to a badal of part from whole, either in reality, as in «ما قام القومُ إلا زيدٌ», or figuratively, as in «ما فيها أحدٌ إلا حمارٌ»; and in the verse the badal is permissible neither in reality nor figuratively, and likewise the example mentioned, because "Allah the Exalted" is a proper name, and likewise "Zayd", so there is no generality in them such that something could be imagined to be included in them and then be excepted. As for the disconnected exception in which the badal is permissible, that is because what precedes it is general, and [the excepted] is imagined to be included in it, so it is substituted for what precedes figuratively. As for his saying 'according to the dialect of those who say «ما جاءني زيد إلا عمروٌ»', we do not know this as a dialect except in the Book of Sībawayh, after he recited verses on the disconnected exception, the last of which is:
1672 - عَشِيَّةَ ما تُغْني الرماحُ مكانَها ... ولا النبلُ إلا المشرفيُّ المُصَمَّمُ
(On the evening when neither the spears availed in their place, nor the arrows — only the Mashrafī sword that cuts through the bone.)
Its text is: 'This strengthens «ما أتاني زيدٌ إلاَّ عمروٌ» and «ما أعانَه إخوانُكم إلا إخوانُه», because they are definites, the latter nouns being neither them nor part of them.' He neither stated nor hinted that «ما أتاني زيدٌ إلا عمرو» is from the speech of the Arabs. One who commented on Sībawayh's words said: 'So this strengthens «ما أتاني زيدٌ إلا عمرو»', i.e. this ought to be established as the speech of the Arabs, because «النبل» is a definite that is not the Mashrafī, just as Zayd is not ʿAmr, and just as Zayd's brothers are not your brothers." The Shaykh said: "«ما أتاني زيدٌ إلا عمرو» is not analogous to the verse, because a generality may be imagined in the verse, since the meaning is: weapons did not avail; whereas no generality is imagined in «زيد». Moreover, if «ما أتاني زيدٌ إلا عمرو» did occur in their speech, it could be valid as «ما أتاني زيد ولا غيره إلا عمروٌ» ('neither Zayd nor anyone else came to me except ʿAmr'), the conjoined element having been omitted because the exception indicates it. As for its being on the voiding of the fāʿil, or on «عمرو» being a badal from «زيد», that is not permissible. As for the verse, it is not of what he mentioned, because «مَنْ» may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and «الغَيبَ» a badal from it, a badal of inclusion, the implied form being: 'none knows the unseen of those in the heavens and the earth except Allah', i.e. their secret and their open affairs none knows except Allah. And if it is granted that «مَنْ» is in a nominative position, a generality may be imagined in it, so «الله» is substituted for it figuratively, as though it were said: 'none of the existing beings knows the unseen except Allah'; or it is by way of figurative locative sense in relation to Allah the Exalted, since that has come concerning Him in the Quran and the Sunna, as in {وَهُوَ الله فِي السماوات وَفِي الأرض} [al-Anʿām: 3] and {وَهُوَ الذي فِي السمآء إله وَفِي الأرض إله} [al-Zukhruf: 84]; [and] he said: 'Where is Allah?' She said: 'In the heaven.' And from the speech of the Arabs: «لا وذو في السماءِ بيتُه» ('No, by the One whose house is in the heaven'), meaning Allah. Since the verse admits these views, interpreting it as he mentioned is not determined." End of his rebuttal of them both.
His rebuttal of Ibn ʿAṭiyya is clear; as for his rebuttal of al-Zamakhsharī, some of it is open to objection. As for his saying "we do not know it as a dialect except in the Book of Sībawayh", that suffices as proof of the validity of using its like; that is why the commentators on the Book of Sībawayh explained these words as being the analogy of the speech of the Arabs, because of the verses he recited. As for his interpreting «ما أتاني زيدٌ إلا عمروٌ» as «ما أتاني زيد ولا غيرُه», what he said is not the only possibility; the validity of the exception in it is that the speaker's saying «ما أتاني زيد» might suggest that ʿAmr also did not come to him, so he negated this suggestion, and this much suffices in a disconnected exception. If the interpretation of «ما أتاني زيد إلا عمروٌ» were as he said, it would not be a disconnected exception but a connected one, whereas the grammarians agreed that it is disconnected. As for interpreting the verse with what he mentioned, figurative usage in that is a perilous matter, and one should not venture upon its like.

semin-durr:149-149.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَوْ تُخْفُوهْ}: the apparent view is that the accusative pronoun in «تُخْفوه» refers to «خيراً», by which all deeds of righteousness are meant. Some permitted it to refer to «السوء», i.e. "or you conceal the evil", and that is far-fetched.

semin-durr:150-150.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {بَيْنَ ذلك}: «ذلك», which is for the singular, was used to point, and what is meant by it is the in-between, i.e. between disbelief and faith; its like has preceded in al-Baqara. «بين» may be accusative governed by «يتخذ», or accusative by an omitted element, since it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «سبيلاً».

semin-durr:151-151.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {حَقّاً} — there are several views on it. The first: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasising the content of the clause before it, so its governing element must be implied and placed after the clause it emphasises; the implied form is "I affirm that as true, truly", and so it is with every maṣdar emphasising something else or itself. The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from His words {هُمُ الكافرون}; Abū al-Baqāʾ said: i.e. "disbelievers without doubt" — and this resembles an explanation of the emphasising maṣdar. Al-Wāḥidī criticised this explanation, saying: "Disbelief cannot be true (ḥaqq) in any way." The answer is that "ḥaqq" here is not meant as what is opposed to falsehood; rather what is meant is that it is established without doubt and that their disbelief is certain. The third: that it is the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "the disbelievers, with a true disbelief"; this too is an emphasising maṣdar, but the difference between it and the first view is that here its governing element is mentioned, namely the active participle, whereas in that one its governing element is omitted, as preceded.

semin-durr:152-152.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ}: the discussion of «بين» entering upon {أَحَدٍ} has preceded in al-Baqara [verse 136], which makes repeating it unnecessary. The majority read «سوف نُؤتيهم» with the nūn of majesty, by way of iltifāt (shift of person) and to agree with His words «وأَعْتدنا». [Translator's note: the source prints «الالتفاف», evidently a slip for «الالتفات».] Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read it with the yāʾ, making the pronoun refer back to the name of Allah the Exalted in His words {والذين آمَنُواْ بالله}. The saying of some, "the reading with the nūn is preferable because it is more majestic and to correspond with «وأعتدنا»", is not good, because both readings are mutawātir (mass-transmitted).

semin-durr:153-153.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَقَدْ سَأَلُواْ} — there are two opinions about this fāʾ. The first: that it conjoins to an omitted clause. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Its implied form is: so pay no heed, O Muḥammad, to their asking and their excess, for it is their habit; they asked Moses for something greater than that." The second: that it is the answer of an implied condition; al-Zamakhsharī said: "i.e. if you find what they asked of you to be enormous, [know that] they asked …". And «أكبَرَ» is the adjective of an omitted noun, i.e. "a request greater than that". The majority read «أكبرَ» with the single-dotted bāʾ, and al-Ḥasan's reading is «أكثر» with the three-dotted thāʾ. His words: {فقالوا أَرِنَا} — this clause explains the greatness and enormity of the request. And {جَهْرَةً} — the discussion of it has preceded [al-Baqara: 55], except that here «جهرةً» may describe the saying or the request, or describe those asking, i.e. "they said, openly", or "they asked, openly"; so it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) or as a maṣdar (verbal noun). The majority read «الصاعقةُ», and al-Nakhaʿī read «الصَّعْقةُ»; the examination of this has preceded in al-Baqara. «وبظلمِهم» — the bāʾ in it is causal, and it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to "the seizing".

semin-durr:154-154.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَوْقَهُمُ} — there are two views on it. The apparent one of them is that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «رَفَعْنا». Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted a second view, namely that it is attached to an omitted element because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الطور». «بميثاقهم» is also attached to the raising, and the bāʾ is causal. They said: in the speech there is the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being "for the breaking of their covenant". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«بميثاقِهم»: because of their covenant, that they might fear and so not break it." The apparent sense of this expression is that there is no need to omit a muḍāf; indeed I say: it is not permissible to posit this muḍāf, because it entails that they broke the covenant and Allah raised the Mount over them as punishment for their act of breaking, whereas the story requires that they intended to break the covenant, so Allah raised the Mount over them, and they feared and did not break it — even though they broke it after that. Abū al-Baqāʾ stated explicitly that they broke the covenant and that He the Exalted raised the Mount as punishment for them, saying: "Its implied form is: for the breaking of their covenant; and the meaning is: and We raised the Mount above them to frighten them, because of their breaking the covenant." The same objection mentioned above applies to it. Someone might say: since they intended to break it and came close to it, it is valid to say "We raised the Mount over them for their breaking the covenant", i.e. for their coming close to breaking it, because what comes close to a thing is given its ruling; so the expression of those who posited a muḍāf, like Abū al-Baqāʾ and others, is valid. «الميثاق» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its object. And «سُجَّداً» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «ادخلوا».
His words: {لاَ تَعْدُواْ} — the majority read «تَعْدُوا» with a quiescent ʿayn and an undoubled dāl, from «عَدا يعدو», like «غزا يغزو». The original is «تَعْدُوُوا» with two wāws: the first is the lām [radical] of the word and the second the pronoun of the agents; the ḍamma was found heavy on the lām of the word and was dropped; with its dropping two quiescent letters met, so the first — the first wāw — was dropped, and the wāw of the agents remained; so its pattern is «تَفْعَوا». Nāfiʿ read it with fatḥa on the ʿayn and a doubled dāl; however, the narrators differed regarding Qālūn from Nāfiʿ: they narrated from him at one time a pure sukūn on the ʿayn, and at another time a concealment (ikhfāʾ) of the fatḥa of the ʿayn. The reading of Nāfiʿ is originally «تَعْتَدوا»; this is indicated by their consensus on {اعتدوا مِنْكُمْ فِي السبت} [al-Baqara: 65] being from al-iʿtidāʾ, which is iftiʿāl from al-ʿudwān (transgression); the assimilation of the tāʾ of iftiʿāl into the dāl was intended, so its vowel was transferred to the ʿayn, and it was changed to a dāl and assimilated. This is a clear reading. As for the pure sukūn narrated from Qālūn, it is something the grammarians do not accept, because it combines two quiescent letters outside their proper conditions. As for the ikhtilās (snatching of the vowel), it comes close to producing some vowel, even if hidden; however, the fatḥa is weak in itself, so it should not be concealed and thereby made weaker still; that is why the Readers did not permit rawm (partial vocalisation) of it in pausing, because of its weakness. Al-Aʿmash read «تَعْتَدُوا», with the original form that Nāfiʿ assimilated.

semin-durr:155-155.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ مَّيثَاقَهُمْ} — there are two views on this «ما». The first: that it is redundant (zāʾida), between the preposition and its genitive noun, for emphasis. The second: that it is a complete indefinite noun, and «نقضِهم» is a badal (substitute) from it; this is as preceded at {فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ مِّنَ الله} [Āl ʿImrān: 159]. «نقض» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its agent, and «ميثاقهم» is its object. There are two views about what the bāʾ governing «ما» here is attached (mutaʿalliq) to. The first: that it is the later «حَرَّمنا» in His words: {فَبِظُلْمٍ مِّنَ الذين هَادُواْ حَرَّمْنَا} [al-Nisāʾ: 160]. On this view it is said: «فبظلمٍ» is also attached to «حَرَّمنا», so it follows that two prepositions identical in wording and meaning are attached to one governing element, which is not permissible except with conjunction or badal. They answered this by saying that His words «فبظلمٍ» are a badal from His words «فبما», with repetition of the governing element. It is then said: if it were a badal, the conjunctive fāʾ would not have entered upon it, because the badal follows by itself without the mediation of a conjunction. This was answered: since the speech between the badal and the one substituted for became long, He repeated the fāʾ because of the length. Abū al-Baqāʾ, al-Zajjāj, al-Zamakhsharī, Abū Bakr and others mentioned this.
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected it with words whose meaning is that this is not permissible because of the long separation between the substituted and the badal; and because what is conjoined to a cause is a cause, so it would follow that some parts of the cause of the prohibition come later in time than the time of the prohibition, and it could then be a cause or part of a cause only by a far-fetched interpretation; [that is because their saying "we killed the Messiah" and their saying against Mary] the slander came only after the forbidding of the good things. He said: "So it is preferable that the implied form be: We cursed them; and it has come explicitly in His words: {فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِم مِّيثَاقَهُمْ لَعنَّاهُمْ}."
The second: that it is attached to an omitted element. Ibn ʿAṭiyya posited it as "We cursed them, humiliated them and sealed their hearts"; he said: "Omitting the answer of such speech is eloquent." Calling the like of this an "answer" is not known in language or in grammatical craft. Abū al-Baqāʾ posited it as: "So for their breaking their covenant, their hearts were sealed, or they were cursed. And it was said: its implied form is: so for their breaking [their covenant] they do not believe, and the fāʾ is redundant." End of quotation. [This, which Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted, al-Zamakhsharī took up and rejected, saying: "If you ask: why do you not claim that the omitted element to which the bāʾ is attached is] what is indicated by His words «بل طَبَع اللَّهُ», so that the implied form is: 'so for their breaking, Allah sealed their hearts'? [I say:] «بل طَبَع الله عليها بكفرهم» is a rejection and denial of their saying «قلوبُنا غُلْفٌ», so it is attached to that." [Translator's note: the source prints «فإنْ قالت», evidently a slip for «فإنْ قلت» ("If you ask").] The Shaykh said: "It is a good answer, and it is ruled out from another aspect too, namely that conjoining with «بل» is for iḍrāb (digression), and iḍrāb is either cancellation or transition, and in the Book of Allah, in statements, it is only for transition, and the second clause conveys what the first does not. What al-Zamakhsharī posited does not allow what we established, because His words {فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ مَّيثَاقَهُمْ وَكُفْرِهِم بَآيَاتِ الله وَقَتْلِهِمُ الأنبيآء بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَقَوْلِهِمْ قُلُوبُنَا غُلْفٌ بَلْ طَبَعَ الله} would be the very content of the clause accompanied by «بل», so the second would convey what the first conveyed; and if you said «مَرَّ زيد بعمرو، بل مَرَّ زيد بعمرو» ('Zayd passed by ʿAmr; rather, Zayd passed by ʿAmr'), it would not be permissible." And al-Zamakhsharī posited it as "We did to them what We did".
His words: {بَلْ طَبَعَ} — this is a digression (iḍrāb) from the preceding speech, i.e. the matter is not as they said in their saying «قلوبُنا غلف». The Readers pronounced the lām of «بل» distinctly before «طبع», except al-Kisāʾī, who assimilated it without divergence; from Ḥamza there is divergence. The bāʾ in «بكفرهم» may be causal, or instrumental, like the bāʾ in «طبعت بالطين على الكيس» ('I sealed the bag with clay'), meaning that He made disbelief like the thing with which one seals, i.e. covering them, so it is like the seal. And His words «إلا قليلاً» may be accusative as the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "except a little faith"; or it may be the naʿt of an omitted time, i.e. "a little time". It may not be accusative as an exception from the fāʿil (agent) of «يؤمنون», i.e. "except a few of them, for they believe", because the pronoun in «لا يؤمنون» refers to those whose hearts were sealed, and faith does not come from one whose heart was sealed with disbelief.

semin-durr:156-156.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَبِكُفْرِهِمْ} — there are two views on it. The first: that it is conjoined to «ما» in His words {فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ}, so it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to what the first is attached to. The second: that it is conjoined to «بكفرهم», which comes after «طبع». Al-Zamakhsharī clarified this with the utmost clarity, raised an objection and answered it in the best way; he said: "If you ask: to what is His saying «وبكفرهم» conjoined? I say: the proper view is that it is conjoined to «فبما نقضِهم», and His saying {بَلْ طَبَعَ الله عَلَيْهَا بِكُفْرِهِمْ} is made speech following His saying {وَقَوْلِهِمْ قُلُوبُنَا غُلْفٌ} by way of digression (istiṭrād). It may also be conjoined to what immediately precedes it, namely His saying «بكفرِهم». If you ask: what then is the meaning of bringing disbelief conjoined to something in which it has already been mentioned — whether it is conjoined to what precedes the iḍrāb or to what follows it — namely His saying {وَكُفْرِهِم بَآيَاتِ الله} and His saying «بكفرهم»? I say: disbelief recurred from them, because they disbelieved in Moses, then in Jesus, then in Muḥammad, so He conjoined some of their disbelief to some; or He conjoined the whole of the conjoined elements to the whole of what they are conjoined to, as though it were said: so for their combining the breaking of the covenant, disbelief in the signs of Allah, killing the prophets and their saying 'our hearts are covered', and for their combining their disbelief with their slander of Mary and their boasting of killing Jesus, We punished them; or: rather Allah sealed them for their disbelief and their combining their disbelief with such and such."
His words: {بُهْتَاناً} — there are five views on its accusative. The most apparent of them: that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), for it [the verb of saying] is made to include the meaning of «كلام» ('speech'), as in «قلت خطبة وشعراً» ('I said a sermon and poetry'). The second: that it is accusative as the type of the maṣdar (verbal noun), as in their saying «قَعَد القرفصاء» ('he sat in the squatting posture'), meaning that the saying may be a slander or not a slander. The third: that it is accusative as the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a slanderous saying", and this is close in meaning to the first. The fourth: that it is accusative by an implied verb from its own root, i.e. "they slandered a slander". The fifth: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive pronoun in «قولهم», i.e. "slandering"; a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi is permissible because it is the fāʿil (agent) in meaning; the implied form is: "and for their saying that, slandering".

semin-durr:157-157.t:
And the words of Allah the Exalted: {وَقَوْلِهِمْ} are conjoined to «وكفرهم». «عيسى» is a badal (substitute) from «المسيح», or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), and likewise «ابن مريم», which may also be an adjective. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted these three views in «رسول الله», except that the badal with derived words is rare; it may be said that «رسول الله» has been treated like non-derived nouns. He also permitted it to be accusative by an implied «أعني» ('I mean'), and there is no need for that. His words «شُبِّه لهم»: «شُبِّه» is passive, and there are two views on it. The first: that it is predicated of the preposition [with its noun] after it, as in your saying «حِيل إليه» and «لُبس عليه». The second: that it is predicated of the pronoun of the one killed, indicated by their saying «إنَّا قتلْنا», i.e. "but the one they killed was made to resemble [him] to them". If it is asked: why may it not refer to the Messiah? The answer is that the Messiah is the one resembled, not the one made to resemble.
[His words]: «لفي شك منه»: «منه» is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of «شك», attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted element; it is not permissible for it to be attached to «شك» itself, because «الشك» takes its complement only with «في», not with «من»; and it should not be said that «مِنْ» has the meaning of «في», for that is a weaker opinion, and we have no need of it here.
And His words: {مَا لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ} — two views are possible regarding «علم». The first: that it is nominative as fāʿil (agent), the governing element being one of the two prepositional phrases, either «لهم» or «به»; when one of them is made what puts it in the nominative, the other is attached to what the nominative-governing one is attached to, namely the implied "being settled". «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), since both conditions for redundancy are met. The second view: that «من علم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «من» also redundant in it, and there are two possibilities for the khabar (predicate). The first: that it is «لهم»; then «به» is either a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the khabar, governed by the implied "being settled", or a ḥāl from «عِلْم», even though it is indefinite, because it precedes it and because it relies on a negation. If it is said: this entails placing the ḥāl of a noun made genitive by a preposition before it, which is a poetic necessity not permissible in ordinary speech — the answer is that we do not grant that; rather, Abū al-Baqāʾ and others transmitted that the position of most of the Basrans is that it is permissible; and even if we granted that it is permissible only in necessity, the genitive here is made genitive by a redundant preposition, and the redundant [preposition] is treated as discarded. Or it is attached to an omitted element by way of clarification, i.e. "I mean by it"; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this, and there is no need for it. It may not be attached to «علم» itself, because what a maṣdar (verbal noun) governs does not precede it. The second possibility: that «به» is the khabar, and «لهم» is attached to the "being settled" as preceded; the lām may also be clarifying and specifying, like the one in His words: {وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ} [al-Ikhlāṣ: 4]. This negative clause admits three views. [The first:] the genitive, as a second adjective of «شك», i.e. "not known". The second: the accusative as a ḥāl from «شك»; this is permissible even though it is indefinite, because it is specified by the description in His words «منه». The third: resumption; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and it is far-fetched.
His words: {إِلاَّ اتباع الظن} — there are two opinions about this exception. The first — and it is the correct one, the majority mentioning no other — is that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), because following conjecture is not of the genus of knowledge. To my knowledge it was read only with «اتِّباع» in the accusative, on the basic rule of the disconnected exception, which is the dialect of the Ḥijāz; in [the dialect of] Tamīm it may be a badal from «علم» according to its wording, and so genitive, or according to its position, and so nominative, because it is in a nominative position, as I set out for you before, «من» being redundant in it. The second — Ibn ʿAṭiyya said — is that it is connected (muttaṣil); he said: "since knowledge and conjecture are joined by the genus of being among the beliefs of certainty; the one who conjectures says by way of figurative usage 'my knowledge in this matter is such-and-such', meaning only his conjecture." End of quotation. This is not agreed upon, because conjecture is that in which one of the two sides is preponderant, and certainty is that in which one of them is decisively affirmed; and even granting it, following conjecture is not of the genus of knowledge but other than it, so it too is disconnected, i.e. "but following conjecture is what they have".
His words: {وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ يَقِيناً} — there are several opinions on the pronoun in «قتلوه». The most apparent of them is that it refers to Jesus, and the majority of exegetes hold this. The second — held by Ibn Qutayba and al-Farrāʾ — is that it refers to knowledge, i.e. "they did not kill the knowledge with certainty", in the manner of their saying «قتلت العلم والرأي يقيناً» ('I killed the knowledge and the opinion with certainty') and «قتلته علماً» ('I killed it in knowledge', i.e. mastered it). The aspect of figurative usage in it is that killing a thing comes about through subduing and mastering it, as though it were said: their knowledge was not a knowledge comprehended; it was only from conjecture and guesswork. The third — held by Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Suddī and a large group — is that it refers to the conjecture; you say «قتلت هذا الأمر علماً ويقيناً», i.e. I verified it; so it is as though it were said: their conjecture was not validated for them, they did not verify it with certainty, and they did not settle the conjecture with certainty.
His words: {يقيناً} — there are five views on it. The first: that it is the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a certain killing". The second: that it is a maṣdar from the meaning of the governing element before it, as its figurative sense preceded, because it is in its meaning, i.e. "they did not become certain of it with certainty". The third: that it is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «قتلوه», i.e. "they did not kill him being certain of his killing". The fourth: that it is accusative by a verb from its own root, omitted because it is indicated, i.e. "they were not certain of it with certainty", and it emphasises the content of the negative clause before it. Abū al-Baqāʾ posited the governing element on this view as affirmative, saying: "its implied form is: they were certain of that, with certainty", and there is an objection to this. The fifth — transmitted from Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī — is that it is accusative governed by what comes after «بل», in His words {رَّفَعَهُ الله}, and that there is a transposition in the speech, i.e. "rather Allah raised him to Himself with certainty". Al-Khalīl and those after him explicitly stated that this is prohibited, i.e. that what comes after «بل» does not govern what is before it; so it should not be held authentic from him. And His words {بَل رَّفَعَهُ الله إِلَيْهِ} are a refutation of what they claimed about killing and crucifying him. The pronoun in «إليه» refers to «الله», with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "to His heaven and the place of His command and prohibition".

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَن تَرِثُواْ}: it is in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of «يَحِلُّ», that is: "It is not lawful for you to inherit women." It was also read «لا تَحِلُّ» with the feminine-marking tāʾ (two dots above), on the interpretation of «أن ترثوا» as "inheritance" (al-wirātha), which is feminine. This is like the reading {ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتُهُمْ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُواْ} [al-Anʿām: 23], with «تكن» made feminine and «فتنتهم» put in the accusative, on the interpretation "then their trial was nothing but their saying"; except that in the verse of al-Anʿām there is a justification, namely that the predicate is feminine, as will come.

And «النساءَ» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Either (a) on the omission of a muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct), that is: "that you inherit the property of women", if the address is to the husbands, because it is reported that when a man among them had no desire for his wife he would hold on to her until she died and he inherited from her, or she ransomed herself from him with her wealth if she did not die; or (b) without any omission, in the sense that the women are like the thing inherited, if the address is to the guardians or to the relatives of the deceased, for it is reported that when one of them died and left a wife and a son by another wife, the son had a greater right to her than she had to herself. It was also said: if the guardian got there first and threw his garment over her, he had the greater right to her, and if she got to her own family first, she had the greater right to herself. So they were forbidden to make them like inherited things. On the basis of what I have said, there is no need to omit one of the two objects, either the first or the second, by making «أن ترثوا» transitive to two objects, as Abū al-Baqāʾ did. He said: "«والنساءَ» has two possible analyses. One: they are the first object, and the women, on this view, are the ones inherited; the people of the Jāhiliyya used to inherit their fathers' wives and say, 'We have a greater right to marry them.' The other: it is the second object, and the implied form is: 'that you inherit property from women.'" End of his words. His saying "they are the first object" means that the second is omitted, its implied form being: "that you inherit women from your fathers."

And «كُرْهاً» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «النساء», that is: that you inherit them unwilling, or compelled. The two Kufan readers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read «كرهاً» here, and in Barāʾa (al-Tawba) and al-Aḥqāf, with ḍamma on the kāf; ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir, on the transmission of Ibn Dhakwān from him, agreed with them in the case of al-Aḥqāf; and the rest read it with fatḥa. The discussion of kurh and karh, whether they have one meaning or not, has already been given in al-Baqara, which makes repeating it unnecessary. The word «كرهاً» has no implied contrary meaning (mafhūm), meaning that it would be permissible to inherit them when they do not dislike it, since it is stated as it is only because that is the usual case.

His saying: {وَلاَ تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ}: two analyses. The clearer is that it is jussive by the prohibitive «لا», conjoining a clause of prohibition to a declarative clause. If, as is the school of Sībawayh, congruity between clauses is not a condition, it is plain; and if we do make it a condition, as some hold, then it is because the clause before it has the sense of prohibition, since the implied meaning is: "Do not inherit women against their will, for it is not lawful for you." On this analysis Abū al-Baqāʾ made it resumptive, meaning that it is not conjoined to the verb before it.

The second, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed, is that it is accusative, conjoined to the verb before it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is possible that «تَعْضُلوهن» is accusative, conjoined to «تَرِثوا», so that the wāw is a particle of association (mushrik) joining a verb to a verb."

Ibn Masʿūd read: «ولا أَنْ تَعْضُلوهن». This reading strengthens the possibility of the accusative, and that preventing women from marrying is, by explicit text, unlawful. Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) rejected this analysis, saying: when you conjoin a verb negated by «لا» to an affirmative one, and both are accusative, the accusative-governing particle is implied only after the conjunction, not after «لا». If you say «أريدُ أن أتوبَ ولا أدخلَ النار» ("I want to repent and not enter the Fire"), the implied form is: «أريد أن أتوبَ وأَنْ لا أدخلَ النار», because the verb seeks the first in the mode of affirmation and the second in the mode of negation; the meaning is "I want repentance and the negation of my entering the Fire." So if the verb governing both conjoined items were itself negated, the same would hold. But if you implied that in the verse it would not be sound: if you said «لا يَحِلُّ أن لا تَعْضُلوهُنَّ» it would not be sound unless you made «لا» redundant (zāʾida) rather than negating, and that is contrary to the apparent sense. As for implying «أن» after the negating «لا», that is not sound either; and if you did imply «أن» after «لا», it would be the conjoining of an implied maṣdar to an implied maṣdar, not the conjoining of a verb to a verb. So Ibn ʿAṭiyya confused the two kinds of conjunction and thought that, because «أَنْ» can be implied after «لا», it is a conjoining of verb to verb. There is a difference between your saying «[لا] أريد أن تقومَ وأن لا تخرج» and your saying «لا أريدُ أن تقومَ ولا أن تخرج». In the first he negates wanting the occurrence of his standing and wants the non-occurrence of his going out, so he has wanted his going out; in the second he negates wanting the occurrence of his standing and of his going out, so he wants neither the standing nor the going out. This has some obscurity in understanding for one who has not trained in the science of Arabic. End of his rebuttal.

There is something to consider in it: the example he gave, «أريد أن أتوب ولا أدخل النار», requires the implied accusative particle to come before «لا», since if it were implied after it the construction would be corrupted; whereas in the verse, implying «أن» after «لا» is sound, for the implied meaning becomes: "It is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will, nor to prevent them." [And what I have said and what Ibn ʿAṭiyya held is supported by the words of al-Zamakhsharī, who said: "If you ask:] «تعضُلوهن», what is the analysis of it? I say: accusative, conjoined to «أن ترثوا», and «لا» is for emphasis of the negation, that is: it is not lawful for you to inherit women nor to prevent them." Al-Zamakhsharī has thus stated this meaning explicitly, and has explicitly stated the redundancy of «لا» which the Shaykh considered contrary to the apparent sense.

There is an omission in the speech, its implied form being «ولا تَعْضُلوهن من النكاح» ("and do not prevent them from marriage") if the address is to the guardians, or «ولا تعضُلوهن من الطلاق» ("and do not prevent them from divorce") if the address is to the husbands. The meaning of ʿaḍl was given in al-Baqara.

His saying: {لِتَذْهَبُواْ}: the lām is attached to «تَعْضُلوهن», and for the bāʾ in «ببعض» there are two analyses. One: it is the bāʾ of transitivity (taʿdiya), equivalent to the hamza, that is: "so that you take away [part] of what you gave them." The other: it is for accompaniment, so the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, attached to an omitted element, that is: "so that you go off accompanied by part of it." «ما» is either a relative noun meaning "that which" or an indefinite noun with a description; on both assumptions the returning pronoun ʿāʾid is omitted, and there is a difficulty in its implied form which was discussed in al-Baqara at {وَممَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ} [verse 3], so refer to it.

His saying: {إِلاَّ أَن يَأْتِينَ}: in this exception there are two views. One: that it is a discontinuous exception (munqaṭiʿ), so «أن يأتينَ» is in the position of the accusative. The other: that it is a continuous exception (muttaṣil), and then there are three analyses. One: it is excepted from a general adverb of time, the implied form being: "do not prevent them at any time except at the time of their committing an indecency." Two: it is excepted from the general circumstances, the implied form being: "do not prevent them in any circumstance except in the circumstance of their committing an indecency." Three: it is excepted from the general cause, the implied form being: "do not prevent them for any reason except for their committing an indecency." / Abū al-Baqāʾ, after relating the discontinuous analysis, said: "The second: it is in the position of ḥāl, the implied form being: except in the circumstance of their committing an indecency. It was also said: it is a continuous exception, the implied form being: do not prevent them in any circumstance except in the circumstance of committing the indecency." End. These two analyses are in reality one, because whoever says that it is accusative as a ḥāl must imply something general from which this ḥāl is excepted.

Ibn Kathīr and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «مُبَيَّنة» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, as a passive participle, throughout the Quran, that is: the one who claims it has made it clear and plain. The rest read it with kasra, as an active participle, and there are two analyses. One: it is from the transitive «بيَّن», so the object is omitted, the implied form being "making clear the state of whoever commits it." The other: it is from the intransitive «بَيَّن», for «بَيَّن» can be transitive and intransitive; one says: «بانَ الشيء وأبان واستبان وبَيَّن وتبيَّن» with one meaning, that is: it became apparent. Some read «مُبيِنَة», with kasra on the bāʾ and sukūn on the yāʾ, an active participle of «أبان», and the two analyses given for the geminated kasra form apply to it, because «أبان» too can be transitive and intransitive. As for «مُبَيِّنات», the two Kufan readers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī), Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read it with kasra on the yāʾ as an active participle, and the rest with fatḥa as a passive participle; the reason for that has already been given.

His saying: {بالمعروف}: for the bāʾ there are two analyses. The clearer is that it is the bāʾ of ḥāl: either from the fāʿil, that is "associating with them in kindness", or from the object, that is "being associated with in kindness."

The second: that it is the bāʾ of transitivity. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «بالمعروفِ» is "an object or a ḥāl."

His saying: {فعسى}: the fāʾ introduces the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and «عسى» is accompanied by it because it is indeclinable in form (jāmida). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: in what respect is it sound for «فعسى» to be the consequence of the condition? I say: in that the meaning is: if you dislike them, then be patient with them despite the dislike, for perhaps there is in what you dislike much good which is not in what you love."

«ويَجْعَلُ» was also read with ḍamma on the lām. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "on the basis that it is a ḥāl", meaning that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), so that a wāw would not have to enter an affirmative imperfect verb. And «عسى» here is complete (tāmma), because it has made «أنْ» and what follows it its subject, the implied meaning being: "your dislike has drawn near", so it needs no implied predicate. The pronoun in «فيه» refers to «شيء», that is: in that disliked thing; it was also said it refers to the dislike indicated by the verb; and it was said it refers to patience, though it has not been mentioned.

[Translator's notes: the source reads «فو كان الفعلُ» where «فلو» is evidently meant, «ولو قت» where «قلت» is meant, and «اي» for «أي»; I translated the intended sense. The sentence «ولو قَدَّرْتَ هذا التقديرَ ... لو قت: لا يَحِلُّ…» is garbled in the text as printed.]

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَّكَانَ زَوْجٍ}: an adverb accusative by «الاستبدال» (replacement). What is meant by «الزوج» here is the plural, that is: "and if you wish to replace wives in the place of wives." That is permitted because the plural of the ones replacing indicates it, since it is not imagined that the addressees share a single wife in place of a single wife; and because the plural sense is intended, the pronoun in «إحداهُنَّ» returns to «زوج» in the plural. The one from whom taking is forbidden is the one being replaced, because she is the one who has taken from him, by the evidence of His saying: {وَكَيْفَ تَأْخُذُونَهُ وَقَدْ أفضى بَعْضُكُمْ إلى بَعْضٍ}, and that applies only to the former wife, not the newly acquired one.

He said {إِحْدَاهُنَّ} to indicate that what is meant by His saying {وَآتَيْتُمْ} is: each one of you gave one of them, that is one of the wives. He did not say "you gave them a qinṭār", so that it would not be imagined that all of the addressees gave the wives a single qinṭār; what is meant is that each one gave his wife a qinṭār. So the word «إحداهن» indicates that the pronoun in «آتيتم» means each and every one, just as the phrase {وَإِنْ أَرَدْتُّمُ استبدال زَوْجٍ مَّكَانَ زَوْجٍ} indicates that what is meant is the replacement of wives in place of wives; so the singular here is meant as plural because of {وَإِنْ أَرَدْتُّمُ}.

And by His saying {وَآتَيْتُمْ} each one individually is meant, because of «إحداهن», which is singular. This eloquent meaning cannot be indicated by anything briefer or more fluent than this construction. The meaning of «القنطار» and its derivation were given in Āl ʿImrān. The pronoun in «منه» returns to «قنطاراً».

Ibn Muḥayṣin read: «آتيتم احداهن», joining the alif of «إحدى», just as {إِنَّهَا لاحْدَى الكبر} [al-Muddaththir: 35] was read, dropping the hamza for lightness, as in his saying:

1560 - إنْ لم أقاتِلْ فالبسوني بُرْقُعاً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(If I do not fight, then dress me in a face-veil ...) [the second half is not given in the source]

By what I have mentioned the meaning of the verse becomes clear.

Abū al-Baqāʾ went on at length about it without achieving anything, and it is necessary to address what he said and to point it out. He said: "In His saying {وَآتَيْتُمْ إِحْدَاهُنَّ قِنْطَاراً} there are two difficulties. One: that he made the pronoun plural while what preceded was two wives (zawjān). The other: that the one he wants to replace is the one to whom he has given wealth, so he forbids him to take it, whereas the one he wants to newly acquire he has not yet given anything, so that he would be forbidden to take it; and this is supported by His saying: {وَكَيْفَ تَأْخُذُونَهُ وَقَدْ أفضى بَعْضُكُمْ إلى بَعْضٍ}. The answer to the first: that «الزوج» means the plural, because the address is to a group of men and each of them may want to replace; it is also possible that it was made plural because the one he wants to newly acquire will end up being a wife, and he may want to replace her as he replaced the first, so it was made plural in that sense. As for the second difficulty, there are two answers. One: he put the overt noun in place of the pronoun, the original being «وآتيتموهن». The other: the one to be replaced is indefinite, so he said «إحداهن» since she is not specified so that the pronoun could return to her. We have mentioned something like this at His saying {فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَاهُمَا الأخرى} [al-Baqara: 282]." End.

In his saying "he put the overt noun in place of the pronoun" there is something to consider, because if the original were so, it would give the impression that all of them gave the wives a qinṭār, as was said before, and that is not the case.

His saying: {أَتَأْخُذُونَهُ بُهْتَاناً}: the interrogative is for denunciation, that is: "Will you do it despite its ugliness?" For the accusative of «بهتاناً وإثماً» there are two analyses. One: that they are accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), that is "because of your slander and your sin." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "even if it is not a motive, as you say «قعدَ عن القتالِ جُنْباً» ('he stayed away from the fighting out of cowardice')." The other: that they are two maṣdars in the position of ḥāl, and for the owner of the ḥāl there are two views. The clearer: that it is the fāʿil in «أتأخذونه», [that is] "slandering and sinning". The other: that it is the object, that is: "will you take it while it is confounding and bewildering, because of its hideousness and the ugliness of the talk about it?"

And «بُهْتان» is of the pattern fuʿlān from «البَهْت»; its meaning was given in al-Baqara. The discussion of «كيف» and its grammatical position was also given in al-Baqara, at His saying {كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ} [al-Baqara: 28].

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَقَدْ أفضى}: the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause after it is in the position of the accusative. He brought «قد» so that the past would be brought near to the present; likewise «أَخَذْنَ», with «قد» implied with it because it was mentioned earlier. And «منكم» has two analyses. The clearer is that it is attached to «أَخَذْنَ». Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that it be a ḥāl from «ميثاقاً» which has been put before it, as if he saw that it could be a description (ṣifa) if it came later, so it would be permissible; but that is weak. And «أفضى» means: he went to its open space (fadāʾ), that is the region of its wideness; one says «فَضَا يفضو», so the alif of «أَفْضى» is from a yāʾ whose origin is a wāw.

semin-durr:77-77.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِذَا فَرِيقٌ}: «إذا» here is the "sudden" (fujāʾiyya) particle. It has already been stated that there are three views about it: the first, and the soundest, is that it is an adverb of place; the second, that it is an adverb of time; the third, that it is a particle. These views have a place other than this one. It has also been said of this «إذا» that it is a sudden, locative one and that it is the answer to «لَمَّا» in His saying {فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ}. On that basis there are two possibilities. The first: it is a fronted khabar (predicate), «فريق» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), «منهم» is an adjective (naʿt) of «فريق», and likewise «يَخْشَون»; and it is permissible that «يخشون» be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «فريق» because of its being qualified. The implied form is: "so in the presence there is a group, being among them, fearing (khāshūn or khāshīn)". The second: «فريقٌ» is a mubtadaʾ, «منهم» is its adjective, and that is what justifies beginning with it (an indefinite noun), and «يَخْشَوْن» is a predicative clause, and it is what governs «إذا». On the first view, what governs it is omitted, according to the rule for adverbs that occur as a khabar. It has been said that here it is an adverb of time, but this is invalid, because in that case it must have a governor, and its governor is either what precedes it or what follows it. It cannot be what precedes it, because what precedes it, namely «كُتب», is past in form and meaning whereas «إذا» is for the future, so that is impossible. If it is said: it is made here to refer to the past, in the sense of «إذ»; it is answered: that is not permissible, because the implied form would then become: "when fighting was prescribed for them, at the time of a group of them fearing", and this requires an answer to «لَمَّا» and it has no answer. Nor can it be what follows it, because if its governor comes after it, it is its answer, and it has no answer here. It was stated at the beginning of al-Baqara that there are two views on «لَمَّا»: the view of Sībawayh, that it is a particle of "occurrence due to occurrence" (ḥarf wujūb li-wujūb), and the view of al-Fārisī, that it is an adverb of time in the sense of «حين». The refutation of him was given there: that it is answered by the negative «ما» and by the sudden «إذا», and that what follows it does not govern what precedes it, which makes repeating it unnecessary; and what immediately follows it cannot govern it, because on his claim it is in the position of the genitive by annexation, and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern the muḍāf. Some have replied that what governs it here is the meaning of «يَخْشَوْن», as if it were said: "they became anxious"; he said: "and «جزعوا» (they became anxious) is what governs «إذا»; and this verse is problematic, because it contains two adverbs, one for what is past and the other for what is future." End of quotation.

His saying: {كَخَشْيَةِ الله}: it has three possibilities. The first, which is the well-known one among the i'rab scholars: it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a fear like the fear of Allah". The second, which is the established view of Sībawayh, repeatedly: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the omitted pronoun of the fear, i.e. "they fear it, the people", that is, "they fear the fear of the people, likening it to the fear of Allah".
The third: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يَخْشَوْن», i.e. "they fear the people like the people of the fear of Allah", that is, "resembling the people of the fear of Allah, or with a greater fear", i.e. a fear greater than that of the people who fear Allah. And «اشدَّ» is conjoined to the ḥāl. So said al-Zamakhsharī. Then he said: "If you ask: why did you depart from the obvious, which is that it be an adjective of the maṣdar, and did not take the implied form to be: 'they fear with a fear [like the fear of] Allah', meaning: like what Allah is feared? I say: His saying {أَوْ أَشَدَّ خَشْيَةً} refuses that, because it and what is conjoined to it are of one ruling; and if you said «يخشون الناسَ أشدَّ خشيةً» it could only be a ḥāl from the pronoun of the group, and it would not be accusative as a maṣdar is, because you do not say «خَشِي فلانٌ أشدَّ خشيةً» putting «خشية» in the accusative while intending the maṣdar; you only say «أشدَّ خشيةٍ», putting it in the genitive. And if you put it in the accusative, «أشدَّ خشيةً» can only be an expression for the agent, as a ḥāl from him — unless you make the fear itself 'fearing', along the lines of their saying «جَدَّ جَدُّه», and claim that its meaning is: 'they fear the people with a fear like a fear that is greater in fearing than the fear of Allah'; on this basis it is also permissible that the position of «أشدُّ» be genitive, conjoined to «خشية الله», meaning 'like the fear of Allah or like a fear greater than it'." End of quotation.

It is permissible to put «خشيةً» in the accusative in another way, namely by conjoining it to the position of the kāf, and «أشدَّ» is then accusative as a ḥāl from «خشية», because it is originally an adjective of an indefinite noun that has been put before it; the original is: "they fear the people like the fear of Allah or a fear greater than it". So «خشية» is not accusative as a tamyīz (specification), so that what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned follows from it and has to be excused. Something similar was given earlier at His saying {أَوْ أَشَدَّ ذِكْراً} [al-Baqara: 200]. The maṣdar is annexed to its object and the agent is omitted, i.e. "like their fear of Allah". And «أو» admits the possibilities mentioned in His saying: {أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً} [al-Baqara: 74]; it may also be for classification (tanwīʿ): meaning that some of them fear them like the fear of Allah, and some of them fear them with a fear greater than the fear of Allah. And «لولا أخَّرْتَنا»: «لولا» is the particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). Ibn Kathīr and the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read «لا يُظْلَمون» in the third person, following the absent persons before it, while the rest read it in the second person, as a shift of address (iltifāt). And «فَتيلاً»: its i'rab has already been given.

semin-durr:78-78.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَيْنَمَا تَكُونُواْ}: «أين» is a conditional noun that jusses two verbs, and «ما» is redundant (zāʾida), permissibly, giving it emphasis; «أين» is an adverb of place, «تكونوا» is jussive (majzūm) by it, and «يُدْرِكْكم» is its apodosis (jawāb). The majority read it jussive, because it is the apodosis of the condition. Ṭalḥa ibn Sulaymān read «يدرِكُكم» in the nominative, and al-Mubarrad explained it as the omission of the fāʾ, i.e. "then death will overtake you". Like it is the saying of another poet:
161 - 2- يا أقرعُ بنَ حابسٍ يا أقرعُ ... إنك إنْ يُصْرَعْ أخوكَ تُصْرَعُ
(O Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis, O Aqraʿ: if your brother is struck down, you will be struck down.)
This is al-Mubarrad's analysis, whereas Sībawayh claims that it is not an apodosis; rather it points to the apodosis, and the intention is that it be put first. There is another analysis for the verse, namely that the nominative «يصرعُ» is the khabar of «إنك» and the condition is parenthetical between them, its apodosis being what is indicated by «إنك تُصْرَعُ», like His saying: {وَإِنَّآ إِن شَآءَ الله لَمُهْتَدُونَ} [al-Baqara: 70]. Al-Zamakhsharī explained it as a case of "supposition" (tawahhum), for he said: "It may be said: it is carried over onto what occupies the place of «أينما تكونوا», namely «أينما كنتم», just as «ولا ناعبٍ» is carried over onto what occupies the place of «ليسوا مصلحين», namely «ليسوا بمصلحين»; so he put it in the nominative, as Zuhayr put it in the nominative:
1613 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يقول لا غائبٌ مالي ولا حَرِمُ
(... he says: "My property is not absent, nor is it forbidden.")
and this is the view of a "Sībawayhian" grammarian", meaning one attributed to Sībawayh; so it is as though he had said: «أينما كنتم». And when the verb of the condition is past in form, the imperfect may be nominative or jussive, as in the saying of Zuhayr:
وإنْ أتاه خليلٌ يومَ مسألةٍ ... يقولُ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And if a friend comes to him on a day of asking, he says ...)
And in its being nominative are the two possibilities mentioned from Sībawayh and al-Mubarrad. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) rejected this, saying that conjunction onto a supposition is not systematic (lā yanqās), and that his statement leads to the omission of the apodosis, which is not omitted unless the verb of the condition is past; if you said «أنت ظالمُ إنْ تفعل» it would not be allowed. And this, as you see, is imperfect. In this rejection there is a consideration (naẓar) that is not hidden.
«ولو كنتم»: they said it has the meaning of «إنْ», and its apodosis is omitted, i.e. «لأدرككم» ("it would have overtaken you"). Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned a strange view of his own about it, saying: "It is possible that it be connected with His saying {وَلاَ تُظْلَمُونَ فَتِيلاً}, i.e. nothing is diminished from what has been written of your appointed terms wherever you are, in the battles of wars or elsewhere; then he begins anew with His saying: {يُدْرِككُّمُ الموت وَلَوْ كُنتُمْ فِي بُرُوجٍ مُّشَيَّدَةٍ}; and the pause on this reading is [on] «أينما تكونوا»." End of quotation. The Shaykh rejected him, saying: "This is an analysis that is not sound, neither from the standpoint of meaning nor of grammatical craft. As for meaning: it is not fitting that it be connected with His saying {وَلاَ تُظْلَمُونَ فَتِيلاً}, because the apparent negation of wrongdoing is only in the Hereafter, according to His saying {قُلْ مَتَاعُ الدنيا قَلِيلٌ والآخرة خَيْرٌ لِّمَنِ اتقى}. As for grammatical craft: the apparent sense of his words indicates that «أينما تكونوا» is attached to His saying {ولا تُظْلمون} in the sense he explained, and this is not permissible, because conditional nouns have the head of the sentence and their governor cannot precede them. If something like «اضربْ زيداً متى جاء» occurs, a governor is implied for it, indicated by «اضرب», not the preceding «اضرب» itself.
If it is said: then al-Zamakhsharī likewise implies a governor indicated by «ولا تُظْلمون», its implied form being «أينما تكونوا فلا تظلمون», omitting «فلا تظلمون» because what precedes it indicates it, and so he is free of the problem mentioned. It is answered: that is not possible, because the apodosis would then be omitted while the verb of the condition is imperfect, and it has been stated that this occurs only when it is past." In this rejection there is a consideration, because he (al-Zamakhsharī) intended to explain the meaning. His (the Shaykh's) saying "it is not fitting that it be connected with «ولا تظلمون»" is not conceded; rather it is fitting, and al-Zamakhsharī made it clear by what preceded, in the best clarification.
The clause of refusal (al-jumla al-imtināʿiyya, i.e. the «لو» clause) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "wherever you are, among places, death will overtake you, even if your condition is that you are in these towers", from which it is understood that its overtaking them elsewhere is a fortiori; and close to it is: «أعطُوا السائل ولو على فرسٍ» ("Give the beggar, even if he is on a horse"). The conditional clause admits two possibilities. The first: it has no position in i'rab, because it is a resumptive report; He the Exalted informed that no one escapes death; and from it is the saying of Zuhayr:
1614 - ومَنْ هابَ أسبابَ المنايا يَنَلْنَه ... ولو رامَ أسباب السماء بسُلَّمِ
(Whoever fears the causes of death, they will reach him, even if he strives for the ways of heaven by a ladder.)
The second: it is in the position of the accusative as the object of "say" that precedes it, i.e. "Say: the enjoyment of this world is little, and say also: wherever you are ...".
The majority read «مُشَيَّدة» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, a passive participle. Naʿīm ibn Maysara read it with kasra, ascribing the action to it (the tower) figuratively, as in their saying «قصيدةٌ شاعرة» ("a poetic poem"), the one described thus being its people; he departed to that for exaggeration in the description.
«البُروج» are fortresses, derived from «التبرُّج», which is display; and from it is {غَيْرَ مُتَبَرِّجَاتِ بِزِينَةٍ} [al-Nūr: 60]. «البَرَجُ» in the eye is its wideness, and from it is the saying of Dhū al-Rumma:
1615 - بيضاءُ في بَرَجٍ صفراءُ في غَنجٍ ... كأنَّها فِضةٌ قد مَسَّها ذَهَبُ
(White in the wideness of her eyes, yellow in coquetry, as though she were silver that gold has touched.)
And their saying «ثوبٌ مُبَرَّجٌ» means that it has pictures of towers on it, like their saying «مِرْطٌ مُرَجَّل», meaning it has pictures of men on it; it is narrated with jīm and with ḥāʾ. «المشيَّدة» means made with «الشِّيد», which is plaster (jiṣṣ); one says «شاد البناء وشَيَّده», repeating the ʿayn (middle radical) for intensification. An instance of the form «شاد» is the saying of al-Aswad:
1616 - شادَه مرمراً وجَلَّله كِلْ ... سَاً فللطير في ذُراه وكُورُ
(He built it of marble and covered it with plaster, so the birds have nests at its summits.)
One also says «أشاد», so that faʿala and afʿala are of the same meaning.
Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī, with a disagreement reported from him, paused on «ما» in His saying «فما لهؤلاء» and in His saying: {مَالِ هذا الرسول} [al-Furqān: 7], and in His saying: {مَالِ هذا الكتاب} [al-Kahf: 49], and in His saying: {فَمَالِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ} [al-Maʿārij: 36]. The others pause on the lām, the genitive-governing particle, without its genitive noun, following the orthography (rasm). This, namely both pauses, ought not to be permitted, because in the first the pause is on the mubtadaʾ without its khabar, and in the second the pause is on the preposition without its genitive noun; it is only permitted out of the necessity of breaking the breath, or as a test.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَا نَكَحَ آبَاؤُكُمْ}: regarding this «ما» there are two views. One: that it is a relative noun (ism mawṣūl) applying to kinds of rational beings, as was given at His saying {مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 3]; this is according to whoever does not allow it to apply to individual rational beings. As for whoever allows that, he says it takes the place of «مَنْ»; so «ما» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of {وَلاَ تَنكِحُواْ}, and the implied meaning is: "and do not marry the women whom your fathers married." The second: that it is a maṣdarī (verbal-noun-forming) «ما», that is: "and do not contract a marriage like the marriage of your fathers which existed in the Jāhiliyya", which was invalid marriage such as shighār marriage and others. A group chose this view, among them Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī, who said: "If its meaning were 'do not marry the women whom your fathers married', the word would have had to be «مَنْ» instead of «ما»." End. That it is forbidden or invalid is made clear from His saying: {إِنَّهُ كَانَ فَاحِشَةً وَمَقْتاً}. His saying: {مِّنَ النسآء}: a parallel was given at the beginning of the sūra.

His saying: {إِلاَّ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ}: about this exception there are two views. One: that it is discontinuous (munqaṭiʿ), since the past cannot coincide with the future, / and the meaning is: when He forbade them marriage to those whom their fathers had married, a doubt reached what had passed in the Jāhiliyya, and what is its ruling? So it was said: "except what has already passed", that is: "but what has passed, there is no sin in it." Ibn Zayd also said about its meaning: "What is meant by marriage is a valid contract," and he took {إِلاَّ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ} to refer to what some of them used to engage in of fornication, saying: "except what has passed on the part of the fathers in the Jāhiliyya of fornication with women; their marriage is permissible for you in Islam." It is as though it were said: "Do not contract marriage with those with whom your fathers contracted, except what has passed of their fornication, for it is permitted to you to marry them." So that too is a discontinuous exception.

The second: that it is a continuous exception (muttaṣil), and it has two meanings. One: that marriage is taken to mean sexual intercourse, and the meaning is: He forbade a man to have intercourse with a woman with whom his father had intercourse, except what has passed on the part of the father in the Jāhiliyya of fornication with the woman, for it is permitted to the son to marry her. This meaning is also reported from Ibn Zayd, except that restriction is necessary in two places: one is His saying {وَلاَ تَنكِحُواْ}, that is "do not have lawful intercourse by marriage"; the other is the restriction in His saying {إِلاَّ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ} to intercourse of fornication, since otherwise intercourse in what has passed might be intercourse other than fornication, or it might be fornication. The implied meaning then becomes: "Do not have intercourse with those with whom your fathers had lawful intercourse by marriage, except those whose intercourse in the past was fornication." On this meaning which Ibn Zayd held, it is also possible that the first «النكاح» means the contract and the second intercourse, that is: "Do not marry those with whom your fathers had intercourse, except those whose intercourse was fornication."

The second meaning: "Do not contract marriage like the marriage of your fathers in the Jāhiliyya, except what preceded from you of those invalid contracts, for it is permitted to you to remain in them in Islam if they are of the kind that Islam confirms." This is on the opinion of those who make «ما» a maṣdarī, which has already been given.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: how is «ما قد سلف» excepted from «ما نكح آباؤكم»? I say: as «غيرَ أنَّ سيوفهم» is excepted from «ولا عيبَ فيهم». He means: if you are able to marry what has passed, then marry it, but nothing else is lawful for you; and that is impossible. The aim is to exaggerate in forbidding it and to block the way to permitting it, as it is bound to the impossible in perpetuity in such sayings as «حتى يَبْيَضَّ القارُّ» ('until the pitch turns white') and «حتى يَلِجَ الجَمَلُ في سَمِّ الخِياط» ('until the camel passes through the eye of the needle')." End. May Allah have mercy on him, he alluded to the verse of al-Nābigha:

1561 - ولا عيبَ فيهم غيرَ أنَّ سيوفَهم ... بِهِنَّ فُلولٌ من قِراعِ الكتائبِ
(There is no fault in them except that their swords are notched from striking the battalions.)

He means: if any fault is found in them, it is this, and no one counts this a fault, so the fault is negated of them by its own proof. But is the exception, on this meaning which al-Zamakhsharī put forward, of the discontinuous kind or the continuous? The truth is that it is continuous, because the meaning is: "Do not marry what your fathers married, except those who have passed and perished," and that is impossible, and its being impossible does not take it out of being continuous. As for the verse of poetry, there is something to consider in it; the apparent sense is that the exception in it too is continuous, because he made "fault" include his saying «غيرَ أنَّ سيوفَهم» in the sense he intended. There is room for investigation in it.

What emerges from the above is that what is meant by marriage in this verse is a valid or invalid contract, or intercourse; or that the first means the contract and the second intercourse. The discussion in al-Baqara has already been given, whether it is literal for both or for one of them, and the disagreement of people about that.

Some claimed that there is an advancing and deferring in the verse, the original being: "and do not marry what your fathers married of women, except what has passed; it was an indecency and an abhorrence, and an evil way." This is invalid both grammatically and in meaning. As for the first, because what is within the scope of «إنَّ» does not precede it; also the excepted does not precede the clause to whose complements it belongs, whether continuous or discontinuous, though there is a weak disagreement about this. As for the second, because He reported that it is an indecency and an abhorrence in past time by His saying «كان», so it is not sound for the past to be excepted from it, since the meaning would become: "it was an indecency in past time, except what occurred of it in past time, which is not an indecency."

«المَقْتُ» is hatred joined with contempt, so it is more specific than hatred. The pronoun in His saying «إنه» refers to the marriage understood from His saying {وَلاَ تَنكِحُواْ}; it can also refer to fornication if {إِلاَّ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ} is taken to mean fornication. And «كان» here does not indicate the past only, because its meaning here is that of "has never ceased"; and this meaning is what led al-Mubarrad to say "it is redundant (zāʾida)."

He was answered by the existence of a khabar (predicate), while the redundant has no khabar; and he perhaps means by its redundancy what I mentioned, that it does not indicate the past only, and so he expressed that by "redundancy."

His saying: {وَسَآءَ سَبِيلاً}: regarding «ساء» there are two views. One: that it runs the course of «بئس» in blame and in operation, so it contains an indefinite latent pronoun explained by what follows, namely «سبيلاً», and the one specifically blamed is omitted, its implied form being: «وساء سبيلاً سبيلُ هذا النكاحِ» ("and evil as a way is the way of this marriage"), like «بِئْسَ الشراب» that is, that water. The second: that it does not run the course of «بِئْس» in operation but is like the other verbs, so it contains a pronoun returning to what the pronoun in «إنه» returns to; and «سبيلاً» on both assumptions is a tamyīz (specification).

About this clause there are two analyses. One: that it has no grammatical position but is resumptive, and the pause is at His saying «ومقتاً», then «وساء سبيلاً» begins anew, that is: "and evil is this way, from marrying those whom the fathers married." The second: that it is conjoined to the khabar of «كان», on the basis that it is a quotation of an implied saying, that saying being what is conjoined to the khabar, and the implied form being: "and something said of it: evil as a way." Abū al-Baqāʾ stated it so. One might say: it can be conjoined to the khabar of «كان» without implying a saying, because this clause is equivalent to a singular; do you not see that it occurs as a khabar by itself, as you say «زيدٌ ساءَ رجلاً» and «كان زيدا ساء رجلاً»? The most that can be said is that you have brought two khabars of «كان», one a singular and the other a clause; unless it is said that this is an inshāʾī (non-declarative) clause, and an inshāʾī clause does not occur as a khabar of «كان», so he needed to imply a saying; and there is discussion in that.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهَاتُكُمْ}: «أمهات» is the plural of «أم»; the hāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the plural, to distinguish rational beings from others. One says for rational beings «أمهات» and for others «أُمَّات», as in his saying:

1562 - وأُمَّاتِ أَطْلاءٍ صغارِ. . . . . ...
(and the mothers of small foals ...)

This is the well-known usage; but «أُمَّات» may also be said of rational beings and «أمهات» of others. The poet combined the two usages for rational beings, saying:

1563 - إذا الأمَّهاتُ قَبُحْنَ الوجوهَ ... فَرَجْتَ الظلامَ بأُمَّاتِكا
(When the mothers have ugly faces, you dispel the darkness with your mothers.)

«أُمَّهة» was also heard for «أُم», with an added hāʾ followed by the tāʾ of femininity. He said:

1564 - أُمَّهتي خِنْدِفُ والياسُ أبي ...
(My mother is Khindif and Ilyās is my father ...)

On this, «أمهات» may be the plural of «أُمَّهة», to which the hāʾ was added; and the hāʾ has come as a redundant letter in several places / they said «هِبْلَع» and «هِجْرَع», from «البَلْع» and «الجَرْع» (swallowing, gulping).

His saying: {وَبَنَاتُكُمْ}: conjoined to «أُمَّهاتكم». «بنات» is the plural of «بنت», and «بنت» is the feminine of «ابن»; the discussion of it, its derivation and its pattern was given in al-Baqara at His saying {يَابَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ} [verse 40]. Except that Abū al-Baqāʾ related from al-Farrāʾ that «بنات» is not the plural of «بنت», meaning with kasra on the bāʾ, but the plural of «بَنة», meaning with fatḥa; he said: "The bāʾ was given kasra to draw attention to what was omitted." I say: this holds only on the belief that its lām is a yāʾ, and we have previously had a disagreement about that, the correct view being that it is a wāw. He also related from others that its origin is «بَنوَة», and on that basis came its plural and its masculine, which is «بنون». He said: "This is the school of the Basrans." I say: there is, in truth, no disagreement between the two views, because whoever says «بنات» is the plural of «بَنة» with fatḥa on the bāʾ must believe that its origin is «بَنَوة», its lām omitted and replaced by the tāʾ of femininity, while whoever says «بنات» is the plural of «بَنَوة» pronounced the original; so there is no disagreement.

Know that the tāʾ of «بنت» and «أخت» is a tāʾ of compensation for the omitted lām, as its statement was given earlier, and it is not for femininity. Two things prove that. One: the tāʾ of femininity requires that what is before it have fatḥa, in speech or in implication, as in thamara and fatāh; whereas here what is before it is sukūn. The second: the tāʾ of femininity is changed to hāʾ in pause, and this one is not changed but stays as it is. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "If it is asked: why is the omitted letter restored in «أخوات» but not in «بنات»? It is said: each of the two plurals was taken to follow its masculine. The masculine of «بنات» was not restored to its omitted letter but they said «بنون», while the masculine of «أخوات» was restored its omitted letter, as they said for the plural of «أخ»: «إخْوة» and «إخْوان»."
