What he said is nothing, because he took the broken plural, which is «إخوة» and «إخوان», as the counterpart of «أَخَوات», a sound plural, and said it was restored in «أخوات» as it was restored in «إخوة». But this too exists in «بنات», because its masculine in the broken plural is restored to its omitted letter. They said «ابن» and «أبناء»; and when they made the sound masculine plural of «أخ» they said «أَخُون» with omission. So they restored the omitted letter in the broken plural of «ابن» and «أخ», but did not restore it in their sound plural. Thus the invalidity of what he said is clear.

His saying: {وَخَالاَتُكُمْ}: the alif of «خالة» and «خال» is converted from a wāw, by the evidence of its plural «أخوال». The Exalted said: {أَوْ بُيُوتِ أَخْوَالِكُمْ} [al-Nūr: 61].

His saying: {مِّنَ الرضاعة}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), so it is attached to an omitted element, the implied form being: "and your sisters by nursing." Abū Ḥaywa read «من الرِّضاعة» with kasra on the rāʾ. {مِّن نِّسَآئِكُمُ}: two analyses. One: that it is a ḥāl from «ربائبكم», the implied form being: "and your stepdaughters who are of your wives." The second: that it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in His saying {فِي حُجُورِكُمْ}, because when it occurs as a ṣila (relative clause) it carries a pronoun, that is: "those who dwell in your care."

«الربائب» is the plural of «ربيبة», who is the daughter of the husband or of the wife, and the masculine is «ربيب». They were so named because one of the spouses brings him up (yarubbuhu) as he brings up his own son. His saying {اللاتي فِي حُجُورِكُمْ} has no implied contrary meaning (mafhūm) because it is stated as it is only for being the usual case. «الحُجُور» is the plural of «حِجْر», with fatḥa or kasra on the ḥāʾ, which is the front of a person's garment; the word was then used for guarding and covering.

His saying: {اللاتي دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ}: a description (ṣifa) of «نسائكم» which is genitive by «مِنْ»; the condition for forbidding the stepdaughter is that one has consummated the marriage with her mother.

It cannot be a description of both the first and the second «نسائكم», for two reasons. One, from the technical side: the first «نسائكم» is genitive by annexation and the second is genitive by «مِنْ», so the two governors differ, and when they differ the description is impossible; you do not say «رأيت زيداً ومررت بعمرٍو العاقلين», making «العاقلين» a description of both. The second, from the side of meaning: the mother of the wife becomes forbidden merely by contracting marriage with the daughter, whether or not he consummated it, according to the majority, whereas the stepdaughter is forbidden only by consummation with her mother.

In al-Zamakhsharī's words there is something implying that this description could go back to the first one in meaning, for he said: "{مِّن نِّسَآئِكُمُ} is attached to «ربائبكم» and its meaning is: the stepdaughter of a woman with whom marriage has been consummated is forbidden to the man, and permitted to him if he has not consummated it. If you ask: is it sound to attach it to His saying {وَأُمَّهَاتُ نِسَآئِكُمْ}? I say: it cannot be free of one of two cases: either it is attached to them and to the stepdaughters, so that their prohibition and the prohibition of the stepdaughters would both be non-absolute; or it is attached to them without the stepdaughters, so that their prohibition would be non-absolute and the prohibition of the stepdaughters absolute. The first is not allowed, because the meaning of «من» with one of the two attachments is the opposite of its meaning with the other. Do you not see that if you say «وأمهاتُ نسائكم من نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن» you have made «مِنْ» for explaining the women and distinguishing the consummated from the unconsummated, and if you say «وربائبكم من نسائِكم اللاتي دَخَلْتُم بهن» you have made «مِنْ» for the beginning of the extent, as you say «بنات رسول الله صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ من خديجة» ("the daughters of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by Khadīja"); and it is not sound for one word in one address to mean two different meanings. The second is not allowed, because what immediately follows is what requires the attachment, unless something irrefutable intervenes. Unless you say: I attach it to the women and the stepdaughters, and I make «من» for connection, as in the saying of the Exalted: {المنافقون والمنافقات بَعْضُهُمْ مِّن بَعْضٍ} [al-Tawba: 67], [and he said]:

1565 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فإني لستُ مِنْكَ ولَسْتَ مِنِّي
(... for I am not of you and you are not of me)

[and his saying]:

1566 - ما أنا من ددٍ ولا ددٌ مِنِي ...
(I am not of play, nor is play of me)

and the mothers of the women are connected to the women because they are their mothers, just as the stepdaughters are connected to their mothers because they are their daughters. Yet they have agreed that the prohibition of the mothers of wives is absolute." End. Then he said: "except what is reported from ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, Zayd, Ibn ʿAmr and Ibn al-Zubayr, that they read «وأمهاتُ نسائكم اللاتي دَخَلْتُم بهن», and Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: 'By Allah, it was revealed only thus.'" His saying "I attach it to the women and the stepdaughters" to the end requires that the restriction in the stepdaughters, namely consummation, applies to «أمهات نسائكم» as well, as was related earlier from ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās. The Shaykh said: "We do not know anyone who established for «مِنْ» the meaning of connection; as for the verse, the line of poetry and the hadith, they are interpreted otherwise."

His saying: {وَحَلاَئِلُ}: the plural of «حليلة», who is the wife; she was so named because she settles (taḥullu) with her husband wherever he is, so it is faʿīla in the sense of fāʿila (active); and the husband is likewise «حليل». He said:

1567 - أغشى فتاةَ الحَيِّ عند حليلِها ... وإذا غَزَا في الجيشِ لا أَغْشاها
(I visit the young woman of the tribe while her husband is present; but when he goes on a campaign with the army I do not visit her.)

It was also said that its derivation is from the word «الحلال» (lawful), since each of them is lawful to the other; this is the view of al-Zajjāj and a group, so «فَعِيل» would be in the sense of mafʿūl (passive), that is: made lawful for him, and he is made lawful for her; except that the entry of the feminine ending weakens this, unless it is said that it runs the course of the non-derived nouns, / like «النطيحة» and «الذبيحة». It was also said that both are from the word «الحَلّ» (untying), the opposite of «العقد» (tying), because each of them unties the waist-wrapper of the other.

{الذين مِنْ أَصْلاَبِكُمْ} is a clarifying description, because «الابن» may be applied to an adopted son, and his wife is not forbidden to the one who adopted him. As for the son by nursing, although his ruling in that is the ruling of the son of the loins, it is made clear by the Sunna, so it does not pose an objection to the noble verse.

«أَصْلاب» is the plural of «صُلْب», which is the back, so called for its strength, derived from «الصَّلابة» (hardness). The more eloquent of its two forms is «صُلْب», with ḍamma on the first letter and sukūn on the second, which is the dialect of the Hijaz; Banū Tamīm and Asad say «صَلَباً», with fatḥa on both. Al-Farrāʾ related that from them in his book «لغات القرآن» (Dialects of the Quran), and he recited, from one of them:

1568 - في صَلَبٍ مثلٍ العِنانِ المُؤْدَمِ ...
(in a back like a smooth rein [of tanned leather])

and he related from them: «إذا أَقُوم اشتكى صَلَبي» ("when I stand up my back hurts").

His saying: {وَأَن تَجْمَعُواْ}: in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the nominative «حُرِّمت», that is: "and joining two sisters is forbidden to you"; what is meant is joining them in marriage. In ownership it is permitted by agreement; as for intercourse by right of ownership, there is a disagreement which this is not the place for.

His saying: {إَلاَّ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ}: a discontinuous exception, so it is accusative in position, as in its parallel earlier, that is: "but what passed in the Jāhiliyya, Allah forgives it." It was also said that the meaning is: except what he contracted before Islam, for after Islam that marriage remains valid, but he chooses one of the two and separates from the other. Something close to this meaning was given earlier at the first {مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ}, and the exception on this view would be continuous; here continuity is not possible at all, because the meaning would be corrupt.

semin-durr:79-79.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {َمَّآ أَصَابَك}: about this «ما» there are two views. The first: it is conditional (sharṭiyya), which is the view of Abū al-Baqāʾ, and he considered it weak that it be a relative (mawṣūla). He said: "It is not good that it mean «الذي», because that would require that what befalls them be past and specific, whereas the meaning is general; the conditional is more apt, and what is meant by the verse is fertility and drought, and for that reason He did not say «ما أصبت»." End of quotation. He means that some say that what is meant by «الحسنة» is obedience and by «السيئة» disobedience; and had that been intended, He would have said «ما أَصَبْتَ», because he is the doer of both the good deed and the bad deed, and so they would only be ascribed to him by his doing them. The second: it is a relative meaning «الذي», and Makkī took this view and denied that it is conditional. He said: "It is not conditional, because it was revealed about a particular thing, namely drought and fertility, and a condition can only be indefinite, possibly occurring and possibly not; the fāʾ entered only because of the indefiniteness in «الذي», although its ṣila is a verb; and this indicates that the verse is not about acts of disobedience and obedience as the people of deviation say; moreover the wording is «ما أصابَك» and He did not say «ما أَصَبْتَ»." End of quotation. The first is more apparent, because the conditional is the basis for indefiniteness — as Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned — whereas the relative is by analogy to it. As for Makkī's statement "because it was revealed about a particular thing": this requires that the relative not be likened to the conditional, because it is only likened to it when indefiniteness is intended and not a particular thing; otherwise, whenever a particular thing is intended it is not likened to the conditional and the fāʾ does not enter its khabar; the grammarians stated this explicitly, and there is widespread disagreement on the question, this not being its place. On the first view «أصابَك» is in the position of the jussive by the condition, and on the second it has no position, because it is a ṣila.
As for «من حسنةٍ», the discussion about it is like the discussion on His saying: {مَا نَنسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ} [al-Baqara: 106], which has already been given. The fāʾ in «فَمِنَ الله» is the apodosis of the condition on the first view and redundant on the second, and the preposition and genitive noun after it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "so it is from Allah"; the clause is in the position of the jussive or the nominative according to the two views. There is disagreement about the address-kāf: it is said that what is meant is everyone; it is said that it is the Messenger and what is meant is his Community; and it is said that it is the group in His saying «إذا فريقٌ», because «فريقاً» is a collective noun and so has a wording and a meaning, and he took its wording into account and used the singular, as in the saying:
1617 - تفرَّق أهلانا بِبَيْنٍ فمنهمُ ... فريقٌ أقامَ واستقلَّ فريقُ
(Our two families were separated by parting; of them one group stayed and another group departed.)
And it was said about His saying {فَمِن نَّفْسِكَ} that the interrogative hamza is omitted, its implied form being «أفمِنْ نفسِك» ("is it from yourself?"), and this is frequent, as in His saying the Exalted: {وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 22] and His saying the Exalted: {بَازِغاً قَالَ هذا رَبِّي} [al-Anʿām: 77], and from it:
1618 - رَفَوْني وقالوا: يا خُوَيْلِدُ لا تُرَعْ ... فقلتُ وأنكرتُ الوجوهَ هُمُ هُمُ
(They soothed me and said: "O Khuwaylid, do not be afraid." I said, not recognizing the faces: "Are they the very ones?")
and his saying: 1619 - أفرحُ أَنْ أُرْزَأ الكرامَ وأنْ ... أُورَثَ ذَوْدَاً شَصائِصاً نَبْلاً
(Should I rejoice that I lose noble ones and inherit barren, worthless camels?)
the implied form being: «وأتلك», «وأهذا ربي», «وأهمُ هُم», «وأأفرحُ». "And none of the grammarians allowed this except al-Akhfash; as for others, they allowed it only before «أم», as in the saying:
1620 - لَعَمْرُكَ ما أدري وإنْ كنت؟ ُ دارِياً ... بسبعِ رَمَيْنَ الجمرَ أم بثمانِ
(By your life, I do not know, even if I am knowing, whether they threw the pebbles with seven or with eight.)
[Translator's note: the printed text of this verse is corrupt in "كنت؟ ُ"; I have given the gloss of the familiar verse.] It was also said that there is an implied statement here, i.e. "they scarcely understand any speech; they say: 'what befalls you ...'".
ʿĀʾisha read «فَمَنْ نفسُك» with fatḥa on the mīm of «من» and a nominative (ḍamma) on the sīn, as mubtadaʾ and khabar, i.e. "what thing is your self that an act should be ascribed to it?". His saying: «رسولاً» has two possibilities: the first: it is a corroborating ḥāl; the second: it is a corroborating maṣdar meaning "sending" (irsāl); and an instance of «رسول» as a maṣdar is the saying:
1621 - لقد كَذَبَ الواشون ما بُحْتُ عندهم ... بِسِرِّ ولا أَرْسَلْتُهمْ برسولِ
(The slanderers have lied: I did not divulge a secret to them, nor did I send them with a message.)
i.e. with a sending, meaning a message (risāla). And «للناس» is attached to «أرسلناك», and the lām is of cause. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a ḥāl from «رسولاً», as though he made it originally an adjective of an indefinite noun and put it before it; and there is a consideration in this.

semin-durr:80-80.t: And {حَفِيظاً}: a ḥāl from the kāf of «أرسلناك», and «عليهم» is attached to «حفيظاً»; and Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed for it what was given earlier for «للناس».

semin-durr:81-81.t: His saying, the Exalted: {طَاعَةٌ}: there are two possibilities for its being nominative. The first: it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "our command is obedience" (أمرنا طاعةٌ); it is not permissible to make this mubtadaʾ overt, because the khabar is a maṣdar standing in place of the verb's wording. The second: it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted, i.e. "from us is obedience" or "with us is obedience". Makkī said: "In speech the accusative as a maṣdar is permissible." Abū ʿAmr and Ḥamza assimilated the tāʾ of «بَيَّت» into the ṭāʾ of «طائفة» because of their closeness, and no feminine marker is attached to the verb because the feminine is figurative (not true). And «منهم» is an adjective of «طائفة». The pronoun in «تقول» may be a pronoun of address to the Messenger, peace be upon him, i.e. "other than what you say and prescribe, O Muḥammad". The reading of ʿAbd Allāh supports it: «بَيَّتَ مُبَيِّتٌ منهم». It may also be a pronoun of the third person for the group, i.e. "she says". Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read «يقول» with the yāʾ of the third person, so the pronoun may refer to the Messenger in the sense given before, or to the group. The pronoun is not made feminine because «الطائفة» has the meaning of the party and the people. And «ما» in «ما يبيِّتون» may be a relative, or an indefinite noun with a description (mawṣūfa), or a maṣdar particle (maṣdariyya).

semin-durr:82-82.t: Ibn Muḥayṣin read {يَتَدَبَّرُونَ}: with assimilation of the tāʾ into the dāl; the original is «يَتَدبرون» [and it differs from the orthography of the copy (rasm)]. The pronoun in «فيه» may refer to the Qur'an, which is the apparent sense, or to what Allah the Exalted informs of, of what they plot by night and conceal, meaning that He informs them of it exactly as it occurs.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والمحصنات}: the majority read this word, whether definite with «ال» or indefinite, with fatḥa on the ṣād; al-Kisāʾī read it with kasra in the plural, except for His saying {والمحصنات مِنَ النسآء} at the head of the juzʾ, where he agreed with the majority. As for the fatḥa, there are two analyses. The better known: that iḥṣān (protection in marriage / chastity) is ascribed to someone other than them, either the husbands or the guardians, for the husband protects his wife, that is, keeps her chaste; and the guardian protects her by giving her in marriage as well; and Allah protects her by that. The second: that this one with fatḥa on the ṣād stands in the place of the one with kasra, meaning that it is an active participle; the fatḥa on the ʿayn of the active participle is irregular in only three words: «أَحْصَنَ فهو مُحْصَن», «أَلْقح فهو مُلْقَح» and «أَسْهَب فهو مُسْهَب».

As for the kasra, iḥṣān is ascribed to them, because they protect themselves by their chastity, or protect their private parts by guarding, or protect their husbands. As for al-Kisāʾī's exception of the one at the head of the juzʾ, he said: "because what is meant by them there is the married women, so the meaning is: their husbands protected them, so they are objects." This is on one of the views about who the muḥṣanāt are here. Although the one at the head of the juzʾ was also read, irregularly, with kasra, even if the married women are meant by it, since the meaning is that they protected their husbands or their private parts, and that is plain. Yazīd ibn Quṭayb read «المُحْصُنات» with ḍamma on the ṣād, as if he did not count the sukūn (as a barrier) and made the ṣād follow the mīm, as in their saying «مُنْتُن».

The root of this material is the indication of prevention, from which «الحِصْن» (fortress), because by it one is protected, and «حِصان» for the horse is from that. One says «أَحْصَنَتِ المرأةُ» and «حَصُنَتْ»; the maṣdar of «حَصُنَت» is «حُصْن» according to Sībawayh and «حَصانة» according to al-Kisāʾī and Abū ʿUbayda; the active participle of «أَحْصَنَتْ» is «مُحْصَنة», and of «حَصُنت» is «حاصِن». He said:

1569 - وحاصِنٍ من حاصناتٍ مُلْسِ ... مِن الأذى ومن قِراف الوَقْسِ
(a chaste woman among chaste, smooth women, free from harm and from the contact of vileness)

She is also called «حَصان», with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ. Ḥassān said describing ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her:

1570 - حَصانٌ رزانٌ ما تُزَنُّ بريبةٍ ... وتصبحُ غَرْثَى مِنْ لُحومِ الغَوافل
(Chaste, dignified, not suspected of any doubt; she rises hungry, abstaining from the flesh of heedless women [i.e. backbiting].)

Iḥṣān occurs in the Quran meaning one of four meanings: marriage, chastity, freedom and Islam. Knowing this will benefit you in the exception that follows it. If marriage is meant by it here, the meaning is: "and the muḥṣanāt, that is the married women, are forbidden to you, except the kind that your right hands possess", either by capture or by ownership through purchase, gift and inheritance; this is the view of some scholars. The first is indicated by the saying of al-Farazdaq:

1571 - وذاتِ حَليلٍ أَنْكَحَتْها رماحُنا ... حَلالٌ لِمَنْ يَبْني بها لم تُطَلَّقِ
(Many a woman with a husband our spears gave in marriage; she is lawful to whoever consummates with her, though she was not divorced.)

meaning that her mere capture made her lawful after the waiting period of clearing the womb. If Islam or chastity is meant, the meaning is that the Muslim women or the chaste women are all forbidden, meaning that no illicit intercourse is to be had with them except what is owned of them by marriage or by right of the right hand; then what is meant by {مَا مَلَكْتَ أَيْمَانُكُمْ} is having authority over them, which is a common measure. On these three analyses the exception is continuous (muttaṣil). If free women are meant, then what is meant is "except what you have acquired by right of the right hand", and on this the exception is discontinuous (munqaṭiʿ).

His saying: {مِنَ النسآء}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), like its parallel earlier. Makkī said: "The benefit of His saying {مِنَ النسآء} is that «المُحْصَناتِ» can apply to persons, so His saying {مِنَ النسآء} removes that possibility. The proof that persons are meant by «المحصنات» is His saying: {والذين يَرْمُونَ المحصنات} [al-Nūr: 4]; if women alone were meant by it, then one who slanders a man would not receive the ḥadd punishment by the text of the Quran, yet they are agreed that his ḥadd is by this text." End. This is strange speech, because, after granting what he said about the verse of al-Nūr, how could anyone imagine that here?

His saying: {كِتَابَ الله}: it has three analyses in its accusative. The clearest: that it is accusative as a confirming maṣdar (verbal noun) of the content of the preceding clause, which is His saying «حُرِّمت», its accusative being by an implied verb, that is: "Allah has prescribed that upon you as a prescription." ʿAbīda al-Salmānī went furthest in making this maṣdar a confirmation of the content of the clause in the saying of the Exalted {فانكحوا مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 3].

The second: that it is accusative by ighrāʾ (urging) with «عليكم», the implied form being: «عليكم كتابَ الله», that is: "hold fast to it", like {عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ} [al-Māʾida: 105]. This is the opinion of al-Kisāʾī and those who followed him: they allowed putting the accusative before in the chapter of ighrāʾ, citing as evidence this verse and the saying of another:

1572 - يا أيُّها المائحُ دَلْوي دونَكَا ... إني رأيْتُ الناسَ يَحْمَدونكا
(O you who draw water, take my bucket; I have seen the people praise you.)

where «دلوي» is accusative by «دونَك», as was given before. The Basrans forbid that, saying that the governor is weak; they interpret the verse as given before, and the line of poetry on the basis that «دلوي» is accusative by «المائح», that is: "the one who drew my bucket."

The third: that it is accusative by an implied verb, that is: "hold fast to the Book of Allah", which is close to ighrāʾ. Abū al-Baqāʾ said about this analysis: "its implied form is: hold fast to the Book of Allah", and «عليكم» is ighrāʾ, meaning that its object is omitted, as «كتاب الله» indicates it, that is: «عليكم ذلك», which makes it more emphatic. As for «عليكم», Abū al-Baqāʾ said: on the view that «كتاب» is a maṣdar, it is attached to the implied verb governing «كتاب» and is not attached to the maṣdar, "because here it is a surplus". He said: "It was also said that it is attached to the maṣdar itself / because it has taken the place of the verb, since it is not mentioned with it, so it is like your saying «مروراً بزيد»." I say: on the view that it is ighrāʾ it has no position, because it stands in the position of an imperative verb; and on the view that it is accusative by an implied verb, that is "hold fast", «عليكم» is attached to «كتاب» itself or to an omitted element as a ḥāl from it.

Abū Ḥaywa read «كَتَبَ اللهُ», with «كتب» a past verb and «الله» its agent; this supports its being accusative as a confirming maṣdar. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ al-Yamānī read «كُتُبُ الله», making it a nominative plural annexed to Allah the Exalted, as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being: "these are the writings of Allah upon you."

His saying: {وَأُحِلَّ}: the two Kufan readers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read «أُحِلَّ» as passive; the rest read it as active. In both readings the verb is conjoined to the verbal clause of His saying «حُرِّمَتْ», and the one who forbids and the one who permits is Allah the Exalted in both places, whether the verb is explicitly ascribed to His pronoun or the agent is omitted because it is known.

Al-Zamakhsharī claimed that the reading «أُحِلَّ» as passive is conjoined to «حُرِّمت», so that a passive verb is conjoined to its like; as for the reading with the active, he made it conjoined to the implied verb governing «كتاب», as if it were said: "Allah prescribed for you the prohibition of that, and made lawful to you what is beyond that." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "What he chose, meaning the distinction between the two readings, is not to be chosen; because what governs «كتابَ الله» is a clause confirming the content of the clause «حُرِّمت» to the end, whereas His saying «وأَحَلَّ لكم» is a foundational clause (taʾsīsiyya), so it is not fitting to conjoin it except to a foundational one like it, not to a confirming clause. The two clauses here are opposites, since one is for prohibition and the other for permission, so the fitting thing is to conjoin one to the other, not to another clause that is not the first. He himself did the same in the reading with the passive, so let this be like it." In this rebuttal there is something to consider.

And {مَّا وَرَاءَ ذَلِكُمْ} is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object): either accusative in position or nominative, according to the two readings of «أحلَّ».

His saying: {أَن تَبْتَغُواْ}: for its position there are three analyses: nominative, accusative and genitive. The nominative is on the basis that it is a badal (substitute) for {مَّا وَرَاءَ ذَلِكُمْ} on the reading «أُحِلَّ» as passive, because «ما» then stands in the place of the agent, and this is a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) from it. As for the accusative, the best is that it is a badal from the preceding «ما» on the reading «أَحَلَّ» as active, as if He said: "and Allah has made lawful to you seeking with your wealth, by marriage or by right of the right hand." Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that its accusative be as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); he said: "meaning: He made clear to you what is lawful as distinct from what is forbidden, desiring that your seeking with your wealth, which Allah made for you a means of support, be in the state of your being muḥṣinīn (chaste)."

The Shaykh attacked him, claiming that he meant by this a covert Muʿtazilite insinuation, then said: "The apparent sense of the verse is other than what he understood, for the apparent sense is that Allah the Exalted has made lawful to us the seeking, with our wealth, of what is other than the forbidden women whose mention preceded, in the state of chastity and not in the state of fornication. On this apparent sense it is not permitted to analyze «أن تبتغوا» as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), because one of the conditions of the mafʿūl lahu is missed, namely the unity of the agent in the governor and the mafʿūl lahu; for the agent of «أحلَّ» is Allah the Exalted, and the agent in «تبتغوا» is the pronoun of the addressees, so they differ. When al-Zamakhsharī sensed this, if he sensed it, he made «أن تبتغوا» depend on an omitted «إرادة» (desiring), so that the agent would be one in «وأحلَّ» and in the mafʿūl lahu, and he made «أن تبتغوا» a mafʿūl lahu only by omitting a muḍāf and putting it in its place; and all this is a departure from the apparent sense." End.

I do not know what this strain is, nor how the condition of unity of agent in the mafʿūl lahu could be hidden from Abū al-Qāsim (al-Zamakhsharī) such that he would say "if he sensed it"!!!

Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed the accusative in it by omission of the preposition. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "As for «ما», meaning in His saying {وَأُحِلَّ لَكُمْ مَّا وَرَاءَ ذَلِكُمْ}, there are two analyses. One: it is in the sense of «مَنْ»; on this, His saying «أن تبتغوا» is in the position of genitive or accusative, on the implication of «بأن تبتغوا» or «لأنْ تبتغوا», that is: women other than those we mentioned are made lawful to you with dowers. The second: that «ما» is in the sense of «الذي», and «الذي» is a metonym for the act, that is: He made lawful to you the obtaining of what is beyond that forbidden act, and «أن تبتغوا» is a badal from it; it is also possible that its original is «بأن تبتغوا» or «لأن تبتغوا»." In what he said there is something to consider which is not hidden.

As for the genitive, it is as Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned; what is in it has been given.

{مُّحْصِنِينَ} is a ḥāl from the agent of «تَبْتغوا», and «غيرَ مسافحين» is a second ḥāl; it can also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مُحْصِنين». The object of «محصنين» and «مسافحين» is omitted, that is: "protecting your private parts, not fornicating with fornicating women"; and it is in reality a confirming ḥāl, because the one who is muḥṣin is not a fornicator. To my knowledge no one has read «محصنين» with fatḥa on the ṣād.

His saying: {فَمَا استمتعتم بِهِ}: two analyses are possible for «ما»: one, that it is conditional (sharṭiyya); the other, that it is a relative noun (mawṣūla). On both assumptions it may mean the women enjoyed, that is, the kind enjoyed, or it may mean the enjoyment which is the act itself. On all the analyses given it is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. If it is conditional, then there is the famous disagreement about its khabar: is it the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the apodosis (jawāb), or both? Its verification was given in al-Baqara. If it is a relative noun, the khabar is His saying {فَآتُوهُنَّ}, and the fāʾ entered because the relative noun resembles a conditional noun; its verification too was given earlier. Then, if what is meant is the kind enjoyed, the returning pronoun to the mubtadaʾ, whether «ما» is conditional or relative, is the accusative pronoun in «فآتوهن», so he has attended to the form of «ما» at one time, using the singular in «به», and to its meaning at another time, using the plural in «منهن» and «فآتوهن». The meaning becomes: "whichever kind of women you have enjoyed, give them", or "the kind which you have enjoyed of women, give them". If enjoyment is what is meant, then the returning pronoun is omitted, its implied form being: "whichever kind of enjoyment you have enjoyed of women, give them their dowers for it", or "whichever kind of enjoyment which you have enjoyed of women, give them their dowers for it."

And «مِنْ» in «منهن» (in the source: «منهم») admits two analyses: one, that it is explicative; the other, that it is partitive; and its position is accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «به». «ما» cannot be a maṣdarī, because the meaning would be corrupted and because the pronoun in «به» returns to it. /
«السِّفاح» is fornication, and its origin is pouring, because the fornicator pours into it; they used to say: «سافحيني وماذيني» (pour for me and be pleasant to me). The «مسافِح» is the one who is open about fornication, and the one who takes lovers (mutakhidh al-akhdān) is the one who is secretive and takes one in hiding.

His saying: {فَرِيضَةً}: a ḥāl from «أجورهن», or a confirming maṣdar, that is: "Allah made that obligatory as an obligation", or a maṣdar not derived from the verb's own form, because the giving is obligatory, as if it were said: "so give them their dowers as an obligatory giving."

[Translator's notes: the source reads «أوزاجَهُنَّ» (for «أزواجهن»), «التفرقه» (for «التفرقة»), «أخرىغيرِ» (two words run together), and «منهم» where «منهن» is evidently meant; I translated the intended sense. «الصَبُّ» is rendered "pouring" as the source's etymology of «السفاح».]

semin-durr:83-83.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَذَاعُواْ بِهِ}: the apodosis of «إذا». The middle radical of «أذاع» is yāʾ, because of their saying «ذاع الشيءَ يذِيع»; and one also says «أذاع الشيء» in the sense of the bare form, and it is transitive by itself and by means of the bāʾ, and the noble verse is on this basis. It was also said that «أذاع» is made to include the meaning of «تَحَدَّثَ» (to speak), so it is made transitive the way that is, i.e. "they spoke of it, divulging it". «الإِذاعة» is spreading (ishāʿa). Abū al-Aswad said:
162 - 2- أذاعُوا به في الناسِ حتى كأنه ... بِعَلْياءِ نار أُوقِدَتْ بثَقُوب
(They spread it among the people until it was like a fire lit on a height with a kindling stick.)
The pronoun in «به» may refer to the matter (al-amr), and may refer to the security or the fear, because the conjunction is with «أو»; and the pronoun in «رَدُّوه» is for the matter only. «الاستنباط» is extracting, and so is «الإِنباط». He said:
162 - 3- نَعَمْ صادقاً والفاعلُ القائلُ الذي ... إذا قال قَوْلاً أنبطَ الماءَ في الثَّرى
(Yes, truthful, the doer, the speaker who, when he speaks a word, brings forth water in the earth.)
One says «نَبَطَ الماءُ يَنْبطُ» with fatḥa or ḍamma on the bāʾ; «النَّبَط» is the water that comes out of a well when its digging first begins. «النَّبَط» is also "a people among mankind, so called because they extract waters and plants". And it is said of a man who is far from being overcome and who is protected: «ما يَجِدُ عدوُّه له نَبَطاً» ("his enemy finds no water-source against him"). Kaʿb said:
162 - 4- قريبٌ ثَراه ما ينال عدوُّه ... له نَبَطاً، آبيْ الهوانِ قَطُوبُ
(Near is his moist earth; his enemy gets no hidden water against him; refusing humiliation, frowning.)
And «منهم» is a ḥāl, either from «الذين» or from the pronoun in «يستنبطونه», and so it is attached to an omitted word. Abū al-Sammāl read «لَعَلْمه» with sukūn on the lām; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is like the sukūn in {فِيمَا شَجَرَ بَيْنَهُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 65]. But it is not like it, because putting sukūn on fa-ʿil with kasra on the ʿayn is regular (muṭṭarid) whereas putting sukūn on one with fatḥa is anomalous; and like the sukūn of «لَعَلْمه» is the saying:
162 - 5- فإنْ تَبْلُه يَضْجَرْ كما ضَجْرَ بازِلٌ ... من الأُدْمِ دُبْرَتْ صَفْحَتاه وغارِبُه
(If you test him he frets, as a mature camel among the pale camels frets whose sides and withers have been galled.)
i.e. «دَبِرت», and he put sukūn."
His saying: {إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً}: it has ten possibilities. The first: it is excepted from the agent of «اتَّبعتم», i.e. "you would have followed Satan, except a few of you", for he did not follow Satan, on the supposition that the bounty of Allah did not reach him, and by "bounty" is meant the sending of Muḥammad ﷺ; and those few are like Qiss ibn Sāʿida al-Iyādī, Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl and Waraqa ibn Nawfal, of those who were on the religion of the Messiah before the mission of the Messenger. It was also said: what is meant is those who had not reached the age of obligation (taklīf), and on this interpretation it was said that the exception is discontinuous (munqaṭiʿ), because the excepted was not included under the address; and there is a consideration in this which appears in the tenth possibility. The second: it is excepted from the agent of «أذاعوا», i.e. "they publicized the matter of security or fear, except a few". The third: it is excepted from the agent of «عَلِمه», i.e. "those of them who extract it would have known it, except a few". The fourth: it is excepted from the agent of «لوجدوا», i.e. "they would have found in what is from other than Allah contradiction, except a few of them, who is the one who does not examine closely, so he thinks falsehood to be truth and the contradictory to be consistent". The fifth: it is excepted from the genitive pronoun in «عليكم», and its interpretation is like that of the first possibility.
The sixth: it is excepted from the agent of «يستنبطونه», and its interpretation is like that of the third. The seventh: it is excepted from the maṣdar indicated by the verb, the implied form being: "you would have followed Satan, except with a little following"; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned this. The eighth: it is excepted from that in which one follows (al-muttabaʿ fīhi), the implied form being: "all of you would have followed Satan except in a few matters in which you did not follow Satan, so the meaning is: you would have followed Satan in everything except in a few matters, in which you would not have followed him"; on this basis it is a "freed" exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh); Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned this, except that in his words there is an objection, namely that he said "i.e. you would have followed Satan, all of you, except a few matters in which you did not follow him", so he made it here excepted from the omitted thing followed in, as its statement was given above, whereas it had been stated earlier that it was excepted from the following (ittibāʿ); so his implied form leads to its being excepted from the thing followed in, and his claim that it is excepted from the following, and these are two different things. The ninth: that what is meant by fewness is nonexistence, he means: "all of you would have followed Satan, with no one among you holding back"; Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported it from a group and from al-Ṭabarī, and rejected it, because the joining of fewness with exception requires its inclusion; he said: "This is a shaky statement and is not like what Sībawayh related of their saying: «هذه أرضٌ قَلَّ ما تنبت كذا» ("this is a land that scarcely grows such-and-such"), i.e. it grows nothing.
And what he said is correct, except that he had earlier in al-Baqara [Translator's note: the source says al-Baqara but the verse cited is from al-Nisāʾ] at His saying the Exalted {وَلَكِن لَّعَنَهُمُ الله بِكُفْرِهِمْ فَلاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً} [al-Nisāʾ: 46] that the diminution here means nonexistence, and the refutation of him was given there; so he was alert to this meaning here but was not alert to it there. The tenth: that the one addressed by «لاتبعتم» is all people in general, and what is meant by "a few" is the Community of Muḥammad ﷺ in particular; and the proponent of this view supported his view with his saying, peace be upon him: "You, among the other nations besides you, are only like the white patch on a black ox."

semin-durr:84-84.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَقَاتِلْ}: in this fāʾ there are five possibilities. The first: it conjoins this clause onto the clause of His saying {فَلْيُقَاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ الله} [al-Nisāʾ: 74]. The second: it conjoins it onto the clause of His saying {فقاتلوا أَوْلِيَاءَ الشيطان} [al-Nisāʾ: 76]. The third: it conjoins it onto the clause of His saying {وَمَا لَكُمْ لاَ تُقَاتِلُونَ} [al-Nisāʾ: 75]. The fourth: it conjoins it onto the clause of His saying {فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ أَجْراً عَظِيماً} [al-Nisāʾ: 74]. The fifth: it is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you wish, then fight"; and the first of these views is the most apparent.
His saying: {لاَ تُكَلَّفُ إِلاَّ نَفْسَكَ}: about this clause there are two views. The first: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «فقاتِلْ», i.e. "fight, not being charged except with yourself alone". The second: it is resumptive; He the Exalted informed him that he is charged with nothing other than himself. The majority read «تُكَلَّفُ» with the address-tāʾ and the verb nominative and passive, and «نفسَك» is the second object. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar read «لا تُكَلِّفْ» like the group, except that he made it jussive; it was said: as the answer to the imperative, and there is a consideration in this; what ought to be is that it is a prohibition. It is a resumptive clause. It cannot be a ḥāl in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, because a request cannot be a ḥāl. «لا نُكَلِّف» was also read, with the nūn of majesty and the verb nominative, and it admits the ḥāl and the resumptive possibilities mentioned.
«التحريض» is urging on something. Al-Rāghib said: "It is as though in origin it is the removal of «الحَرَضْ», like «قَذِّيْتُه», i.e. I removed its speck; and «أَحْرضته» means I spoiled it, like «أقذيته», i.e. I put a speck in it. «الحَرَضُ» in origin is what is not counted and has no good in it, and therefore one says of one on the brink of destruction «حَرَض». He the Exalted said: {حتى تَكُونَ حَرَضاً} [Yūsuf: 85]; and «أَحْرَضَه» is such, he said:
162 - 6- إني امرؤٌ رابني هَمٌّ فَأَحْرضني ... حتى بُليِتُ وحتى شَفَّني السَّقَمُ
(I am a man whom a worry troubled and wore me out, until I was worn and sickness consumed me.)"
And «بأساً وتنكيلاً» is a tamyīz; «التنكيل» is the tafʿīl form from «النَّكْل», which is the fetter, and then it came to be used for every punishment.

semin-durr:85-85.t:
{والكِفْلُ}: the share (naṣīb), except that its use for evil is more frequent, the opposite of «النصيب», although «الكِفْلُ» has been used for good; He the Exalted said: {يُؤْتِكُمْ كِفْلَيْنِ مِن رَّحْمَتِهِ}. Its origin, they said, is borrowed from the «كِفْلِ البعير», which is a cloth wrapped around its hump so that it may be ridden; it is so called because it does not cover the whole of its back but only a portion of it. Because its use for evil predominates and the use of «النصيب» for good, He differentiated between the two in this noble verse, bringing «الكِفْل» with the bad deed and «النصيب» with the good deed. And «منها»: the apparent sense is that «مِنْ» here is causal, i.e. "a share because of it and a portion because of it"; it may also be for beginning (ibtidāʾiyya). «المُقِيت» is the one able (muqtadir). He said:
152 - 7- وذي ضِغْن كَفَفْتُ الودَّ عنه ... وكنتُ على إساءته مُقيتا
(Many a one with rancour, from whom I withheld affection, though I was able, despite his wrongdoing.)
i.e. able (muqtadir), and from it:
162 - 8- ليت شِعْري وأَشْعُرَنَّ إذا ما ... قَرَّبوها منشورةً ودُعِيتُ
ألِيَ الفضلُ أم عليَّ إذا حو ... سِبْتُ؟ إني على الحسابُ مُقيتُ
(Would that I knew, and I shall know, when they bring it near unrolled and I am called: is the credit mine or against me when I am reckoned? I am able over the reckoning.)
Al-Naḥḥās said: "It is derived from «القُوت» (sustenance), which is the amount by which a person's body is preserved from perishing"; so the origin of «مُقيت» is «مُقوِت», like «مقيم».

semin-durr:86-86.t:
«التحية» in origin is kingship (mulk). He said:
126 - 9- أَؤمُّ بها أبا قابوسَ حتى ... أُنيخَ على تَحِيَّته بجُندي
(I head with it toward Abū Qābūs until I make my troops kneel at his greeting/kingship.)
And another said:
163 - 0- ولكل ما نال الفتى ... قد نلتُه إلا التحِيَّهْ
(Everything the young man has attained, I have attained, except the taḥiyya.)
It is said: «التحية» is survival and kingship, and from it is «التحيات لله»; then it was used for the greeting (salām) figuratively. Its pattern is tafʿila, and the original is «تَحْيِيَة», so it was assimilated; this assimilation is obligatory, contrary to al-Māzinī; and the origin of the origin is «تَحْيِيٌّ», because it is the maṣdar of «حَيّا», and «حَيّا» is faʿʿala, and the maṣdar of faʿʿala is on the pattern tafʿīl, unless its lām is weak, as in «زكَّى» and «غَطَّى» [in which one of the two yāʾs is dropped] and the tāʾ of the feminine is given in exchange for it, so one says «تزكية» and «تغطية», except what is anomalous in the saying:
163 - 1- باتَتْ تُنَزِّي دلوَها تَنْزِيَّاً ... كما تُنَزِّي شَهْلَةٌ صبيَّاً
(She spent the night making her bucket leap, a leaping, as an old woman makes a boy leap.)
However, this anomaly is not permissible in the like of «حَيّا», because its ʿayn and lām are both weak with yāʾ; and some have joined what has hamza as its lām to the weak-lām verbs, such as «نَبّأ تنبئة» and «خَبّأ تخبئة». Similar to it: «أَعْيِيَة» and «أَعِيَّة», plural of «عَيِيٌّ». Al-Rāghib said: "The origin of «التحيَّة» is from life (ḥayāh); then every supplication was made a taḥiyya because all of it does not go beyond the attainment of life or a cause of life. The origin of the taḥiyya is that you say «حَيَّاك الله», then in the usage of the Sharia it came to be used for a specific supplication."
And His saying the Exalted: {أَوْ رُدُّوهَآ}, i.e. return the like of it, because returning its very self is impossible, so the muḍāf is omitted, like {وَسْئَلِ القرية} [Yūsuf: 82]. The origin of «حَيُّوا» is «حَيِّيُوا»; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was found heavy, so the ḍamma was dropped and two sākin letters met, the yāʾ and the wāw, so the yāʾ was dropped and what precedes the wāw was given ḍamma. And His saying «بأحسنَ» means with a greeting better than that first greeting.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَن لَّمْ}: «مَنْ» is conditional, which is the apparent sense, and it may be a relative noun (mawṣūla). His saying «فممَّا ملكت» is either the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) or the khabar (predicate) of the relative noun, and the conditions for the entry of the fāʾ into the khabar are present. And «منكم» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يستطِعْ».

For the accusative of «طَوْلاً» there are three analyses. The clearest is that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «يستطع». On this, regarding «أن ينكحَ» there are three views. The first view: that it is in the position of the accusative by «طَوْلاً», as an object of the tanwīn-bearing maṣdar (verbal noun), because it is the maṣdar of «طُلْت الشيء», that is, "I attained it", and the implied meaning is: "and whoever cannot attain marriage to the muḥṣanāt." Similar is the saying of al-Farazdaq:

1573 - إن الفرزدق صخرةٌ ملمومَةٌ ... طالَتْ فليسَ ينالها الأوعالا
(Al-Farazdaq is a compact rock; it towered, so the mountain goats cannot reach it.)

that is: it towered over the mountain goats so they could not reach it. The operation of a tanwīn-bearing maṣdar is frequent. He said:

1574 - بضربٍ بالسيوف رؤوسَ قومٍ ... أَزَلْنا هامَهُنَّ عن المَقيل
(By striking with swords the heads of a people, we removed their skulls from their resting place.)

and the saying of Allah the Exalted: {أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً ذَا} [al-Balad: 14-15]. This view was held by al-Fārisī.

The second view: that «أَنْ ينكحَ» is a badal (substitute) from «طَوْلاً», a badal of the thing for the thing, because «الطَّوْل» is capability or surplus, and marriage is a capability and a surplus.

The third view: that it is on the omission of the preposition; then these differed: some of them implied «إلى», that is: "means to marry"; some of them implied the lām, that is: «لأنْ ينكِحَ». On these two assumptions the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of a description of «طَوْلاً», so it is attached to an omitted element; then, when the preposition is omitted, the famous disagreement arises about the position of «أَنْ»: is it accusative or genitive? It was also said that the implied lām with «أنْ» is the lām of the mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), that is: "means for the sake of marrying them."

The second analysis of the accusative of «طولاً»: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi on the omission of a muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct), that is: "and whoever among you cannot, for lack of means for marrying the muḥṣanāt"; on this «أن ينكح» is the object of «يستطع», that is: "whoever cannot marry the muḥṣanāt for lack of means."

The third analysis: that it is accusative as a maṣdar. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is sound that «طَوْلاً» is accusative as a maṣdar, the governor in it being the istiṭāʿa (ability), because the two are the same in meaning, and «أن ينكح» on this is the object of the ability or of the maṣdar." He means that «الطَّوْل» is ability in meaning, as if it were said: "whoever among you cannot do so with an ability."

His saying: «فممَّا»: the fāʾ has already been discussed: either the apodosis or redundant in the khabar, according to the two views on «مَنْ». In this verse there are seven analyses. One: that it is attached to a verb implied after the fāʾ, the implied form being: «فلينكحْ مِمَّا مَلَكَتْه أيمانكم» ("let him marry from what your right hands possess"), and «ما» on this is relative, meaning "that which", that is: "the kind which they possess", and the object of that implied verb is omitted, the implied form being: "let him marry a woman, or a slave girl, from what your right hands possess"; so «مما» is in reality attached to an omitted element, because it is a description of that omitted object; and «مِنْ» is partitive, like «أكلت من الرغيف» ("I ate of the loaf"); and «من فتياتكم» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the implied pronoun in «مَلَكَتْ» which refers to the relative «ما»; and «المؤمناتِ» is a description of «فتياتِكم».

Two: that «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) and «ما» is the object of that implied verb, that is: «فلينكح ما ملكَتْه أَيْمانكم». Three: that «مِنْ» in «من فتياتكم» is redundant and «فتياتِكم» is the object of that implied verb, that is: «فلينكح فتياتِكم», and «مِمَّا ملكت» is attached to the verb itself, with «من» for the beginning of the extent, or to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «فتياتكم» put before it, with «مِنْ» partitive. Four: that the object of «فلينكح» is «المؤمنات», that is: "let him marry the believing girls", and «مِمَّا ملكت» as in the analysis before it, and «من فتياتكم» a ḥāl from that omitted returning pronoun. Five: that «مما» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being: «فالمنكوحة مما ملكت» ("the woman to be married is from what ... possess"). Six: that «ما» in «ممَّا» is maṣdarī, that is: «فلينكح مِنْ مِلْك أيمانكم» ("let him marry from the ownership of your right hands"); and this maṣdar must stand in the position of the object, like {هذا خَلْقُ الله} [Luqmān: 11], so that marriage may validly apply to it. Seven, and it is the strangest of them, reported from a group among them Ibn Jarīr: "that in the verse there is an advancing and deferring, and that the implied meaning is: whoever among you cannot afford to marry the believing muḥṣanāt, let some of you marry from others the girls", so «بعضُكم» is the agent of that implied verb, and on this His saying {والله أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمَانِكُمْ} is parenthetical between that implied verb and its agent. The like of this should not be said.

His saying: {والله أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمَانِكُمْ}: a clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar, brought after His saying {مِّن فَتَيَاتِكُمُ المؤمنات} to convey that outward faith is sufficient in marrying a believing slave girl outwardly, and that it is not a condition for that to know her faith with certain knowledge, since none is aware of that except Allah the Exalted; in it too is a reassurance about marrying slave girls, for they used to shrink from that.

His saying: {بَعْضُكُمْ مِّن بَعْضٍ}: also mubtadaʾ and khabar; this clause was likewise brought as reassurance regarding marriage with slave girls, as was said above, and the meaning is: some of you are of the same kind as others in lineage and religion, so the free man should not hold himself above marrying a slave girl when there is need for it. How fine is the saying of the Commander of the Believers ʿAlī: "People, in respect of likeness, are equals: their father is Adam and their mother Eve."

His saying: {بِإِذْنِ أَهْلِهِنَّ}: attached to «انكحوهن»; some implied an omitted muḍāf, that is "with the permission of those with authority over them", and those with authority over their marriage are the owners.

And «بالمعروف» has three analyses. One: that it is attached to «آتوهُنَّ», that is: "give them their dowers in kindness." / Two: that it is a ḥāl from «أجورهن», that is: "accompanied by kindness", meaning not delayed. Three: that it is attached to His saying «فانكِحوهن», that is: "marry them in kindness, with the permission of their people, with a dower like that of their equals and with witnesses to it", and this is what is customary. It was also said: there is an omission in the speech, the implied form being: «وآتوهُنَّ أجورهن بإذن أهلهن», so he omitted from the second because the first indicates it, like {والذاكرين الله كَثِيراً والذاكرات} [al-Aḥzāb: 35], that is: "the women who remember Allah". It was also said: there is an implied muḍāf, that is: "and give their masters their dowers", because nothing of the dower is handed to the slave girl.

His saying: {مُحْصَنَاتٍ غَيْرَ مُسَافِحَاتٍ}: two ḥāls from the object of «فآتوهن», and «محصنات» on this means married women. It was also said: «محصنات» is a ḥāl from the object of «فانكحوهن», and on this «محصنات» means chaste or Muslim women, and the meaning is: "marry them in the state of their being chaste, not in the state of their fornicating and taking lovers." It has been given earlier that «محصنات» is read with kasra and with fatḥa on the ṣād, what it means, and that «غيرَ مسافحين» is a confirming ḥāl.

{وَلاَ مُتَّخِذَاتِ}: conjoined to the ḥāl before it. «الأخْدان» is the object of «متخذات» because it is an active participle; «أخدان» is the plural of «خِدْن», like «عِدل» and «أَعْدال»; the khidn is the companion. It has been given that the open fornicator (musāfiḥ) is the one who is public about fornication and the one who takes lovers (mutakhidh al-akhdān) is the one who is secretive about it, and likewise among women; fornication in the Jāhiliyya was divided into these two kinds.

His saying: {فَإِذَآ أُحْصِنَّ}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read «أُحْصِنَّ» with ḍamma on the hamza and kasra on the ṣād, as a passive; the rest read it with fatḥa on both, as an active. The meaning of the first: "when they are protected by marriage", so the one who protects them is the husband; the meaning of the second: "when they protect their private parts or their husbands", and that is clear from what preceded.

The fāʾ in «فإنْ» is the apodosis of «إذا», and the fāʾ in «فعليهن» is the apodosis of «إنْ»; so the second condition and its apodosis are ordered upon the existence of the first. A parallel is: «إن أكلت فإنْ ضربت عمراً فأنت حر» ("If you eat, then if you strike ʿAmr, you are free"); he is not freed until he first eats and then second strikes ʿAmr. If you dropped the fāʾ entering «إن» in a structure like this the ruling would be reversed, and he would have to strike first and eat second. This is known from the rules of grammar, namely that the second condition is made a ḥāl, so it is necessary to be engaged in it first.

His saying: {مِنَ العذاب}: attached to an omitted element, because it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما», which is «على»; so the governor of it is a semantic one, and in reality it is what this preposition and its genitive noun are attached to. It cannot be a ḥāl from «ما» which is genitive by the annexation of «نصف» to it, because the ḥāl must be operated upon by what operates upon its owner, and «نصفُ» is the governor of its owner, in the genitive by annexation, but it does not operate on the ḥāl because it is not one of the operating nouns; except that some hold that when it is a part of the muḍāf ilayhi (the annexed term) that is permissible in it, and the half is a part, so that is permitted.

His saying: {ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ}: «ذلك» is the mubtadaʾ, and «لِمَنْ خشي» is a preposition and its genitive noun, its khabar; what «ذلك» points to is marrying a believing slave girl for one who lacks the means. «العَنَتْ» in origin is the breaking of a bone after it has set, then it was borrowed for every hardship; what is meant here is the punishment that fornication leads to, worldly and of the Hereafter. «منكم» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «خَشِي», that is: "while he is one of you". It is also possible that «مِنْ» is explicative.

His saying: {وَأَن تَصْبِرُواْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ}: mubtadaʾ and khabar, by interpreting it as a maṣdar, and it is like His saying {وَأَن تعفوا أَقْرَبُ للتقوى} [al-Baqara: 237].

semin-durr:87-87.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ}: the answer to an omitted oath. About the clause of this oath together with its answer there are three possibilities. The first: it is in the position of the nominative as a second khabar for His saying «اللَّهُ», with «لا إلهَ إلا هو» being the first khabar clause. The second: it is also a khabar for His saying «الله», and «لا إله إلا هو» is a parenthetical clause between the mubtadaʾ and its khabar. The third: it is resumptive, with no grammatical position. The i'rab of {الله لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ} [verse 255] and {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ} [verse 3] has already been given in al-Baqara.
His saying: {إلى يَوْمِ القيامة}: it has three possibilities. The first: that it is in its normal sense, of the end of a limit. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "and the gathering would be in the graves, or «ليجمعنَّكم» is made to include the meaning of «ليحشرنَّكم» (He will assemble you), so it is made transitive with «إلى»", meaning that if "gathering" is made to include the meaning of "assembling" there is no need to imply "gathered in". Abū al-Baqāʾ said — after allowing that it may mean «في» — "It was said: it is in its normal sense, i.e. He will gather you in the graves; on this basis it may be an object (mafʿūl bihi) and it may be a ḥāl, i.e. He will gather you, arriving at the reckoning of the Day of Resurrection." By his saying "an object" he means that it is an optional complement (faḍla) like other optional complements, as in «سرت إلى الكوفة»; but that is only correct if "gathering" is made to include the meaning of "assembling", as was stated; as for his implying the ḥāl as «مُفَضِين» ("arriving"), it is not permissible, because it is a restrictive "being". The second: it has the meaning of «في», i.e. "on the Day of Resurrection", and its like is the saying of al-Nābigha:
163 - 2- فلا تَتْرُكَنِّي بالوعيدِ كأنني ... إلى الناسِ مَطْلِيُّ به القارُ أَجْرَبُ
(So do not leave me with threats, as though I were, among the people, a mangy camel smeared with tar.)
i.e. «في الناس». The third: it has the meaning of «مع» ("with"), and its meaning is not clear. «القيامة» has the meaning of «القِيام» (standing), like «الطَّلابة» and «الطِّلاب»; they said that the tāʾ entered it for intensification, like «عَلاَّمة» and «نَسَّابة», because of the severity of the terror that occurs in it, and it was so named because people stand in it for the reckoning; He the Exalted said: {يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الناس لِرَبِّ العالمين} [al-Muṭaffifīn: 6]. About the clause «لا ريب فيه» there are two possibilities. The first: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from «يوم», so the pronoun in «فيه» refers to it. The second: it is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar indicated by «ليجمعنَّكم», i.e. "a gathering about which there is no doubt", and the pronoun refers to it; the first is more apparent. «ومَنْ أصْدَقُ»: the like of this clause was given earlier. And «حديثاً» is accusative as a tamyīz. The majority read «أَصْدَقُ» with a pure ṣād, while Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read it with an admixture of zāy (ishmām); and so for every sākin ṣād followed by a dāl, as in «تَصْدُقون» and «تَصْدِيَةً»; and this is as Ḥamza did in {الصراط} [al-Fātiḥa: 6] and {بِمُصَيْطِرٍ} [al-Ghāshiya: 22], for homogeneity, aiming at lightness.

semin-durr:88-88.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَمَا لَكُمْ}: mubtadaʾ and khabar. And «في المنافقين» has three possibilities. The first: it is attached to what the khabar «لكم» is attached to, i.e. "what thing is there for you — or established for you — concerning the affair of the hypocrites?". The second: it is attached to the meaning of «فئتين» (two parties), for it is equivalent to "What is the matter with you that you are divided over the affairs of the hypocrites?", so the muḍāf is omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place. The third: it is attached to an omitted word as a ḥāl from «فئتين», because in origin it is an adjective of it, the implied form being "two parties divided concerning the hypocrites", and the adjective of an indefinite noun, when put before it, becomes accusative as a ḥāl.
About «فئتين» there are two possibilities. The first: it is a ḥāl from the kāf and mīm in «لكم», and its governor is the being-established to which «لكم» is attached, and similar to it is {فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ التذكرة مُعْرِضِينَ} [al-Muddaththir: 49]; and it has been stated that this ḥāl is necessary, because the sentence is not complete without it, and this is the view of the Basrans for everything that occurs in this construction. The second — the view of the Kufans — is that it is accusative as the khabar of an implied «كان», the implied form being: "What is the matter with you concerning the hypocrites that you were two parties?", and they allowed «ما لك الشاتمَ», i.e. "what is the matter with you that you were the one who reviles"; the Basrans do not allow that, because it is a ḥāl and a ḥāl is not made definite, and the necessity of its coming indefinite in this construction shows that it is a ḥāl; and this is as they said of «ضربي زيداً قائماً», that «قائماً» may not be accusative as the khabar of an implied «كان» but as a ḥāl because of the necessity of its being indefinite. The derivation of «الفئة» was given earlier in al-Baqara.
His saying: {والله أَرْكَسَهُمْ}: mubtadaʾ and khabar, and it has two possibilities, the more apparent of which is that it is a ḥāl, either from «المنافقين» — which is the apparent sense — or from those addressed, the link being the wāw, as if He reproached them for their disagreement over these people, while the circumstance is that Allah has turned them back to disbelief. The second: it is resumptive; He the Exalted informed about them thus. And «بما كَسَبوا» is attached to «أَرْكَسهم» and the bāʾ is causal, i.e. "because of what they earned", and «ما» is a maṣdar particle or means «الذي», the returning pronoun being omitted on the second view, not [on] the first, on the sound opinion.
«الإركاس» is turning back and returning, and from it is «الرِّكْس» for dung; he, peace be upon him, said of the dung when it was brought to him: "It is a rikṣ"; and Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt said:
163 - 3- فَأُرْكِسوا في جحيم النار إنَّهمُ ... كانوا عصاةً وقالو الإفْكَ والزورا
(So they were cast back into the blaze of the Fire, for they were disobedient and spoke falsehood and lies.)
i.e. they were turned back. Al-Rāghib said: "«الرِّكْس» and «النِّكْس» mean base; but «الرِّكْس» is stronger, because «النِّكَس» is that whose top has been made its bottom, and «الرِّكس» is that which has become excrement after having been food. It was said: «أَرْكسه» means He destroyed him. He said:
163 - 4- بشُؤْمِك أَرْكَسْتَني في الخَنا ... وأَرْمَيْتَني بضروبِ العَنا
(By your ill omen you cast me back into obscenity and hurled upon me kinds of hardship.)
And it was said: «الإركاس» is leading astray, and from it:
136 - 5- وأَرْكَسْتَنِي عن طريق الهدى ... وصَيَّرْتَنِي مَثَلاً للعِدى
(You turned me back from the path of guidance and made me an example for the enemies.)
And it was said: it is turning upside down, and from it:
163 - 6- رُكِّسوا في فتنةٍ مظلمةٍ ... كسوادِ الليلِ يَتْلُوها فِتَنْ
(They were turned head-down into a dark trial, like the blackness of night, followed by trials.)
One says «أَرْكس» and «رَكَّس» with shadda and «رَكَس» without: three dialectal forms with one meaning, and «ارتكس» is the intransitive, i.e. he went back." ʿAbd Allāh read «ركَسَهم» in the triliteral form, and «رَكَّسهم» and «رُكِّسوا» were read with shadda in both. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "There is another form in it, «رَكَسه الله», without hamza and without shadda, and I do not know anyone who read it." I say: it was stated earlier that ʿAbd Allāh read «والله ركسهم» without hamza or shadda, and Abū al-Baqāʾ's statement is saving, for he only claimed lack of knowledge that it is a reading, not the absence of any reading of it. Al-Rāghib said: "except that «أركسه» is stronger than «رَكَسه», as «أَسْفَله» is stronger than «سُفْلَه»", and there is a consideration in this.

semin-durr:89-89.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لَوْ تَكْفُرُونَ}: two possibilities are permitted for «لو». The first: that it is a maṣdar particle. The second: that it is in its normal sense, being a particle for "what would have occurred because of the occurrence of something else". On the first, it is interpreted with what follows it as a maṣdar, and that maṣdar is in the position of the object of «وَدُّوا», and in that case it has no apodosis; the implied form is: "they wished your disbelief". On the second, the object of «وَدَّ» is omitted, and the apodosis of «لو» is also omitted, since the meaning indicates both, the implied form being: "they wished your disbelief — if you disbelieved as they disbelieved, they would be pleased by that".
And «كما كفروا» is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "a disbelief like their disbelief", or a ḥāl from the pronoun of that maṣdar, as is the view of Sībawayh. And «فتكونوا» is conjoined to «تكفرون», the implied form being: "they wished your disbelief, and so your being equal with them in their law". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And if it were put in the accusative as the answer to wishing, it would be permissible." The Shaykh found a flaw in this, in that the accusative in the answer to wishing, when the wishing is expressed by the wording of a verb, requires attestation from the Arabs; indeed, if it occurred, its being an answer would not be established, because «ودَّ» in the sense of wishing has as its object verbal nouns, not entities; so if the verb is put in the accusative after the fāʾ it is not determined that it is a fāʾ of answer, as it is possible that it is a case of conjoining the implied maṣdar to the overt maṣdar, which would then be of the type:
163 - 7- لَلُبْس عباءةٍ وتَقَرَّ عيني ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(To wear a cloak and for my eye to be cooled ... )
meaning that it is as though the maṣdar that is the object of «يود» is overt, and the maṣdar implied by «أن» and the verb is conjoined to it; so he made the omitted maṣdar overt in contrast to the one implied by «أن» and the verb, otherwise the omitted maṣdar is overt only by this interpretation; rather, what is transmitted is that the verb is put in the accusative in the answer to wishing when it is by a particle, such as «ليت», «لو» and «ألا» when they carry the sense of wishing. In what the Shaykh said there is a consideration, because al-Zamakhsharī did not mean by wishing the one understood from the verb of wishing (wadāda), but the one understood from the word «لو», which indicates wishing, and the accusative has occurred in its answer, as in His saying: {فَلَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةً فَنَكُونَ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 102]. I have already given the verification of this question, so what al-Zamakhsharī said is clear without hesitation. «وسواءً» is the khabar of «تكونون», and in origin it is a maṣdar standing in place of the active participle meaning "equal"; for that reason it is singular, as in «رجال عَدْلٌ».

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يُرِيدُ الله لِيُبَيِّنَ}: for a construction like this, people have several schools. The school of the Basrans: that the object of «يريد» is omitted, the implied form being: "Allah wants to forbid what He has forbidden, to permit what He has permitted, and to legislate what has preceded, for the sake of making clear to you." Some ascribed this to Sībawayh. So what the willing is attached to is something other than the clarifying and what is conjoined to it. They interpreted it thus only so as not to require the verb to be made transitive to its object, which comes after it, by means of the lām, which is impossible, nor to require implying «أَنْ» after a redundant lām.

The second school, also ascribed to some of the Basrans: that the verb before the lām be implied as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), with the preposition and its genitive noun after it as its khabar (predicate). So {يُرِيدُ الله لِيُبَيِّنَ} is implied as "Allah's willing is for the clarification", and his saying:

1575 - أريدُ لأنْسَى ذِكْرَها. . . . . . . .
(I want, so as to forget her memory ...)

that is, "my willing is ..."; and His saying, the Exalted: {وَأُمِرْنَا لِنُسْلِمَ}, that is: "we were commanded what we were commanded in order that we submit." In this view the verb is interpreted as a maṣdar without a maṣdar particle, which is weak, as in «تَسْمَعُ بالمُعَيْدَيِّ خيرٌ مِنْ تراه» ("that you hear of al-Muʿaydī is better than that you see him"). They said its implied form is «أنْ تسمعَ»; when «أن» was omitted, the verb was made nominative while being in the interpretation of a maṣdar because of the implied particle. So too here. Thus the genitive lām on the first view is in the position of the accusative, since it is attached to «يريد», and on this second view in the position of the nominative, since it occurs as a khabar.

The third: the school of the Kufans, that the lām itself governs the accusative without an implied «أَنْ», and it and what follows it are the object of the willing. The Basrans forbade this, because the lām is established as governing the genitive in nouns, so it is not permissible for it to govern the accusative. For them the accusative is by an implied «أن», as given above.

The fourth, which al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ held: that the lām is redundant (zāʾida), with «أَنْ» implied after it, and the clarifying is the object of the willing. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "{يُرِيدُ الله لِيُبَيِّنَ}: Allah wants to make clear. The lām was added to confirm the willing of clarification, as it was added in «لا أبا لك» to confirm the annexation of «father»." As you see, this lies outside the sayings of the Basrans and the Kufans, and in it «أن» is implied after a redundant lām, whereas it is not implied, in what the grammarians have stated, except after a lām which is for cause (taʿlīl) or for denial (juḥūd).

Some said: the lām here is the lām of consequence (ʿāqiba), like that in His saying {لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوّاً وَحَزَناً} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 8]. He did not mention the object of the clarifying but omitted it as known. Some implied: "to make clear to you what brings you near"; some: "that patience in refraining from marrying slave girls is better"; some: "what He detailed of the laws"; some: "the matter of your religion"; and these are close to one another.

Another good analysis is possible in the verse: that the question is of the chapter of iʿmāl (conflict of governors): «يبيِّن» and «يَهْدي» contend over {سُنَنَ الذين مِن قَبْلِكُمْ}, because each of them seeks it in meaning, and the question is of the operation of the second, with the pronoun omitted from the first, its implied form being: "to make it clear to you and to guide you to the ways of those before you." «السُّنَّة» is the path. This is supported by the fact that the exegetes reported that every ruling on prohibition and permission regarding women that He made clear to us in the preceding verses was likewise the ruling in the former nations, or that He made clear to you the benefits, because the laws, though they differ in themselves, agree in the benefit.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
Some claimed that in His saying, the Exalted: {والله يُرِيدُ أَن يَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ} there is a repetition of His saying {يَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ} which is conjoined to «ليبين». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The repetition of Allah's willing repentance for His servants is a strengthening of the first report; and the purpose in the verse is only to report the willing of those who follow desires, so Allah's willing was put first as a preface that exposes the corruption of the willing of those who follow desires." What he said holds only on the basis that the noun governed by the lām in «ليبين» is the object of the willing, not that it is a cause; and it has been given that this is the view of the Kufans and is weak, and he himself also weakened it. Once this is established we say: there is no repetition in the verse, because the attachment of willing to repentance in the first is in the sense of cause, and in the second in the sense of object, so the two things attached differ.

His saying: {وَيُرِيدُ الذين}: nominative, conjoined to «والله يريد», conjoining a verbal clause to a nominal clause; it cannot be accusative because the meaning would be corrupted, since the implied meaning would become: "Allah wants to relent, and wants to want those who ...". Al-Rāghib preferred that the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial), as a pointer that He wants repentance for you while they want you to incline away; so he differentiated between the two reports by putting the subject first in the first clause and last in the second, in order to show that the second is not by conjunction." He was answered that Allah's willing repentance is not restricted by another's willing the inclination, and that the wāw is directly followed by an affirmative imperfect verb. He brought the first clause nominal to indicate permanence, and the second verbal to indicate occurrence.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يُرِيدُ الله أَن يُخَفِّفَ}: in this clause there are two possibilities. One, which is the sounder: that it is resumptive, with no grammatical position. The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from His saying {والله يُرِيدُ أَن يَتُوبَ}, the governor in it being «يريد», that is: "Allah wants to relent toward you, wants to lighten your burden." In this analysis there is something to consider on two grounds. One: that it leads to separation between the ḥāl and its governor by a clause conjoined to the clause of the governor of the ḥāl, within the clause conjoined to; and the conjoined clause, which is «ويريد الذين يتبعون», is a clause foreign to the ḥāl and its governor. The second: that the verb that occurs as a ḥāl governs an overt noun, so the link is made by an overt noun, because «يريد» governs the name of Allah, / whereas it should have governed its pronoun; and linking by an overt noun occurs only in a clause occurring as a khabar or a ṣila (relative clause), not in one occurring as a ḥāl or a description, unless there is a report of usage for it; and this analysis would become like: «بكر يخرج يضربُ بكر خالداً» ("Bakr goes out, Bakr strikes Khālid"). The object of the lightening is not mentioned, so it is omitted; it was said its implied form is: "He lightens for you the burden of reflection and removes bewilderment"; it was also said: "the sin of what you commit."

His saying: «ضعيفاً»: there are four analyses of its accusative. The clearest: that it is a ḥāl from «الإِنسان», and it is a confirming ḥāl. Second: that it is a tamyīz (specification); they said that because «مِنْ» can enter it, and this is a mistake. Third: that it is by omission of the preposition, the original being «خُلِق من شيء ضعيف» ("created of a weak thing"), that is from despised water or a drop of fluid; then when the described noun and the preposition were omitted, the verb reached it directly and made it accusative. The fourth, to which Ibn ʿAṭiyya alluded: that it is accusative as a second object of «خلق»; they said it is sound that «خُلِق» be in the sense of «جُعِل», which gives it the power to be transitive to two objects, so that His saying «ضعيفاً» is a second object. What he mentioned is strange; we have not seen them state that «خلق» can be like «جعل» and be transitive to two, despite their enumeration of the verbs that are transitive to two; rather we have seen them say that «جعل», when in the sense of «خلق», is transitive to one.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ أَن تَكُونَ}: about this exception there are two views. One, which is the sounder: that it is a discontinuous exception (munqaṭiʿ), for two reasons. One: that trade is not included among the properties consumed wrongfully, so as to be excepted from them, whether you explain "wrongfully" as without compensation or as not by a lawful way. The second: that what is excepted is a "being", and a "being" is not property among properties. The second view: that it is continuous (muttaṣil), and the holder of this view argued that the meaning is: "do not consume them by any means except that it be trade." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is weak, because He said «بالباطل» (wrongfully), and trade is not of the kind of wrongfulness; and there is an omission of a muḍāf in the speech, its implied form being: except in the state of its being trade, or at the time of its being trade." End. So «أن تكون» is in the position of the accusative by exception, and the verification of that has already been given.

The Kufans read «تجارةً» in the accusative, on the basis that «كان» is incomplete (nāqiṣa) and its subject is latent in it, referring to the properties; a muḍāf must be omitted from «تجارة», its implied form being: "unless the properties be properties of trade". It is also possible that the pronoun is explained by the «تجارة» that comes after it, that is: "unless the trade be a trade", as in his saying:

1576 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... إذا كان يوماً ذا كواكبَ أَشْنعا
(... when it was a day with stars, most dreadful)

that is: "when the day was a day ..." Abū ʿUbayd preferred the reading of the Kufans. The rest read «تجارةٌ» in the nominative, on the basis that it is the complete (tāmma) «كان». Makkī said: "The most frequent in the speech of the Arabs is that their saying {إِلاَّ أَن تَكُونَ} in exception is without a pronoun in it, in the sense of 'occurs and takes place'." The discussion of that has already been given in al-Baqara.

And {عَن تَرَاضٍ} is attached to an omitted element, because it is a description (ṣifa) of «تجارة», so its position is nominative or accusative according to the two readings. The origin of «تراض» is «تراضِوٌ» with a wāw, because it is the maṣdar of «تراضى», the pattern tafāʿul from «رَضِي»; and «رَضِي» is of the wāw-roots, by the evidence of «الرُّضوان». The wāw, being final after a kasra, was changed to yāʾ, so you say «تراضياً». And «منكم» is a description of «تراضٍ», so it is in the position of the genitive, and «من» is for the beginning of the extent. ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, read «تُقَتِّلوا» with shadda, for intensification, and the meaning is: "let not some of you kill others."

semin-durr:90-90.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ الذين يَصِلُونَ}: there are two views on it, the more apparent of which is that it is a continuous exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), the thing excepted from being His saying {فَخُذُوهُمْ واقتلوهم}; those excepted on this view are a disbelieving people, and the meaning of "connection" (waṣla) here is connection by treaty and truce. Abū ʿUbayd said: "It is the connection of lineage", but al-Naḥḥās judged him mistaken, because lineage was established between the Prophet ﷺ and the Companions and the polytheists, and despite that it did not prevent them from fighting them. The second: that it is discontinuous (munqaṭiʿ) — the view of Abū Muslim al-Iṣfahānī and the choice of al-Rāghib. Abū Muslim said: "When Allah made emigration obligatory on everyone who embraced Islam, He excepted whoever had an excuse, saying {إِلاَّ الذين يَصِلُونَ}, and they are a people who intended emigration to the Messenger and to support him, and there was a covenant between them and the Muslims, so they stayed with them until deliverance became possible for them; and after that He excepted whoever went to the Messenger and his Companions because he fears Allah in this, and also does not fight the disbelievers because they are his relatives, or because he fears for his children who are in their hands." On this view it is a discontinuous exception, because these excepted ones did not come under His saying: {فَمَا لَكُمْ فِي المنافقين فِئَتَيْنِ}, and those excepted on this view are believers.
And {بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِّيثَاقٌ} may be a clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the genitive as an adjective of «قوم»; and it may be that «بينكم» alone is an adjective of «قوم», so that it is in the position of the genitive and is attached to an omitted word, with «ميثاق» on this view nominative as an agent, because the adverbial relies on a qualified noun; and this possibility is nearer, because describing with a single word is the basis for describing with a clause.
His saying: {أَوْ جَآءُوكُمْ}: it has two possibilities, the more apparent of which is that it is conjoined to the ṣila, as if it were said: "or except those who came to you, their breasts constrained", so the excepted are two classes of people: one reaching a people under covenant, and the other one who came neither fighting the Muslims nor his own people. The second: it is conjoined to the adjective of «قوم», which is His saying {بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِّيثَاقٌ}, so the excepted is one class that differs according to whom they reach, whether a covenanter or a disbeliever.
