Al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya chose the first. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The right view is conjunction onto the ṣila because of His saying {فَإِنِ اعتزلوكم فَلَمْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ} after His saying: {فَخُذُوهُمْ واقتلوهم}, so He established that their holding back from fighting is one of the two causes of their deserving non-interference with them and leaving them alone. If you say: each of the two connections has an effect on the validity of the exception — deserving non-interference — namely the connection with the covenanters and the connection with those holding back; why did you not allow the conjunction to be on the adjective of «قوم», with His saying {فَإِنِ اعتزلوكم} being an affirmation of the ruling of their connection to those holding back and their mixing with them and their following their ways? I say: it is permissible, but the first is more apparent and more in keeping with the style of the speech." End of quotation.
It is more apparent for two reasons, one from the standpoint of grammatical craft and the other from the standpoint of meaning. As for the first: its conjunction onto the ṣila is because the relation in it is predicative (isnādiyya); that is, the excepted is spoken about and judged to have a ruling opposite to that of what is excepted from; so if you take the conjunction to be onto the ṣila, it is spoken of by what you conjoined, unlike when you conjoin it to the adjective, for then it is a restriction on «قوم», who are a restriction in the ṣila about whose possessor something is said; and whenever the matter revolves between the relation being predicative and its being restrictive, making it predicative is preferable, for its independence.
The second, from the standpoint of meaning: conjunction onto the ṣila leads to the cause of not interfering with them being their leaving off fighting and holding back from it, and this is a near cause; while conjunction onto the adjective leads to the cause of not interfering with them being their reaching a people who hold back from fighting, and this is a distant cause; and when the matter revolves between a near cause and a distant one, considering the near is preferable.
The majority affirm «أو», while in the codex of Ubayy it is «جاؤوكم» without «أو», and al-Zamakhsharī analysed it in one of four ways: either as an explication (bayān) of «يَصِلون», or a substitute (badal) for it, or an adjective of «قوم» after an adjective, or as resumptive.
The Shaykh said: "These are possible, and in some of them there is weakness, namely the explication and the substitute, because explication does not occur with verbs, and because the substitute is not feasible since it is not it, nor part of it, nor inclusive of it." End of quotation. The reply to him needs reflection and consideration.
His saying: {حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ}: it has seven possibilities. The first: this clause has no position; rather, a supplication against them is brought, that their breasts be constrained from fighting, and this is reported from al-Mubarrad, except that al-Fārisī rejected it, arguing that we are commanded to supplicate against the disbelievers that enmity be cast among them, so we say "O Allah, cast enmity among the disbelievers"; but His saying {أَوْ يُقَاتِلُواْ قَوْمَهُمْ} would then be a negation of what the Muslims' supplication against them required. Some people replied to this rejection, so Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The statement of al-Mubarrad is explained as follows: the supplication against them that they not fight the Muslims is a declaration of their incapacity, and the supplication against them that they not fight their own people is a belittling of them, i.e. they are of less account and more insignificant and dispensable, as you say, when you want this meaning: «لا جعل الله فلاناً عليَّ ولا معي» ('May Allah not make so-and-so against me nor with me'), the meaning being: I can do without him and stand without him." Another replied that it may be a request for their death, on the grounds that His saying «قومهم» may be used to express those who are not of them but rather their enemies.
The second: «حَصَرِت» is a ḥāl from the agent of «جاؤوكم», and when the ḥāl is a past verb there is disagreement: does it need to be accompanied by «قد» or not? The preponderant opinion is that it does not need it, because of how often it occurs, and on this basis «قد» is not implied before «حَصِرَتْ», while whoever stipulates that implies it here. The third: «حَصِرَتْ» is an adjective of an omitted ḥāl, the implied form being: "or they came to you as a people whose breasts are constrained".
Abū al-Baqāʾ called it a "preparatory ḥāl" (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa), and this possibility is also ascribed to al-Mubarrad. The fourth: that it is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of «قوم» after an adjective, with «أو جاؤوكم» parenthetical. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The reading of whoever dropped «أو» — namely Ubayy — indicates it", so the Shaykh reported from him; but what I saw in his i'rab is the dropping of «أو جاؤوكم» altogether, and this is his text. He said: "One is: it is genitive as an adjective of «قوم», and what is between them is also an adjective, and «جاؤوكم» is parenthetical; and some of the Companions read «بينكم وبينهم ميثاق حصرت صدورهم», omitting «أو جاؤوكم»." This is his text, and it fits this possibility better.
The fifth: that it is a substitute from «جاؤوكم», a badal of inclusion, because coming includes constraint and other things; the Shaykh also reported it from Abū al-Baqāʾ. The sixth: that it is a khabar after a khabar, and this is the wording of al-Zajjāj, meaning that it is a resumptive clause by which He informed of the constraint of the breasts of these people from fighting after informing about them with what preceded. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, after relating al-Zajjāj's statement: "A distinction is made between a ḥāl and a resumptive khabar in your saying «جاء زيد ركب الفرسَ»: if you intend a ḥāl by «رَكب الفرس» you imply «قد», and if you intend a khabar after a khabar you do not need to imply it." The seventh: that it is the apodosis of an implied condition, the implied form being: "if they come to you, their breasts are constrained"; it is the opinion of al-Jurjānī, and there is weakness in it for lack of an indication of that.
The majority read «حَصِرَتْ» as a past verb, while al-Ḥasan, Qatāda and Yaʿqūb read «حَصِرةً» accusative as a ḥāl, on the pattern of «نَبَقَة», and this supports «حَصِرت» being a ḥāl; al-Mahdawī reported it from ʿĀṣim in the narration of Ḥafṣ, and from al-Ḥasan «حَصِراتٍ» and «حاصراتٍ» were also narrated.
These two readings admit that «حَصِراتٍ» and «حاصراتٍ» are accusative as a ḥāl, or genitive as an adjective of «قوم», because the sound feminine plural has the same genitive and accusative; but there is weakness in both, in that the adjective governing an overt noun in the nominative is, in the eloquent usage, either singular like the verb or in a broken plural, and its sound plural is rare. You say: «مررت بقومٍ ذاهب جواريهم» or «قيام جواريهم», and rarely «قائماتٍ جواريهم». «حَصِرةٌ» was also read with the nominative, as a fronted khabar, with «صدوُرهم» the mubtadaʾ, the clause also being a ḥāl. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And if «حصرةٌ» was read with the nominative, then it is as a khabar, «صدورهم» a mubtadaʾ, and the clause a ḥāl."
His saying: {أَن يُقَاتِلُونَكُمْ}: its original is «عن أَنْ»; when the preposition was dropped, the well-known disagreement arose: is it in the position of the genitive or the accusative? «الحَصْر» is constraint; its origin is in place, then it was extended. He said:
163 - 8- ولقد تَسَقَّطَني الوشاة فصادَفُوا ... حَصِراً بسِرِّكِ يا أُميمُ ضَنِيناً
(The slanderers tried to trip me up and found me constrained about your secret, O Umayma, and miserly with it.)
And His saying: {فَلَقَاتَلُوكُمْ}: the lām is the apodosis of «لو» because it is conjoined to the apodosis, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is the lām of correspondence and pairing, standing in the place of the first; had the first not been there, you would say «لقاتلوكم»", which is a strange designation, and Makkī preceded him in it. The majority read «فَلَقاتلوكم» from the mufāʿala form. Mujāhid and a group read «فَلقتلوكم» in the triliteral form, and al-Ḥasan and al-Jaḥdarī read «فلقتَّلوكم» with shadda. Al-Jaḥdarī read «السَّلْم» with fatḥa on the sīn and sukūn on the lām, and al-Ḥasan with kasra and sukūn on the lām. His saying: {لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ سَبِيلاً}: «لكم» is attached to «جَعَل», «سبيلاً» is the object of «جَعَل», and «عليهم» is a ḥāl from «سبيلاً» because in origin it is an adjective of an indefinite noun that has been put before it; and «جعل» may mean «صَيَّر» (to make), in which case «سبيلاً» is the first object and «عليهم» the second object, fronted.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَن يَفْعَلْ}: «مَنْ» is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is «فسوف»; the fāʾ here is obligatory because the apodosis is not fit to serve as a condition's answer by itself. «ذلك» points to the killing of selves. «عدواناً وظلماً» are two ḥāls (circumstantial), that is: "transgressing, wronging", or objects of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi), and the conditions for the accusative are fulfilled. «عِدواناً» was also read with kasra on the ʿayn.

The majority read «نُصْليه» from «أصلى», the nūn being for magnification. Al-Aʿmash read «نُصَلِّيه» with shadda. «نَصليه» was also read with fatḥa on the nūn, from «صَلَيْتُه النار» ("I roasted him in the fire"), from which comes «شاة مَصْلِيَّة» ("a roasted sheep"). And «يَصْليه» with the yāʾ of the third person. For the agent there are two possibilities: one, that it is the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted; the second, that it is a pronoun referring to what «ذلك» points to, the killing, because it is a cause of that. He made «ناراً» indefinite for magnification.

semin-durr:31-31.t:
Ibn Jubayr and Ibn Masʿūd read {كبير} in the singular, and what is meant by it is disbelief. Al-Mufaḍḍal read «يُكَفِّرْ» and «يُدْخِلْكم» with the yāʾ of the third person, for Allah the Exalted. And Ibn ʿAbbās read «مِنْ سيئاتكم» with the addition of «من».

Nāfiʿ alone read «مَدْخَلاً», here and in al-Ḥajj, with fatḥa on the mīm, and the rest read it with ḍamma; they did not differ about the ḍamma in the one in al-Isrāʾ. As for the one with ḍamma on the mīm, it admits two analyses. One: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it has been established that the maṣdar-noun (ism al-maṣdar) of a quadriliteral verb and above is like the passive participle; the thing entered is omitted on this, that is: "and He will admit you to Paradise with an admission." The second: that it is a noun of place of entry, and then there are two possibilities for its accusative: one, that it is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), which is the school of Sībawayh; the second, that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), which is the school of al-Akhfash. So it is with every specified place after «دخل», in which these two schools exist. This reading is clear, because the maṣdar-noun and the noun of place follow their verbs.

As for Nāfiʿ's reading, it needs an interpretation, because the one with fatḥa on the mīm comes only from the triliteral, whereas the preceding verb, as you see, is quadriliteral. So it was said that it is accusative by an implied verb which is a mutual counterpart (muṭāwiʿ) of this verb, the implied form being: «يُدْخلكم فتدخلون مَدْخلاً», and «مَدْخلاً» is accusative as given above: either as a maṣdar or as a place, in its two forms.

It was also said: it is a maṣdar with the augment letters dropped, like {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17], on one of the two views.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
And «ما» in His saying, the Exalted: {مَا فَضَّلَ الله} is a relative noun (mawṣūla) or an indefinite noun with a description, and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is the hāʾ in «به». «بعضَكم» is the object of «فَضَّل», and «على بعض» is attached to it.

His saying: {واسألوا}: the majority keep the hamza in the imperative of «السؤال» directed to the addressee when a wāw or fāʾ precedes it, as in {فَاسْأَلِ الذين} [Yūnus: 94] and {واسألوا الله مِن فَضْلِهِ} [al-Nisāʾ: 32]. Ibn Kathīr and al-Kisāʾī transfer the vowel of the hamza to the sīn, for lightness, because of the frequency of its use. If neither a wāw nor a fāʾ precedes it, all of them transfer, as in {سَلْ بني إِسْرَائِيلَ} [al-Baqara: 211]; and if it is for a third person, all of them keep the hamza, as in {وَلْيَسْأَلُواْ مَآ أَنفَقُواْ} [al-Mumtaḥana: 10]. Ibn ʿAṭiyya erred in reporting the agreement of the readers on the hamza in such as {وَاسْأَلُواْ مَآ أَنفَقْتُمْ} [al-Mumtaḥana: 10]; their agreement is not on this but on {وَلْيَسْأَلُواْ مَآ أَنفَقُواْ}, as given above. Easing the hamza is the dialect of the Hijaz, and it is possible that it is from the dialect of those who say «سال يسال» with a pure alif; the verification of that was given in al-Baqara at «سَلْ بني إسرائيل», so refer to it. This applies only to «سل» and «فسل»; as for «وسَلوا» it does not apply there, because it should have been said «سالوا» like «خافوا»; but it may be said that the omission became fixed because of frequent circulation.

It is transitive to two objects; the Majestic Name is the first object, and for the second there are two views. One: that it is omitted; Ibn ʿAṭiyya implied «أمانيَّكم» ("your wishes"), and others implied "something of His bounty", omitting the described noun and keeping its description, like «أطعمته من اللحم» ("I fed him of the meat"), that is: something of it, with «مِنْ» partitive. The second: that «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), and the implied meaning is: {واسألوا الله مِن فَضْلِهِ} (ask Allah His bounty). This holds only on the opinion of al-Akhfash, for the absence of the two conditions, namely the indefiniteness of the genitive noun and the speech being non-affirmative.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنَا}: it has six analyses, and that calls for an introduction before it, namely that «كل» must have something annexed to it. They differed over its implied form: it was said to be «ولكلِّ إنسانٍ» (for every person), it was said "for every property", and it was said "for every people". If the implied form is «لكلِّ إنسان», then there are three analyses.

One: «ولكلِّ إنسانٍ موروثٍ جعلنا مواليَ», that is: "and for every person who is inherited from we have made heirs from what he left"; so in «ترك» there is a pronoun returning to «كل», and the speech is complete here, and «مِمَّا ترك» is attached to «مواليَ» because of the meaning of inheritance in it, or to an implied verb, that is: "they inherit from what ...". «مواليَ» is the first object of «جعل» in the sense of "made into", and «لكل» is a preposition and its genitive noun that are the second object, put before its governor; and «الوالدان» is nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or by an implied verb, that is: "they inherit from what ...", as if it were said: "and who is the heir?", and it was said: "they are the parents and the near kin." The original is: "and We have made for every deceased person heirs who inherit from what he left: they are the parents and the near kin."

The second: that the implied form is: «ولكلِّ إنسانٍ موروثٍ جَعَلنا وُرَّاثاً مما ترك ذلك الإنسان» ("and for every person who is inherited from We have made heirs from what that person left"); then He explained the person annexed to «كل» by His saying «الوالدان», as if it were said: "and who is this person who is inherited from?", and it was said: "the parents and the near kin." The analysis is as in the previous analysis. The only difference between them is that the parents in the first are heirs and in the second are those inherited from. On these two analyses the speech is two clauses, there is no omitted pronoun in «جعلنا», «موالي» is the first object and «لكل» the second object.

The third: that the implied form is: «ولكل إنسان وارثٍ مِمَّنْ تركه الوالدان والأقربون جعلنا موالي», that is "inherited from"; so by «المَوْلى» is meant the one inherited from, and «الوالدان» is nominative by «ترك», and «ما» is in the sense of «مَن», and the preposition and its genitive noun are a description of the muḍāf ilayhi (annexed term) «كل», and on this the speech is a single clause; and in this there is great remoteness.

The fourth: if the implied form is «ولكل قوم» (for every people), then the meaning is: "for every people whom We have made heirs there is a share of what their parents and near kin left." So «لكل» is a khabar put first, «نصيب» a mubtadaʾ put last, «جَعَلْناهم» a description of «قوم», the pronoun returning to them being the object of «جَعَل», and «مواليَ» either a second object or a ḥāl (circumstantial), on the basis that it means "We created"; and «مِمَّا ترك» is a description of the mubtadaʾ; then the mubtadaʾ was omitted and its description left, the muḍāf ilayhi «كل» was omitted and its description left too, and the pronoun returning to the described noun was omitted. A parallel is: «لكلِّ خلقه الله إنساناً مِنْ رزق الله» ("for everyone Allah created as a human being there is a share of Allah's provision"), that is: for everyone whom Allah created as a human being there is a share of Allah's provision.

The fifth: if the implied form is «ولكلِّ مال» (for every property), they said the meaning is: "for every property of what the parents and near kin left We have made heirs, that is, those who take charge of it and possess it." They made «لكل» attached to «جعل», «مما ترك» a description of «كل», and «الوالدان» the agent of «ترك»; so on this and on the two analyses before it, the speech is a single sentence. Though this is good, it has a separation between the description and the described noun by a clause that governs the described noun. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "It is like your saying «بكلِّ رجلٍ مررت تميميٍ», and there is something to consider in the permissibility of that." I say: no consideration is needed, because separation has been found between the described and its description by a clause governing the annexed term of the described noun, as in the saying of the Exalted: {قُلْ أَغَيْرَ الله أَتَّخِذُ وَلِيّاً فَاطِرِ السماوات} [al-Anʿām: 14], where «فاطر» is a description of «الله», and they were separated by «أتَّخِذُ», the governor of «غير»; so this is more fitting.

The sixth: that «لكلِّ مال» be a second object of «جعل», on the basis that it means "making into", and «موالي» the first object; and the analysis is as given above. This is the end of what has been said about this verse, and to Allah be praise.

His saying: {والذين عَاقَدَتْ}: for its position there are four analyses. One: that it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is His saying «فآتوهم». The second: that it is accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation) with an implied verb, and this is more preferable since a command comes after it. The third: that it is nominative, conjoined to «الوالدان والأقربون»; if it is meant that the parents are those inherited from, the pronoun in «فآتوهم» returns to «موالي», and if it is meant that they are heirs, it may return to «مواليَ» and to the parents and what is conjoined to them. The fourth: that it is accusative, conjoined to «مواليَ». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "that is: 'We made those whom ... pledged heirs', and that was so and was abrogated." The Shaykh rebutted him by the invalidity of the conjunction, saying: "since the implied meaning would become: 'for every person, or every part of property, We made heirs and those whom your right hands have pledged'." Then he said: "If it is made a conjunction of clauses and the second object is omitted since the meaning indicates it, that is possible, that is: 'We made heirs for every part of the property, or for every person, and We made those whom your right hands have pledged heirs'; and after that, there is a strain in it." End.

The Kufans read «عَقَدَتْ», and the rest «عاقَدَتْ» with alif; and the shadda in «عَقَّدت» is reported from Ḥamza. The reciprocal form (mufāʿala) is apparent here, because what is meant is alliance (muḥālafa). The object is omitted in each of the readings, that is: «عاقَدْتَهم» (you made a pact with them) or «عَقَدْتَ حِلْفهم» (you contracted their alliance); and the ascription of the pledging or contracting to the «أيمان» is figurative (majāz), whether «الأيمان» means the limb (the right hands) or the oath. It was also said that there is an omitted muḍāf, that is: «عقدت ذوو أيمانكم» ("those possessing your right hands/oaths contracted").

semin-durr:91-91.t: And the sīn in {سَتَجِدُونَ}: is for the future, in its basic sense. They said: here it is not for the future but to indicate continuity, which is not apparent. ʿAbd Allāh read «رُكِسوا» in it, in the lightened triliteral form, and Ibn Jinnī reported from him «رُكِّسُوا» with shadda.

semin-durr:92-92.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ أَن}: the like of this construction has already been given: {مَا كَانَ لَهُمْ أَن يَدْخُلُوهَآ إِلاَّ خَآئِفِينَ} [al-Baqara: 114]. And «إلا خَطَأً» has four possibilities. The first: it is a discontinuous exception, which is the view of the majority if the negation is taken in its literal meaning; and it cannot be continuous, for the meaning would become: "except by mistake, in which case he may kill him". The second: it is continuous if the negation is taken to mean prohibition, and the meaning becomes: "except by mistake, as when he knew him to be a disbeliever and killed him, and then the unseen disclosed that he was a believer". The third: it is a "freed" exception, and then in its being accusative there are three possibilities: the first, that it is an object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi), i.e. "it is not fitting for him to kill him for any reason except for mistake alone"; the second, that it is a ḥāl, i.e. "it is not fitting for him to kill him in any state except the state of mistake"; the third, that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "except a killing by mistake"; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned these possibilities. The fourth possibility: that «إلا» has the meaning of «ولا», the implied form being: "It is not for a believer to kill a believer, deliberately or by mistake"; some of the scholars mentioned it; Abū ʿUbayda related from Yūnus, who said: "I asked Ruʾba ibn al-ʿAjjāj about this verse and he said: 'He may not kill him deliberately nor by mistake'", so he put «إلا» in the place of the wāw, and it is like the saying of the poet:
1639 - وكلُّ أخٍ مفارِقُه أخوه ... لَعَمْرُ أبيك إلا الفرقدانِ
(Every brother is left by his brother — by your father's life — except the two Farqads.)
except that al-Farrāʾ rejected this view, saying that the like of that is not permissible unless another exception precedes it, so that the second is conjoined to it, as in the saying:
1640 - ما بالمدينة دارٌ غيرُ واحدةٍ ... دارُ الخليفةِ إلا دارُ مروانا
(There is no house in Medina except one — the house of the Caliph — except the house of Marwān.)
This is al-Farrāʾ's opinion; as for others, they claim that «إلا» can be a conjunction with the meaning of the wāw without condition, and the verification of this has been given at His saying: {لِئَلاَّ يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَيْكُمْ حُجَّةٌ إِلاَّ الذين} [al-Baqara: 150].
The majority read «خَطَأً» with hamza on the pattern of «نبأ»; and al-Zuhrī read «خَطَا» on the pattern of «عصا», and there are two analyses of it: one, that the lām of the word was dropped for lightness, as the lām of «دم», «يد», «أخ» and their like was dropped; the other, that he lightened the hamza by replacing it with an alif, which met the tanwīn and was dropped because of the meeting of two sākin letters, as is done with all the maqṣūr nouns. Al-Ḥasan read «خَطاءً» on the pattern of «سَماء».
His saying: {فَتَحْرِيرُ}: the fāʾ is the apodosis of the condition, or redundant in the khabar if «مَنْ» means «الذي"; and «تحريرُ» is nominative either as an agent, i.e. "emancipation is obligatory upon him", or as a mubtadaʾ with the khabar omitted, i.e. "upon him is emancipation", or the reverse, i.e. "what is obligatory is emancipation". «الدِّيَةُ» in origin is a maṣdar, then it was applied to the money taken for killing, and for that reason He said «مُسَلَّمَةٌ إلى أهله», and an act is not handed over, only things are; you say: «وَدَى يَدِي دِيةً ووَدْياً» like «وَشَى يَشِي شِيَةً», the fāʾ of the word being dropped, and its counterpart in the sound verb is the lām, as in «زِنة» and «عِدة». «إلى أهله» is attached to «مُسَلَّمة», as you say «سَلَّمت إليه كذا»; and it may be an adjective of «مُسَلَّمة», though there is weakness in this.
And «خطأ» in His saying «من قتل مؤمناً خطأ» is accusative: either as a maṣdar, i.e. "a killing by mistake", or as a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "possessing error" or "mistaken".
His saying: {إِلاَّ أَن يَصَّدَّقُواْ}: there are two views on it. The first: it is a discontinuous exception. The second: it is continuous. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: to what is «أَنْ يصَّدَّقوا» attached, and what is its position? I say: it is attached to «عليه» or to «مُسَلَّمَةٌ», as though it were said: 'the blood-money is obligatory upon him, or he hands it over, except when they give it as charity to him', and its position is the accusative as an adverbial of time, with the omission of the word for time implied, as in their saying «اجِلسْ ما دام زيد جالساً»; and it may be a ḥāl from «أهله», meaning 'except as givers of charity'." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) judged him mistaken in both these analyses. As for the first, the grammarians stated explicitly that «أَنْ» and what follows it cannot stand in the place of an adverbial of time, and that this is peculiar to the maṣdar «ما»; if you said «آتيك أن يصيحَ الديك», i.e. at the time of its crowing, it would not be permissible. As for the second, Sībawayh also explicitly forbade it; he said, about the Arabs' saying «أنت الرجل أن تنازلَ، أو أن تخاصمَ», i.e. "you are the man for dueling or disputing": "The accusative here is the accusative of the object of purpose, because the future cannot be a ḥāl." So its being discontinuous is the correct view. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It was also said: it is continuous, and the meaning is: upon him is the blood-money in every case except in the case of its being given as charity to him."
The majority read «يَصَّدَّقوا» with shadda on the ṣād, the original being «يتصدَّقوا», the tāʾ being assimilated into the ṣād. This original form was reported as a reading from Ubayy. Abū ʿAmr read, in the narration of ʿAbd al-Wārith — and it is ascribed to al-Ḥasan and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān — «تَصَدَّقوا» with the address-tāʾ, the original being «تَتصدقوا» with two tāʾs, the second being assimilated. «تَصْدُقوا» was also read, with the address-tāʾ and lightened ṣād, and it is like the previous one, except that its lightening is by dropping one of the two tāʾs — the first or the second, with disagreement about that — while the lightening of the first was by assimilation.
His saying: {فَمَن لَّمْ يَجِدْ}: its object is omitted, i.e. "whoever does not find a slave"; and it has the meaning of finding a lost thing, therefore it takes one object. And His saying: {فَصِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ}: it is nominative on one of the possibilities mentioned for His saying {فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ}, which was given earlier, i.e. "upon him is fasting", or "fasting is obligatory upon him", or "what is obligatory for him is fasting". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "In other than the Qur'an the accusative would be permissible, as «فليصم صومَ شهرين»." There is a consideration in this, because the known usage is to say «صمتُ شهرين ويومين», and they do not say «صمتُ صومَ — nor صيامَ — شهرين».
His saying: {تَوْبَةً}: it has three possibilities for being accusative. The first: it is an object of purpose (mafʿūl min ajlihi), the implied form being "He legislated that as a repentance from Him". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is not permissible for its governor to be «صوم» except by omission of a muḍāf, i.e. 'for the occurrence of repentance' or 'for the attainment of repentance'", meaning that he needed to imply that muḍāf and did not say that the governor is the fasting because one of the conditions of its being accusative is lacking, since the agent of the fasting is not the agent of the repentance. The second: it is accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. "a return from Him to ease, in that He moved you from the heavier to the lighter", or "a repentance from Him", i.e. an acceptance from Him, from «تاب عليه» when He accepted his repentance; so the implied form is: "He relented toward you with a relenting". The third: it is accusative as a ḥāl, but with the omission of a muḍāf, the implied form being: "upon him is such-and-such, while being one possessing repentance", and this is not permissible without implying this muḍāf, because if you said «فعليه صيامُ شهرين تائباً من الله» it would not be permissible. And «ومِن الله» is in the position of the accusative because it is an adjective of «توبة», and so is attached to an omitted word.

semin-durr:93-93.t: And {مُّتَعَمِّداً}: a ḥāl from the agent of «يَقتلْ». It is narrated from al-Kisāʾī with sukūn on the tāʾ, as if fleeing from the succession of vowels. And «خالداً» is accusative as a ḥāl from an omitted word, and there are two implied forms for it. The first: «يُجْزاها خالداً فيها» ("he will be recompensed with it, abiding in it"); if you wish you may make it a ḥāl from the accusative or the nominative pronoun. The second: «جازاه» ("He recompensed him"), by the evidence of «وغضب الله عليه ولعنَه», where the past is conjoined to it; on this basis it is a ḥāl from the accusative pronoun only, and it is not permissible that it be a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «جزاؤه», for two reasons: one, that it is a muḍāf ilayhi, and a ḥāl coming from a muḍāf ilayhi is weak or impossible; the other, that it leads to separating the ḥāl from its owner by a foreign element, which is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, namely «جهنم».

semin-durr:94-94.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَتَبَيَّنُواْ}: the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read it from «التثبُّت» (verifying), and the rest from «البيان» (clarity). It was said: the two are close, because whoever verifies a thing makes it clear; so said Abū ʿUbayd, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya affirmed it as sound. Al-Fārisī said: "«التثبُّت» is the opposite of rushing in, and what is meant is deliberateness, and «التثبت» is more specific to this place; His saying {وَأَشَدَّ تَثْبِيتاً} [al-Nisāʾ: 66] indicates it, i.e. 'more forceful for them than what they were admonished with, that they not rush into it'", so he chose the reading of the two brothers. A group reversed this and preferred the reading of the majority, saying: because one who verifies may not get clarity. Al-Rāghib said: "because it is rarely the case except after verification, and there may be verification without clarity; and it was contrasted with haste in his saying, peace be upon him: 'Clarity is from Allah and haste is from Satan.'" I say: this strengthens the reading of the two brothers also. And tafaʿʿala in both readings has the meaning of istafʿala, which denotes seeking, i.e. seek verification or clarity.
And His saying: {لِمَنْ ألقى}: the lām here is for conveyance, and «مَنْ» is a relative — or a separated one; «ألقى» here is past in wording but has the meaning of the future, i.e. «لمن يُلْقي», because a prohibition is not about what has occurred and passed, and the past, when it occurs as a ṣila, is suitable for the past and for the future. Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamza read «السَّلَم» with fatḥa on the sīn and the lām, without an alif, and the rest of the seven read «السلام» with an alif; it is narrated from ʿĀṣim «السِّلْم» with kasra on the sīn and sukūn on the lām. As for «السلام», the apparent sense is that it is the greeting. It was also said: submission and compliance; and «السَّلَم» — with fatḥa on both — is compliance only, and likewise {السلم} [verse 208] with kasra and sukūn. Al-Jaḥdarī read it with fatḥa and sukūn on the lām, and the discussion of it has been given in al-Baqara, so turn your attention to it. The clause of «لست مؤمناً» is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying. The majority read the second mīm of «مؤمناً» with kasra, an active participle, and Abū Jaʿfar with fatḥa, a passive participle, i.e. "we do not grant you safety concerning yourself"; this reading is narrated from ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar.
His saying {تَبْتَغُونَ}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «تقولوا», i.e. "do not say that while seeking...". His saying: «كذلك»: this is the khabar of «كان», put before it and before its subject, i.e. "before Islam you were like the one who rushed in and did not verify". And His saying {فَمَنَّ الله}: the apparent sense is that this clause is part of the completion of His saying {كذلك كُنْتُمْ مِّن قَبْلُ}, so it is conjoined to the clause before it. It was also said: rather, it is part of the completion of His saying «تبتغون»; and the first is more apparent. And His saying «فتبيِّنوا» was read like the previous one; it was said: it is a verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī) of the first, and it was said: it is not emphasis, because of the difference in what each is attached to, for the implied form of the first is "so seek clarity in the matter of the one you kill" and of the second, "so seek clarity about the favour of Allah", or "verify it"; the context indicates that, and because the basis is the absence of emphasis. The majority read «إنَّ الله» with kasra on the hamza; it was also read with fatḥa on the basis that it is governed by «تبينَّوا» or on the omission of the lām of cause, and if it was read with fatḥa along with «التثبيت» then it is on the lām of cause only. «المغانم» is the plural of «مَغْنَم», which is suitable for the maṣdar, the time and the place, and then is applied to [every] thing taken from the enemy's property in raiding, applying the maṣdar to the passive participle, as in «ضَرْب الأمير» ("the ruler's striking", i.e. what he struck/coined).

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {عَلَى النسآء}: attached to «قَوَّامون», and so is «بما»; the bāʾ is causal (sababiyya), and it may be for ḥāl (circumstantial), in which case it is attached to an omitted element, because it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «قَوَّامون», its implied form being: "deserving it by Allah's favoring them." «ما» is maṣdarī (forming a verbal noun); it was also said to be in the sense of "that which", but that is weak, because of the omission of the returning pronoun without justification. The first «بعض» means the men and the second «بعض» the women, and the verse turned away from the two pronouns, not saying "by what Allah favored them over them", because of the vagueness in «بعض». And «بما أنفقوا» is attached to what the first is attached to. «ما» here may be in the sense of "that which" without weakness, because the omission has a justification, that is: "and by what they spent of their wealth."

And {مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ} is attached to «أَنْفَقوا», or to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the omitted pronoun. His saying: {فالصالحات قَانِتَاتٌ حَافِظَاتٌ}: «الصالحات» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what follows are two khabars (predicates) of it. «للغيب» is attached to «حافظات». «أل» in «الغيب» is a substitute for the pronoun according to the Kufans, as in His saying {واشتعل الرأس شَيْباً} [Maryam: 4], that is "my head", and his saying:

1577 - لَمْياءُ في شَفَتيْها حُوَّةٌ لَعَسٌ ... وفي اللِّثاتِ وفي أَنْيابِها شَنَبُ
(Lamyāʾ, on her lips a dusky redness, and in the gums and in her eye-teeth a coolness/brightness.)

that is: "her gums".

The majority read the Majestic Name in the nominative in «حَفِظ اللهُ». About «ما» on this reading there are three analyses. One: that it is maṣdarī, and the meaning is: "by Allah's guarding them", that is by His granting them success, or by the counsel from Him, the Exalted, upon them. The second: that it is in the sense of "that which" and the returning pronoun is omitted, that is: "by that which Allah guarded for them of their husbands' dowers and the maintenance upon them"; al-Zajjāj said this. The third: that «ما» is an indefinite noun with a description, with the returning pronoun also omitted, as established for the relative in the sense of "that which".

Abū Jaʿfar read the Majestic Name in the accusative, and about «ما» there are again three analyses. One: that it is in the sense of "that which"; the second: an indefinite noun with a description, and in «حَفِظ» there is a pronoun returning to «ما», that is: "by what she guarded of righteousness and obedience". A muḍāf must be omitted, its implied form being: "by what she guarded of the religion of Allah or the command of Allah", because the sacred Essence is guarded by no one. The third: that «ما» is maṣdarī, and the meaning is: "by their guarding Allah in complying with His command"; the returning pronoun was permitted to be singular referring to the plural of females because they are in the sense of the genus, as if it were said: "of whoever is righteous", so the pronoun returned in the singular by this consideration. The scholars rejected this analysis because of the pronoun's lack of agreement with what it returns to, and this is the answer to that. Ibn Jinnī made it like the saying of the poet:

1578 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فإنَّ الحوادِثَ أودى بها
(... for misfortunes have destroyed it/them)

that is: «أَوْدَيْنَ» (they destroyed); and it should be said: the original is «بما حَفِظَتِ اللهَ», and «الحوادث أَوْدَت», because the pronoun may return to the plural of females as to a single one of them; you say «النساءُ قامت» ("the women stood" with a singular verb); except that it is irregular to drop the feminine tāʾ from the verb ascribed to a feminine pronoun.

ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd) read, and it is so in his codex, «فالصوالحُ قوانتٌ حوافظٌ» in the broken plural. Ibn Jinnī said: "It is closer to the meaning for giving the sense of multitude, which is intended here", meaning that fawāʿil is of the plurals of multitude, whereas the sound plural is a plural of paucity unless it is joined with the alif and lām. The apparent sense of Abū al-Baqāʾ's wording is that it is for paucity even if joined with «أل»; for he said: "The sound plural does not indicate multitude by its coinage, though it has been used for it, as in the saying of the Exalted {وَهُمْ فِي الغرفات آمِنُونَ} [Sabaʾ: 37]." In what Abū al-Fatḥ (Ibn Jinnī) and Abū al-Baqāʾ said there is something to consider, for «الصالحات» in the well-known reading is definite with «أل», and it has been given that it is for generality, except that the generality conveying multitude is not from the plural form but from «أل»; and once it is established that «الصالحات» is a plural of multitude, it necessarily follows that «قانتات» and «حافظات» are for multitude, because it is a predicate about all, so it conveys multitude; do you not see that when you say «الرجال قائمون» it must be that each one of the men is standing, and it is not permissible that some of them be seated? So the well-known reading is adequate for the intended meaning.

His saying: {فِي المضاجع}: two analyses. One: that «في» is in its normal sense of containing, attached to «اهجروهن», that is: "leave sleeping with them", i.e. sleeping beside them, without speaking to them or eating with them. The second: that it is for cause. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "and leave them because of the beds, as you say «في هذه الجناية عقوبة» ('for this offence there is a punishment')." Makkī made this analysis the only one and forbade the first, saying: "«في المضاجع» is not a locus for the desertion but a cause for the desertion of those who hold back, and its meaning is: leave them because of their holding back from sleeping with you." In this there is something to consider that is not hidden. Al-Wāḥidī's words suggest that it may be attached to «نشوزهن», for after relating a statement from Ibn ʿAbbās he said: "the meaning on this is: those whose recalcitrance in the beds you fear"; and the statement that he related from Ibn ʿAbbās is his saying: "All this is in the bed, when she disobeys by refusing to lie down with him." But that is not permissible, so as not to require separation between the maṣdar and its object by a foreign element. Some implied a conjoined element after His saying «واللاتي تخافون», that is: "and those whose recalcitrance you fear and who have become recalcitrant", as if he means that it is not permissible to proceed to admonition and what follows merely on fear. It was also said that there is no need for that, because fear means certainty; and it was said that predominance of conjecture suffices in that. /

His saying: {فَلاَ تَبْغُواْ عَلَيْهِنَّ سَبِيلاً}: for the accusative of «سبيلا» there are two analyses. One: that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the second: that it is by omission of the preposition. These two analyses are built on the explanation of what «البغي» is here. It was said: it is wrongdoing, from His saying {فبغى عَلَيْهِمْ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 76]; on this it is intransitive, and «سبيلاً» is accusative by omission of the preposition, that is "by a way". It was said: it is seeking, from their saying «بَغَيْتُه» ("I sought it"). About «عليهن» there are two analyses. One: that it is attached to «تبغوا». The second: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «سبيلاً», because it is originally a description of the indefinite noun, put before it.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {شِقَاقَ بَيْنِهِمَا}: two analyses. One: that «الشقاق» is annexed to «بين», which has the sense of containing (ẓarfiyya), the original being «شقاقاً بينهما», but latitude was used in it, so the event was annexed to its adverbial, its adverbial sense remaining, as in «سَرَّني مسير الليلة» ("tonight's journey pleased me"), and from this is {مَكْرُ الليل} [Sabaʾ: 33]. The second: that it has left its adverbial sense and become like the other nouns, as if what is meant by it is the association and companionship between the two spouses; Abū al-Baqāʾ leaned to this, saying: "and «البَيْن» here is the union that exists between the spouses."

And {مِنْ أَهْلِهِ}: two analyses. One: that it is attached to «ابعثوا», so it is for the beginning of the extent. The second: that it is attached to an omitted element because it is a description of the indefinite noun, that is "being of his family", so it is partitive.

His saying: {إِن يُرِيدَآ}: the two pronouns in «يُريدا» and «بينهما» may return to the two spouses, that is: "if the two spouses want reconciliation, Allah will grant success between the two spouses"; or both to the two arbiters; or the first to the two arbiters and the second to the two spouses; or the reverse. The two spouses were made latent pronouns although they have not been mentioned, because the mention of the men and women indicates them. Abū al-Baqāʾ made the pronoun in «بينهما» return to the two spouses only, whether it is said that the pronoun of «يريدا» returns to the two arbiters or the two spouses.

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وبالوالدين إِحْسَاناً}: its parallel was given in al-Baqara, except that here He said {وَبِذِي القربى} repeating the bāʾ, and that is because this is concerning this community, so the care for it is greater, and the repetition of the bāʾ indicates additional emphasis, so that suits here, unlike the verse of al-Baqara, which concerns the Children of Israel. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «إحسانٌ» in the nominative, on the basis that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate) is the preposition and its genitive noun before it; what is meant by this clause is the command to do good, although it is declarative, like His saying {فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ} [Yūsuf: 83].

His saying: {والجار ذِي القربى}: the majority read «الجار» in the genitive, and what is meant by it is the one near in kinship, and by «الجارِ الجُنُب» the one distant in kinship. From Maymūn ibn Mihrān: «والجارِ ذي القربى» "what is meant is the near neighbor." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is an error, because on his interpretation he combined «أل» and annexation, since the form of the speech would have been «وجارِ ذي القربى»." The words of Ibn Mihrān can be made sound on the basis that «ذي القربى» is a badal (substitute) from «الجار» with an omitted muḍāf, that is: «والجار جارِ ذي القربى», like his saying:

1579 - نَضَر اللهُ أعظماً دفنوها ... بسجستانَ طلحةِ الطَّلَحاتِ
(May Allah make radiant the bones they buried in Sijistān, those of Ṭalḥa of the Ṭalaḥāt.)

that is: "the bones of Ṭalḥa"; and among their sayings: «لو يعلمون: العلمُ الكبيرةِ سنةٌ» that is: "the knowledge of the elder is a sunna", so he omitted the badal because the speech indicates it.

Some read «والجارَ ذا القربى» in the accusative. Al-Zamakhsharī analyzed it as ikhtiṣāṣ (specification), like His saying {حَافِظُواْ عَلَى الصلوات والصلاة الوسطى} [al-Baqara: 238].

«الجُنُب» is a description on the pattern fuʿul, like «ناقة سُرُح»; the singular, dual and plural, masculine and feminine, are alike in it, as in «رجال جُنُب»; the Exalted said: {وَإِن كُنتُمْ جُنُباً} [al-Māʾida: 6]; some make it dual and plural, and similar is «شُلُل». From ʿĀṣim: «والجار الجَنْب» with fatḥa on the jīm and sukūn on the nūn, which is also a description, meaning "the one set aside", like their saying «رجلٌ عَدْل»; the alif of «الجار» is from a wāw, as in their saying «تجاوروا» and «جاوَرْتُه»; it is pluralized as «جِيرة» and «جيران». «الجَنابة» is distance. He said:

1580 - فلا تَحْرِمَنِّي نائلاً عن جَنابةٍ ... فإني أمرؤٌ وَسْطَ القِبابِ غريبُ
(Do not deny me a gift because of distance, for I am a man in the midst of the tents, a stranger.)

because the person is left to one side, and from this is {واجنبني وَبَنِيَّ} [Ibrāhīm: 35].

His saying: {بالجنب}: two analyses are possible for the bāʾ: one, that it is in the sense of «في»; the second, that it is in its normal sense, and that is better. On both assumptions it is attached to an omitted element because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الصاحب». And {وَمَا مَلَكَتْ}: it is possible that "other than male and female slaves" is meant by «ما», carrying it to kinds, as in {مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 3]; and it is possible that everything a person owns of animals is meant, so the rational was mixed with the non-rational and «ما» was brought.

semin-durr:95-95.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِنَ المؤمنين}: attached to an omitted word because it is a ḥāl, and as to its owner there are two possibilities. The first: it is «القاعدون», so the governor of the ḥāl in reality is «يستوي». The second: it is the latent pronoun in «القاعدون», because «أل» has the meaning of «الذي», i.e. "those who stayed behind in this state"; and «مِنْ» may also be explicative.
His saying {غَيْرُ أُوْلِي الضرر}: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim read «غير» nominative, the rest accusative, and al-Aʿmash genitive. The nominative has two aspects, the more apparent of which is that it is a badal from «القاعدون»; it is more apparent because the sentence is a negation, and the badal with a negation is preferable, for what has been established in the working of grammar. The second: it is nominative as an adjective of «القاعدون», and this has to be interpreted, because «غير» does not become definite by annexation, and it is not permissible for the adjective and the qualified noun to differ in definiteness and indefiniteness. Its interpretation is either that «القاعدين», when they were not particular people but the genus was meant, resembled an indefinite noun and so were described as an indefinite is described, or that «غير» can become definite when it occurs between two opposites; and all this is as given earlier in the i'rab of {غَيْرِ المغضوب عَلَيْهِم} [al-Fātiḥa: 7] in one of the possibilities. All of this is a departure from the established principles, and so I chose the first. Like it:
164 - 1- وإذا اُقْرِضْتَ قَرْضاً فاجْزِهِ ... إنما يَجْزي الفتى غيرُ الجَمَلْ
(When a loan is lent to you, repay it; it is only the man, not the camel, who repays.)
with «غير» nominative, as Abū ʿAlī mentioned; but the narration for others is «ليس الجمل». The accusative is on one of three possibilities. The first: the accusative as an exception from «القاعدون», which is the most apparent because it is the one spoken about. The second: from «المؤمنين», which is not clear. The third: as a ḥāl from «القاعدون». And the genitive is as an adjective of «المؤمنين», and its interpretation is as given in the nominative-as-adjective possibility.
And His saying: {فِي سَبِيلِ الله بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ}: both prepositional phrases are attached to «المجاهدون», and «المجاهدون» is conjoined to «القاعدون». His saying: {دَرَجَةً}: it has four possibilities. The first: it is accusative as a maṣdar because «درجة» stands in the place of the single instance (marra) of preferring, as though it were said "He preferred them with a preferring", like «ضربته سوطاً». The second: it is a ḥāl from «المجاهدين», i.e. "possessing a degree". The third: it is accusative as an adverbial, i.e. "in a degree and station". The fourth: it is accusative by the dropping of the preposition, i.e. "by a degree".
His saying: {وَكُلاًّ وَعَدَ الله الحسنى}: «كلاً» is the first object of «وعد», put before it, and «الحسنى» is the second object. «وكلُّ» was also read, nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the clause after it being its khabar, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "promised it"; and this is like the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir in Sūrat al-Ḥadīd {وَكُلاًّ وَعَدَ الله الحسنى} [verse 10]. His saying «أجراً»: for its being accusative there are four possibilities. The first: the accusative as a maṣdar from the meaning of the preceding verb, not from its wording, because the meaning of «فَضَّل الله» is "He rewarded".
The second: the accusative by dropping the preposition, i.e. "He preferred them with a reward". The third: the accusative as a second object, because «فضَّل» is made to include "gave", i.e. "He gave them a reward as a favour from Him". The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from «درجات». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«أجراً» is accusative as a ḥāl from the indefinite noun «درجات», put before it", and this is not apparent, because if it came after «درجات» it could not be an adjective of «درجات» for lack of agreement, since «درجات» is plural and «أجر» is singular. So one of them rejected it, but this is an oversight, for «أجراً» is a maṣdar, and the most eloquent usage in it is to make it singular and masculine in all cases.

semin-durr:96-96.t: His saying, the Exalted: {دَرَجَاتٍ}: it has six possibilities: the four mentioned for «درجة»; the fifth, that it is a badal from «أجراً»; the sixth — mentioned by Ibn ʿAṭiyya — that it is accusative by an implied verb, as an emphasis of the reward, as you say: «لك عليَّ ألفُ درهمٍ عُرْفاً», as if you had said "I acknowledge it an acknowledgement"; and there is a consideration in it. And «مغفرة ورحمة» are conjoined to «درجات», and the accusative is permissible for both through their verbs, i.e. "He forgave them a forgiveness and had mercy on them a mercy".

semin-durr:97-97.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّ الذين تَوَفَّاهُمُ}: «توفَّاهم» may be past, and no feminine marker is attached to the verb because the feminine is figurative; and the reading «توفَّتْهم» with the feminine tāʾ indicates that it is a past verb. It may also be imperfect from which one of the two tāʾs has been dropped, the original being «تتوفاهم».
And «ظالمي» is a ḥāl from the pronoun of «توفَّاهم», and the annexation is not pure (ghayr maḥḍa), since the original is «ظالمين أنفسَهم». As to the khabar of this «إنَّ» there are three possibilities. The first: it is omitted, its implied form being: "Those whom the angels take in death have perished", and His saying {قَالُواْ فِيمَ كُنتُمْ} would then explain that omitted clause. The second: it is {فأولئك مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ}, and the fāʾ entered redundantly in the khabar, likening the relative to the conditional noun, and «إنَّ» does not prevent that, though al-Akhfash forbids it; and on this basis His saying {قَالُواْ فِيمَ كُنتُمْ} is either an adjective of «ظالمي» or a ḥāl for the angels, with «قد» implied with it according to those who stipulate that, and on the view of its being an adjective the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "wronging themselves, the angels saying to them". The third: that it is «قالوا فيم كنتم», and the returning pronoun must be implied too, i.e. "they said to them such-and-such"; «فيم» is the khabar of «كنتم», and it is the interrogative «ما» whose alif was dropped when it was governed by a preposition, and the verification of that has been given at His saying: {فَلِمَ تَقْتُلُونَ أَنْبِيَآءَ الله} [al-Baqara: 91]; and the clause «فيمَ كنتم» is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying. «وفي الأرض» is attached to «مستضعفين», and it is not permissible that «في الأرض» be the khabar with «مستضعفين» a ḥāl, as that is permissible in the like of «إن زيدٌ قائماً في الدار», because there would be no benefit in this khabar.
His saying: {فَتُهَاجِرُواْ}: accusative in the answer to the interrogative, and the verification of that has been given. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«ألم تكن» is an interrogative with the meaning of reproach, «فتهاجروا» is accusative as the answer to the interrogative, because the negation became an affirmation through the interrogative." End of his statement. His saying "because the negation..." to the end does not appear as a justification of his saying "accusative as the answer to the interrogative", because that is not correct; nor is it correct to make it the reason for his saying "with the meaning of reproach". And «ساءت»: the discussion of {ساء} has been given, and that it follows the course of «بِئْس», so what is stipulated for the agent of «بئس» is stipulated for its agent. And «مصيراً» is a tamyīz.

semin-durr:98-98.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ المستضعفين}: about this exception there are two views. The first: it is continuous, the thing excepted from being His saying: {فأولئك مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ}; and the pronoun refers to those taken in death while wronging themselves. This speaker said: it is as if it were said "those are in Gehenna except the oppressed", so on this basis it is a continuous exception. The second — and it is the sound one — is that it is discontinuous, because the pronoun in «مَأواهم» refers to His saying: {إِنَّ الذين تَوَفَّاهُمُ}, and these who are taken in death are either disbelievers or disobedient by staying behind, as the commentators said, and they are able to emigrate, so the oppressed are not included among them, and so it is discontinuous. And «من الرجال» is a ḥāl from «المستضعفين», or from the latent pronoun in them, and so is attached to an omitted word.
His saying: {لاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ حِيلَةً}: in this clause there are four possibilities. The first: it is resumptive, an answer to an implied question, as if it were asked: "What is the aspect of their being oppressed?" and so it was said thus.
The second: it is a ḥāl. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "a ḥāl that explains the meaning of being oppressed." I say: he seems to point to the meaning that I gave earlier about its being an answer to an implied question. The third: it is explicative of the very word «المستضعفين», because the aspects of oppression are many, so He clarified by one of its possibilities, as if it were said: "except those who were oppressed because of their incapacity to do such-and-such". The fourth: it is an adjective of «المستضعفين», or of «الرجال» and those after them; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it, and excused describing what is made definite with al-alif wa-l-lām by clauses that have the status of indefinites, in that what is made definite by them, when it is not specific, allows that, as in the saying:
164 - 2- ولقد أَمُرُّ على اللئيم يَسُبُّني ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I often pass by the base man who curses me ...)
and I have given the statement of the question several times already.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الذين يَبْخَلُونَ}: it has seven analyses. One: that it is accusative, a badal (substitute) from «مَنْ», and it is plural by carrying it to the meaning. Two: that it is accusative as a badal from «مختالاً», and also plural for the reason given. Three: that it is accusative by way of blame (dhamm). Four: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and about its khabar (predicate) there are two views. One: that it is omitted; some implied «مُبْغَضُون» ("hated"), by the evidence of {إِنَّ الله لاَ يُحِبُّ}; some implied «معذبون» ("tormented"), because of His saying {وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَاباً}; al-Zamakhsharī implied «أَحِقَّاء بكل مَلامة» ("deserving of every blame"); and Abū al-Baqāʾ implied «أولئك قرناؤهم الشيطان» ("those, their companion is Satan"). The second: that the khabar is His saying {إِنَّ الله لاَ يَظْلِمُ مِثْقَالَ}, and His saying {والذين يُنْفِقُونَ} is conjoined to the mubtadaʾ, with the returning pronoun omitted, the implied meaning being: "those who are miserly, and those who spend their wealth to be seen by people: Allah does not wrong them by the weight of an atom, or the weight of an atom for them." Al-Zajjāj held this, and it is very strained because of the many intervening elements and also because of the unsteadiness of the meaning. Five: that it is the khabar of a latent mubtadaʾ, that is: "they are those who ...". Six: that it is a badal from the latent pronoun in «فخوراً»; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and it is unsteady. Seven: that it is a description of «مَنْ», as if it were said: "He does not love the arrogant, the boastful, the miserly."

And «بالبخل» has two analyses. One: that it is attached to «يأمرون», so the bāʾ is for transitivity, as in «أمرتك بكذا» ("I commanded you to do such-and-such"). The second: that it is the bāʾ of ḥāl (circumstantial), the thing commanded being omitted, and the implied meaning is: "and they command people to thank them while being engaged in miserliness", so in meaning it is like the saying of the poet:

1581 - أجْمَعْتَ أَمْرَيْنِ ضاعَ الحَزْمُ بينهما ... تِيْهَ الملوكِ وأفعالَ المماليكِ
(You have combined two things between which prudence was lost: the pride of kings and the deeds of slaves.)

«المُخْتال» is the arrogant, ignorant one. «المُخْتال» is an active participle of «اختال يختال», that is: he was proud and conceited about himself, and its alif is from a yāʾ, because of their saying «الخُيَلاء» and «المَخْيِلة»; it was also heard: «خَالَ الرجلُ يَخال خَوْلاً» with the first meaning, so for this meaning there are two roots: kh-y-l and kh-w-l. «الفخر» is counting a person's merits and fine qualities, and «فخور» is a form of intensification.

In «البخل» there are four dialectal forms: fatḥa on the khāʾ and the bāʾ, which Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read; ḍamma on both, which al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read; fatḥa on the bāʾ and sukūn on the khāʾ, which Qatāda and Ibn al-Zubayr read; and ḍamma on the bāʾ and sukūn on the khāʾ, which the majority of people read. «البُّخْل» and «البَخَل» are like «الحُزْن» and «الحَزَن», and «العُرْب» and «العَرَب». And {مِن فَضْلِهِ} may be attached to «آتاهم», or to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «ما» or from the pronoun returning to it.

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying: {والذين يُنْفِقُونَ}: it has three analyses. One: that it is nominative, conjoined to «الذين يبخلون», and the khabar (predicate) is {إِنَّ الله لاَ يَظْلِمُ}; that and its weakness have been given. The second: that it is genitive, conjoined to «الكافرين», that is: "We have prepared for the disbelievers and for those who spend their wealth to be seen by people"; Ibn Jarīr said it. The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar is omitted, that is: "tormented", or "their companion is Satan". On the first two it is a conjunction of single words, and on the third a conjunction of clauses.

His saying: {رِئَآءَ الناس}: three analyses. One: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and the conditions for the accusative are met. The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «ينفقون», meaning a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in the place of the ḥāl, that is: "showing off". The third: that it is a ḥāl from the relative noun itself; al-Mahdawī mentioned it. And «رئاءَ» is a maṣdar annexed to its object.

His saying: {وَلاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}: three analyses. One: that it is resumptive. The second: that it is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause); on these two analyses it has no grammatical position. The third: that it is a ḥāl from the agent of «ينفقون». But the last two analyses, I mean conjunction to the ṣila and being a ḥāl, are ruled out on the analysis related from al-Mahdawī, namely that «رئاءَ» is a ḥāl from the relative noun itself; so as not to require separation between the parts of the ṣila, or between the ṣila and what it governs, by a foreign element, namely «رئاءَ», because it is a ḥāl from the relative noun and has no attachment to the ṣila, unlike the case if we make it a mafʿūl lahu or a ḥāl from the agent of «ينفقون», for on both analyses it is governed by «ينفقون», so it is not foreign, and the separation by it is of no concern.

In making {وَلاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ} a ḥāl there is something to consider, in that / some stated that the imperfect verb negated by «لا» is like the affirmative one in that the wāw of ḥāl does not enter it, and that is a point of hesitation. «لا» was repeated in His saying «ولا باليوم», and so was the bāʾ, to signal that faith is negated of each one separately. If you said «لا أضرب زيداً وعمراً», it could mean the negation of striking the pair, which does not necessarily entail the negation of striking each one individually, and it could mean its negation of each individually; but if you say «ولا عمراً», this second is settled.

His saying: {فَسَآءَ قِرِيناً}: about this «ساء» there are two possibilities. One: that it has been transferred to blame and runs the course of «بئس», so it contains a pronoun as its agent explained by the indefinite noun after it, which is «قريناً», and the one specifically blamed is omitted, that is: "evil as a companion is he", and this refers either to Satan, which is the apparent sense, or to «مَن»; the ruling on «نعم» and «بئس» has been given. The second: that it is in its normal sense, so it is transitive and its object is omitted, and «قريناً» on this is accusative as a ḥāl or by qaṭʿ (disjunction), and the implied meaning is: «فساءَه» that is: "Satan has harmed his companion."

They argued for the first analysis that he should have dropped the fāʾ from «فساء», or «قد» should accompany it; because it would then be a conjugated past verb, and what is so and occurs as an apodosis (jawāb) to a condition is stripped of the fāʾ or accompanied by «قد»; this is the sense of the Shaykh's words. There is something to consider in it, because of the saying of the Exalted {وَمَن جَآءَ بالسيئة فَكُبَّتْ} [al-Naml: 90] and {وَإِنْ كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٍ فَكَذَبَتْ} [Yūsuf: 27]; so whatever interpretation is given to this and the like is given to that. Among those who held that «قريناً» is accusative as a ḥāl is Ibn ʿAṭiyya, but it is possible that he held that «ساء» is transitive, and possible that he held the opinion of the Kufans, for they make what comes after «نعم» and «بئس» accusative as a ḥāl.

«القرين» is the companion who is constantly with one, and it is faʿīl in the sense of mufāʿil, like «الخليط» and «الجليس». «القَرْن» is the rope, because two camels are coupled with it. He said:

1582 - وابنُ اللَّبونِ إذا ما لُزَّ في قَرَنٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And the young camel in its second year, when it is tied in a rope-coupling ...)

semin-durr:100-100.t:
And {مُهَاجِراً}: accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «يَخْرج». His saying: {ثُمَّ يُدْرِكْهُ}: the majority read «يدركْه» jussive, conjoined to the condition before it, with its apodosis «فقد وقع». Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read it accusative. Ibn Jinnī said: "This is not easy; its domain is poetry, not the Qur'an", and he recited:
164 - 3- وسأترُكُ منزلي لبني تميم ... وألحقُ بالحجازِ فاستريحا
(I shall leave my home to the Banū Tamīm and join the Hijaz, and so find rest.)
"and the verse is stronger than this because the condition precedes the conjoined element", meaning that the accusative by an implied «أن» occurs only after the wāw and the fāʾ in the answer to the eight things, or a conjunction, in a detail whose place is the books of grammar, and the accusative by an implied «أن» elsewhere than those places is a poetic necessity, like the previous verse and the saying of another:
164 - 4-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ويَأْوي إليها المستجيرُ فيُعْصَما
(... and the one seeking protection takes refuge in it and is protected.)
Al-Zamakhsharī followed Abū al-Fatḥ in that, and recited the first verse. This question was allowed by the Kufans for another basis, namely that a verb occurring between the condition and the consequence may be nominative, accusative or jussive when it occurs after the wāw and the fāʾ, and they argued from the saying of the poet:
164 - 5- ومَنْ لا يُقَدِّمْ رِجْلَه مطمئنةً ... فَيُثْبِتَها في مستوى القاعِ يَزْلَقِ
(Whoever does not advance his foot steadily and plant it on level ground will slip.)
and the saying of another:
164 - 6- ومَنْ يَقْتَرِبْ منا ويخضع نُؤْوِه ... ولا يَخْشَ ظلماً ما أقامَ ولا هَضْما
(Whoever draws near us and submits, we shelter him, and he need not fear wrong or injustice as long as he stays.)
And if that is established with the wāw and the fāʾ, let it be permissible with «ثم», because it is a conjunction. Al-Nakhaʿī and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read it with ḍamma on the kāf, and Ibn Jinnī analysed it as an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. «ثم هو يدركُه الموت», conjoining a nominal clause to a verbal one, which is the clause of the condition: the jussive verb and its agent; and on that basis Yūnus explained the saying of al-Aʿshā:
164 - 7- إنْ تركَبوا فركوبُ الخيل عادتُنا ... أو تَنْزِلون فإنَّا معشرٌ نُزُلُ
(If you ride, riding horses is our custom; or if you dismount, we are a company of dismounters.)
i.e. «وأنتم تنزلون», and like it:
164 - 8- إنْ تُذْنِبوا ثم تأتيني بَقِيَّتُكُمْ ... فما عليَّ بذنبٍ عندكم حُوبُ
(If you sin, then the remnant of you comes to me, there is no blame on me for a sin with you.)
i.e. «ثم أنتم تأتيني». I say: he means that it is not to be explained as ignoring the jussive particle so that the verb after it is nominative, as it is nominative in «أليم يأتيك» without dropping the yāʾ; the grammarians recited this verse as showing that the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the vowel implied on the weak letter, and they joined other verses to it; but that they claim that the jussive particle is ignored and argue from this verse, no. Some analysed it another way, namely that he wanted to pause on the word, so he transferred the vowel of the pronoun hāʾ to the kāf that was sākin because of the jussive, like the saying of another:
164 - 9- عَجِبْتُ والدهرُ كثيرٌ عَجَبُهْ ... مِنْ عَنَزِيٍّ سَبَّني لم أَضْرِبُهْ
(I marvelled — and time's marvels are many — at a man of ʿAnaza who cursed me, and I did not strike him.)
he means «لم أَضْرِبْه» with sukūn on the bāʾ because of the jussive, then he transferred to it the vowel of the hāʾ, so the wording became «ثُم يُدْرِكُهْ»; then he treated continuous speech like a pause, so two sākin letters met and he needed to vowel the first, which is the hāʾ, so he gave it ḍamma, because it is the original and also for conformity. These possibilities sharpen the mind and refine it.

semin-durr:101-101.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَن تَقْصُرُواْ}: this is on the omission of the preposition, i.e. «في أَنْ تَقْصُروا», so «أَنْ» has the two well-known possibilities of position, and this preposition is attached to the word «جُناح», i.e. "there is no blame upon you in shortening the prayer". The majority read «تَقْصُروا» from the triliteral «قَصَر». Ibn ʿAbbās read «تُقْصِروا» from «أَقْصر», and these are two dialectal forms, qaṣara and aqṣara, as al-Azharī related them, and al-Ḍabbī read, from his narrators, the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās. Al-Zuhrī read «تُقَصِّروا» with shadda, for intensification. His saying: {مِنَ الصلاة}: about «مِنْ» there are two possibilities, the more apparent of which is that it is partitive, and this is the meaning of Abū al-Baqāʾ's statement, who claimed that it is the view of Sībawayh and that it is an adjective of an omitted word, its implied form being "something of the prayer". The second: it is redundant, and this is the opinion of al-Akhfash, who stipulates no condition for its being redundant. And «أن يَفْتِنَكم» is the object of «خِفْتم». ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and Ubayy read «من الصلاة أن يَفْتنكم», dropping the conditional clause, and «أَنْ يفْتنكم» in this reading is an object of purpose; the dialect of the Hijaz is «فَتَن» triliteral, and Tamīm and Qays say «أفتن» quadriliteral.
And «لكم» is attached to an omitted word, because it is a ḥāl from «عَدُوّاً», for in origin it is an adjective of an indefinite noun and then was put before it; Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be attached to «كان», and there is disagreement on the question whose detail has been given. «عَدُواً» is singular although what is meant is the plural, for what was verified earlier in al-Baqara; and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. It was also said: the sentence is complete at His saying {مِنَ الصلاة}, and the conditional clause is resumptive, so that it was even said that it was revealed a year after the revelation of what precedes it, and in that case its apodosis is also omitted, but is implied from the same kind as what follows it; this is a weak view, and the delay of its revelation does not require that it be resumptive.

semin-durr:102-102.t:
The pronoun in «فيهم» refers to those who travel in the land; it was also said: to those who fear; both are possible. The pronoun in «وليأخذوا» apparently refers to «طائفة», because of its nearness to it, and because the pronoun in His saying {سَجَدُواْ} is for it. It was also said: it refers to another group, which is the one guarding the praying one. Al-Zajjāj preferred its referring to all of them, saying: "because it is more awe-inspiring to the enemy". «السلاح» is what one fights with, and its plural is «أَسْلِحَة», and it is masculine, and may be feminine in the sense of the weapon's edge; al-Ṭirimmāḥ said:
165 - 0- يَهُزُّ سِلاحاً لم يَرِثْها كَلالةً ... يشكُّ بها منها غموضَ المَغَابِنِ
(He brandishes a weapon he did not inherit remotely, with which he pierces the hidden folds of the body.)
so he returned the pronoun to it as the pronoun of a feminine. One says «سِلاح» like «حِمار», «سِلْح» like «ضِلْع», «سُلَح» like «صُرَد», and «سُلْحان» like «سُلْطان», as Abū Bakr ibn Durayd reported. «السَّلِيح» is a plant which, when camels graze it, they grow fat and their milk becomes abundant; and what a camel throws out of its belly is called «سُلاح» on the pattern of «غُلام», then it was used for every excrement, so that it was said of the bustard: «سِلاحُه سُلاحه» ("its weapon is its dung").
His saying: {لَمْ يُصَلُّواْ}: the clause is in the position of the nominative because it is an adjective of «طائفة» after an adjective, and it may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, because the indefinite noun before it was specified by being described by another. Al-Ḥasan read «فَلِتَقُمْ» with kasra on the lām of the imperative, which is the original. Abū Ḥaywa read «وليأت» on the basis of treating «الطائفة» as masculine. From Abū ʿAmr is narrated both the clear pronunciation and the assimilation in «ولتأت طائفة», and the aspects of these are clear. In His saying {وَلْيَأْخُذُواْ حِذْرَهُمْ وَأَسْلِحَتَهُمْ} there is a figure of speech, in that caution (ḥidhr) — which is one of the abstract meanings — is made something taken together with weapons, making it like an instrument, and it is like His saying the Exalted: {تَبَوَّءُوا الدار والإيمان} [al-Ḥashr: 9] in one of the possibilities. The discussion of «لو» occurring after {وَدَّ} [verse 109] has already been given, here and in al-Baqara. «أَمْتِعاتِكم» was read, which is anomalous in that it is a plural of a plural, like their saying «أَسْقِيات» and «أَعْطِيات». And His saying: {أَن تضعوا} is like His saying: {أَن تَقْصُرُواْ}, which has been given.

semin-durr:103-103.t: His saying, the Exalted: {قِيَاماً وَقُعُوداً}: two ḥāls from the agent of «اذكروا», and likewise «وعلى جُنوبكم», for it is equivalent to "lying on their sides", and so is attached to an omitted word. And His saying: {فَإِذَا اطمأننتم}: the discussion of this root has been given in al-Baqara, with the people's disagreement about it, and whether it is transposed or not. Abū al-Baqāʾ stated here that the hamza is original and that the pattern of «الطُّمَأْنينة» is fuʿaʾlīla, and that «طأمن» is another independent root; this is the view of al-Jarmī. And «موقوتاً» is an adjective of «كتاباً» in the sense of "limited by times"; it is from the lightened «وَقَت» like «مضروب» from «ضرب»; and he did not say «مَوْقوتة» with the tāʾ, taking into account «كتاب», which in origin is a maṣdar.

semin-durr:104-104.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ تَهِنُواْ}: the majority read it with kasra on the hāʾ, and al-Ḥasan with fatḥa, from «وَهِن» with kasra in the past, or from «وَهَن» with fatḥa, and the ʿayn was given fatḥa only because it is a guttural letter, so it is like «يَدَع». ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read «تُهانوا» from «الإهانة», passive, and its meaning is: "do not engage in such cowardice and weakness as would be a cause of your being humiliated", like their saying «لا أُرَيَنَّك ههنا» ("let me not see you here"). Al-Aʿraj read «أن تكونوا» with fatḥa, as a cause. Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb and Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir read «تِئْلمون فإنهم يِئْلمون كما تِئْلمون» with kasra on the imperfect prefix, and Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ with kasra on the address-tāʾ only; and this is an established dialect. I had earlier stated in al-Fātiḥa that whoever puts kasra on the imperfect prefix excepts the tāʾ, and I mentioned the anomaly of «تِيجل» and its explanation, so turn your attention to it. Abū al-Baqāʾ added, for the reading with kasra on the imperfect prefix, the changing of the hamza into yāʾ, while others left that unqualified.

semin-durr:105-105.t: His saying, the Exalted: {بالحق}: in the position of the accusative as a corroborating ḥāl, and so attached to an omitted word, and the owner of the ḥāl is «الكتاب», i.e. "We sent it down, accompanied by the truth". And «لتحكمْ» is attached to «أَنْزلنا». And «أراك» is transitive to two objects, one of which is the omitted returning pronoun and the second the address-kāf, i.e. «بما أراكه الله». «الإراءَة» here may be from opinion (raʾy), as you say «رأيتُ رَأْيَ الشافعي», or from knowing, and on either implication the verb before the transfer by hamza is transitive to one and after it to two, as you know. And «للخائنين» is attached to «خصيماً», and the lām is for cause, in its normal sense; it was also said that it means «عن», which is nothing, since the meaning is sound without that. The object of «خصيماً» is omitted, its implied form being «خصيماً البرآء»; and «خصيم» may be a form of intensification like «ضريب», and may be of the meaning of mufāʿil, like «خَلِيط» and «جَلِيس», meaning "disputing with", "mixing with" and "sitting with".

semin-durr:108-108.t: And {يَسْتَخْفُونَ}: it has two possibilities, the more apparent of which is that it is resumptive, merely to report that they seek concealment from Allah the Exalted through their ignorance. The second: it is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of «مَنْ» in His saying: {لاَ يُحِبُّ مَن كَانَ خَوَّاناً أَثِيماً}, the pronoun being plural in view of its meaning if you take «مَنْ» as an indefinite noun with a description; or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from «مَنْ» if you take it as a relative, the pronoun being plural in view of its meaning also. «وهو معهم» is a circumstantial clause: either from Allah the Exalted or from those who conceal; and «إذ» is accusative by the governor in the adverbial that occurs as a khabar, which is «معهم».

semin-durr:109-109.t: The discussion of the like of {هَا أَنْتُمْ هؤلاء} has already been given. And His saying: {فَمَن يُجَادِلُ}: «مَنْ» is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and «يجادل» is its khabar; «أم» is discontinuous (munqaṭiʿa) and is not a conjunction. The apparent sense of Makkī's expression is that it is a conjunction, for he said: "and «أم من يكونُ مثلُها» is conjoined to it", i.e. like «مَنْ» in His saying {فَمَن يُجَادِلُ}; and this is open to consideration, because about the discontinuous «أم» there is disagreement: is it called a conjunction or not?

semin-durr:112-112.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ثُمَّ يَرْمِ بِهِ}: about this hāʾ there are several statements. The first: it refers to «إثماً»; and of two elements conjoined by «أو», the pronoun may refer to the conjoined one, as in this verse, and to the one conjoined to, as in His saying {وَإِذَا رَأَوْاْ تِجَارَةً أَوْ لَهْواً انفضوا إِلَيْهَا} [al-Jumuʿa: 11]. The second: it refers to the earning indicated by the verb, like {اعدلوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ للتقوى} [al-Māʾida: 8]. The third: it refers to one of the two mentioned, as indicated by the conjunction with «أو», for it is equivalent to "then he hurls one of the two mentioned". The fourth: there is an omission in the sentence, and the original is: «ومَنْ يكسِبْ خطيئة ثم يرم بها», and this is as was said about His saying: {والذين يَكْنِزُونَ الذهب والفضة وَلاَ يُنفِقُونَهَا} [al-Tawba: 34], i.e. "they hoard gold and do not spend it". And «أو» here is for the specification of what was vague, and its counterparts have been given. Muʿādh ibn Jabal read «يَكِسِّبْ» with kasra on the kāf and shadda on the sīn, the original being «يَكْتَسِبْ»; the tāʾ of iftiʿāl was assimilated into the sīn and the kāf was given kasra for conformity, and this is similar to {يَخْطَفُ} [al-Baqara: 20], whose explanation was given in al-Baqara. Al-Zuhrī read «خَطِيَّة» with shadda, which is the regular lightening of it.
His saying: {وَلَوْلاَ فَضْلُ الله}: about the apodosis of «لولا» there are two possibilities, the more apparent of which is that it is mentioned, namely His saying «لَهَمَّتْ». The second: it is omitted, i.e. «لأضلُّوك», and then He began a new clause, saying «لَهَمَّتْ», i.e. «لقد هَمَّتْ». Abū al-Baqāʾ said on this possibility: "And like the omission of the apodosis here is its omission in His saying: {وَلَوْلاَ فَضْلُ الله عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ وَأَنَّ الله تَوَّابٌ حَكِيمٌ} [al-Nūr: 10]." It seems that the one who implied the apodosis as omitted found it problematic that His saying «لهمَّتْ» be the apodosis, because the wording requires the negation of their intending that, while the point is that what occurred is that they did intend, according to what is narrated in the story; for that reason he implied it as omitted. And the one who made it present answered this in one of two ways: either by specifying the intention, i.e. "they would have intended an intention that has effect with you", or by specifying the leading astray, i.e. "they would lead you astray from your religion and your law"; and neither of these two intentions occurred. And «اَنْ يُضِلُّونك» is on the omission of the bāʾ, i.e. «بأن يُضِلُّوك», so there is the well-known disagreement about its position; and «مِنْ» in «من شيء» is redundant, and «شيء» is meant as a maṣdar, i.e. "they do not harm you with harm, little or much".

semin-durr:114-114.t:
